name: ALARA BMA Neuro Access Kit (ALARA BMAN and ALARA BMAC kits)
composition: Bone marrow aspiration needle kit that combines pedicle pilot-hole preparation with proximity feedback to nerves and bone marrow aspiration during spine surgery; BMAC variant adds a needle for cancellous bone core biopsy.

regulatory.reference: K240664 (decision 2024-08-09) and K243945 (decision 2025-04-24), product code KNW; predicates Ranfac Bone Marrow Aspiration Needle K131157 and ALARA Neuro Access Kit K190163
on_label_indications: 'Indicated for aspiration of bone marrow or autologous blood. The ALARA BMA Neuro Access Kit is indicated for pedicle pilot hole preparation, locating, and identifying spinal roots/nerves by providing proximity feedback. The ALARA BMAC Needle is intended for use in harvesting core biopsy samples of cancellous bone and/or bone marrow.' No claim for the use of the marrow in fusion. Regulatory frame for every BMAC system: the 510(k)s (product codes JQC, QBV, ORG) clear a point-of-care centrifuge kit to prepare a bone marrow concentrate, or PRP to be mixed with bone graft; several state 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established'. Injection of BMAC into a joint, tendon or osteonecrotic femoral head is an off-label use of the device. FDA treats the autologous marrow product as outside premarket review (not an HCT/P when minimally manipulated and used homologously, 21 CFR 1271.3(d)(4); or same-surgical-procedure exception) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Class-level evidence for BMAC as an extender in fusion is mostly uncontrolled.
applications.caveats: Aspiration during pedicle preparation is on-label; use of the marrow as graft extender is the surgeon's choice and not claimed. Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: As above. Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; no separate payment for the aspiration kit.
bd.notes: SurGenTec pairs marrow aspiration with its spine graft delivery products; the BMA kit makes harvest a no-extra-incision step.

name: SMART M-CELL Bone Marrow Concentration System and SMART M-CELL PRP Concentration System
composition: Disposable kits for a centrifuge: one concentrates bone marrow aspirate, one extracts platelet concentrate from venous blood; both predicated on Harvest SmartPReP2.

regulatory.reference: K250518 (SMART M-CELL Bone Marrow Concentration System) and K250516 (SMART M-CELL PRP Concentration System), both decision 2026-04-02, product code QBV (Class I centrifuge for preparation of cell concentrate and/or plasma concentrate, 21 CFR 862.2050); predicate SmartPReP2 K052925
on_label_indications: K250518: 'intended to be used in the clinical laboratory or intraoperatively at point-of-care for the safe and rapid preparation of a cell concentrate from bone marrow.' K250516: platelet concentrate from a small volume of venous whole blood after centrifugal separation. Product code QBV states 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established.' Regulatory frame for every BMAC system: the 510(k)s (product codes JQC, QBV, ORG) clear a point-of-care centrifuge kit to prepare a bone marrow concentrate, or PRP to be mixed with bone graft; several state 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established'. Injection of BMAC into a joint, tendon or osteonecrotic femoral head is an off-label use of the device. FDA treats the autologous marrow product as outside premarket review (not an HCT/P when minimally manipulated and used homologously, 21 CFR 1271.3(d)(4); or same-surgical-procedure exception) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

challenge: QBV is a new Class I code created to move marrow and plasma concentrators out of the PRP-for-bone-graft code; the label here carries no in vivo claim at all.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Cleared 2026-04-02; no in vivo indication. Off-label injection.

evidence.title: Inefficacy of autologous bone marrow concentrate in stage three osteonecrosis: a randomized controlled double-blind trial
evidence.finding: Class-level: Core decompression with BMAC vs without in stage 3 osteonecrosis (23 hips per arm, 19 patients per arm): 15 of 23 hips in each arm needed THR; BMAC added nothing.

name: Adaptive Autologous Processing System (AAPS)
composition: Single-use syringe assembly with a hollow threaded plunger and locking collar for density separation in a desktop centrifuge; plasma and buffy coat are aspirated into a secondary chamber and red cells discarded.

regulatory.reference: BK230807 (Adaptive Autologous Processing System, decision 2023-05-10, ORG; predicate Arthrex Double Syringe (ACP) System BK190406)
on_label_indications: 'Indicated to be used for the safe and rapid preparation of autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from a small sample of peripheral blood at the patient point-of-care. The PRP is mixed with autograft and/or allograft bone prior to application to a bony defect for improving handling characteristics.' Clinical evidence in the summary is bench only (platelet yield, recovery, function, bone graft retention). Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Bench testing only in the 510(k); graft handling on-label, no healing claim. Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Graft handling only. Class-level evidence for spine PRP is neutral to negative. Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

evidence.title: Platelet gel (AGF) fails to increase fusion rates in instrumented posterolateral fusions
evidence.finding: Class-level (different platelet-gel system): 76 instrumented PLFs with iliac crest graft plus autologous growth factor platelet gel vs matched controls: nonunion 25% vs 17% (p=.18), no benefit. System is a proprietary platelet-gel method, not one of the brands in this file.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered: cash-pay in the clinic; kit cost bundled into the procedure or patient fee. No HCPCS code for the product; CPT 0232T (PRP injection) is Category III and generally non-covered by Medicare and most commercial plans for musculoskeletal use. Chronic diabetic wound PRP is the one covered exception (CMS NCD 270.3, 2021).
bd.notes: A textbook example of a bench-only ORG clearance that chains to Arthrex ACP as predicate.

name: BTI ENDORET Kit (PRGF-Endoret, plasma rich in growth factors)
company: B.T.I. Biotechnology Institute, S.L. (Miñano, Álava, Spain)
composition: Closed tube-based kit and dedicated centrifuge producing a leukocyte-free, moderate-platelet (about 2-3x) plasma rich in growth factors, activated with calcium chloride; the original PRGF technique of Anitua.

regulatory.reference: BK251157 (ENDORET Kit, decision 2025-10-03, ORG)
on_label_indications: 'Designed to be used for the safe and rapid preparation of autologous platelet-rich-plasma (PRP) from a small sample of peripheral blood at the patient's point of care. The PRP is mixed with autograft and/or allograft bone prior to application to a bony defect for improving handling characteristics.' Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. challenge: The knee-OA RCTs were run on BTI's European-marketed system years before the 2025 US clearance, and the clearance itself covers only bone graft handling.

applications.evidence_summary: Two RCTs of PRGF-Endoret vs HA: Sanchez 2012 (n=176) response rate 14.1 percentage points higher (p=.044); Vaquerizo 2013 (n=96) PRGF superior to a single Durolane injection.
applications.caveats: Comparator was HA, not placebo; HA itself has weak evidence (AAOS 2021 not recommended); BTI-linked authors; European system equivalence to the 2025 US kit assumed, not verified. Off-label in the US.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Off-label.

evidence.title: A randomized clinical trial evaluating plasma rich in growth factors (PRGF-Endoret) versus hyaluronic acid in the short-term treatment of symptomatic knee osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: PRGF-Endoret (BTI) vs HA, three weekly injections: response rate 14.1 percentage points higher with PRGF (95% CI 0.5 to 27.6; p=.044); secondary outcomes numerically favored PRGF without significance.

evidence.title: Comparison of intra-articular injections of plasma rich in growth factors (PRGF-Endoret) versus Durolane hyaluronic acid in the treatment of patients with symptomatic osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial
evidence.finding: Three weekly PRGF-Endoret (BTI) injections vs one Durolane injection: PRGF was significantly more effective on pain and function scores.

evidence.title: Effect of Intra-articular Platelet-Rich Plasma vs Placebo Injection on Pain and Medial Tibial Cartilage Volume in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: The RESTORE Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.finding: Class-level (placebo-controlled, product not named): Leukocyte-poor PRP (a commercial product, not named in the abstract) vs saline: 12-month knee pain change -2.1 vs -1.8 (difference -0.4, 95% CI -0.9 to 0.2) and no cartilage-volume benefit.

evidence.title: Platelet gel (AGF) fails to increase fusion rates in instrumented posterolateral fusions
evidence.finding: Class-level (different platelet-gel system): 76 instrumented PLFs with iliac crest graft plus autologous growth factor platelet gel vs matched controls: nonunion 25% vs 17% (p=.18), no benefit. System is a proprietary platelet-gel method, not one of the brands in this file.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered: cash-pay in the clinic; kit cost bundled into the procedure or patient fee. No HCPCS code for the product; CPT 0232T (PRP injection) is Category III and generally non-covered by Medicare and most commercial plans for musculoskeletal use. Chronic diabetic wound PRP is the one covered exception (CMS NCD 270.3, 2021).
bd.notes: Isto's biologics (NovaBone, Magellan/Precise) are sold to spine and trauma accounts; a hiring manager may ask how Precise supersedes Magellan.

name: AMNIOEFFECT (surgical placental allograft)
ownership_history: MiMedx Surgical portfolio; launched 2023 (launch year from company materials, not independently confirmed).
composition: Placental membrane allograft for surgical use; layer composition not confirmed from a primary source.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)
on_label_indications: Homologous use as a surgical barrier/covering; MiMedx positions it for 'lower extremity repair, plastic surgery, vascular surgery and multiple orthopedic repairs and reconstruction'.

applications.evidence_summary: No published orthopedic study of AMNIOEFFECT located (PubMed 2026-10-23); the only registered trial is in thyroid/parathyroid surgery scars (NCT07173621, n=334, enrolling).
applications.caveats: Barrier/wrap use only.

evidence.title: AMNIOEFFECT vs standard of care on post-operative healing after transcutaneous thyroid and parathyroid surgery
evidence.finding: Enrolling by invitation; completion 2027; not orthopedic.

bd.reimbursement: Surgical use; bundled in DRG/APC; no Q-code located.
bd.notes: Named by MiMedx as a driver of 2025 Surgical growth.

name: AXIOFILL (placental particulate)
ownership_history: MiMedx; launched about 2021 as a particulate successor to its earlier placental particulate (AmnioFill). FDA issued a Warning Letter on 21 Dec 2023 after inspections; RFD determination March 2024 that it is not a 361 HCT/P; MiMedx sued in N.D. Georgia and keeps selling it while the case runs.
composition: Human placental-derived particulate (MiMedx calls it a particulate wound dressing) for deep wound defects.

regulatory.reference: Contested. MiMedx markets it as a 361 HCT/P; FDA Warning Letter 21 Dec 2023 and a March 2024 Request-for-Designation decision that it does not meet Section 361 criteria (FDA treats it as Section 351). Litigation pending (N.D. Ga.).
on_label_indications: MiMedx positioning: 'replacement or supplementation of damaged or inadequate integumental tissue'. FDA has determined it is not a 361 product, so no lawful 361 indication is settled.

challenge: A hiring manager will ask which particulate placental products FDA has already called 351: AXIOFILL (MiMedx), Interfyl (Celularity) and PalinGen Flow (Amnio Technology) are the named examples; StimLabs and BioTissue moved their particulates to 510(k).

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for deep integumental defects; no published study of AXIOFILL in post-debridement diabetic-foot or osteomyelitis cavities located (PubMed 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: FDA classification dispute; not a bone void filler; no antibiotic delivery.

bd.reimbursement: No Q-code located for AXIOFILL (HCPCS lookup 2026-10-23); surgical use bundled.
bd.notes: The litigation outcome will set precedent for particulate placental products.

name: Catalyze (formerly Clarix Flo / Neox Flo; amniotic membrane and umbilical cord particulate)
ownership_history: TissueTech/BioTissue particulate sold as Clarix Flo (surgical) and Neox Flo (wound). BioTissue Holdings obtained 510(k) K253204 for 'Catalyze' on 5 June 2026; BioStem holds rights to commercialize it and owes BioTissue a clearance payment of up to $10M.
composition: Lyophilized, micronized human amniotic membrane and umbilical cord extracellular matrix particles (AM/UC particulate).

regulatory.reference: K253204 (Catalyze, cleared 2026-06-05, product code KGN; predicate K231325 StimLabs Corplex P)
on_label_indications: Management of partial- and full-thickness wounds, pressure, venous, diabetic and chronic vascular ulcers, tunneled/undermined wounds, surgical wounds (donor sites/grafts, post-Mohs, post-laser, podiatric, dehiscence), trauma wounds and draining wounds (K253204 indications for use)

challenge: The 510(k) is a wound-dressing clearance. Injecting the particulate into a knee, tendon or ligament (as in the published Clarix Flo case series) is off-label for the device and, for the old 361 version, non-homologous.

applications.evidence_summary: Uncontrolled AM/UC particulate series: Castellanos 2019 prospective pilot (50 mg, pain 74 to 37 on WOMAC-A at 24 weeks) and Mead 2020 (n=42, KL 3-4, 74% PGIC improvement at 12 months). BioTissue then took the same tissue into a saline-controlled Phase 2 (TTAX03).
applications.caveats: No control arm; author ties to TissueTech; off-label for the 510(k) device.

applications.evidence_summary: 10 collegiate football players injected for MCL, hamstring and abdominal tears returned to play at about 30 days (retrospective, author is a BioTissue speaker).
applications.caveats: n=10, no comparator; muscle/ligament rather than chronic tendinopathy.

applications.evidence_summary: Cleared for tunneled/undermined and diabetic wounds, so it can fill a soft-tissue cavity after debridement; no study after osteomyelitis resection located.
applications.caveats: Wound dressing, not a bone void filler or antibiotic carrier.

evidence.title: Injectable Amniotic Membrane/Umbilical Cord Particulate for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Prospective, Single-Center Pilot Study
evidence.finding: WOMAC-A pain fell from 74.3 to 37.4 at 24 weeks; some patients needed a second injection; uncontrolled.

evidence.title: Intra-Articular Injection of Amniotic Membrane and Umbilical Cord Particulate for the Management of Moderate to Severe Knee Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: KL 3-4 knees: 74% reported significant improvement (PGIC) at 12 months; OMERACT-OARSI response 81%; author fees from TissueTech.

evidence.title: Injection of Amniotic Membrane and Umbilical Cord Particulate for Muscle and Ligament Tears in Collegiate Football Athletes: A Single-Center, Retrospective Study
evidence.finding: Return to play at 29.6 days on average; no complications; no control.

bd.reimbursement: Q4155 (NeoxFlo or ClarixFlo, 1 mg) exists for the legacy product; as a 510(k) wound dressing it falls in the 510(k) skin-substitute category under the 2026 flat-rate rule.
bd.notes: Second human-tissue particulate to reach 510(k) after StimLabs Corplex P.

name: Corplex P / Theracor P / Allacor P (umbilical cord and amnion particulate, 510(k))
ownership_history: StimLabs, LLC. First clearance K231325 (2 Feb 2024), updated K242828 (18 Oct 2024); Theracor K253339 (22 Dec 2025).
composition: Dehydrated human perinatal-tissue extracellular-matrix particles (umbilical cord based) applied as a wound dressing.

on_label_indications: Wound management indications per the 510(k) (same indication list Catalyze copied: partial/full-thickness wounds, ulcers, surgical and trauma wounds, tunneled wounds)

challenge: The first human birth-tissue particulate to use the 510(k) door rather than claim 361 status; it is the predicate for BioTissue's Catalyze. Wound labeling only.

applications.evidence_summary: Cleared wound dressing that can fill tunneled defects after debridement; StimLabs real-world wound series (NCT07215741, n=23) completed 2025; no osteomyelitis study located.
applications.caveats: Wound dressing only.

evidence.title: Case series of StimLabs dehydrated human umbilical cord particulate for acute and chronic wounds
evidence.finding: Enrolling by invitation.

bd.reimbursement: Q4231 (Corplex P per cc) is retired; HCPCS A2035 ('Corplex P/Theracor P/Allacor P, mg') now applies; as a 510(k) product it sits in the 510(k) skin-substitute category under the 2026 flat-rate rule.

name: Adaptos Fuse Bone Graft (PLCL/TCP/bioactive glass granules)
composition: Granules of poly(L-lactide-co-epsilon-caprolactone) (PLCL), tricalcium phosphate and bioactive glass, supplied in open-bore syringes.

on_label_indications: Bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to stability, 'posterolateral spine, intervertebral disc space, and pelvis'; granules must be mixed with autograft prior to use; in interbody fusion must be used with a cleared cage

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Adaptos Fuse OR Biomendex).
applications.caveats: Cleared February 2026; no clinical data yet; autograft extender label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Adaptos Fuse interbody).
applications.caveats: With a cleared cage.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Cleared Feb 2026; US launch not confirmed.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Finnish polymer-ceramic maker; US partner not identified.

name: Citrepore Bone Void Filler
ownership_history: Acuitive Technologies, Inc. (Allendale, NJ), maker of the Citregen citrate-polymer tendon screws.
composition: Highly porous, pliable, sponge-like polymer-bioceramic composite: 60 wt% citrate-based elastomeric polymer and 40 wt% 45S5 bioactive glass (ASTM F1538).

on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure, surgically created or from traumatic injury; filling bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities and pelvis'; may be combined with saline, autogenous blood and/or bone marrow; resorbs and is replaced with bone

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Citrepore OR citrate-based bioactive glass bone void filler).
applications.caveats: Cleared 2024 on bench and animal data; no human series.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Citrepore calcaneus).
applications.caveats: Extremities named.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No trial registered; company launch details not read.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Sponge-style handling is the differentiator versus putties.

name: AGN1 (JGH1) injectable triphasic calcium-based bone graft substitute, Local Osteo-Enhancement Procedure (LOEP)
composition: Resorbable triphasic calcium-based implant material, injected as a paste that cures in situ; used for LOEP in the osteoporotic proximal femur.

regulatory.reference: K181342 (JGH1 Bone Graft Substitute, July 2018); K181585 (JGH1 Core Decompression Procedure Kit, July 2018). Link between the 'JGH1' 510(k) name and the 'AGN1' name used in publications is assumed, not sourced.
on_label_indications: JGH1 paste: bone graft substitute injected or digitally packed into open bone voids/gaps not intrinsic to stability 'extremities and pelvis' to cure in situ; voids may be from benign bone cysts and tumors (adults and pediatric patients 6 and older), surgical or traumatic; can augment provisional hardware such as K-wires; temporary support only
Prophylactic augmentation of the osteoporotic proximal femur (LOEP) is not a cleared indication

applications.evidence_summary: First-in-human prospective cohort of 12 postmenopausal osteoporotic women: injected femurs gained about 58 to 68% femoral-neck areal BMD over untreated controls at 12 weeks to 5-7 years, FEA strength up 22 to 41%, AGN1 resorbed and replaced with bone (PMID 31802158; QCT follow-up PMID 40297188).
applications.caveats: n=12, uncontrolled except contralateral femur, company-supported; surrogate endpoints (BMD, finite element strength), not fracture. The pivotal RESTORE RCT (NCT04796350, n=2,400 planned, recruiting, primary completion est. April 2027) is the fracture-prevention test.
applications.challenge: Any claim of hip-fracture prevention is investigational until RESTORE reads out.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: AGN1 OR JGH1 bone cyst curettage).
applications.caveats: The cleared void-filler indication names benign cysts and tumors; no case series located.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: AGN1 OR JGH1 core decompression osteonecrosis). A JGH1 core decompression procedure kit (K181585) was cleared in 2018.
applications.caveats: Kit clearance is for the instruments; no outcomes located.

evidence.title: Treatment of bone loss in proximal femurs of postmenopausal osteoporotic women with AGN1 local osteo-enhancement procedure (LOEP) increases hip bone mineral density and hip strength: a long-term prospective cohort study
evidence.finding: Treated femoral-neck aBMD rose 58 to 68% over controls and estimated femoral strength by 22 to 41% through 5-7 years.

evidence.title: AGN1 local osteo-enhancement procedure increases proximal femur volumetric bone mineral density of women with post-menopausal osteoporosis as assessed by quantitative computed tomography analysis
evidence.finding: QCT showed AGN1 resorption with new bone formation and increased volumetric BMD at 5-7 years.

evidence.title: RESTORE - Study of AGN1 LOEP to Prevent Secondary Hip Fractures
evidence.finding: Pivotal randomized trial of AGN1 LOEP versus control at index hip fracture surgery to prevent secondary hip fractures; recruiting.

pipeline.expected_milestone: RESTORE primary completion estimated April 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov)

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: A novel, procedure-defining use (prophylactic augmentation) that would need coding and coverage work; RESTORE results drive any payer story. Additional AgNovos trials: STRONG (NCT03268356, n=13), RECONFIRM (NCT05202678, EU, n=150), GRACE (NCT05966974, n=44).

name: Montage XT Cranial Cement (Montage and Permatage settable bone putty family)
company: Abyrx, Inc. (manufacturer of record Orthocon, Inc.)
ownership_history: Orthocon, Inc. is the 510(k) holder and FDA letters are addressed in care of Abyrx, Inc., Stamford, CT; Abyrx markets Montage. A reported transaction created MedEdge Holdings as owner of Abyrx and Kairuku (date and terms unverified). SurgiCor was the announced US distributor from 2014 to 2017.
composition: Two-component settable, resorbable calcium phosphate putty (Montage) and a flowable paste; XT doubles hardening time; Permatage is a non-resorbable variant

regulatory.reference: K221933 (Montage Settable, Resorbable Bone Putty, cranial GXP, 2023-01-13); K231475 (Montage-QS, 2023-10-12); K232771 (Montage Flowable, 2024-02-16); K241027 (Permatage, 2024-09-26); K253854 (Montage XT Cranial Cement, Special 510(k), 2026-01-02); K253732 (Permatage Flowable, 2026-03-13); K261265 (Permatage XT, 2026-06-15); separate MQV bone void filler clearances K222063 and K243526
on_label_indications: Self-setting calcium phosphate cement indicated for use in the repair of neurosurgical burr holes, contiguous craniotomy cuts and other cranial defects with a surface area no larger than 25 cm2; should be used only in skeletally mature individuals (K253854, identical to predicate K221933)
Cardiothoracic (sternotomy) clearance September 2023 for Montage Settable Bone Putty

applications.evidence_summary: No published clinical data found on PubMed as of 2026-10-22; the January 2026 XT cranial clearance was a Special 510(k) (30-day review) resting on the 2023 predicate.
applications.caveats: Cranial flap fixation with Montage Flowable (NCT07103330, n=100, start March 2026) is outside the labeled indication.

applications.evidence_summary: Labeled to 25 cm2 like the legacy cements; no cranioplasty series.
applications.caveats: Eight cranial and bone-void 510(k)s in three years with no clinical publications.

evidence.title: Evaluation of cranial flap fixation with Montage Flowable Settable Bone Paste
evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting as of July 2025 verification; estimated start March 2026, primary completion December 2027; compares flap fixation with paste alone against metallic hardware.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Flap-fixation data 2027 to 2028 if the study enrolls; any flap-fixation claim would need a new 510(k) or De Novo (source: ClinicalTrials.gov record and K253854 labeling).

bd.reimbursement: Bundled; no separate code.
bd.notes: Fastest-moving 510(k) filer in product code GXP (8 clearances 2023 to 2026); distribution historically through SurgiCor and Abyrx's own channels, with Acumed and OsteoMed hosting Montage 510(k) PDFs on their sites, which suggests but does not prove a CMF distribution relationship (unverified).

name: DB-CSD, DB-Orthopedics, DB-Composite and DB-EZ Bone Void Filler family
composition: Family of synthetic calcium-based fillers: DB-CSD calcium sulfate; DB-Composite calcium sulfate/calcium phosphate powder mixed with solution; DB-EZ premixed calcium phosphate powder in a PEG-based polymer putty; DB-Orthopedics (details not read).

regulatory.reference: K212353 (DB-EZ, Sept 2021); K210193 (DB-Composite, March 2021); K200752 (DB-Orthopedics, April 2020); K171161 (DB-CSD, Sept 2017)
on_label_indications: DB-CSD: bone void filler for voids and gaps in the 'extremities and pelvis'; 'biodegradable and biocompatible and may be used in an infected site' (K171161)
DB-Composite: extremities, posterolateral spine, pelvis (K210193); DB-Orthopedics: extremities, spine, pelvis (K200752); DB-EZ: extremities and pelvis (K212353)

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: DB-CSD OR Dimensional Bioceramics calcium sulfate osteomyelitis).
applications.caveats: 'May be used in an infected site' is not an antibiotic-delivery claim; same limitation as the STIMULAN record.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: DB-EZ OR DB-Composite OR Dimensional Bioceramics tibial plateau).
applications.caveats: Extremities named for all four labels.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Small private maker of calcium sulfate and calcium phosphate fillers; no company page was read. Predicate chain leans on Skeletal Kinetics' Skaffold NMX.

name: Synthecure Synthetic Calcium Sulfate
composition: Synthetic calcium sulfate bone void filler, biodegradable, provided sterile single-use.

on_label_indications: Implant to fill bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities and pelvis' not intrinsic to stability; resorbs and is replaced with bone; 'may be used at an infected site'

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Synthecure calcium sulfate).
applications.caveats: No antibiotic-delivery claim; an unrelated 2025 paper on antimicrobial calcium sulfate mixing formulas is not about this product (PMID 41079838).

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Synthecure tibial plateau).
applications.caveats: Extremities named.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Another entrant against STIMULAN and OSTEOSET; company details not read.

name: Agili-C implant
ownership_history: Developed by CartiHeal (Kfar Saba, Israel); Smith+Nephew, Inc. is the PMA applicant of record at the 2022-03-29 approval. Acquisition date and price not independently verified in this sweep (S+N announcement not read).
composition: Cell-free, biphasic resorbable scaffold: calcium carbonate (aragonite, from coral) osseous phase with a hyaluronic acid-reinforced chondral phase; press-fit into the prepared defect.

regulatory.reference: P210034 (approved 2022-03-29); supplement S001 approved 2026-06-04 (labeling updated with post-approval study results)
on_label_indications: Agili-C scaffold is indicated for the treatment of an International Cartilage Repair Society (ICRS) grade III or above knee-joint surface lesion(s), with a total treatable area of 1-7 cm2, without severe osteoarthritis (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 0-3) (FDA PMA record)
Contraindication in the IFU: severe osteoarthritis of the index knee (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)

applications.evidence_summary: Pivotal open-label RCT NCT03299959 (n=251, 26 centers, US and Europe/Israel, 2:1 Agili-C vs debridement/microfracture): overall KOOS superior at every visit to 24 months, responder rate (>=30-point KOOS gain) 77.8% vs 33.6% (P<.0001), >=75% MRI defect fill 88.5% vs 30.9%, failures 7.2% vs 21.4%. Registry shows a 60-month primary endpoint; results posted December 2025.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded, open-label; control arm was microfracture or debridement only (not ACI/OCA); 24-month publication is the basis of the PMA; 60-month results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov but not yet located in PubMed; comparator performance (microfracture) is a known weak control.
applications.challenge: A hiring manager will ask whether the label's K-L 0-3 permission (mild-moderate OA) rests on the RCT subgroup or on the single-arm OA cohort; the RCT enrolled K-L 0-3.

applications.evidence_summary: Talar use is off-label. A 2021 J Foot Ankle Surg case series reports Agili-C in complex talar OCL (n not recoverable from the indexed record); a 2023 systematic review pools multilayer biomimetic scaffolds in the talus. No randomized study of Agili-C in the talus located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Off-label; tiny case series; abstract not indexed so n was not confirmed.

evidence.title: Aragonite-Based Scaffold Versus Microfracture and Debridement for the Treatment of Knee Chondral and Osteochondral Lesions: Results of a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.finding: Implant group had superior overall KOOS at all follow-ups to 24 months; responder rate 77.8% vs 33.6%; failure 7.2% vs 21.4%.

evidence.title: Aragonite-Based Scaffold for the Treatment of Joint Surface Lesions in Mild to Moderate Osteoarthritic Knees: Results of a 2-Year Multicenter Prospective Study
evidence.finding: KOOS pain rose from 49.6 to 79.5 and IKDC from 37.8 to 65.8 at 24 months in knees with K-L 2-3 OA; MRI defect fill 78.7%.

evidence.title: Acellular Aragonite-Based Scaffold for the Treatment of Joint Surface Lesions of the Knee: A Minimum 5-Year Follow-Up Study
evidence.finding: Overall KOOS 45 to 86 at minimum 5 years with one failure revised to a metal implant; MOCART 64.

evidence.title: Agili-C vs surgical standard of care for joint surface lesions of the knee (pivotal RCT, 60-month primary endpoint)
evidence.finding: Completed 2024-11-14; results posted 2025-12-05 (not read in detail).

evidence.title: Complex Osteochondral Lesions of the Talus Treated With a Novel Bi-Phasic Aragonite-based Implant
evidence.finding: Case series of Agili-C in talar osteochondral lesions (abstract not indexed; findings not read).

pipeline.expected_milestone: First US commercial case reported in 2023 (company release); PMA labeling updated June 2026 with post-approval study results.

bd.reimbursement: Outpatient/ASC implant; no separate pass-through or HCPCS code located; coverage varies by payer.
bd.notes: Smith+Nephew sells through its Sports Medicine direct force, alongside REGENETEN (existing atlas record), BST-CarGel ex-US and Cartiform heritage via Osiris. A hiring manager will probe single-arm OA data, the 5-year label update, and whether payers treat the device as investigational.

name: Influx SPARC Integrative Bone Matrix
ownership_history: Isto Biologics (Hopkinton, MA; Keensight Capital majority since September 2025 per the existing magellan record). SPARC reportedly grew out of Advanced Biologics' tissue-processing method (OsseoGen) under a collaboration from 2020; Advanced Biologics merged into Isto in October 2023 (trade-press summary, not read in full).
composition: Cellular bone allograft described by its authors as a 'next generation integrative bone matrix' with intrinsic osteogenic, osteoconductive and osteoinductive properties, designed to preserve endogenous growth factors and viable cells (Hofmann 2024, 2026). Catalog copy (not read in full) says processing keeps osteoprogenitor cells while removing red and white blood cells, is DMSO-free and is implantable on thawing.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER); no 510(k) in openFDA for 'sparc' bone products or 'influx' (searched 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: Bone repair or reconstruction (catalog description); IFU not read

challenge: Every published series is Isto-linked: the 2024 foot-and-ankle chart review author consults for Isto, and the 2026 pooled analysis was Isto-funded with data collection and analysis support. The 2026 Cureus paper does not name the product; the attribution to SPARC rests on its pooling of the two earlier SPARC (IBM) studies.

applications.evidence_summary: Hofmann 2024: 20 retrospective foot and ankle fusions with INFLUX SPARC, complete radiographic fusion in all by 24 weeks (mean 8.5 weeks), no major complications or reinterventions.
applications.caveats: Retrospective, n=20, plain radiographs, consultant author; procedure mix (forefoot vs hindfoot) not separable from the abstract.

applications.evidence_summary: Hofmann 2026 pooled 35 high-risk patients (mean 2.6 nonunion risk factors): the 17 foot-and-ankle arthrodeses all fused by 24 weeks (median 6 weeks), 0% nonunion.
applications.caveats: Isto-funded; no control group; high-risk cohort not the same as established nonunion.

applications.evidence_summary: Same pooled analysis: 18 spine patients, 95 of 95 posterolateral and 33 of 33 interbody levels fused by 12 months (median 6 months).
applications.caveats: Isto-funded; small; fusion method not CT-adjudicated in the abstract.

evidence.title: Initial clinical evaluation of a novel integrative bone matrix (IBM) in foot and ankle fusion procedures
evidence.finding: All 20 foot and ankle fusions with INFLUX SPARC fused radiographically by 24 weeks (mean 8.5 weeks); no major complications or reinterventions; PROMs improved.

evidence.title: Clinical Outcomes Following Use of a Next-Generation Cellular Bone Matrix in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Arthrodesis: A Retrospective Analysis
evidence.finding: Pooled two single-center series (18 spine, 17 foot and ankle) in high-risk patients: 100% fusion in both cohorts and 0% nonunion or graft-related adverse events; no control group.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the APC (outpatient/ASC) or bundled in MS-DRG.
bd.notes: Isto sells through independent distributors alongside Magellan BMAC and the Influx allograft family; an Isto-funded spine series (Passias, Front Musculoskelet Disord 2025) is cited in the 2026 paper but was not located in PubMed. No FDA letter about SPARC found in the sources read.

name: OssiGraft Prime viable bone matrix
ownership_history: Ossium Health (Indianapolis/San Francisco), private; raised a $52 million Series C; core business is organ-donor-derived bone marrow for transplant. OssiGraft distribution agreements with Extremity Medical (US) and Enovis.
composition: Vertebral-body-derived viable bone matrix, about 80% cancellous, from organ donors averaging 35 years; first case was an ankle fusion (July 2024); won a 2024 Orthopedics This Week Spine Technology Award

regulatory.reference: OssiGraft IFU (OHC-IFU-0002 Rev 05, hosted by Enovis): OssiGraft is an HCT/P that meets the 21 CFR 1271.10 criteria for regulation solely under section 361; no 510(k)/PMA/De Novo found
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (361 homologous use, presumed)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical data; marketing rests on younger donor age and vertebral-body sourcing (a 2018 lab study found vertebral-body marrow MSCs at least as osteogenic as iliac crest MSCs, PMID 29795650, unrelated to Ossium).
applications.caveats: Company claims only.

applications.evidence_summary: First case was an ankle surgery (2023); no published outcomes; no trauma data.
applications.caveats: Press releases only.

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical publications found.
applications.caveats: New entrant; evidence gap.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Distribution-partner model (Extremity Medical, Enovis); a new entrant competing on donor sourcing rather than clinical data.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None public.

name: Viable Matrix Plus Bone Allograft
company: Medline (Medline Unite foot and ankle); processed by VIVEX Biologics
ownership_history: Sold by Medline Industries under the Unite Foot and Ankle line; the US IFU (80-671 Rev. 01, posted 2025) states the donor was cleared by the Medical Director of VIVEX Biologics, Inc.
composition: Cryopreserved viable bone allograft of cancellous chips and demineralized bone fibers in a syringe, preserved with a 100% polyampholyte-based cryoprotectant that is not rinsed before use (IFU). Medline claims an average of 1.5 million viable cells per cc and over 92% post-thaw viability.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; processor VIVEX registered with CBER); no 510(k) in openFDA for 'viable matrix' (searched 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: 'Intended for use as a bone void filler' (IFU 80-671 Rev. 01)

challenge: IFU donor-testing list (CMV, HIV-1/2, HBV, HCV, HTLV-I/II, syphilis; optional EBV, Toxoplasma, T. cruzi, WNV, Zika) includes no Mycobacterium tuberculosis test.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of Viable Matrix Plus located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Recently added to a distributor catalog (2025 documents); launch year unconfirmed.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in ankle fusion located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: None beyond class caveats.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged into the procedure APC in outpatient/ASC cases.
bd.notes: Medline's entry shows cellular allograft being sold as a catalog line item by a med-surg distributor with GPO reach, a price-pressure signal for the category. No FDA letter found in the sources read.

name: Virtuos Lyograft (shelf-stable cellular bone allograft)
ownership_history: Limited market release and first implant announced July 26, 2022 (Baylor Scott and White, Fort Worth). Co-branded with MTF Biologics, which processes the tissue, holds inventory and invoices hospitals; Orthofix holds exclusive worldwide marketing rights and books marketing fees (Orthofix FY2025 10-K). Orthofix merged with SeaSpine in January 2023.
composition: Moldable cortical fibers plus cancellous granules containing endogenous cells, lyophilized with a proprietary lyopreservation solution so it can be stored at room temperature and rehydrated in about two minutes. Orthofix claims a minimum of 750,000 cells per cc, about 250,000 of them MSCs, osteoprogenitors and other bone-forming cells, and lot-release osteoinductivity testing.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; MTF Biologics establishment registered with CBER); no 510(k) in openFDA for 'virtuos' (the 'Lyograft' 510(k) K192452 is an unrelated B. Braun device)
on_label_indications: Not stated on the product page; refer to IFU (not read). Positioned for 'spine and orthopedic procedures'.

challenge: 'Cellular' and 'freeze-dried' sit uneasily together: Orthofix says the process retains 'intact cells', not viable cells, and the only performance data are 'identical fusion rates to Trinity Elite' in a 2-level athymic rat PLF model on file.

applications.evidence_summary: No published clinical study of Virtuos Lyograft located (PubMed search 'Lyograft' 2026-10-23 returned nothing); company cites unpublished rat PLF data.
applications.caveats: Data on file only.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study located (PubMed search 'Lyograft' 2026-10-23). The sponsor's autograft-controlled TLIF study (NCT05614284) stopped at 6 patients; a 150-patient historically controlled study (NCT06686017) runs to 2029.
applications.caveats: Historical control, sponsor-run; no randomized comparison planned.

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for orthopedic procedures; no foot-and-ankle study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Room-temperature storage suits ASCs without -65 C freezers.

evidence.title: A Prospective, Post-Market, Multicenter Comparative Analysis of the Efficacy of Virtuos and Autograft Bone Graft in Lumbar Fusion Surgery
evidence.finding: Terminated May 2024 after 6 enrolled ('protocol redesign'); no results posted.

evidence.title: A Prospective Post-Market Historically Controlled Open-Label Study to Assess the Efficacy of Virtuos in Lumbar Fusion
evidence.finding: Enrolling by invitation since June 2025; 1-2 level lumbar DDD; primary completion estimated January 2029. n is planned enrollment.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Orthofix post-market historically controlled lumbar fusion study NCT06686017 (150 planned, enrolling by invitation, primary completion 2029-01); an earlier Virtuos vs autograft TLIF comparison (NCT05614284) was terminated after 6 patients for 'protocol redesign'.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs; packaged in OPPS outpatient.
bd.notes: Orthofix books marketing-service fees from MTF rather than product revenue (FY2025 10-K). Shelf stability removes dry-ice logistics, the practical barrier to cellular grafts in ASCs. No FDA letter about Lyograft found in the sources read.

name: Rotium Bioresorbable Wick
company: Atreon Orthopedics (Columbus, OH; 510(k) applicant Nanofiber Solutions, LLC)
ownership_history: Nanofiber Solutions spun out Atreon Orthopedics to commercialize Rotium; clearances K183236 (2019-03-11), K201414 (2020), K231641 (2023), K250021 (2025-02-27, new product code OWW).
composition: Electrospun bioresorbable synthetic nanofiber scaffold placed as an interpositional wick between the tendon and the greater tuberosity footprint during repair.

regulatory.reference: K250021 (Rotium; Nanofiber Solutions, LLC; decision 2025-02-27; 21 CFR 878.3300 surgical mesh, product code OWW, Class II); earlier Rotium Bioresorbable Wick K183236 (2019-03-11), K201414 (2020-06-25), K231641 (2023-07-05; product code MAI)
on_label_indications: Management and protection of tendon injuries without substantial loss of tendon tissue in patients requiring surgical intervention (K250021 Indications for Use; this is not a rotator-cuff-reinforcement or suture-augmentation indication)

applications.evidence_summary: Technique papers only (Beleckas 2023, PMID:36814979; Mousad 2025, PMID:40656718); a planned ultrasound-healing RCT was withdrawn with zero enrollment (NCT04361266).
applications.caveats: No clinical outcome data.

evidence.title: Bioaugmentation of rotator cuff repair with an interpositional nanofiber scaffold
evidence.finding: Surgical technique description; no outcomes.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No registered outcome trial active; next milestone is any comparative clinical series

bd.reimbursement: Packaged into the procedure payment.
bd.notes: Start-up in a category dominated by Smith+Nephew and Arthrex; included as the 'emerging' example in the rotator cuff adjacent note.

challenge: K250021 is a tendon-injury management/protection indication; any rotator-cuff augmentation claim is outside the cleared wording.

name: PearlMatrix P-15 Peptide Enhanced Bone Graft (formerly P-15L / i-FACTOR+ Matrix)
ownership_history: Cerapedics; investigational name P-15L / i-FACTOR+ Matrix during the ASPIRE IDE (2018-2025).
composition: P-15 peptide on anorganic bone mineral in a collagen-based matrix (the lumbar/interbody formulation of the ABM/P-15 technology); Class III drug-device combination product

regulatory.reference: P240001 (PearlMatrix P-15 Peptide Enhanced Bone Graft; FDA decision 2025-06-18; Cerapedics press releases are dated June 23, 2025). S001 approved 2025-12-11 (180-day track) adds ALIF, TLIF, PLIF, OLIF/ATP and LLIF approaches and titanium alloy and PEEK/titanium cages; S002 (2026-04-07) and S003 (2026-09-16) are manufacturing/lab-site notices. Predecessor i-FACTOR is P140019 (2015-11-03).
on_label_indications: PearlMatrix is indicated for intervertebral body fusion in skeletally mature patients: one level, L2-S1, DDD with up to Grade I spondylolisthesis, with a PEEK TLIF fusion device and supplemental internal fixation, after at least six months of nonoperative treatment (P240001, 2025-06-18)
S001 (approved 2025-12-11): additional open or minimally invasive approaches (ALIF, TLIF, PLIF, OLIF/ATP, LLIF) and use with titanium alloy and PEEK/titanium cages

applications.evidence_summary: ASPIRE pivotal RCT (NCT03438747; Harrop 2025, n=290 at 33 US sites, single-blind, ~60% high-risk): composite clinical success 55.5% vs 37.5% local autograft (noninferior and superior, p=0.002); CT fusion 84.3% vs 58.5% at 24 months; time to fusion HR 1.87. Device-related SAEs similar; the January 2026 company release notes a higher rate of secondary surgical interventions with PearlMatrix than autograft.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; control arm fusion (58.5%) is far below typical TLIF literature because of strict CT criteria and high-risk enrollment, which flatters the treatment delta.

applications.evidence_summary: ALIF, PLIF, OLIF and LLIF indications were added by supplement in January 2026 on the strength of the TLIF pivotal plus cage/approach equivalence; no approach-specific RCT.
applications.caveats: Label expansion without new pivotal data for each approach.

applications.evidence_summary: On-label single-level OLIF/LLIF since January 2026 via supplement; evidence extrapolated from ASPIRE TLIF.
applications.caveats: Same as ALIF.

evidence.title: P-15 peptide enhanced bone graft in TLIF: a randomized, controlled IDE study demonstrating improved composite clinical success
evidence.finding: CCS 55.5% vs 37.5%; fusion 84.3% vs 58.5% at 24 months; similar device-related SAEs.

evidence.title: P-15 peptide enhanced bone graft improves time to fusion in TLIF: a randomized, controlled IDE study
evidence.finding: Kaplan-Meier fusion 57.6% vs 26.9% at 6 months and 81.1% vs 54.9% at 24 months; HR 1.87 for time to fusion.

evidence.title: An assessment of P-15L bone graft in TLIF with instrumentation (ASPIRE)
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; 72-month follow-up continues to 2028.

evidence.title: ASPIRE pivotal PMA IDE study (company summary in FDA approval release)
evidence.finding: Primary 24-month composite clinical success met with superiority vs autograft; faster fusion at 6 months.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Approved 2025-06-18 (P240001); first US patient July 2025; S001 approach/cage expansion approved 2025-12-11 (company announced January 2026).

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in the level-based spinal fusion MS-DRG family in force since FY2025 (402, 426-430, 447-451, 456-458; 523-525 added FY2027; 471-473 cervical) inpatient; no NTAP or pass-through found in sources reviewed; physician +20930 bundled. Cerapedics publishes a PearlMatrix coding guide (PDF, not text-extractable in this sweep).
bd.notes: Breakthrough Device designation April 2021; approval came 180 days-class on a panel-track PMA. The TLIF label puts PearlMatrix head-to-head with Infuse for the first on-label TLIF biologic, eight months before Medtronic's TLIF approval.

challenge: PMA P240001 approved 2025-06-18 (openFDA, pass 2); supplement S001 label expansion approved 2025-12-11 and announced 2026-01-13. Pass 3 could not reach the FDA PMA search page (bot challenge).

name: Arthrex SpeedFLEX Implant (pre-sutured decellularized human dermis)
ownership_history: Arthrex, Inc. (Naples, FL); allograft donor processing referenced to LifeNet Health in the 510(k).
composition: Decellularized human allograft dermis pre-sutured with FiberWire passing suture and TigerLink SutureTape, four sizes, sterile single-use.

regulatory.reference: K251690 (2025-09-30), product codes OWY/GAT; primary predicate Medeor Matrix K103787 (porcine dermis), reference device MTF Fascia K120479 (allograft fascia, 510(k) 2012)
on_label_indications: Intended for general surgical procedures for reinforcement of soft tissue where weakness exists, and for reinforcement of soft tissues repaired by suture or suture anchors during tendon repair surgery including (but not limited to) rotator cuff, patellar, Achilles, biceps, quadriceps tendon (K251690)

challenge: First clear sign that a human dermal allograft patch took the 510(k) route (with a collagen xenograft predicate) rather than 361 HCT/P; it implies FDA may regard pre-sutured allograft dermis as a mesh device.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of SpeedFLEX located (cleared September 2025). Arthrex's ArthroFlex dermal matrix (see record) has one small nonrandomized comparative study.
applications.caveats: Newly cleared; no clinical data.

applications.evidence_summary: Label covers patellar, Achilles, biceps and quadriceps tendons; no clinical data.
applications.caveats: Newly cleared.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the procedure.
bd.notes: Positions Arthrex's catalog: ArthroFlex (361 allograft), SpeedFLEX (510(k) allograft), DX Matrix (xenograft).

name: BioBrace implant (BioBrace, BioBrace Reinforced, BioBrace RC Delivery System, Extra-Articular Ligament Augmentation Kit)
ownership_history: Developed by Biorez, Inc. (New Haven, CT). CONMED acquired Biorez on 2022-08-09 for $85.5M upfront in cash plus earn-outs up to $165.0M on revenue targets ($84.5M paid as of 2024-12-31 per CONMED FY2024 10-K).
composition: Bioresorbable biocomposite scaffold: highly porous (about 80%) sponge of insoluble bovine tendon type I collagen reinforced with poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA) multifilament yarn; a 'Reinforced' variant adds more PLLA.

regulatory.reference: K203267 (2021-04-30); K241906 BioBrace Reinforced (2024-07-29); K242187 BioBrace (2024-11-27); K250395 BioBrace RC Delivery System (2025-04-07); K252946 Extra-Articular Ligament Augmentation Kit (2025-10-15). Class II surgical mesh, 21 CFR 878.3300
on_label_indications: Reinforcement of soft tissue where weakness exists (general surgical procedures)
Reinforcement of soft tissues repaired by suture or suture anchors during tendon repair surgery including rotator cuff, patellar, Achilles, biceps or quadriceps tendons (K203267 summary)
K242187 adds ligament repair (e.g., medial collateral and lateral collateral ligament) to the same reinforcement language

challenge: No peer-reviewed clinical outcome study of BioBrace was found; PubMed returns only surgical-technique papers. The 510(k) cleared it as reinforcement mesh, not as a healing-promoting or 'bioinductive' device; efficacy claims rest on CONMED's pivotal REinForce RCT (not yet complete). The predicate was STR Graft (K121216).

applications.evidence_summary: No published clinical study of BioBrace in rotator cuff repair located (PubMed search 2026-10-23); CONMED's pivotal REinForce RCT (NCT05997381, n=268, single-blind, arthroscopic repair of full-thickness tears with BioBrace vs standard repair) has primary completion estimated December 2026. Technique papers only.
applications.caveats: Pivotal RCT incomplete; sponsor-run; class evidence for collagen patches (REGENETEN) exists but is not transferable to a different scaffold.

applications.evidence_summary: Cleared for tendon and extra-articular ligament repair reinforcement (patellar, Achilles, biceps, quadriceps, MCL/LCL). No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23); CONMED is running a 500-patient real-world ACL-augmentation study (NCT06948591) and investigator trials in Brostrom repair (NCT07401095, NCT07708584) and subscapularis repair (NCT05487677).
applications.caveats: ACL reconstruction augmentation is not among the ligaments named in the clearance text read; the K252946 kit targets extra-articular ligaments.
applications.challenge: A hiring manager will probe whether ACL use is promoted on-label.

evidence.title: REinForce: BioBrace implant for arthroscopic repair of full-thickness rotator cuff tears (pivotal RCT)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion estimated 2026-12; no results.

evidence.title: Real-world evaluation of BioBrace augmentation in ACL reconstruction
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion estimated 2030-06.

evidence.title: Subscapularis repair augmentation for total shoulder arthroplasty (Stanford)
evidence.finding: Investigator-led; recruiting.

evidence.title: Maximal repair versus bridging reconstruction with BioBrace (Nova Scotia Health Authority)
evidence.finding: Investigator-led massive rotator cuff tear trial; recruiting.

pipeline.expected_milestone: REinForce primary completion est. 2026-12 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the arthroscopic procedure (OPPS/ASC); no separate payment found.
bd.notes: BioBrace is CONMED's largest recent growth bet (earn-out up to $165M); five 510(k)s in four years expand sizes, reinforced variant, delivery system and ligament kit. Competes with REGENETEN (S+N), Tapestry (Zimmer Biomet), Integrity (Anika) and synthetic meshes (Xiros, Artelon).

name: Integrity Implant (hyaluronic acid-based patch system)
ownership_history: Anika Therapeutics (510(k) applicant). Anika's separate Parcus Medical business was divested to Medacta in 2025 (Anika milestones page, search summary); no link to this patch was found. Correction to the sweep brief: the patch is hyaluronic acid-based (HYAFF), not collagen.
composition: Partially resorbable knitted mesh of resorbable HYAFF (esterified hyaluronic acid) multifilament fibers and non-resorbable polyethylene terephthalate (PET) fibers, fixed with PEEK bone staples, PLGA tendon tacks or suture.

regulatory.reference: K223538 (2023-08-17); K250997 (2025-06-17). Predicate: Collagen Tendon Sheet K112423; product code OWX; Class II surgical mesh, 21 CFR 878.3300
on_label_indications: The Integrity Implant is indicated for the management and protection of tendon injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon tissue (K223538 summary)

applications.evidence_summary: No published clinical outcome study of Integrity Implant located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Anika's post-market confirmatory study (NCT06741527, n=150, single-arm, rotator cuff augmentation) and a 20-patient MRI study (NCT06353893, Foundation for Orthopaedic Research and Education, completed Feb 2026) are the only registered data.
applications.caveats: Post-market, single-arm; the label is protection of tendon injuries, not a retear-reduction claim.

applications.evidence_summary: Label language is tendon-agnostic ('tendon injuries'); no non-rotator-cuff study located.
applications.caveats: No data.

evidence.title: Post-market confirmatory interventional study of the Integrity Implant System for rotator cuff tear augmentation
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion estimated 2027-06.

evidence.title: Postoperative MRI evaluation of the Integrity bio-inductive implant augmentation of rotator cuff tears
evidence.finding: Completed 2026-02; results not located.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Post-market study primary completion est. 2027-06.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the procedure (OPPS/ASC).
bd.notes: Anika also pursues Hyalofast PMA; Integrity is its soft-tissue growth product; the 'Retractable Implant Inserter' K261869 (2026-09-17) extends the system.

name: Kerecis Tendon Protect (fish skin)
ownership_history: Kerecis Limited (Iceland). Coloplast acquired Kerecis in 2023 (general knowledge, not verified in this sweep).
composition: Solid sheets of North Atlantic cod fish skin (at least 0.4 mm thick) wrapped around the repaired tendon as a gliding barrier and scaffold for host tissue deposition.

regulatory.reference: K243843 (2025-06-04), product code OWY
on_label_indications: Kerecis Tendon Protect is indicated for the management and protection of tendon injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon tissue (K243843)

applications.evidence_summary: No published tendon-specific study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Kerecis's fish-skin graft has an RCT in diabetic foot ulcers (NEJM Evid 2024) that does not apply to tendon use.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is from wounds; the 510(k) rests on non-clinical testing.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the procedure.
bd.notes: New entrant (2025) in the tendon protector sheet segment.

name: RejuvaKnee Collagen Meniscus Implant
ownership_history: Collagen Matrix, Inc. is the 510(k) submitter; trade press attributes the announcement to Regenity Biosciences (rebranded company); Regenity said it would seek a strategic US commercialization partner (search summary).
composition: Semilunar implant of bovine type I collagen (nominally 99%) derived from meniscus, resorbable scaffold replaced by the patient's own tissue.

regulatory.reference: K242302 (2024-10-02), product code OLC (same as CMI)
on_label_indications: Intended for use in surgical procedures for the reinforcement and repair of soft tissue injuries of the medial meniscus; the patient must have an intact meniscal rim and anterior and posterior horns for attachment of the mesh (K242302)

applications.evidence_summary: No published human study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23); the company cites a 12-month animal study and cadaver work (press, unverified). Clearance relied on the CMI predicate.
applications.caveats: No clinical data; commercial partner unannounced.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed in the US yet (as of coverage).
bd.notes: Second US collagen meniscus implant after Stryker's CMI.

name: Tapestry Biointegrative Implant (Tapestry, Tapestry RC)
ownership_history: Developed by Embody, Inc. Zimmer Biomet announced the acquisition on 2023-01-05 ($155M upfront plus up to $120M over three years on regulatory/commercial milestones) and closed it in February 2023 (trade press).
composition: Resorbable implant composed of collagen and poly(D,L-lactide), a non-constricting protective layer between tendon and surrounding tissue; supplied standalone, in an insertion sleeve, or on an introducer for arthroscopic delivery (K252647).

on_label_indications: Tapestry Biointegrative Implant is indicated for the management and protection of tendon injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon tissue (K252647)

challenge: The indication is 'management and protection of tendon injuries' - the same language as the Rotation Medical Collagen Tendon Sheet indication (K112423, the predicate of Integrity); it does not claim to improve healing or reduce retear. Zimmer's own PMCF rotator cuff study (NCT06287853) is listed as suspended.

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed clinical outcome study of Tapestry in rotator cuff repair located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Zimmer post-market studies: subscapularis repair after shoulder arthroplasty (NCT05735119, n=100, active), Tapestry RC PMCF (NCT06287853, n=170, suspended), Ohio State gluteus medius repair (NCT05492396, n=30).
applications.caveats: Post-market follow-up only; no comparator; sponsor-run.

applications.evidence_summary: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy repair augmentation case series (NCT05998785) was terminated at n=8 in 2024; a 2025 Clin Podiatr Med Surg article describes technique. No published comparative data located.
applications.caveats: Terminated tiny study; technique/expert opinion only.

evidence.title: Post-market clinical follow-up: subscapularis repair augmented with Tapestry after shoulder arthroplasty
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; primary completion estimated 2026-11.

evidence.title: Tapestry rotator cuff repair PMCF
evidence.finding: Listed as suspended; start estimated 2026-12.

evidence.title: Insertional Achilles tendinopathy repair augmented with Tapestry (Embody)
evidence.finding: Terminated with 8 enrolled (2024-08).

evidence.title: Evaluation of healing following open gluteus medius repair with biointegrative implant (Ohio State)
evidence.finding: Investigator-led; active, not recruiting.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Subscapularis PMCF primary completion est. 2026-11.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the procedure (OPPS/ASC); no separate payment.
bd.notes: Zimmer Biomet paid $155M upfront for Embody (2023) to enter biologic tendon augmentation, with milestone-linked contingent payments.

name: Xiros Poly-Tape / Infinity-Lock, Jewel and Pitch-Patch soft tissue reinforcement devices
ownership_history: Xiros Ltd (UK); Xiros plc and Neoligaments Ltd both appear as earlier 510(k) applicants in openFDA. The sweep brief called this 'Xiros LARS'; Xiros and LARS are different companies (see lars-ligament).
composition: Permanent woven or warp-knitted polyethylene terephthalate (PET/polyester) tape, tube (Jewel) or patch (Pitch-Patch).

regulatory.reference: K222978 Poly-Tape/Infinity-Lock Soft Tissue Reinforcement Device (2022-12-27); K242237 Jewel (2025-07-15); K211563 Pitch-Patch (2021-08-13); K230671 Pitch-Patch (2023-05-31). Product codes QUW/FTL; Class II surgical mesh, 21 CFR 878.3300
on_label_indications: Poly-Tape/Infinity-Lock: reinforcement of soft tissues repaired by suture or other fixation during tendon and ligament repair including rotator cuff, patellar, Achilles, biceps, quadriceps, MCL, LCL, spring, deltoid, ulnar collateral ligaments or other tendons/extra-articular ligaments; not intended to replace normal body structure or provide full mechanical strength (K222978)
Pitch-Patch: permanent implantable device for reinforcement of rotator cuff tears (K211563)
Jewel: tubular mesh to support soft tissue repaired during ligament repair surgery, or to hold an allograft or autograft (K242237)

applications.evidence_summary: No published clinical study of Poly-Tape, Jewel or Pitch-Patch located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Permanent PET tape/patch is a different risk profile from resorbable scaffolds.
applications.caveats: Permanent synthetic; clearance rests on mechanical equivalence.

applications.evidence_summary: Pitch-Patch (K211563, K230671) is cleared for reinforcement of rotator cuff tears; no published clinical study located.
applications.caveats: No data.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged in the procedure.
bd.notes: Xiros's US presence is through 510(k) clearances; US distribution partner(s) not verified.

name: Agilon Moldable / Agilon Strip and Morpheus (osteoSPAN granule bone grafts)
composition: osteoSPAN granules (about 65% porous biphasic calcium salts, primarily calcium carbonate with a thin calcium phosphate layer; origin not stated in the text read, a coral-type structure is implied by the description) suspended in an organic binder; Agilon Strip adds collagen.

regulatory.reference: K240621 (Morpheus Moldable / Agilon Moldable, April 2024, summary not retrievable); K193487 (Agilon Strip, March 2020); K193168 (Agilon Moldable, Feb 2020); K190371 (Morpheus-C, 2019)
on_label_indications: Agilon Moldable and Strip (K193168, K193487): voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities, pelvis, and posterolateral spine' not intrinsic to stability; alone in the extremities and pelvis, but must be mixed with autograft in the posterolateral spine

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Agilon OR osteoSPAN OR Biogennix posterolateral fusion). A 2024 materials paper characterized an osteoSPAN-type nanocrystalline hydroxycarbonapatite graft (PMID 38747324).
applications.caveats: Materials characterization only.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Agilon OR osteoSPAN tibial plateau).
applications.caveats: Alone-use is allowed in the extremities and pelvis.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Biogennix (Irvine, CA) also has Morpheus.

name: BonVie+ and EP Granules BVF
composition: Resorbable bone void filler of hydroxyapatite, calcium carbonate and calcium chloride particles with degradable polymers (PCL, PEG, PLGA); BonVie+ is a kit that molds granules in a silicone mat, EP Granules BVF is the preformed-granule predicate.

regulatory.reference: K250346 (BonVie+, Feb 2025); K180853 (EP Granules BVF, Aug 2018)
on_label_indications: Implant to fill bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities and pelvis' that are not intrinsic to stability; surgically created or traumatic; resorbs and is replaced with bone (K250346, K180853)

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: BonVie OR Elute EP Granules).
applications.caveats: Clearance rests on bench data and predicate equivalence.

applications.evidence_summary: The cleared BonVie+ carries no antibiotic. Elute's antibiotic-loaded version, EP Granules + tobramycin, is under an FDA IDE (see the separate record); no published human data on either.
applications.caveats: BonVie+ has no infection claim.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Platform company: the cleared granules are the base for the antibiotic combination pivotal trial.

name: CaP Spheres Pellet Pack
ownership_history: Zimmer Biomet's spine business was spun into ZimVie (2022) and sold to H.I.G. Capital as Highridge Medical (April 2024); whether this clearance moved with it, or is still sold, is unverified. Company field shortened; original: Zimmer Biomet Spine, Inc. (510(k) holder; current owner unverified)
composition: Calcium phosphate spheres supplied as a pre-packed pellet pack for graft-extender use (composition detail beyond 'calcium phosphate' not read).

on_label_indications: Bone void filler for bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure, surgically created or from traumatic injury
Used with autograft as a bone graft extender gently packed into voids or gaps in the posterolateral spine; predicates AttraX Putty (K151584) and Magnifuse (K123691)

challenge: Marketing status and owner unverified after the ZimVie and Highridge transactions; do not present as an active Zimmer Biomet product without checking.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: CaP Spheres Pellet Pack; Zimmer Biomet calcium phosphate spheres posterolateral fusion).
applications.caveats: Extender-only label (must be used with autograft).

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Thin record: only the 510(k) was found; no company product page located.

name: Cove Putty / Cove Strip (sold as OsteoCove in the Orthofix line)
ownership_history: SeaSpine Orthopedics Corporation held the clearances; Orthofix and SeaSpine merged in January 2023 (Orthofix press materials).
composition: Collagen-ceramic composite: biphasic ceramic granules (about 70% beta-TCP / 30% hydroxyapatite per Orthofix brochures) with Type I bovine collagen, hydrated with saline at point of use; granule surface topography is the claimed osteoinductive feature.

regulatory.reference: K231030 (Cove Putty, Sept 2023); K242273 (Cove Putty / OsteoCove Putty, Sept 2024); K230486 and K232668 (Cove Strip / OsteoCove Strip, 2023)
on_label_indications: Cove Putty: fill voids and gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; 'indicated for use with autograft as a bone graft extender in the posterolateral spine and pelvis'; for intervertebral body fusion it must be used as an extender with a cage cleared for use with a bone void filler (K242273)
Cove Strip / OsteoCove Strip (K232668): posterolateral spine and pelvis only, must be used with autograft as an extender
Extremities are not named in these indications

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Cove OR OsteoCove OR SeaSpine synthetic graft posterolateral fusion).
applications.caveats: Extender-only label (must be used with autograft). Orthofix launched OsteoCove after 510(k) clearance in October 2023; its brochures cite bench and animal data, not human outcomes.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: OsteoCove OR Cove Putty interbody).
applications.caveats: Putty (K242273) is on-label in interbody fusion only as an autograft extender with a cage cleared for bone void filler use; the Strip is not.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: OsteoCove OR Cove pelvis).
applications.caveats: Pelvis is named in the label.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Orthofix sells it through its spine biologics reps next to Trinity ELITE and Accell Evo3. The Cove and OsteoCove names appear to be the same product under two names (same brochure text); the 510(k) lists both names together.

name: JAZBI Resorbable Bone Void Filler
ownership_history: SDIP Innovations (Australia); no acquirer found.
composition: Porous biphasic calcium phosphate (beta-TCP plus hydroxyapatite) granules in a polymeric matrix (poly(propylene carbonate) and GPTMS); MR Safe labeling claimed.

on_label_indications: Bone void filler for bony voids or defects not intrinsic to stability, from benign bone cysts and tumors, surgical creation or trauma; gently packed or placed into voids of the 'extremities and pelvis'; resorbs and is replaced with bone

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: JAZBI SDIP resorbable bone void filler).
applications.caveats: Cleared in 2026; no clinical data yet.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: JAZBI tibial plateau).
applications.caveats: Extremities named.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Cleared May 2026; no trial registered.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Very new; no company page read.

name: OssDsign Catalyst Bone Void Filler (formerly Osteo3 ZP Putty)
ownership_history: Sirakoss Ltd (Aberdeen) developed Osteo3 ZP Putty; OssDsign AB markets it as Catalyst (acquisition details not sourced; the same 510(k) text describes both).
composition: Nanosynthetic silicon-substituted calcium phosphate granules (5.8 wt%) suspended in a resorbable polymer gel (30 wt% granules / 70 wt% gel); putty.

regulatory.reference: K232315 (Sept 2023); K193075 (Osteo3 ZP Putty, Sirakoss Ltd, June 2020)
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for bone voids or defects of the skeletal system 'posterolateral spine, intervertebral disc space, extremities, and pelvis' not intrinsic to stability; must be used with morselized autograft 1:1 by volume in the posterolateral spine; in intervertebral body fusion with autograft 1:1 and a cage cleared for a bone void filler (K232315)

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: OssDsign Catalyst OR Osteo3 ZP Putty posterolateral). Registered: first-in-human TLIF + instrumented PLF study (NCT05114135, n=17, completed April 2023, no results posted) and an OssDsign spine registry (NCT05329129, n=450 planned, recruiting to 2030).
applications.caveats: Autograft 1:1 extender label; evidence is registry-only.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: OssDsign Catalyst OR Osteo3 interbody).
applications.caveats: On-label with a cleared cage and 1:1 autograft.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: OssDsign Catalyst extremities).
applications.caveats: Extremities named; a rabbit femoral defect study compared two silicate-containing CaP grafts (PMID 42231723).

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: OssDsign is better known for cranial implants (Cranioplug, Cranial PSI per openFDA); Catalyst is its spine entry.

name: OsteoFlo NanoPutty, HydroPutty and HydroFiber
ownership_history: SurGenTec, LLC (Boca Raton, FL); privately held, no acquirer found.
composition: Fully synthetic hydrophilic grafts: NanoPutty is quadphasic particles (hydroxyapatite, alpha-TCP, beta-TCP, bioactive glass) in a bioresorbable polymer binder; HydroPutty is carbonated apatite granules and bioglass in a synthetic polymer binder; HydroFiber is the fibrous form. Delivered with SurGenTec's GraftGun.

regulatory.reference: K251720 (OsteoFlo HydroFiber, July 2025, summary not retrievable); K243949 (HydroFiber, May 2025); K242797 (HydroFiber, Dec 2024); K231716 (HydroPutty, Oct 2023); K200064 (NanoPutty, Aug 2020)
on_label_indications: HydroFiber (K243949): bone void filler for osseous defects not intrinsic to stability, packed into the 'extremities, pelvis, intervertebral disc space, and posterolateral spine'; standalone or with autograft as an extender; in intervertebral body fusion must be used with a cage cleared for a bone void filler
NanoPutty (K200064) and HydroPutty (K231716): extremities and pelvis only; the earlier HydroFiber clearance (K242797) lacked the extremities

applications.evidence_summary: Retrospective chart review of 129 patients (211 lateral mass and 199 interbody fusions) using OsteoFlo mixed with a cellular allograft (Vimax): Bridwell grade I fusion 77.8% of lateral-mass and 92.0% of interbody levels at 1 year (PMID 40242813).
applications.caveats: No control group; the product used (2021 to 2022) was the NanoPutty/HydroPutty generation whose labels named extremities and pelvis only, so the spine use then was off-label; mixed with a cellular allograft, so the effect of the synthetic alone is not isolated.

applications.evidence_summary: Same series: 92.0% Bridwell I fusion at 1 year across 199 interbody levels (PMID 40242813). A 2026 case report used stand-alone HydroFiber-type graft in a postoperative osteomyelitis/discitis salvage (PMID 42724889); a rabbit PLF study showed noninferiority to iliac autograft (PMID 42003666).
applications.caveats: Interbody label requires a cage cleared for bone void filler use; case report and animal study are not clinical evidence of equivalence.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: OsteoFlo tibial plateau OR extremity).
applications.caveats: Extremities now named for HydroFiber (May 2025).

evidence.title: Rate of fusion using novel synthetic bone graft mixed with cellular allograft product in lumbar fusions
evidence.finding: Bridwell grade I fusion at 1 year was 77.8% (lateral mass) and 92.0% (interbody) with OsteoFlo plus a cellular allograft.

evidence.title: A Novel Nano-Synthetic Hydrophilic Bone Graft (OsteoFlo HydroFiber) Is a Non-inferior Alternative to Iliac Crest Autograft in a Rabbit Posterolateral Fusion Model
