evidence.finding: In rabbits, HydroFiber was noninferior to iliac crest autograft for posterolateral fusion.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Named in the existing new-clearances tracker; the 2023 to 2025 clearances expanded the label from extremities/pelvis to spine, which is the commercial story.

name: ReBOSSIS (cotton-like beta-TCP/vaterite/PLGA graft)
composition: Electrospun composite in a glass-wool-like (cotton-ball) form: beta-tricalcium phosphate, siloxane-containing vaterite (calcium carbonate) and a resorbable PLGA scaffold.

on_label_indications: ReBOSSIS (K240453): bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to stability, packed into 'extremities, pelvis, posterolateral spine, and intervertebral disc space'; extremities and pelvis alone or hydrated with blood; in the posterolateral spine and disc space hydrated with bone marrow aspirate and mixed with autograft; with a cleared cage in interbody fusion

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: ReBOSSIS posterolateral fusion). A rabbit PLF study tested the electrospun PLGA/beta-TCP material (PMID 32577102).
applications.caveats: Preclinical only; US commercial partner not identified.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: ReBOSSIS interbody).
applications.caveats: Cleared 2024 with an interbody cage; no human data located.

evidence.title: Electrospun PLGA and β-TCP (Rebossis-85) in a Lapine Posterolateral Fusion Model
evidence.finding: Animal posterolateral fusion model of the electrospun PLGA/beta-TCP material.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Japan-made; US route to market not identified.

name: Recent US bone void filler clearances relevant to trauma (2024-2026 tracker)
company: Various (Elute, RTI Surgical, Artoss, SDIP Innovations, Stryker, SurGenTec, Anika, Acuitive)
ownership_history: Tracker record, not a single product.
composition: Mixed: synthetic resorbable calcium salts, nanocrystalline HA, citrate-based polymer/ceramic (CITREPORE), hyaluronic-acid-based injectable, moldable allograft

regulatory.reference: K241555 RTI Surgical Moldable Bone Void Filler (2025-02-21, RTI Surgical, Inc.); K250346 Elute BonVie+ (2025-02-26, Elute, Inc.); K250521 NanoBone SBX Putty / NanoBone QD (2025-04-07, applicant Biocomposites, Ltd., which owns Artoss/NanoBone); K252797 JAZBI Resorbable Bone Void Filler (2026-05-26, SDIP Innovations Pty Ltd); K261008 Vitoss BiModal foam strip family (2026-04-24, Stryker Spine); K240450 Citrepore (2024-11-06, Acuitive Technologies); SurGenTec OsteoFlo HydroFiber K242797 (2024-12-23), K243949 (2025-05-28), K251720 (2025-07-02); Anika Tactoset Injectable Bone Substitute K212083 (2021-08-31), K231968 (2023-12-20); Fibergraft BG Putty GPS K253147 (2025-10-22, Prosidyan); openFDA: K241555 (RTI Moldable BVF, 2025-02-21); K250346 (Elute BonVie+, 2025-02-26); K250521 (Biocomposites NanoBone SBX, 2025-04-07); K252797 (SDIP JAZBI, 2026-05-26); K261008 (Stryker Vitoss family, 2026-04-24)
on_label_indications: All are standard MQV 'bone void filler for voids not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure' clearances; none is antibiotic-eluting; the only new antibiotic-eluting authorization in the window is CERAMENT G's open-fracture 510(k) (K234008, 2024-03-13)

applications.evidence_summary: None of these clearances carried clinical data; they expand the commodity void-filler field. Artoss is running a 200-patient US trauma registry of NanoBone (NCT06256458) and Advanced Medical Solutions a 200-patient RCT of its FDBS filler vs MBCP putty in orthopaedic defects (NCT06326827, start October 2026).
applications.caveats: Bench-only clearances; the list was built from product-code listings and may be incomplete.

evidence.title: Multicenter prospective registry of NanoBone bone graft substitute in acute trauma patients (Artoss)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion December 2026.

evidence.title: Randomised investigation of FDBS (GraftR3) vs MBCP Putty in filling orthopaedic bone defects (Advanced Medical Solutions)
evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting; start October 2026.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled inpatient MS-DRG / packaged outpatient APC for all.
bd.notes: Signal: FDA cleared at least five MQV fillers in 2025-2026 but no antibiotic-eluting competitor to CERAMENT G; Biocomposites' genex G pivotal (start June 2026) is the first real one.

name: TnR Cranial Implant (formerly TnR CFI)
composition: 3D-printed porous, osteoconductive, resorbable scaffold of polycaprolactone and beta-tricalcium phosphate with interconnected pores, in burr-hole plug, strip and block geometries (15 x 33 to 67 mm strips, 15 x 30 to 50 mm blocks); resorbs over roughly 18 to 24 months per company

regulatory.reference: K251959 (2026-07-30, product code GXP, Traditional 510(k)); predicate Osteopore PCL Scaffold Bone Void Filler K051093
on_label_indications: Repair of neurosurgical burr holes, craniotomy cuts, and other cranial defects; augmentation or restoration of bony contour in the cranial skeleton

applications.evidence_summary: US clearance July 2026 rested on biocompatibility, toxicological risk assessment and GLP animal studies; the company claims more than 20,000 clinical uses in Korea since a 2021 MFDS approval, which is a promotional figure with no published US or peer-reviewed series located.
applications.caveats: No US distributor named as of October 2026; the 510(k) summary carries no size ceiling, unlike the cements.

applications.evidence_summary: Block and strip geometries are labeled for other cranial defects without a cm2 limit, but no clinical data exist for use beyond burr holes and kerfs.
applications.caveats: Label breadth exceeds evidence.

pipeline.expected_milestone: US commercial launch and distributor announcement pending (Korean press, August 2026).

bd.reimbursement: Bundled; no code.
bd.notes: Second 3D-printed PCL-TCP cranial scaffold cleared in the US after Osteopore; T&R Biofab sells PCL craniofacial implants in Korea and Europe.

name: Ventris Synthetic Bone Putty and Porous Biologic Scaffold
composition: Synthetic Bone Putty: biphasic ceramic granules in an alkylene oxide polymer carrier. Porous Biologic Scaffold: collagen mesh pouch prefilled with either demineralized bone matrix (version 1) or activated biphasic ceramic granules (version 2).

regulatory.reference: K240458 (Synthetic Bone Putty, March 2024; K221644 original Sept 2022); K240765 and K250556 (Porous Biologic Scaffold, 2024 to 2025)
on_label_indications: Synthetic Bone Putty (K240458): osseous defects not intrinsic to stability, packed into the 'pelvis, posterolateral spine, or intervertebral disc space', standalone or with autograft as an extender; with a cleared cage in intervertebral fusion
Porous Biologic Scaffold (K240765): pelvis and posterolateral spine, combined with autograft as an extender

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Ventris Medical synthetic bone putty OR porous biologic scaffold).
applications.caveats: No literature found for either product.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Ventris Medical synthetic bone putty interbody).
applications.caveats: Interbody indication added March 2024 (with a cleared cage).

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Spine-only labels (no extremities).

name: Arthrex Angel cPRP and Bone Marrow Processing System
company: Arthrex (exclusive distributor); manufactured by Cytomedix/Nuo Therapeutics heritage (Angel originally a Sorin/COBE Cardiovascular device)
ownership_history: COBE Cardiovascular cleared the Angel whole-blood separation system in 2004 (K042473); Sorin Group sold Angel to Cytomedix in 2010; Cytomedix (later Nuo Therapeutics) obtained a second 510(k) in November 2012 for processing a mixture of blood and bone marrow aspirate and granted Arthrex exclusive worldwide rights for non-wound-care uses. Current manufacturing/ownership chain not verified for 2025-2026.
composition: Automated, sensor-driven centrifuge and single-use kit that produces platelet-rich plasma or concentrated bone marrow aspirate with adjustable hematocrit/platelet levels.

regulatory.reference: BK110046 (Angel Whole Blood Separation System, Cytomedix; decision 2012-11-07; the clearance that added processing of a blood plus bone marrow aspirate mixture); BK180180 (Arthrex Angel System Kits, Arthrex; decision 2018-07-05); both CBER 510(k)s, product code ORG 'platelet and plasma separator for bone graft handling', 21 CFR 864.9245. Original COBE Angel K042473 (2004-11-19, CDRH, product code JQC).
on_label_indications: Point-of-care preparation of platelet-rich plasma, including PRP concentrate from a mixture of blood and bone marrow aspirate, to be mixed with autograft/allograft bone (FDA product code ORG wording; Arthrex markets it as a 'cPRP and bone marrow processing system')

applications.evidence_summary: Same class evidence as other BMAC systems (Hernigou RCT, Papakostidis meta-analysis); device-specific data are bench comparisons of cell yield published by Arthrex.
applications.caveats: Manufacturer-authored yield comparisons; no clinical outcome trial with this device in the hip.

applications.evidence_summary: Class evidence only (Hernigou 2005).
applications.caveats: Off-label clinical claims.

bd.reimbursement: Same as Harvest: no separate inpatient payment; office/ASC coding via 20939 add-on or 38232 with frequent payer denials.
bd.notes: Arthrex's strength is its sports-medicine and foot-and-ankle rep network, not trauma; in hip osteonecrosis the pull is through arthroplasty and hip-preservation surgeons.

name: Arthrex Vortex Threaded Bone Marrow Recovery Needle
composition: Threaded bone marrow aspiration needle sold alongside the Angel system for iliac crest and other marrow harvest; a harvest accessory, not a concentrator.

regulatory.reference: K213213 (decision 2021-11-19, product code KNW; predicate Ranfac Bone Marrow Aspiration Needle K131157)
on_label_indications: Intended for use in aspirating bone marrow.

No claim about the use of the aspirate (joint injection, osteonecrosis, nonunion). Regulatory frame for every BMAC system: the 510(k)s (product codes JQC, QBV, ORG) clear a point-of-care centrifuge kit to prepare a bone marrow concentrate, or PRP to be mixed with bone graft; several state 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established'. Injection of BMAC into a joint, tendon or osteonecrotic femoral head is an off-label use of the device. FDA treats the autologous marrow product as outside premarket review (not an HCT/P when minimally manipulated and used homologously, 21 CFR 1271.3(d)(4); or same-surgical-procedure exception) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Class-level: BMAC equalled PRP at 2 years in one RCT (Anz 2022, n=90); another RCT-level signal is lacking.
applications.caveats: The needle clearance covers aspiration only. Off-label use of the aspirate.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Class-level: Hernigou's 116-patient series was positive (no control), but two RCTs of BMAC with core decompression found no benefit (Hauzeur 2018; Pepke 2016).
applications.caveats: The needle clearance covers aspiration only. Off-label use of the aspirate.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Class-level: Hernigou 2005 (n=60 tibial nonunions, 53 united) is an uncontrolled series.
applications.caveats: The needle clearance covers aspiration only. Off-label use of the aspirate.

evidence.title: Bone Marrow Aspirate Concentrate Is Equivalent to Platelet-Rich Plasma for the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis at 2 Years: A Prospective Randomized Trial
evidence.finding: Class-level (system not specified in abstract): BMAC vs leukocyte-rich PRP: no difference in IKDC or WOMAC over 24 months; both improved from baseline, BMAC not superior (NCT03289416). Enrollment count from the registry.

evidence.title: Inefficacy of autologous bone marrow concentrate in stage three osteonecrosis: a randomized controlled double-blind trial
evidence.finding: Class-level: Core decompression with BMAC vs without in stage 3 osteonecrosis (23 hips per arm, 19 patients per arm): 15 of 23 hips in each arm needed THR; BMAC added nothing.

evidence.title: Percutaneous autologous bone-marrow grafting for nonunions. Influence of the number and concentration of progenitor cells
evidence.finding: Class-level: 60 noninfected atrophic tibial nonunions injected with 20 cm3 concentrated marrow: 53 united; union required more than 1500 progenitors/cm3 and about 55,000 total progenitors; no control arm and no commercial kit named.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered for orthopedic use: cash-pay. Bone marrow harvest codes bill separately for the surgeon when done with an operation (inpatient bundled in MS-DRG).
bd.notes: Arthrex bundles the needle with Angel; competes with Ranfac Marrow Cellution (side-port needle) and Jamshidi-type needles that cost a fraction of the price.

name: Bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) and percutaneous marrow injection
company: Multiple device makers (Terumo/Harvest SmartPrep, Arthrex Angel, Zimmer Biomet BioCUE, EmCyte, Celling); autologous point-of-care
ownership_history: Terumo Americas agreed to acquire Harvest Technologies on 2011-05-11. Device clearances are for the centrifuge/concentration system, not for a cellular claim.
composition: Autologous iliac crest marrow aspirate concentrated 4-10x at point of care; osteoprogenitor (CFU-F) dose is the biologically relevant variable

regulatory.reference: Concentration systems cleared under 510(k) (e.g., SmartPrep, Angel) for preparing autologous PRP/BMC; same-surgical-procedure exception under 21 CFR 1271.15(b) covers minimal manipulation; any osteoinductive claim is off-label; Device clearances: Harvest SmartPReP2 BMAC K103340 (CDRH, product code JQC, 2010-12-06); CBER 510(k)s under product code ORG 'platelet and plasma separator for bone graft handling' (21 CFR 864.9245): Arthrex/Cytomedix Angel BK110046 (decision 2012-11-07) and Arthrex Angel System Kits BK180180 (2018-07-05), Arthrex ACP Max BK210655 (2022-09-22), Isto/Arteriocyte Precise Cell Concentration System BK200540 (2022-03-17). The ORG labeling is PRP from blood (or a blood and bone-marrow-aspirate mixture) mixed with autograft/allograft to improve handling; no device carries a cell-therapy, fracture-healing or nonunion claim
on_label_indications: Devices: rapid preparation of autologous bone marrow concentrate / platelet concentrate at the point of care; no labeled fracture-healing claim

applications.evidence_summary: Hernigou 2005 injected concentrated marrow into 60 atrophic tibial nonunions and showed union correlated with CFU-F count and concentration (threshold about 1,500 progenitors per mL); a 2024 systematic review of 25 studies found aseptic nonunion success 79-100% (marrow) and 50-100% (BMAC) but extremely heterogeneous designs.
applications.caveats: No US RCT; dose-response data from a single French group; outcomes confounded by concomitant fixation and grafts.
applications.challenge: Ask which centrifuge delivers the Hernigou progenitor dose; most cannot be shown to.

applications.evidence_summary: Hernigou 2020: early percutaneous BMC in 231 Gustilo II-III open fractures (gap under 10 mm) vs 67 no-graft and 76 early ICBG controls, with lower infection and better healing in the BMC group.
applications.caveats: Non-randomized, single-center.

applications.evidence_summary: 2025 network meta-analysis of 15 RCTs (1,286 patients) ranked PRP+BMAC among the best strategies for healing time; diamond-concept series use BMAC with RIA graft.
applications.caveats: Pooled RCTs are small and mostly ex-US.

applications.evidence_summary: Attia 2022 meta-analysis (PMID 35612823) of 718 athlete Jones fractures: union 98.5% with orthobiologic augmentation (mostly BMAC or BMA plus DBM) vs 93.8% with fixation alone; Murawski and Kennedy 2011 (PMID 21212308) 26 athletes with percutaneous screw plus BMAC, mean radiographic healing 5 weeks, one delayed union.
applications.caveats: No comparative trial; selection of high-risk athletes for augmentation; return-to-play unchanged.

applications.evidence_summary: Pinzur 2009 (PMID 19254506): 44 high-risk diabetic Charcot patients (46 feet, 28 with open wounds) corrected with ring fixation plus platelet-rich concentrate and bone marrow aspirate; 42 of 46 feet showed radiographic union, two amputations.
applications.caveats: Single surgeon, no control, PRP and BMA combined.

applications.evidence_summary: Hernigou 2005 (PMID 15995108): percutaneous concentrated marrow injection into 60 atrophic tibial nonunions, union in 53, with union correlating with progenitor count. Tricot 2017 (PMID 28416462): 115 ankle/hindfoot fusions, allograft plus DBM plus BMA vs autograft plus DBM, nonunion 13% vs 18%, infection 4% vs 11%. Anastasio 2025 review (PMID 40680688): moderate-to-high evidence for nonoperative delayed union/nonunion, questionable benefit in arthrodesis.
applications.caveats: Tibial, not foot, data for the strongest series; progenitor yield varies 10-fold between patients and harvest sites; cost and harvest morbidity unjustified by RCT data.

applications.evidence_summary: Routinely layered into bone-block TTC fusions (PMID 34677103: 14 patients, femoral-head allograft plus BMAC plus DBM fibers).
applications.caveats: Never isolated.

applications.evidence_summary: Arthroscopic fixation plus DBM and BMAC injection united 15 of 17 early scaphoid nonunions (Lee 2026, PMID:42098735); a French case report describes concentrated marrow injection in scaphoid nonunion (Maincourt 2025, PMID:39732339). No comparative study.
applications.caveats: Selected nonunions with minimal sclerosis; adds iliac aspiration morbidity and a centrifuge disposable.

applications.evidence_summary: The foundational percutaneous BMAC data are tibial (Hernigou 2005, PMID 15995108: 60 atrophic tibial nonunions, 53 united, failures received fewer progenitors; technique paper PMID 16951103). Humeral nonunions were included in the ORTHO-1 expanded-MSC feasibility trial (28 femur/tibia/humerus nonunions; PMID 29598897).
applications.caveats: Dose-response depends on progenitor count, which most surgeons do not measure; evidence does not separate the humerus.

applications.evidence_summary: Navani 2024 crossover RCT (n=40) found intradiscal BMC improved pain and function vs placebo at 12 months (open-label, crossover).
applications.caveats: See PRP record; same trial.

evidence.title: Percutaneous autologous bone-marrow grafting for nonunions: influence of the number and concentration of progenitor cells
evidence.finding: Concentrated marrow (20 mL) injected into 60 noninfected atrophic tibial nonunions; mineralized callus volume and healing correlated with number and concentration of CFU-F; nonunions that failed received fewer progenitors.

evidence.title: Early injection of autologous bone marrow concentrates decreases infection risk and improves healing of acute severe open tibial fractures
evidence.finding: 231 BMC-treated open tibial fractures vs 67 no-graft and 76 ICBG controls; BMC associated with lower infection and better healing (abstract truncated).

evidence.title: Bone marrow aspirate and BMAC: does the literature support use in long-bone nonunion?
evidence.finding: 25 studies; aseptic nonunion success 79-100% (BM) and 50-100% (BMAC); 18/24 report union over 80%; Level III; needs Level I data.

evidence.title: BMP, PRP and BMAC in delayed union or nonunion: systematic review and network meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: 15 RCTs; PRP and BMP shortened healing time and raised healing rate vs standard care; PRP+autograft and PRP+BMAC ranked highest by SUCRA.

evidence.title: Surgical management of Jones fractures in athletes: orthobiologic augmentation, a systematic review and meta-analysis of 718 fractures
evidence.finding: Union 98.5% augmented vs 93.8% fixation alone; no difference in return to play.

evidence.title: Percutaneous internal fixation of proximal fifth metatarsal Jones fractures with Charlotte Carolina screw and bone marrow aspirate concentrate
evidence.finding: Mean healing 5 weeks; one delayed union, one refracture.

evidence.title: Use of platelet-rich concentrate and bone marrow aspirate in high-risk patients with Charcot arthropathy of the foot
evidence.finding: 42 of 46 feet united at mean 26 months.

evidence.title: Clinical assessment of 115 cases of hindfoot fusion with two different types of graft: allograft+DBM+bone marrow aspirate versus autograft+DBM
evidence.finding: Nonunion 13% vs 18%, not significant; allograft group had fewer infections.

evidence.title: Concentrated bone marrow aspirate applications in bony fusion for foot and ankle orthopaedic surgery: a review
evidence.finding: Narrative review: supportive for percutaneous nonunion treatment, uncertain for arthrodesis; RCTs needed to justify cost.

evidence.title: Effect of osteogenic progenitor cell concentration on the incidence of foot and ankle fusion

evidence.finding: 21 studies; pooled healing 44%/73%/90%/86% at 3/6/9/12 months; authors note lack of high-quality evidence.

evidence.title: Orthobiologic injections for discogenic chronic low back pain: crossover RCT (Pain Physician 2024)
evidence.finding: Intradiscal BMC improved pain and function vs saline trigger-point control; open-label crossover.

bd.reimbursement: Harvest/concentration is bundled into the surgical procedure; CPT 38220/38222 marrow aspiration may be reported by some surgeons; CPT 0232T (PRP injection) is Category III and widely non-covered; no separate payment for BMAC in the facility.

name: Cyclone PRP Concentrating System and Cyclone Blood and Bone Marrow Concentration (BBMC) System
ownership_history: Alliance Partners also filed the Swann-Shidi bone marrow aspiration needle (K121181). Not to be confused with the Nakoma ACP cervical plate that shares the 'ACP' letters in the 510(k) database.

on_label_indications: Indication and product-code text not retrievable; expected ORG for the PRP kit. Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated. Regulatory frame for every BMAC system: the 510(k)s (product codes JQC, QBV, ORG) clear a point-of-care centrifuge kit to prepare a bone marrow concentrate, or PRP to be mixed with bone graft; several state 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established'. Injection of BMAC into a joint, tendon or osteonecrotic femoral head is an off-label use of the device. FDA treats the autologous marrow product as outside premarket review (not an HCT/P when minimally manipulated and used homologously, 21 CFR 1271.3(d)(4); or same-surgical-procedure exception) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

name: EmCyte PureBMC SupraPhysiologic Concentrating System
ownership_history: Privately held (Fort Myers, FL).
composition: Single-use kit (30 mL system) for a benchtop centrifuge that concentrates 50-60 mL of bone marrow aspirate to a few mL of BMAC; used in the Andrews RCT and a Cleveland Clinic hip OA trial with EmCyte's Aspire needle.

regulatory.reference: K183205 (PureBMC SupraPhysiologic Concentrating System 30 mL, decision 2019-05-30, product code JQC, 21 CFR 862.2050 clinical centrifuge)
on_label_indications: Intended 'to be used in a clinical laboratory or intraoperatively at the point of care for the safe and rapid preparation of platelet concentrate from a small sample of bone marrow aspirate. The safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established.' Regulatory frame for every BMAC system: the 510(k)s (product codes JQC, QBV, ORG) clear a point-of-care centrifuge kit to prepare a bone marrow concentrate, or PRP to be mixed with bone graft; several state 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established'. Injection of BMAC into a joint, tendon or osteonecrotic femoral head is an off-label use of the device. FDA treats the autologous marrow product as outside premarket review (not an HCT/P when minimally manipulated and used homologously, 21 CFR 1271.3(d)(4); or same-surgical-procedure exception) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

challenge: The clearance states in its own text that in vivo effectiveness is not established; every clinical use is off-label by the clearance's own wording.

applications.evidence_summary: Only RCT using the product (Anz 2022, n=90, NCT03289416): BMAC (PureBMC) equalled EmCyte PRP at 2 years, not superior. Cleveland Clinic RCT of BMAC vs triamcinolone for hip OA (NCT04990128, n=100) is recruiting.
applications.caveats: No placebo arm; EmCyte collaborated. Cell yield varies by patient. Off-label injection.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Class-level: Hernigou 116-patient series positive but uncontrolled; two RCTs negative (Hauzeur 2018, Pepke 2016).
applications.caveats: Off-label.

evidence.finding: Andrews Research & Education Foundation RCT (NCT03289416, n=90) of knee OA: BMAC made with EmCyte PureBMC vs PRP made with EmCyte Pure PRP II (EmCyte is a listed collaborator): no difference in IKDC or WOMAC over 24 months; both groups improved from baseline and plateaued at 3 months; BMAC was not superior to PRP. name: Harvest SmartPReP 2 BMAC System
company: Terumo BCT (Terumo Blood and Cell Technologies), via Harvest Technologies Corp.
ownership_history: Harvest Technologies (Plymouth, MA) was acquired by Terumo Americas Holding (agreement announced 2011-05-11, $70 million plus milestones). Terumo Blood and Cell Technologies' 2021 release still lists the 'Harvest BMAC Procedure Pack' among its products; no 2025-2026 Terumo product page for the SmartPReP/BMAC system was found, so current catalog status is unconfirmed.
composition: Point-of-care dual-chamber centrifuge and disposable that concentrates nucleated cells and platelets from 60-120 mL of autologous bone marrow aspirate in about 15 minutes.

regulatory.reference: K991430 (SmartPReP Centrifuge System, 1999-05-28); K052925 (SmartPReP2 Centrifuge System, 2006-01-04); K103340 (SmartPReP2 BMAC System and SmartPReP Platelet Concentration System, Special 510(k), decision 2010-12-06); product code JQC (blood-cell centrifuge), applicant Harvest Technologies Corp.
on_label_indications: Clinical laboratory or intraoperative point-of-care preparation of platelet poor plasma and platelet concentrate from a small sample of blood and of a cell concentrate from bone marrow

challenge: The 510(k) clears the centrifuge for making a concentrate, not any clinical claim; any 'stem cell' or healing claim for BMAC is off-label. Hernigou's manually processed marrow evidence does not transfer to this specific device. 2026 catalog status of the Harvest line under Terumo was not confirmed.

applications.evidence_summary: Class evidence: Hernigou's bilateral-hip RCT (125 patients, 25-year follow-up) and Papakostidis 2015 meta-analysis (7 studies, OR 0.2 for collapse) favor BMAC-augmented decompression in pre-collapse disease; post-collapse RCT negative (Hauzeur 2018). None used this device. A 192-patient US RCT (Johns Hopkins, NCT06123481) is recruiting.
applications.caveats: Single-center dominance (Hernigou); device-agnostic evidence; cell dose is rarely measured in practice.

applications.evidence_summary: Hernigou 2005: percutaneous injection of concentrated marrow united 53 of 60 atrophic tibial nonunions, with union correlating with progenitor concentration above ~1,500 CFU-F/mL.
applications.caveats: Tibial data; uncontrolled; concentration achieved by a lab cell separator, not a point-of-care device.

evidence.title: Cell therapy versus simultaneous contralateral decompression in symptomatic corticosteroid osteonecrosis: a thirty year follow-up prospective randomized study of 125 adult patients.
evidence.finding: THA in 24% of marrow-grafted hips versus 76% of decompression-only hips; collapse 28% versus 72%.

evidence.title: The role of cell therapy in osteonecrosis of the femoral head. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 7 studies.
evidence.finding: Odds of collapse reduced (OR 0.2, 95% CI 0.08-0.6) and THA conversion halved (OR 0.6, p=0.06) with marrow cell implantation versus core decompression alone.

evidence.title: Percutaneous autologous bone-marrow grafting for nonunions. Influence of the number and concentration of progenitor cells.
evidence.finding: Union in 53 of 60 atrophic tibial nonunions; non-union cases received significantly fewer progenitors.

evidence.title: Inefficacy of autologous bone marrow concentrate in stage three osteonecrosis: a randomized controlled double-blind trial.
evidence.finding: No difference in THA requirement (15 of 23 hips in each arm) or clinical/radiographic outcomes in post-collapse ARCO III.

bd.reimbursement: No separate payment for BMAC preparation in the inpatient setting; in the office/ASC setting CPT 38232 (bone marrow harvest) or 20939 (bone marrow aspiration for grafting, add-on) may be billed but many payers deny BMAC as investigational; disposable cost is borne by the facility.
bd.notes: Capital-plus-disposable model; Terumo BCT distributes directly and through orthopedic distributors. The orthobiologics BMAC market has shifted toward Arthrex (Angel) and smaller players as Terumo's focus is apheresis.

name: Marrow Cellution Bone Marrow Aspiration System
ownership_history: Ranfac, a century-old maker of single-use biopsy and aspiration needles, makes Marrow Cellution; sold as its own product and as an OEM device.
composition: Side-port aspiration needle that draws marrow in small (about 1 mL) lateral-flow draws without centrifugation, targeting cell-rich inner cortex; the aspirate is injected without a concentration step.

regulatory.reference: K150563 (Marrow Cellution Bone Marrow Aspiration Needle, decision 2015-05-22, product code KNW; predicates Ranfac Aspiration Needle with Adjustable Guide K140991, Ranfac Bone Marrow Aspiration Needle K131157)
on_label_indications: 'Intended for use for aspiration of bone marrow or autologous blood using a standard piston syringe.' No claim about what the aspirate is used for. Regulatory frame for every BMAC system: the 510(k)s (product codes JQC, QBV, ORG) clear a point-of-care centrifuge kit to prepare a bone marrow concentrate, or PRP to be mixed with bone graft; several state 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established'. Injection of BMAC into a joint, tendon or osteonecrotic femoral head is an off-label use of the device. FDA treats the autologous marrow product as outside premarket review (not an HCT/P when minimally manipulated and used homologously, 21 CFR 1271.3(d)(4); or same-surgical-procedure exception) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: Retrospective cohort of 160 patients (262 knees) KL 2-4 injected with Marrow Cellution aspirate: VAS for daily activity 7.29 to 3.76 at six months (p<0.0001); no control group.
applications.caveats: Uncontrolled, short follow-up, retrospective; bench work by the method's proponents shows higher CFU-F than centrifuged BMAC (Scarpone 2019) but no randomized clinical comparison is published (OSU comparison NCT06388993, n=6, recruiting). Off-label.

name: Grafton DBM / Grafton Plus DBM Paste / Grafton DBF fibers
ownership_history: Developed by Osteotech (Eatontown, NJ); Medtronic completed its acquisition of Osteotech on 2010-11-16 ($6.50 per share, about $123 million). Older 510(k)s (K042707, K043048, K051188, K051195) list Osteotech as sponsor.
composition: Human demineralized bone matrix (particles or fibers) in a glycerol carrier (gel, putty, flex, matrix, paste forms); each lot sourced from a single donor

regulatory.reference: K251193 (Grafton DBM, Grafton Plus DBM Paste, Magnifuse; cleared 2025-06-12; 21 CFR 888.3045, product codes MQV/MBP); earlier Osteotech clearances K042707, K043048, K051188, K051195
on_label_indications: Bone graft extender, bone graft substitute and bone void filler for voids or gaps in the spine, pelvis and extremities that are not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (per K251193 summary as described in the FDA listing)

applications.evidence_summary: Prospective intra-patient trial (Cammisa 2004, n=120): Grafton gel/autograft composite fused 52% of sides vs 54% for ICBG at 24 months by blinded plain radiograph (kappa 0.51); Korean intra-patient comparison (Chang 2021, n=19): Grafton 70.4% vs DBX 66.7% side fusion at 24 months.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded 2004 study with 30% loss to follow-up; DBM osteoinductivity varies by donor and lot, and a 2020 rat study (SeaSpine-funded) found large between-brand differences.

applications.evidence_summary: Widely used as a local-bone extender in posterior cervical fusion under the general spine void-filler label; no posterior-cervical-specific study retrieved.
applications.caveats: Extrapolated from lumbar data.

applications.evidence_summary: Commonly used as the extender alongside rhBMP-2 in long constructs; no deformity-specific comparative study retrieved.
applications.caveats: Usage inferred from practice patterns, not trial data.

applications.evidence_summary: DBMs are the default autograft extender in nonunion revision; no RCT isolates Grafton's effect in femoral nonunion. Osteoinductivity varies lot to lot and by carrier.
applications.caveats: Donor and processing variability; glycerol carrier historically raised nephrotoxicity questions at high volumes (animal data).

applications.evidence_summary: Used as an extender in Masquelet stage two.
applications.caveats: Extender only; not a stand-alone substitute for critical defects.

applications.evidence_summary: DBM is the default autograft extender in nonunion and Masquelet second stage, but PubMed search found no RCT of any DBM in long-bone nonunion; evidence is case series and lot-to-lot osteoinductivity variability is documented. A 2025 foot-and-ankle systematic review (363 patients) found 'limited evidence'.
applications.caveats: Osteoinductive potency varies by donor and processing; no tibial nonunion comparative data; claims of osteoinduction are product-marketing, not label.
applications.challenge: If asked for the best DBM nonunion study, the honest answer is that there is none at Level I-II.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a volume extender with RIA/ICBG in the Masquelet second stage in many series; no isolated effect estimate.
applications.caveats: Confounded by autograft.

applications.evidence_summary: Class-level evidence: Hartman 2025 systematic review (PMID 39850040) of 13 DBM foot/ankle studies, 363 patients; union 85.6% for ankle/hindfoot arthrodesis, 100% for fifth-metatarsal and calcaneal fracture cohorts, nonunion 8.8% overall. Schlickewei 2022 (PMID 35807177) found no difference in arthroscopic ankle fusion nonunion with DBM (12.9%) vs without (14.8%).
applications.caveats: Low-level, heterogeneous evidence; no study shows superiority over autograft or over no graft; brand not always specified.

applications.evidence_summary: DBM combined with bone marrow aspirate is the common adjunct in NFL Jones-fracture series (Lareau 2015, PMID 26353796; Hunt and Anderson 2011 revision series, PMID 21632977).

applications.evidence_summary: Used routinely as a graft extender in Charcot and TTC bone-block series (e.g., PMID 34677103 combined femoral-head allograft, BMAC and DBM fibers in 14 TTC fusions).

applications.evidence_summary: DBM is the most common off-the-shelf extender mixed with autograft or cellular allograft at upper-extremity nonunion revision, but no DBM-specific comparative humeral nonunion study was found; the practice rests on surgeon habit and lower-limb/spine data.
applications.caveats: Osteoinductivity varies by donor and lot; DBM products are tested by the manufacturer in athymic rodent assays, not in humans.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23 on the brand name). applications.caveats: Extremities void filler covers the anatomy; fusion is surgeon practice.

evidence.title: Comparison of Fusion Rate between Demineralized Bone Matrix versus Autograft in Lumbar Fusion: Meta-Analysis

applications.caveats: Label allows use as an autograft extender in the spine; the DBM is not a stand-alone graft claim.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23 on the brand name). applications.caveats: Label says 'spine' without naming interbody cage packing; whether interbody use is inside the cleared indication is a regulatory judgment the company, not the atlas, should confirm.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23 on the brand name). applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23 on the brand name). applications.caveats: Void-filler labeling covers extremities; foot and ankle fusion use is surgeon practice inside that wording.

evidence.title: Comparison of Fusion Rate between Demineralized Bone Matrix versus Autograft in Lumbar Fusion: Meta-Analysis
evidence.finding: Class-level, not product-specific: across 8 non-randomized comparative studies, fusion rate did not differ significantly between DBM and autograft in posterolateral (RR 1.03) or interbody (RR 1.13) fusion.

name: APEX Biologix XCELL PRP Platelet Concentrating System (60 mL)
composition: 60 mL single-use disposable for a benchtop centrifuge; compared against EmCyte PurePRP in a UCSF pilot of PRP cellular composition.

regulatory.reference: BK180252 (XCELL PRP Platelet Concentrating System 60 ml, decision 2019-04-05)
on_label_indications: Product-code and indication text not retrievable; as a 2019 CBER PRP clearance it is expected to sit in ORG (PRP for mixing with bone graft). Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). A UCSF pilot (NCT07491367, n=20, recruiting) characterizes platelet composition from XCELL vs EmCyte PurePRP; no clinical endpoint.
applications.caveats: Off-label injection.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered: cash-pay in the clinic; kit cost bundled into the procedure or patient fee. No HCPCS code for the product; CPT 0232T (PRP injection) is Category III and generally non-covered by Medicare and most commercial plans for musculoskeletal use. Chronic diabetic wound PRP is the one covered exception (CMS NCD 270.3, 2021).
bd.notes: Regenerative-clinic oriented kit vendor; the clearance details are thin because the FDA page was not retrievable.

name: Arthrex ACP Double Syringe System and ACP Max PRP System
ownership_history: Privately held (Naples, FL). Arthrex sells its own ACP line and, separately, distributes the Angel cPRP/marrow system (see arthrex-angel). The Genesis Biologics AAPS 510(k) cites the Arthrex Double Syringe (ACP) System (BK190406) as its predicate, so ACP is the reference device for newer ORG clearances.
composition: Single-use double-syringe device: venous blood is drawn into the outer syringe, spun in a benchtop centrifuge, and the plasma fraction is drawn into the inner syringe (generally described as a leukocyte-poor, low-platelet PRP). An independent benchtop test of four kits (GPS III, SmartPReP2, Magellan, ACP) found three buffy-coat kits at 3-6x baseline platelets and one plasma-sampling kit at only 1.5x; the abstract does not name that kit, but ACP is the plasma-sampling design. ACP Max (2022) is the successor system.

regulatory.reference: BK070069 (Arthrex Double Syringe (ACP, Autologous Conditioned Plasma) System, decision 2008-12-12, FDA product code FMF 'Syringe, piston', 21 CFR 880.5860); BK190406 (Arthrex Double Syringe (ACP) System, 2019-11-06); BK210655 (Arthrex ACP Max PRP System, decision 2022-09-22, product code ORG, 21 CFR 864.9245). CBER-reviewed BK numbers, not K numbers.
on_label_indications: BK210655 sits in product code ORG, whose FDA definition is 'preparation of autologous platelet rich plasma from a small sample of peripheral blood for mixing with bone graft to improve handling characteristics'. Arthrex's own ACP Max summary text was not retrievable; the wording is the ORG classification definition.
The first ACP clearance (BK070069) was filed as a piston syringe (880.5860), not as a platelet separator: the 2008 clearance carries no therapeutic indication at all.

Not cleared for injection into knees, tendons or any soft tissue. Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

challenge: A hiring manager will ask why a device cleared as a piston syringe and a bone-graft-handling kit is sold for knee and tendon injections, and and how a plasma-sampling, low-platelet preparation compares with buffy-coat PRP.

applications.evidence_summary: Best brand-specific evidence is negative: a double-blind single-center RCT (n=120 knees, 30 per arm, PRP prepared with the Arthrex ACP-System) found no evidence that PRP, hyaluronic acid or glucocorticoid beat placebo for pain over 6 months (Tschopp 2023).
applications.caveats: Single center, low baseline pain (median NRS 32.5), early-stage OA; the ACP-System is a plasma-based, low-platelet preparation. Class-level: meta-analyses of PRP vs HA (Belk 2021, 18 RCTs) favor PRP while the largest placebo-controlled RCT (Bennell 2021, n=288) was negative. Off-label injection use.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Class-level, product-unspecified RCTs in lateral epicondylitis are mixed (Mishra 2014 n=230 positive at 24 weeks only; Peerbooms 2010 n=100 positive vs corticosteroid).
applications.caveats: Several investigator-initiated ACP trials are registered (Tampere NCT01851044 lateral epicondylitis n=120; Bispebjerg NCT02417987 Achilles n=60; McMaster NCT01668953 terminated) but no published report naming the Arthrex device was confirmed. Off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23). Registry shows a Schulthess Klinik ACP rotator cuff repair RCT (NCT01266226, n=129, completed) but no report confirmed by search.
applications.caveats: Class-level: PRFM and PRP augmentation of cuff repair has been neutral in RCTs (Rodeo 2012 n=79, Castricini 2011 n=88). Off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: On-label only in the narrow sense of preparing PRP to mix with bone graft for handling; the label makes no healing or nonunion claim. Class-level: PRP was inferior to rhBMP-7 for persistent nonunion (Calori 2008, n=120, 68.3% vs 86.7% union). Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

evidence.title: A Randomized Trial of Intra-articular Injection Therapy for Knee Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Double-blind single-center trial of glucocorticoid, HA, PRP (prepared with the Arthrex ACP-System) or placebo, 30 knees per arm, KL 1-3: no evidence that any active injection beat placebo for pain within 6 months.

evidence.title: Analysis of Platelet-Rich Plasma Extraction: Variations in Platelet and Blood Components Between 4 Common Commercial Kits
evidence.finding: Class-level, includes ACP: Benchtop test of GPS III, SmartPReP2, Magellan and ACP (Device Technologies) on blood from 3 donors: three kits sampling the buffy coat gave 3-6x baseline platelets and white cells while one plasma-sampling kit gave only 1.5x (the abstract does not say which kit; ACP is the double-syringe design that draws plasma).

evidence.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma Versus Hyaluronic Acid for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): 18 level-1 studies (811 PRP, 797 HA patients): WOMAC total improvement 44.7% vs 12.6%; leukocyte-poor PRP gave better IKDC than leukocyte-rich.

evidence.title: Effect of Intra-articular Platelet-Rich Plasma vs Placebo Injection on Pain and Medial Tibial Cartilage Volume in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: The RESTORE Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): Leukocyte-poor PRP (a commercial product, not named in the abstract) vs saline: 12-month knee pain change -2.1 vs -1.8 (difference -0.4, 95% CI -0.9 to 0.2) and no cartilage-volume benefit.

evidence.title: Efficacy of platelet-rich plasma for chronic tennis elbow: a double-blind, prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial of 230 patients
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): Leukocyte-enriched PRP needling vs active control: no difference at 12 weeks (pain improvement 55.1% vs 47.4%, p=.163); at 24 weeks 71.5% vs 56.1% (p=.019) and success 83.9% vs 68.3% (p=.037).

evidence.title: Positive effect of an autologous platelet concentrate in lateral epicondylitis in a double-blind randomized controlled trial: platelet-rich plasma versus corticosteroid injection with a 1-year follow-up
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): PRP vs corticosteroid: VAS success 73% vs 49% at one year (p<.001); the platelet-concentrate system is not named in the abstract.

evidence.title: Application of rhBMP-7 and platelet-rich plasma in the treatment of long bone non-unions: a prospective randomised clinical study on 120 patients
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): Persistent long-bone nonunions: union in 86.7% with rhBMP-7 vs 68.3% with PRP; PRP was the weaker arm.

No clinical indication; clinical data in the summary are bench-level. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

The ACP/Angel PRP it activates is class-level evidence only (see arthrex-acp, arthrex-angel). Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

name: Aurix System (formerly AutoloGel System) PRP gel for chronic wounds
ownership_history: Cytomedix, Inc. (formerly Informatix Holdings 1998, Autologous Wound Therapy 1999; Cytomedix 2000) renamed Nuo Therapeutics in 2014; Chapter 11 in 2001-2002 and again January 2016; operations furloughed 1 May 2019 while seeking a Medicare coverage reconsideration; restarted October 2021 after the April 2021 NCD revision. Cytomedix bought the Angel business from Sorin in April 2010 (see arthrex-angel). SEC filings: nuot20170409_s1, aurx20240630_10q.
composition: Single-use disposable and desktop centrifuge for preparing PRP (up to 60 mL of blood) that is gelled with calcium chloride and thrombin and applied as a gel to wounds. Not an orthopedic injection product.

regulatory.reference: BK060007 (Autologel System, Cytomedix, decision 2007-09-20); K030340 (AutoloGel Process Centrifuge Model B4360, decision 2003-04-11, product code JQC). Aurix is the current name for AutoloGel per CMS.
on_label_indications: K030340: 'designed to be used at the patient's point of care for the safe and rapid preparation of autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from a small sample of the patient's blood (up to 60 ml)'. Wound indications under BK060007 not retrieved; CMS conditions coverage on the device's FDA-cleared indications including exuding cutaneous wounds. Injection of PRP into joints or tendons is an off-label use of any PRP device and is not covered by NCD 270.3 (autologous product is 361-exempt only when minimally manipulated).

challenge: Medicare's only national PRP coverage decision (NCD 270.3) was reopened at the manufacturer's request (2019, per CMS): coverage with evidence development in 2012, then from 2021 up to 20 weeks for chronic non-healing diabetic wounds when the preparing device is cleared for exuding cutaneous wounds; the company still shut down from 2019 to 2021.

applications.evidence_summary: Driver 2006 blinded multicenter RCT (72 randomized) of PRP gel vs saline-gel dressing on diabetic foot ulcers: per-protocol healing 68.4% vs 42.9%; 81.3% vs 42.1% (p=.036) only after excluding wound-size outliers.
applications.caveats: Per-protocol analysis after an audit excluded 32 of 72 patients; significance appeared only after an outlier adjustment; PRP prepared with bovine thrombin. CMS NCD 270.3: March 2008 determination of inadequate evidence; 2012 revision CED for diabetic, venous and pressure wounds; effective 2021-04-13 coverage of autologous PRP for chronic non-healing diabetic wounds for 20 weeks under 1862(a)(1)(A), MAC discretion beyond that, PDGF and acute surgical wound uses non-covered. Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

evidence.title: A prospective, randomized, controlled trial of autologous platelet-rich plasma gel for the treatment of diabetic foot ulcers
evidence.finding: 72 randomized to PRP gel or saline-gel dressing; 32 excluded from the per-protocol analysis after an audit; healing 13/19 (68.4%) vs 9/21 (42.9%), and 13/16 (81.3%) vs 8/19 (42.1%, p=.036) only after excluding wound-size outliers.

bd.reimbursement: Medicare covers autologous PRP for chronic non-healing diabetic wounds for 20 weeks (NCD 270.3, effective 2021-04-13) when the preparing device's FDA-cleared indications include exuding cutaneous wounds; beyond 20 weeks and other wounds are MAC-determined; acute surgical wounds non-covered.
bd.notes: The case study in how a single NCD decides a PRP company's fate; a hiring manager could ask what Nuo's restart implies for orthopedic PRP coverage (it does not extend).

Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).

name: Cascade Fibrinet / Cascade Autologous Platelet System (PRFM)
company: Cascade Medical Enterprises (Fibrinet); distributed for spine by Vertical Spine, LLC
ownership_history: Cascade Medical's PRFM line; a 2018 Cochrane review table lists the 'Cascade Autologous Platelet System' under the Musculoskeletal Transplant Foundation, which suggests MTF Biologics acquired it (not confirmed from a primary source). Vertical Spine filed a parallel Fibrinet 510(k) in 2012.
composition: Disposable kit that makes a platelet-rich fibrin matrix (PRFM): platelet-rich plasma is gelled by calcium chloride in the tube to a solid fibrin membrane that can be sutured or placed at a repair site.

regulatory.reference: BK020051 (Cascade Medical Fibrinet, Autologous Platelet System, decision 2002-12-20, Blood Bank Supplies KSS); BK030024 (2003-06-02); BK060006 (2006-02-16, KSS); BK120009 (Fibrinet Autologous PRP System, Cascade, received 2012-02-24, decision 2012-08-01, ORG); BK120008 (same, Vertical Spine, 2012-08-01); BK170096 (Fibrinet Platelet System, 2017-11-21)
on_label_indications: BK120009 is in product code ORG: PRP for mixing with bone graft to improve handling; the 2002-2006 clearances were filed as blood-bank supplies. Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

challenge: The one rigorous rotator-cuff trial of this product was negative, yet PRFM is still marketed for tendon repair augmentation.

applications.evidence_summary: Rodeo 2012 (n=79, PRFM at the tendon-bone interface, product per a Cochrane table the Cascade Autologous Platelet System): no improvement in ultrasound tendon healing at 6 or 12 weeks or in outcome scores. A second PRFM RCT (Castricini 2011, n=88) was also null but its product is not named in the abstract.
applications.caveats: Single-center RCT; Cochrane review notes the trial stopped early and PRP composition was not characterized. Off-label (cleared for bone graft handling).

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).

Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

evidence.title: The effect of platelet-rich fibrin matrix on rotator cuff tendon healing: a prospective, randomized clinical study
evidence.finding: PRFM (a Cochrane review table lists the Cascade Autologous Platelet System) at the tendon-bone interface vs standard repair: no difference in ultrasound tendon healing at 6 or 12 weeks or in outcome scores.

evidence.title: Platelet-rich plasma augmentation for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: a randomized controlled trial

evidence.title: Analysis of Platelet-Rich Plasma Extraction: Variations in Platelet and Blood Components Between 4 Common Commercial Kits
evidence.finding: Class-level, includes GPS III among four kits: Benchtop test of GPS III, SmartPReP2, Magellan and ACP (Device Technologies) on blood from 3 donors: three kits sampling the buffy coat gave 3-6x baseline platelets and white cells while one plasma-sampling kit gave only 1.5x (the abstract does not say which kit; ACP is the double-syringe design that draws plasma).

evidence.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma Versus Hyaluronic Acid for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): 18 level-1 studies (811 PRP, 797 HA patients): WOMAC total improvement 44.7% vs 12.6%; leukocyte-poor PRP gave better IKDC than leukocyte-rich.

evidence.title: Application of rhBMP-7 and platelet-rich plasma in the treatment of long bone non-unions: a prospective randomised clinical study on 120 patients
evidence.finding: Class-level (product not named): Persistent long-bone nonunions: union in 86.7% with rhBMP-7 vs 68.3% with PRP; PRP was the weaker arm.

company: Multiple (Arthrex ACP/Angel, Zimmer Biomet GPS III, Harvest SmartPReP APC, EmCyte, others)

regulatory.reference: Preparation devices cleared under product code JQC (blood separation for PRP); no PRP product has an FDA-cleared indication for fracture healing; Cleared by CBER under product code ORG 'platelet and plasma separator for bone graft handling' (21 CFR 864.9245), e.g., Arthrex ACP Max BK210655 (2022-09-22), Arthrex Angel BK180180 (2018-07-05), Isto Precise BK200540 (2022-03-17), RegenLab RegenKit-THT BK090048 (2010-05-18, product code FMF), and older CDRH centrifuges (JQC); labeling is PRP for mixing with bone graft to improve handling, no fracture-healing indication
on_label_indications: Devices: preparation of platelet-rich plasma from autologous blood at the point of care. No clinical fracture-healing indication is labeled.

challenge: Evidence is weak and the signal is inconsistent: the Cochrane review found a single eligible trial (n=21), and the 2024 umbrella meta-analysis of nonunion/delayed union found a healing-rate benefit only when meta-analyses were pooled, not when individual studies were pooled. A hiring manager will expect the candidate to say PRP in long-bone fracture is not supported, and that its use in hip and femur trauma is negligible.

applications.evidence_summary: Umbrella meta-analysis (Zhu 2024; 5 meta-analyses, 13 studies, 1,362 patients) found PRP shortened healing time by about 1-2 months but did not improve union rate when individual studies were pooled; Cochrane 2012 found insufficient evidence.
applications.caveats: Low-quality, heterogeneous trials, mostly tibia and mixed sites; PRP preparation varies widely.

applications.evidence_summary: A hip-fracture PRP trial was noted as 'underway' in the 2012 Cochrane review; no positive femoral neck RCT located.
applications.caveats: No evidence of benefit.

applications.evidence_summary: Evidence is weak and inconsistent: a 2024 umbrella meta-analysis (5 meta-analyses, 13 studies, 1,362 patients) found PRP improved healing rate only when meta-analyses were pooled, not when individual studies were pooled, and shortened healing time by about 2 weeks with no effect on pain; the 2022 Front Med review (13 studies, 459 patients, 3 RCTs) reached similar tentative conclusions.
applications.caveats: Small, heterogeneous, mostly ex-US trials; PRP formulations are not standardized; Category III CPT with no payment.
applications.challenge: Do not present PRP as a nonunion treatment option; present it as unproven.

applications.evidence_summary: No acute fracture RCT supports PRP; the 2014 and later meta-analyses of acute fracture adjuncts exclude it for lack of data.
applications.caveats: No evidence.

applications.evidence_summary: Weak evidence. Bibbo 2010 (PMID 21056862) reviewed 'only a handful' of basic-science and clinical foot/ankle PRP papers; a prospective Arthrex ACP ankle-arthrodesis study (NCT01131455) was terminated after 10 patients; Bolia 2024 (PMID 38704857) rated the arthrodesis PRP evidence as low quality.
applications.caveats: No RCT shows PRP improves foot/ankle fusion; the only positive high-risk series combined PRP with marrow aspirate (Pinzur 2009).

applications.evidence_summary: Pinzur 2009 (PMID 19254506) used platelet-rich concentrate plus marrow aspirate in 46 Charcot feet with 42 unions; PRP's independent contribution is unknown.
applications.caveats: Confounded single-arm series.

applications.evidence_summary: Weak. A 30-patient trial of intra-articular PRP after pinning of intra-articular distal radius fractures reported better PRWE pain and function at 3 and 6 months (Namazi 2016, PMID:26774901), self-graded level III; a 14-patient scaphoid trial from the same group (PMID:27999456) is uninterpretable. The 2022 PRP-in-fractures meta-analysis has been retracted (PMID:35693268).
applications.caveats: Small single-center trials without blinding; no union endpoint; the only meta-analysis is retracted. The honest position is that PRP has no demonstrated role in upper-extremity fracture or nonunion healing.

applications.evidence_summary: Navani 2024 (Pain Physician) randomized 40 patients to saline trigger-point injection, intradiscal PRP or intradiscal BMC with crossover; both biologics improved pain and function vs placebo at 12 months, but the trial was open-label and all placebo patients crossed over at 3 months.
applications.caveats: Open-label, n=40, authors affiliated with regenerative clinics, crossover design precludes a 12-month placebo comparison.

evidence.title: Platelet-rich plasma in the treatment of delayed union and nonunion fractures: An umbrella meta-analysis.
evidence.finding: Pooling meta-analyses gave RR 1.30 for healing rate, but pooling individual studies showed no effect on healing rate; healing time shortened (MD about -2 months).

evidence.title: Platelet rich therapies for long bone healing in adults (Cochrane review).
evidence.finding: One eligible trial (high tibial osteotomy, n=21); evidence insufficient to support routine use.

evidence.title: Platelet-rich plasma for the treatment of bone defects: from pre-clinical rational to evidence in the clinical practice. A systematic review.
evidence.finding: 64 articles (45 preclinical, 19 clinical): preclinical signal weakens on radiographic/biomechanical endpoints; clinical benefit 'still under debate' with low-quality heterogeneous literature.

evidence.title: Clinical effectiveness of PRP for long-bone delayed union and nonunion: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: 13 studies (3 RCTs); PRP associated with higher healing rate and shorter time but low-quality evidence.

evidence.title: Platelet-rich plasma concentrate to augment bone fusion
evidence.finding: Review: only a handful of foot/ankle PRP papers; proposes a risk classification for when to augment.

evidence.title: Autologous concentrated platelet-rich plasma (Arthrex ACP) for local application in ankle arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Terminated after 10 patients; no results posted.

evidence.title: Comparative studies of bone graft and orthobiologics for foot ankle arthrodesis: a critical review
evidence.finding: Critical review of autograft, allograft, DBM, calcium sulfate/phosphate, rhBMP-2, rhPDGF-BB, PRP and BMAC in ankle/hindfoot arthrodesis emphasizing low quality of evidence for most.

evidence.title: Investigating the effect of intra-articular PRP injection on pain and function improvement in patients with distal radius fracture
evidence.finding: Lower PRWE pain and disability scores with PRP at 3 and 6 months.

evidence.title: Efficacy of platelet-rich plasma in the treatment of fractures: a meta-analysis (RETRACTED)
evidence.finding: Retracted publication; must not be cited as support.

evidence.title: Adjunctive platelet-rich plasma in non-union lower extremity fracture management: A systematic review and meta-analysis (Chin J Traumatol 2026; DOI 10.1016/j.cjtee.2026.06.001)
evidence.finding: Pooled tibial/femoral nonunion studies (search to Oct 31, 2025) comparing PRP gel/concentrate/composite graft vs standard care; the abstract frames efficacy as 'still debated' (pooled estimate not extracted).

evidence.title: The Safety and Effectiveness of Orthobiologic Injections for Discogenic Chronic Low Back Pain: A Multicenter Prospective, Crossover, Randomized Controlled Trial with 12 Months Follow-up (Pain Physician 2024)
evidence.finding: Intradiscal PRP and BMC each improved NRS pain and function vs saline trigger-point injection; all placebo patients crossed over; no adverse events, hospitalizations or surgeries at 12 months.

evidence.title: 510(k) summary BK241083, OrthoAscent FG-001 Platelet Rich Plasma Device (prepared Sept 5, 2024)
evidence.finding: Documents the cleared intended use (mix with bone graft to improve handling) and the statement that the PRP has not been evaluated for any clinical indication.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 0232T (PRP injection, any site) is a Category III code that most payers, including Medicare, deny; inpatient use is bundled with no separate payment.
bd.notes: PRP revenue in orthopedics is a sports-medicine and office-injection story; trauma volume is marginal and shrinking as evidence accumulates.

ownership_history: Device-only market; no product owns the biologic.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No sponsor is pursuing an efficacy claim; PRP will remain a device-prepared, off-label-use autologous product.

name: Ranfac Autologous Platelet Separator (Cervos Platelet system)
ownership_history: Ranfac; the GUDID brand name for the kit is 'Cervos Platelet Single PB' (premarket submission BK200543).
composition: Single-use disposable PRP separator (single-spin) for a benchtop centrifuge, sold by Ranfac under the Cervos name.

regulatory.reference: BK200543 (Ranfac Autologous Platelet Separator, received 2020-11-13, decision 2021-02-24, product code ORG, 21 CFR 864.9245)
on_label_indications: Product code ORG: PRP for mixing with bone graft to improve handling; brand-specific text not retrievable. Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Off-label injection.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Graft handling on-label only; no healing claim. Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered: cash-pay in the clinic; kit cost bundled into the procedure or patient fee. No HCPCS code for the product; CPT 0232T (PRP injection) is Category III and generally non-covered by Medicare and most commercial plans for musculoskeletal use. Chronic diabetic wound PRP is the one covered exception (CMS NCD 270.3, 2021).

name: RegenKit (THT, BCT, ATS) PRP kits and RegenBMC
company: Regen Lab (RegenLab SA, Switzerland; Regen Lab USA, LLC, Jersey City, NJ)
ownership_history: Swiss maker RegenLab SA holds the older RegenKit clearances; Regen Lab USA, LLC is the applicant on the 2026 RegenBMC clearance.
composition: Evacuated blood-collection tubes containing a separator gel and anticoagulant (single-spin, closed system) that give PRP; the THT variant adds a thixotropic gel separator; RegenBMC processes a mix of blood and bone marrow aspirate.

regulatory.reference: BK090048 (RegenKit-THT, decision 2010-05-18, FMF piston syringe 880.5860); BK110061 (RegenKit-BCT family, 2012-05-08); BK120066 (RegenKit-ATS-3, BCT-1 Plus, BCT-2 Plus, received 2012-11-02, decision 2014-02-05, ORG); BK210661 (RegenKit Wound Gel, 2022-07-08); BK251274 (RegenBMC / RegenKit-THT-BMC, decision 2026-05-29, ORG)
on_label_indications: BK251274: 'safe and rapid preparation of autologous platelet concentrate platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from a small sample of peripheral blood or a small sample of a mixture of peripheral blood and bone marrow. The PRP is mixed with autograft and/or allograft bone prior to application to a bony defect for improving handling characteristics.' Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated.
The first RegenKit clearance (2010) was filed as a piston syringe, not a PRP device.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Off-label injection. RegenKit is widely used in Europe and Asia for joint injection (CE-marked); no study naming the product was confirmed here.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Graft handling on-label (2026 RegenBMC); no healing claim. Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered: cash-pay in the clinic; kit cost bundled into the procedure or patient fee. No HCPCS code for the product; CPT 0232T (PRP injection) is Category III and generally non-covered by Medicare and most commercial plans for musculoskeletal use. Chronic diabetic wound PRP is the one covered exception (CMS NCD 270.3, 2021).
bd.notes: Tube-based closed system with no dedicated centrifuge or kit-lock-in; the 2026 RegenBMC clearance extends the use to blood-plus-marrow mixtures for graft handling.

name: Royal MAXX PRP and MAXX BMC Concentration Systems
ownership_history: Privately held. Royal Biologics also sells Amnio-Maxx amniotic products (NCT07209475, diabetic foot ulcers).
composition: Disposable point-of-care kits for a benchtop centrifuge: MAXX PRP concentrates platelets; MAXX BMC concentrates bone marrow aspirate.

regulatory.reference: BK210563 (Royal Maxx Autologous PRP Concentration System, received 2021-03-17, decision 2021-04-16, product code ORG); BK210632 (Royal MAXX BMC and MAXX PRP Concentration Systems, decision 2022-02-11)
on_label_indications: BK210563 is in product code ORG: PRP prepared for mixing with bone graft to improve handling; BK210632 BMC indication text not retrievable. Regulatory frame for every PRP kit: 510(k)s in product code ORG (21 CFR 864.9245) clear the device to prepare PRP 'to be mixed with bone graft' at the point of care to improve handling; older JQC, KSS and FMF clearances cover a centrifuge, a blood-bank supply or a piston syringe and carry no therapeutic indication. Injection of PRP into a joint or tendon is an off-label use of the device. FDA has not approved or cleared PRP as a treatment for those uses; the autologous preparation sits outside premarket review (361-exempt, same-surgical-procedure rule) only while it stays minimally manipulated. Regulatory frame for every BMAC system: the 510(k)s (product codes JQC, QBV, ORG) clear a point-of-care centrifuge kit to prepare a bone marrow concentrate, or PRP to be mixed with bone graft; several state 'the safety and effectiveness of this device for in vivo indications for use has not been established'. Injection of BMAC into a joint, tendon or osteonecrotic femoral head is an off-label use of the device. FDA treats the autologous marrow product as outside premarket review (not an HCT/P when minimally manipulated and used homologously, 21 CFR 1271.3(d)(4); or same-surgical-procedure exception) only while it stays minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Graft-handling scope only (PRP); the BMC kit cleared 2022 has no retrieved indication text. Spine PRP data are neutral to negative at class level (Carreon 2005). Injection of PRP or BMAC into joints or tendons is off-label for the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Off-label injection.

evidence.title: Platelet gel (AGF) fails to increase fusion rates in instrumented posterolateral fusions
evidence.finding: Class-level (different platelet-gel system): 76 instrumented PLFs with iliac crest graft plus autologous growth factor platelet gel vs matched controls: nonunion 25% vs 17% (p=.18), no benefit. System is a proprietary platelet-gel method, not one of the brands in this file.

name: Affinity (hypothermically stored amniotic membrane) and Novachor
ownership_history: Affinity launched 2014 by NuTech Medical, acquired by Organogenesis 2017; Novachor launched December 2021.
composition: Fresh (never dried or frozen), hypothermically stored amniotic membrane (Affinity); Novachor is a fresh placental (chorion-containing) membrane.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)
on_label_indications: 361 HCT/P used as a protective barrier and wound covering; Organogenesis positions it for open wounds in the surgical setting

applications.evidence_summary: Serena 2020 RCT (76 DFUs): hypothermically stored amniotic membrane closed more DFUs than standard care at 12 weeks (60% vs 38%); not a post-osteomyelitis population, so no evidence for this application specifically.
applications.caveats: Organogenesis employee among authors; small trial.

applications.evidence_summary: A 10-patient NuTech 'Affinity for chondral defects' study (NCT02837484) has unknown status and no results.
applications.caveats: Non-homologous use; unpublished.

evidence.title: A randomized controlled clinical trial of a hypothermically stored amniotic membrane for use in diabetic foot ulcers
evidence.finding: Closure 60% vs 38% at 12 weeks (Cox p=0.04); HR 1.75.

evidence.title: NuTech Affinity for the Treatment of Chondral Defects
evidence.finding: Status unknown; no results.

bd.reimbursement: Medicare: HCPCS Q-code 'Q4159 Affinity per sq cm'. From 1 Jan 2026 the CY2026 PFS (CMS-1832-F, 31 Oct 2025) and OPPS rules pay non-BLA skin substitutes as incident-to supplies at one flat rate (CMS fact sheet: approximately $127.28 per cm2; MiMedx and Organogenesis 10-Ks state $127.14 per cm2), before geographic adjustment, grouped by FDA pathway (361 HCT/P, PMA, 510(k)). The MAC skin-substitute LCDs that would have cut covered products were withdrawn 24 Dec 2025; L35041 (Novitas), L36377 (First Coast) and L36690 (CGS) remain. In inpatient or OR use the graft is bundled into the DRG/APC (facilities often report C1762 connective tissue).
bd.notes: Organogenesis 10-K risk factor names Affinity, Novachor and NuShield as products FDA could decide are not 361.

name: AlloWrap DS and AlloWrap Dry (amniotic membrane)
ownership_history: AlloSource (Centennial, CO), non-profit tissue bank. A 2023 hand-surgery paper credits AlloWrap to Stryker, suggesting Stryker distributes it in some channels (not confirmed).

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)
on_label_indications: 'Biologic barrier following surgical repair' for open and minimally invasive procedures (AlloSource product page)

applications.evidence_summary: Adjacent barrier use: AlloSource-sponsored RCT of AlloWrap to reduce prevertebral soft-tissue inflammation in two-level ACDF (NCT04684901, n=50) is enrolling; no results.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a barrier around repairs; one ulnar-nerve transposition technique paper mentions it; no comparative tendon study located.

evidence.title: A Randomized, Controlled Study to Evaluate Effectiveness of AlloWrap Amniotic Membrane for the Reduction of Post-Operative Soft Tissue Inflammation in Two-Level ACDF
evidence.finding: Enrolling by invitation; completion 2027.

evidence.title: The modified fascial sling technique for ulnar nerve anterior transposition: surgical techniques and results
evidence.finding: Technique paper: AlloWrap (credited to Stryker as supplier) wrapped around the transposed ulnar nerve before a fascial sling; no comparator.

bd.reimbursement: Q4150 ('AlloWrap DS or Dry, 1 sq cm') for outpatient wound use; surgical use bundled.

evidence.finding: 85% vs 25% healed at 12 weeks; mean 3.8 grafts per healed wound; tissue cost about $1,400 per healed DFU.

name: AmnioFix (dHACM sheet) and AmnioCord (dehydrated umbilical cord)
ownership_history: MiMedx Group (Marietta, GA); AmnioFix sold since about 2011 (sheet). AmnioCord is the surgical umbilical-cord sheet sold alongside it.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)
on_label_indications: Homologous use as a barrier, covering or wrap at a surgical site (FDA's 2017/2020 guidance: sheet amniotic membrane used as a barrier or covering is generally a 361 HCT/P). MiMedx positions its Surgical line for 'lower extremity repair, plastic and reconstructive surgery, vascular procedures, and multiple orthopedic repairs'.

evidence.title: Prospective trial of non-healing DFUs treated with standard care with or without BR-AC

applications.caveats: Barrier only.

applications.caveats: Press-release data only.

evidence.title: Single layer placental-based allograft plus SOC vs SOC (DFU)

name: BioSphere Putty, BioSphere MIS and BioSphere Flex (spherical bioactive glass)
ownership_history: Privately held, Wayne, PA; founded 2011; no acquirer found.
