name: CopiOs Bone Void Filler (sponge and paste)
ownership_history: Originated at Centerpulse Spine-Tech (2004 clearance); Kensey Nash Corp. (2007 clearances), then DSM Biomedical after DSM bought Kensey Nash (2012); a ZimVie-domain CopiOs product page surfaced in search results but returned 404 when fetched on 2026-10-23. Zimmer Biomet to ZimVie to Highridge Medical chain is not sourced.
composition: Collagen-ceramic composite: resorbable sponges or compressed-powder discs of calcium phosphate and Type I bovine dermal collagen; the paste is made by mixing with autologous blood products.

regulatory.reference: K071237 (June 2007) and K072384 (modification, September 2007); the product-code listing also shows K033679 (2004, Centerpulse Spine-Tech, 'Copsios')
on_label_indications: Used in combination with autologous blood products such as bone marrow, for filling bone voids or gaps of the skeletal system (extremities, pelvis, spine) not intrinsic to the stability of the bone structure
Voids may be from trauma or surgeon-created; packed gently into the void and resorbs during healing

challenge: Current owner and whether the product is still sold are unverified; ownership chain is inferred from search snippets.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: CopiOs posterolateral fusion; CopiOs bone void filler spine).
applications.caveats: Label lists spine; a PubMed hit for 'CopiOs' returned only an unrelated cell-based combination paper.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: CopiOs tibial plateau; CopiOs bone void filler extremities).
applications.caveats: Label lists extremities.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: The ZimVie CopiOs page returned 404 on 2026-10-23 and Highridge's site lists no CopiOs; current seller unknown.

name: IsoTis Mozaik / OsteoStrux / Collage osteoconductive scaffold (putty and strip)
ownership_history: IsoTis Orthobiologics originated the Mozaik line; Integra LifeSciences held the 2006 to 2014 clearances; SeaSpine acquired Integra's US spine business (2015) and merged with Orthofix in January 2023. Dates beyond the Orthofix merger not re-sourced.
composition: Collagen-ceramic matrix: about 80% beta-TCP and 20% Type I collagen, 60 to 80% porosity (per Orthofix product pages).

regulatory.reference: K141841 (Integra Mozaik Strip, Aug 2014); K062353 (Mozaik putty, Dec 2006); K063124 (strips, 2007); K091302 (moldable morsels, 2009). No 510(k) under the names OsteoStrux or Collage was found in openFDA.
on_label_indications: Integra MOZAIK Strip (K141841): bone void filler for voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'in the extremities, spine, and pelvis' not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; also surgically treated osseous or traumatic defects; resorbed and replaced with bone
The mapping of OsteoStrux and Collage names to these clearances is not sourced

challenge: OsteoStrux and Collage are listed with the same composition as Mozaik but no 510(k) under those names was found; do not state they share a clearance.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Mozaik OR OsteoStrux collagen beta-TCP posterolateral fusion).
applications.caveats: A SeaSpine brochure cites a retrospective posterolateral fusion study with 90% fusion; it is not in PubMed and was not found, so it is not graded.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Mozaik OR OsteoStrux tibial plateau).
applications.caveats: Extremities named in the label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Mozaik OR OsteoStrux pelvis).
applications.caveats: Pelvis named in the label.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Older Orthofix collagen-ceramic family sold under several names; same composition shown for Mozaik, OsteoStrux and Collage.

name: MBCP / MBCP+ (biphasic calcium phosphate)
ownership_history: Biomatlante SA (Vigneux-de-Bretagne, France) was bought by Advanced Medical Solutions Group plc in December 2019 for about 8 million euros plus up to 0.3 million euros in milestones (AMS announcement). The 510(k) holder remains Biomatlante.
composition: Macroporous biphasic calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite plus beta-TCP) granules, blocks and shaped pieces; MBCP+ and a putty form exist.

on_label_indications: MBCP (K032268): bone void filler for bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities, spine and pelvis' not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; a filler without initial mechanical properties, so rigid fixation is often recommended
Contraindications in the 2003 form include osteomyelitis, implantation in necrotic sites, degenerative bone disease and intra-articular implantation
MBCP+ (K063527): same void-filler indication, extremities, spine and pelvis

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: MBCP biphasic calcium phosphate tibial plateau OR fracture OR osteotomy). Biomatlante registered two small pilot trials (NCT00206791, n=3; NCT00289575 in femoral head osteonecrosis, n=12, status unknown) without published results.
applications.caveats: Label requires rigid fixation; sales are mainly European.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: MBCP posterolateral fusion; MBCP spine).
applications.caveats: Label names spine; European spine use in cages and putty is reported by the company, not located in PubMed.

applications.evidence_summary: Registered pilot (NCT00289575, n=12) but no published results; the 2003 label lists implantation in necrotic sites as a contraindication.
applications.caveats: Label conflict.
applications.challenge: The cleared label's contraindication for necrotic sites sits awkwardly with an osteonecrosis use.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: AMS said sales were mainly European (about 4 million euros of biosurgical sales in 2018). US commercial presence is unverified; no US distributor was identified.

name: MagnetOs (Granules, Putty, Easypack Putty, Flex Matrix)
ownership_history: Technology from Xpand Biotechnology (Netherlands; AttraX predicate); Kuros Biosciences (SIX: KURN) acquired Xpand in 2016. Kuros remains independent; On 2025-01-07 Kuros Biosciences USA, Inc. announced a five-year exclusive sales agency agreement under which Medtronic's spinal division acts as exclusive sales agent for MagnetOs in mutually agreed US spine territories, converting an earlier trial arrangement into a strategic alliance. Per the Kuros investor release as summarized by search (the IR page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; the structure and term are mirrored by BoneZone and Medical Design & Development), Kuros keeps contracts, hospital partnerships and revenue recognition and may sell directly in non-contracted territories and non-spine markets. No financial terms were disclosed. No Globus Medical acquisition occurred (Globus's 2025 deal was Nevro).
composition: Biphasic calcium phosphate (65-70% beta-TCP / 30-35% hydroxyapatite) with a submicron, needle-shaped surface topography ('NeedleGrip'); Putty/Easypack add a resorbable polymer binder; Flex Matrix is a collagen-based strip

regulatory.reference: openFDA (FDA 510(k) database) MagnetOs entries: K161859 (MagnetOs, Xpand Biotechnology BV, 2017-02-24); K171563 (Putty, 2017-08-24); K181958 (Putty, 2018-12-06); K211201 (Easypack Putty, 2021-09-02); K213111 (Granules, 2022-01-10); K213959 (Flex Matrix, 2022-04-14); K230736 (Putty, 2023-12-20); K233245 (Flex Matrix, 2023-11-21); K233607 (Easypack Putty, 2023-12-15); K232347 (Granules, 2024-01-19); K240442 (Putty, 2024-04-01); K241212 (Easypack Putty, 2024-06-27); K243474 (MagnetOs MIS, 2025-05-23); applicant Kuros Biosciences B.V. (Xpand earlier). All product code MQV bone void fillers.; openFDA: K230736 (MagnetOs Putty, 2023-12-20); K233607 (Easypack Putty, 2023-12-15); K232347 (Granules, 2024-01-19); K240442 (Putty, 2024-04-01); K241212 (Easypack Putty, 2024-06-27); K243474 (MagnetOs MIS, 2025-05-23). Applicant Kuros Biosciences B.V.
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; posterolateral spine (extender and, for Granules/Putty, standalone); interbody use with a cleared cage (Easypack Putty, Granules, Flex Matrix). Not cleared as osteoinductive by FDA or TGA.

applications.evidence_summary: Dutch multicenter intra-patient RCT (Stempels 2024, NCT03625544, n=100, 128 segments): 1-year CT fusion 79% on the MagnetOs Granules side vs 47% on the autograft side, noninferior and indicating superiority. Ongoing: Easypack Putty standalone vs DBM+local bone (NCT04679844, n=60), Flex Matrix + local bone vs Trinity ELITE (NCT05037968, n=100), Flex Matrix vs cellular allograft observational (NCT06415123), Putty vs local autograft up to 3 levels (NCT04679896, n=30, completed).
applications.caveats: Investigator-sponsored with Kuros as collaborator; the surprisingly low autograft-side fusion (47%) is a per-side CT metric that makes the delta look larger than clinical nonunion rates; the osteoinductive mechanism (M2 macrophage polarization) is a company claim supported by preclinical work and is not an FDA-cleared claim.

applications.evidence_summary: Interbody clearance (2024) for Easypack Putty, Granules and Flex Matrix with cleared cages; no interbody clinical outcomes published.
applications.caveats: Interbody evidence gap; a single-arm LLIF study (NCT04128852) was withdrawn.

applications.evidence_summary: The MaxA RCT enrolled deformity and up-to-6-level constructs (T10-S2), so part of the evidence applies to longer fusions; a 140-patient adolescent idiopathic scoliosis intra-patient RCT (NCT07512336, UMC Utrecht) starts 2026.
applications.caveats: Subgroup data not published separately.

applications.evidence_summary: NCT07225751: prospective, randomized, single-blind, multicenter study of MagnetOs vs autogenous bone graft in hindfoot or ankle fusion, 126 patients, 7 sites, started 2025-11-25, primary completion October 2028. The first randomized autograft-controlled synthetic trial in the foot since Augment.
applications.caveats: No foot/ankle results yet; spine evidence is the basis for the claim.

applications.evidence_summary: Covered by the same trial (NCT07225751).
applications.caveats: As above.

evidence.title: Efficacy of biphasic calcium phosphate ceramic with a needle-shaped surface topography versus autograft in instrumented posterolateral spinal fusion
evidence.finding: Per-side 1-year CT fusion 79% MagnetOs vs 47% autograft (difference 32 points, 95% CI 23-41); noninferiority met.

evidence.title: MagnetOs Flex Matrix mixed with local autograft vs Trinity Elite mixed with local autograft in up to four-level instrumented PLF
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion December 2026; first head-to-head of a ceramic vs a cellular allograft.

evidence.title: MagnetOs Easypack Putty standalone vs DBX/Grafton mixed with local autograft in 1-2 level instrumented PLF
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion June 2027.

evidence.title: MagnetOs compared to autogenous bone graft in patients undergoing hindfoot or ankle fusions
evidence.finding: Recruiting; Kuros-sponsored.

evidence.title: Randomized intra-patient controlled trial of MagnetOs granules vs autograft in instrumented posterolateral spinal fusion
evidence.finding: Completed October 2023; spine.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs; no separate payment.
bd.notes: Kuros IR (Jan 7, 2025 release): five-year exclusive sales agency agreement under which Medtronic's spine division sells MagnetOs in mutually agreed US spine territories; Kuros supports Medtronic's sales force but keeps responsibility for contracts, hospital partnerships and revenue recognition, and continues to sell directly in non-contracted territories and outside spine; the deal converted an initial trial agreement. FY2025 (Mar 10, 2026 release): group revenue USD 146.1M (+72%), direct MagnetOs sales USD 143.9M (+71%), first net profit USD 2.6M, 2026 guidance at least 35% growth, 2028 target USD 300-330M; a 510(k) for the MagnetOs MIS Delivery System is cited without a date; the release states MagnetOs is not FDA cleared as an osteoinductive bone graft.

challenge: Medtronic agreement terms and FY2025 revenue (USD 146.1M; MagnetOs 143.9M) read from Kuros IR pages 2026-10-22. 510(k) numbers confirmed in openFDA (K230736, K233607, K232347, K240442, K241212, K243474). The 'osteoinductive' language is marketing; FDA cleared MagnetOs as an osteoconductive bone void filler.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Hindfoot/ankle RCT primary completion October 2028 (ClinicalTrials.gov); product is already marketable under 510(k), so the trial is for claims and adoption rather than approval.

name: Mastergraft (Granules, Matrix, Putty, Strip)
ownership_history: Medtronic Sofamor Danek original product line (first clearance 2002).
composition: Biphasic calcium phosphate (15% hydroxyapatite / 85% beta-TCP) granules; Matrix/Putty/Strip combine the ceramic with bovine type I collagen

on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure in the extremities, pelvis and posterolateral spine, as an autograft extender (per Mastergraft family labeling; verify form-specific wording)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed comparative clinical study of Mastergraft retrieved; it is the ceramic extender most often paired with Infuse in Medtronic constructs and is the ceramic component of the rhBMP-2/CRM (Amplify) carrier studied by Dimar 2009.
applications.caveats: Evidence gap for the standalone product.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Medtronic direct reps; frequently bundled with Infuse kits in pricing conversations.

name: NanoBone SBX Putty and NanoBone QD
ownership_history: Artoss GmbH (Rostock, Germany) developed NanoBone; Biocomposites Ltd acquired Artoss in June 2023 (company press release); Biocomposites is TA Associates-backed with Novo Holdings co-investing (see the Stimulan record).
composition: Phase-pure, non-sintered nanocrystalline hydroxyapatite embedded in a highly porous silica gel matrix, delivered as granulate in an aqueous gel (putty) in a syringe or cartridge applicator.

regulatory.reference: K250521 (NanoBone SBX Putty and QD, April 2025); K190110 (April 2019); K161351 (Oct 2016); K141189 (NanoBone granulate, Jan 2015)
on_label_indications: NanoBone SBX Putty and NanoBone QD (K250521): implant to fill bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities, posterolateral spine, intervertebral disc space, and pelvis' not intrinsic to stability; surgically created or traumatic; in intervertebral body fusion must be used with a cage cleared for a bone void filler

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: NanoBone SBX OR NanoBone lumbar posterolateral). Artoss registered a NanoBone vs local autograft study in 1 to 2 level PLF (NCT04615260, n=40 planned, active, no results) and a 330-patient spine registry (NCT04439032, completed primary Oct 2024, no results located).
applications.caveats: Dental NanoBone literature is extensive but not relevant to this label.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: NanoBone SBX interbody).
applications.caveats: On-label only with a cleared cage.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: NanoBone tibial plateau OR fracture).
applications.caveats: Extremities named.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Artoss Inc. ran the US spine registry; Biocomposites' US reach is via direct and distributor channels.

name: Opening-wedge osteotomy ceramic wedges (Arthrex HATriC, OSferion; Cross.Bone)
ownership_history: HATriC cleared to Arthrex 2004 (K040381); OSferion (Olympus Terumo Biomaterials beta-TCP) distributed by Arthrex as an osteotomy wedge; Cross.Bone wedge K071876.
composition: HATriC: 60% HA / 40% beta-TCP biphasic ceramic wedge; OSferion: 100% high-purity beta-TCP wedge

regulatory.reference: K040381 (HATriC, 2004-05-12); K071876 (Cross.Bone wedge, tibial osteotomy with internal fixation); OSferion wedge K number not retrieved
on_label_indications: Bone void filler or bone graft substitute in bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (extremities, pelvis, spine); not a load-bearing device; use with adequate post-operative immobilization (HATriC)

applications.evidence_summary: Beta-TCP and HA/TCP wedges fill large opening-wedge gaps with locking plates; meta-analyses show no overall nonunion difference vs no filler or graft, and a 2026 systematic review of 1,640 knees found no outcome benefit from any filler for gaps under 10 mm. A 2026 bilateral-knee RCT (n=42) found TCP granules gave better WOMAC/VAS than allograft.
applications.caveats: Clearance is for a void filler with a 'not load-bearing' statement, while the clinical use is structural gap support under a plate; cleared without clinical data.

evidence.title: The use of bone void fillers may not impact outcomes after medial opening wedge HTO: systematic review
evidence.finding: 28 studies; 36% allograft, 30% no filler, 22% synthetic, 12% autograft; no outcome difference; fillers may add complications for gaps under 10 mm.

evidence.title: Allogenous bone graft versus synthetic calcium-phosphate graft in opening wedge HTO
evidence.finding: 84 knees (bilateral), randomized by knee; TCP granules superior on WOMAC and VAS at 2.1 years; consolidation 54.8%; no loss of correction.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled inpatient MS-DRG or packaged into the outpatient osteotomy APC (HTO is increasingly outpatient).
bd.notes: Sold as a system accessory with Arthrex's osteotomy plates; evidence says the plate, not the wedge, is doing the work.

name: Osteopore PCL Scaffold Bone Filler (Osteoplug, Osteoplug-C, Osteomesh)
composition: 3D-printed bioresorbable polycaprolactone scaffold (mushroom-shaped 14 mm burr-hole plug, mesh sheets 50 x 50 x 1 mm) with 400 to 600 micron pores; resorbs over 18 to 24 months

regulatory.reference: K051093 (Osteopore, Inc., Osteopore PCL Scaffold, 2006-03-17, product code GXP)
on_label_indications: Repair of neurosurgical burr holes, craniotomy cuts and other cranial defects; augmentation or restoration of bony contour in the craniofacial skeleton

applications.evidence_summary: 12-patient Singapore series of Osteoplug after chronic subdural hematoma drainage: no depressions, no infection, osteointegration on CT at one year, mean 16 months follow-up.
applications.caveats: No comparative study; US sales small and through a non-exclusive distributor.

evidence.title: Use of Osteoplug polycaprolactone implants as novel burr-hole covers
evidence.finding: Good cosmesis in all 12 patients, radiographic osteointegration at one year, no infection or adverse systemic reaction at mean 16 months.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled.
bd.notes: Zimmer Biomet holds exclusive craniofacial distribution for EMEA and APAC (24 countries, signed July 2024, five-year term; sales began in Europe, Australia and Hong Kong, three-fold unit growth 2024 H2 to 2025 H1; Saudi access July 2026). US distribution is a separate, non-exclusive two-year agreement with Bioplate for cranial and neurosurgery (date unverified). The TnR clearance used Osteopore as predicate, so a second PCL entrant now competes in the same niche.

name: PRO-DENSE Bone Graft Substitute (and PRO-DENSE Core Decompression Kit, PRO-DENSE LoVisc)
ownership_history: Wright Medical Technology (Memphis/Arlington, TN); Stryker since November 2020.
composition: Injectable triphasic composite of calcium sulfate with brushite and beta-TCP granules (75% calcium sulfate / 25% calcium phosphate) that sets in situ; LoVisc is a lower-viscosity formulation (K200507 2020, K213342 2022).

on_label_indications: Bone graft substitute to be injected or digitally packed into open bone voids/gaps that are not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure, in the extremities, pelvis and spine
Core Decompression Procedure Kit cleared for delivery into the decompression tract

applications.evidence_summary: Civinini 2012 (37 hips, stages IC-IIIA): core decompression plus BMAC plus Pro-Dense backfill, 86.5% clinical success and 78% radiographic non-progression at a mean 20.6 months; no control arm.
applications.caveats: Single-center, short follow-up, combined with BMAC so the contribution of the filler cannot be isolated.

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for metaphyseal void fill; no femur-specific data located.
applications.caveats: Class-level use only.

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for metaphyseal trauma voids on the strength of a canine proximal humerus model and bone-tumor series; no plateau RCT; Wright's brochure itself states canine results may not translate to humans.
applications.caveats: Preclinical plus case-series evidence only for trauma.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as an injectable extender; no nonunion data found.
applications.caveats: Expert opinion.

applications.evidence_summary: Used for calcaneal cyst and post-reduction void fill; Stryker's efficacy claims come from a canine proximal-humerus defect model.
applications.caveats: No clinical foot/ankle series found.

evidence.title: The use of an injectable calcium sulphate/calcium phosphate bioceramic in the treatment of osteonecrosis of the femoral head.
evidence.finding: Harris hip score improved 68 to 86; 29 of 37 hips improved or did not collapse; 3 conversions to THA.

evidence.title: PRO-DENSE 510(k) K182823 summary
evidence.finding: Substantial equivalence with bench and animal data; indication expanded to pediatric patients 6 years and older.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in inpatient MS-DRG (core decompression of the hip is often inpatient or hospital outpatient; filler packaged into the APC).
bd.notes: The core decompression kit is a niche differentiated SKU: a dedicated 510(k) for a procedure where most competitors sell generic void fillers.

catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

name: Pro Osteon (200 / 200R / 500 / 500R coralline hydroxyapatite)
ownership_history: Developed by Interpore International (Irvine, CA); the Pro Osteon 500R 2007 summary names Biomet Osteobiologics; Zimmer Biomet since the 2015 Zimmer-Biomet merger. Acquisition dates not re-sourced.
composition: Coral-derived porous hydroxyapatite blocks and granules (the Interpore coralline line): Pro Osteon 200 is coral converted to hydroxyapatite; Pro Osteon 500/500R is a coral-carbonate skeleton with a thin calcium phosphate surface layer that resorbs faster (composition per a 2019 marine-materials review; not re-checked against the IFU).

regulatory.reference: K063346 (Pro Osteon 500R, expanded indications, April 2007); earlier K980817 and K990131 (500R), K000515 (200R), K004003 (200R with calcium sulfate)
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure, gently packed into the skeletal system 'extremities, spine and pelvis' (K063346)
Surgically created or traumatic osseous defects; may be combined with autogenous bone marrow aspirate, autogenous blood or sterile fluids
A secondary IFU listing reports contraindications for growth-plate fractures, segmental defects and infected sites (IFU not read in full)

applications.evidence_summary: Bucholz 1989 (PMID 2537166): metaphyseal defects in 40 displaced tibial plateau fractures were filled with cancellous autograft or interporous hydroxyapatite (the Interpore 200 material that became Pro Osteon); no significant radiographic or clinical difference at 15 to 34 months. A 2013 review of tibial plateau graft substitutes (PMID 23351879) found hydroxyapatite step-off at follow-up of 2 mm or more in 5.4%.
applications.caveats: Allocation method is not stated and follow-up differed (15.4 vs 34.5 months); 1989 fixation and imaging standards; the product tested is the older Interpore 200, not the 2007 500R label.

applications.evidence_summary: Interpore coralline hydroxyapatite mixed about 70/30 with iliac autograft in 27 consecutive adolescent idiopathic scoliosis posterior fusions: all achieved solid fusion at 27 months average (PMID 12401014).
applications.caveats: Single-center case series without a control; 2002; coral material from the Interpore era.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Pro Osteon lumbar posterolateral fusion; coralline hydroxyapatite spine fusion).
applications.caveats: Label covers spine; Zimmer Biomet registered an observational Pro Osteon study (NCT00858598) that was withdrawn with zero enrollment.

evidence.title: Interporous hydroxyapatite as a bone graft substitute in tibial plateau fractures
evidence.finding: Metaphyseal defects filled with interporous hydroxyapatite or cancellous autograft showed no significant difference in radiographic or clinical results.

evidence.title: Supplementation of autogenous bone graft with coralline hydroxyapatite in posterior spine fusion for idiopathic adolescent scoliosis
evidence.finding: All 27 patients had solid fusion at an average 27 months using coralline hydroxyapatite mixed with limited iliac autograft.

evidence.title: Use of bone graft substitutes in the management of tibial plateau fractures
evidence.finding: Systematic review reports hydroxyapatite and calcium phosphate cement substitutes with low rates of secondary articular depression and no good-quality RCTs for graft substitutes.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Mature, low-visibility line in the Zimmer Biomet biologics catalog; presence in the current catalog was not confirmed on a company page (GUDID lists device identifiers). Coral-derived raw material is a supply and diligence topic.

name: Vitoss / Vitoss BA / Vitoss BA2X (beta-TCP with bioactive glass)
ownership_history: Orthovita (Malvern, PA) launched Vitoss in 2000; Stryker completed its acquisition of Orthovita on 2011-06-28 (tender offer at $3.85 per share, agreement dated 2011-05-16, about $316 million).
composition: Ultraporous beta-tricalcium phosphate (nanoscale pores, ~90% porosity) with bovine collagen in Foam/Flow forms; Vitoss BA and BA2X add 45S5 bioactive glass (20% and 2x that amount) to the collagen-TCP composite

regulatory.reference: K083033 (Vitoss, 2008-11-06); K103173 (Vitoss BA BiModal, 2011-02-07); K153608 (BiModal foam strip, 2016-02-12); K163621 (Vitoss BA Injectable, 2017-05-02); K242280 (BiModal foam strip, 2024-08-29); K261008 (BiModal family, 2026-04-24); applicant Orthovita / Stryker Spine; K102545 is a special 510(k) for a Vitoss formulation; openFDA: K083033 (Vitoss BGS and Foam, Orthovita, 2008-11-06); K103173 (Vitoss BA BiModal, 2011-02-07); K153608 (2016); K163621 (Vitoss BA Injectable, 2017-05-02); K242280 (Vitoss family incl. BBTrauma and BA2X, Stryker Spine, 2024-08-29); K261008 (Vitoss family, Stryker Spine, 2026-04-24)
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure in the extremities, pelvis and posterolateral spine; posterolateral spine use as an autograft extender (typical Vitoss labeling; verify)

applications.evidence_summary: Single-surgeon prospective series with lamina autograft/Vitoss: 100 instrumented PLFs with 3.8% (one-level) and 9.5% (two-level) pseudarthrosis by CT (Epstein 2009); 60 noninstrumented geriatric PLFs with 15% pseudarthrosis (Epstein 2008); 40 instrumented PLFs with 3 pseudarthroses (Epstein 2006). A Chinese RCT of generic beta-TCP + local bone vs ICBG (Dai 2008, n=62) found 100% fusion in both arms.
applications.caveats: No RCT of the Vitoss brand; the Dai RCT used a beta-TCP whose brand is not stated in the abstract; Vitoss BA bioactive glass versions have no published spine RCT.

applications.evidence_summary: Ceramic extenders such as Vitoss are routinely mixed with rhBMP-2 in long constructs; no deformity-specific trial retrieved.
applications.caveats: Practice-pattern inference.

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for trauma voids (BBTrauma); evidence is class-level from plateau meta-analyses of synthetic fillers versus autograft; no Vitoss-specific RCT in trauma found.
applications.caveats: Non-structural foam; surgeons often pair it with a cement or hardware raft for plateau depression.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as an autograft extender in nonunion and Masquelet second stage; no comparative trauma data found.
applications.caveats: Expert-opinion level.

applications.evidence_summary: Class-level: Lee 2023 (PMID 38018529) retrospective comparison of highly porous beta-TCP plus BMAC vs no graft in midfoot arthrodesis, 44 patients/89 joints; union 91.5% vs 76.2% (p=0.048).
applications.caveats: Brand not stated; BMAC confounds; midfoot arthrodesis for arthritis and deformity, not all Charcot.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a void filler under the reduced posterior facet; no Vitoss-specific calcaneal series found.
applications.caveats: Granular TCP does not provide the immediate structural support a setting cement does.

applications.evidence_summary: Class evidence only: granular beta-TCP added nothing to angle-stable plating in a 39-patient RCT (Jakubietz 2011, PMID:21600042). No Vitoss-specific wrist trial found.
applications.caveats: Negative class-level result.

applications.evidence_summary: Synthetic void fill for the metaphyseal defect is described in the augmentation literature (Biermann 2019) without Vitoss-specific outcomes.
applications.caveats: No product data.

evidence.title: Beta tricalcium phosphate: observation of use in 100 posterolateral lumbar instrumented fusions
evidence.finding: Pseudarthrosis 3.8% (one-level) and 9.5% (two-level) with lamina autograft/Vitoss by dynamic X-ray and CT.

evidence.title: Noninstrumented posterolateral lumbar fusions in predominantly geriatric patients using lamina autograft and beta tricalcium phosphate
evidence.finding: 15% pseudarthrosis in noninstrumented 1-2 level fusions with Vitoss strips soaked in marrow aspirate.

evidence.title: Single-level instrumented posterolateral fusion of lumbar spine with beta-tricalcium phosphate versus autograft: a prospective, randomized study with 3-year follow-up
evidence.finding: 100% radiographic fusion in both beta-TCP + local bone and ICBG arms; all ICBG patients had donor-site pain.

evidence.title: Surgical fixation methods for tibial plateau fractures (Cochrane review)
evidence.finding: Six trials (368 participants) compared bone substitute vs autograft; all small and at high risk of bias; insufficient evidence to pick the best void filler.

evidence.title: The efficiency of highly porous beta-tricalcium phosphate with bone marrow aspirate concentrate in midfoot joint arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Union 91.5% with beta-TCP plus BMAC vs 76.2% without.

evidence.title: Midfoot joint arthrodesis using compression plate with lag screw augmenting with highly porous beta-TCP and BMAC
evidence.finding: 97.3% joint union (73 of 75 joints).

evidence.title: The use of beta-tricalcium phosphate bone graft substitute in dorsally plated, comminuted distal radius fractures
evidence.finding: No advantage of granular beta-TCP with angle-stable plating.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Stryker Spine direct reps; Stryker's biologics bag also includes Bio4 (Osiris/Smith+Nephew manufactured) and Cortoss for VCF.

challenge: Vitoss, Vitoss BA and BA2X are current on Stryker's catalog page (2026-10-22); K numbers still not retrieved (FDA 510(k) search is bot-gated).
catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

name: chronOS beta-TCP (granules, blocks, Strip, Vivify)
ownership_history: Developed by Synthes/Mathys (Switzerland); Synthes acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2012 and merged into DePuy Synthes.
composition: Pure-phase beta-tricalcium phosphate, 60% porosity with interconnected 100-500 micron pores; chronOS Strip combines beta-TCP granules with a polylactide-co-caprolactone polymer; chronOS Vivify adds collagen

regulatory.reference: K013072 (chronOS TCP, 2002-11-26); K041350 (chronOS, 2004-07-08); K043045 (chronOS, 2005-01-07; may be combined with autogenous blood/marrow); K053022 (chronOS beta-TCP, 2006-01-23); K071046 (chronOS Composite, 2007-10-23); applicant Synthes (USA)
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps that are not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; gently packed into bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system (extremities, spine and pelvis); may be combined with autogenous blood and/or bone marrow (K043045)

applications.evidence_summary: The best RCT for beta-TCP as a local-bone extender in instrumented PLF (Dai 2008, n=62) showed 100% fusion in both the beta-TCP and ICBG arms at 3 years with no donor-site pain in the TCP arm; brand of beta-TCP not specified in the abstract.
applications.caveats: Small single-center RCT, fusion by plain radiograph; the K013072 label does not say 'posterolateral' explicitly.

applications.evidence_summary: Beta-TCP granules are among the synthetic fillers pooled in plateau meta-analyses (Cooper 2022: 6 RCTs, 353 fractures, synthetics equal to autograft on depression with less blood loss and shorter surgery); no chronOS-specific plateau RCT found.
applications.caveats: Class-level evidence; granular TCP offers less immediate structural support than cement.

applications.evidence_summary: Beta-TCP wedges and granules are the most studied synthetic HTO fillers (Bei 2022 meta-analysis: 5 RCTs, 8 NRS, 769 patients; no difference in nonunion overall but higher nonunion when combined with long locking plates). chronOS wedge is sold ex-US; US HTO wedges with 510(k) are Arthrex HATriC and OSferion.
applications.caveats: chronOS HTO wedge US clearance not confirmed; evidence is class-level.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a resorbable void filler after calcaneal and tibial-plateau reduction; no chronOS-specific calcaneal outcome study found.
applications.caveats: Evidence gap.

applications.evidence_summary: Preformed beta-TCP wedges are one option for Cotton and Evans opening-wedge osteotomies.
applications.caveats: No comparative data.

applications.evidence_summary: Granular beta-TCP added to dorsal angle-stable plating gave no functional, radiographic or complication difference in a 39-patient RCT (Jakubietz 2011, PMID:21600042).
applications.caveats: Small, dorsal plating (now uncommon); negative result.

applications.evidence_summary: Synthetic void fillers appear in the augmentation systematic review (Biermann 2019, PMID:30903343) with level II-IV clinical data; the 2026 RCT meta-analysis found synthetic graft reduced complications but, unlike biologic graft, did not shorten healing time or reduce pain (Daher 2026, PMID:42750779).
applications.caveats: Product-specific proximal humerus data for chronOS not found.

applications.evidence_summary: Cleared for craniofacial defects and craniotomy openings to 25 cm2 on substantial equivalence; no chronOS-named cranial clinical series located.
applications.caveats: Granular beta-TCP lacks the cohesion of a cement and needs containment.

applications.evidence_summary: Dental 510(k) with no clinical data; beta-TCP in sinus lifts is supported by generic beta-TCP literature rather than chronOS trials.
applications.caveats: Commodity.

applications.evidence_summary: A 2023 systematic review of beta-TCP as alveolar cleft graft found only small series and no RCT against iliac crest.
applications.caveats: Off-label in children; no brand-specific data.

evidence.title: Single-level instrumented posterolateral fusion with beta-tricalcium phosphate versus autograft: prospective randomized study, 3-year follow-up
evidence.finding: Equivalent fusion and outcomes; eliminated iliac crest harvest morbidity.

evidence.title: Autologous versus synthetic bone grafts for the surgical management of tibial plateau fractures: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: Six RCTs; no significant difference in articular depression; synthetic grafts had 90 mL less blood loss and 16 min shorter surgery; other outcomes comparable.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of bone substitute materials in opening wedge high tibial osteotomy: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Bone substitutes safe for gaps over 10 mm with locking plates; no overall nonunion difference; low-quality evidence.

evidence.title: The use of beta-tricalcium phosphate bone graft substitute in dorsally plated, comminuted distal radius fractures
evidence.finding: No advantage of additional granular bone graft substitute with angle-stable plating.

evidence.title: Bone graft augmentation reduces complications in osteosynthesis of proximal humerus fractures: a meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: Five RCTs; graft augmentation lowered complication odds (OR 0.21); synthetic subgroup did not improve healing time or pain.

evidence.title: Beta-tricalcium phosphate as alveolar bone grafting in cleft lip and palate: systematic review
evidence.finding: Small heterogeneous studies; beta-TCP alone or with autograft produced bone fill but without controlled comparison to iliac crest.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: DePuy Synthes direct force; the company's spine biologics bag is DBX (MTF), ViviGen (LifeNet), chronOS and FIBERGRAFT (Prosidyan, promoted under an exclusive US agreement since 2018).

name: Durolane (stabilized hyaluronic acid, single injection)
ownership_history: PMA P170007 is held by Bioventus LLC (approved 2017-08-29). Durolane originated as NASHA (non-animal stabilized hyaluronic acid) developed in Sweden; the chain of owners before Bioventus was not re-sourced.
composition: NASHA: non-animal, stabilized (cross-linked) hyaluronic acid made by bacterial fermentation; single intra-articular injection.

on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative nonpharmacological therapy or simple analgesics, e.g., acetaminophen

applications.evidence_summary: The two published saline-controlled NASHA RCTs missed their primary endpoints: Altman 2004 (n=346) showed no overall difference from placebo, and Arden 2014 (n=218) found no difference at 6 weeks in the primary analysis, with only a post-hoc benefit in patients without effusion.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Both pivotal-type trials failed their primary analysis; the FDA decision rested on the PMA file, which was not read here.
applications.challenge: Be ready to explain how a single-injection HA with two missed primary endpoints in the literature won a 2017 PMA and a UnitedHealthcare preferred slot.

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of a single intra-articular injection of non-animal stabilized hyaluronic acid (NASHA) in patients with osteoarthritis of the knee (Altman, Osteoarthritis Cartilage)
evidence.finding: NASHA was not superior to placebo for the primary efficacy analysis; patients whose OA was confined to the knee showed significant benefit.

evidence.title: A randomized saline-controlled trial of NASHA hyaluronic acid for knee osteoarthritis (Arden, Curr Med Res Opin)
evidence.finding: No significant difference in 6-week responder rate (about 30.6% NASHA vs 26% saline) in the main analysis; post-hoc benefit in patients without clinical effusion.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Medicare Part B with HCPCS J7318 (per 1 mg); Bioventus FY2025 10-K says Durolane, Gelsyn-3 and Supartz FX are reimbursed under Part B and that CMS pricing changes lowered Durolane and Gelsyn-3 rates from July 2022. UnitedHealthcare commercial/exchange 2026-10-01 policy covers Durolane after criteria (preferred).
bd.notes: Bioventus reported HA products as 49% of 2025 revenue (46% in 2024, 43% in 2023) and flags in risk factors that FDA reclassifying HA from device to drug, or CMS policy shifts, could hit that portfolio.

name: Euflexxa (1% sodium hyaluronate)
ownership_history: PMA approved 2004-12-03 under the name Nuflexxa/NUXFLEXXA, renamed Euflexxa by supplement S002 (2005-10-20); sponsor Ferring Pharmaceuticals Inc. throughout in openFDA.
composition: 1% non-cross-linked sodium hyaluronate made by bacterial fermentation (non-avian, 'BioHA'); 3 weekly injections.

regulatory.reference: P010029 (original approval 2004-12-03; most recent supplement S040 on 2024-09-23)
on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative nonpharmacologic therapy and to simple analgesics (e.g., acetaminophen)

applications.evidence_summary: Altman 2009 (n=588): 3 weekly Euflexxa injections lowered VAS pain by 25.7 mm versus a smaller fall with saline at 26 weeks, a statistically significant but modest difference; an Actavis/Teva-sponsored RCT of a generic hyaluronate (n=599) also had a Euflexxa arm that beat vehicle.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Pivotal RCT sponsor (Ferring) not confirmed in the abstract; the Actavis trial was a competitor's equivalence study with Euflexxa as the active reference.

evidence.title: A double-blind, randomized, saline-controlled study of the efficacy and safety of EUFLEXXA for treatment of painful osteoarthritis of the knee, with an open-label safety extension (the FLEXX trial) (Altman, Semin Arthritis Rheum)
evidence.finding: At 26 weeks Euflexxa produced a larger VAS pain reduction than saline (25.7 mm vs a smaller change in the saline arm) and better function and quality-of-life scores.

evidence.title: Safety and efficacy of retreatment with a bioengineered hyaluronate for painful osteoarthritis of the knee: results of the open-label Extension Study of the FLEXX Trial (Altman, Osteoarthritis Cartilage)
evidence.finding: Open-label retreatment extension of FLEXX; supports tolerability of a repeat course but has no control group.

evidence.title: Double-blind randomized study of a generic hyaluronate injectable viscosupplement vs Euflexxa vs vehicle (Actavis)
evidence.finding: Registry results: WOMAC pain change at week 26 of -54.49 with Euflexxa versus -36.86 with vehicle (units as posted); the generic arm was -51.43.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill, HCPCS J7323 per dose. UnitedHealthcare commercial/exchange policy effective 2026-10-01 covers Euflexxa after criteria (with Durolane and Gelsyn-3); no prior authorization required.
bd.notes: Euflexxa is one of three UnitedHealthcare-preferred products in the 2026 policy, which is a contracting win; Ferring is private.

name: Gel-One (cross-linked hyaluronate, Gel-200)
ownership_history: PMA P080020 held by Seikagaku Corp. (approved 2011-03-22). Zimmer Biomet is reported (trade press, undated, 2012-2013 start) to be the exclusive US distributor; current term not located.
composition: Cross-linked hyaluronate derived from chicken combs (Gel-200 in the pivotal trial); single injection.

on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to non-pharmacologic therapy, NSAIDs or analgesics, e.g., acetaminophen

applications.evidence_summary: Strand 2012 (n=379, 2:1 vs phosphate-buffered saline): single-injection Gel-200 beat saline on WOMAC pain over 13 weeks, a short horizon; a retreatment safety analysis (Strand 2016) found no new signal.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Seikagaku authors, 13-week primary window only; 2015 label revision says effectiveness of repeat cycles has not been established.

evidence.title: A multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing a single intra-articular injection of Gel-200, a new cross-linked formulation of hyaluronic acid, to phosphate buffered saline for treatment of osteoarthritis of the knee (Strand, Osteoarthritis Cartilage)
evidence.finding: Significant WOMAC pain advantage for Gel-200 at week 13 and favored it at each visit; no related serious adverse events.

evidence.title: Evidence for safety of retreatment with a single intra-articular injection of Gel-200 for treatment of osteoarthritis of the knee from the double-blind pivotal and open-label retreatment trials (Strand, BMC Musculoskelet Disord)
evidence.finding: Retreatment analysis from pivotal and open-label extension data; supports safety of repeat injection, not efficacy.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill, HCPCS J7326 per dose. UnitedHealthcare 2026-10-01 policy: typically excluded.
bd.notes: Zimmer Biomet relationship carried forward in trade press; a Japanese Gel-One co-development deal (Ono) was announced August 2025 and does not affect US rights.

name: Gelsyn-3 (sodium hyaluronate 0.8%; originally Sinovial / Gel-Syn)
ownership_history: PMA holder is IBSA Institut Biochimique SA (P110005, approved 2014-05-09 as Sinovial/Gel-Syn, renamed GELSYN-3 by 2017); Bioventus markets Gelsyn-3 in the US per its FY2025 10-K. The exact IBSA-Bioventus license terms were not located.
composition: 0.8% non-cross-linked sodium hyaluronate from bacterial fermentation; 3 injections.

on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative nonpharmacologic therapy and simple analgesics (e.g., acetaminophen)

applications.evidence_summary: IBSA registered a 381-patient double-blind non-inferiority RCT of Sinovial versus Synvisc (NCT00556608); no published results or saline-controlled brand study were located, so the efficacy claim rests on the PMA file (not read).
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Active-comparator design only; no placebo arm found.

evidence.title: Efficacy evaluation of intra-articular hyaluronic acid (Sinovial) vs Synvisc in symptomatic knee osteoarthritis: double-blind, randomised non-inferiority study (IBSA)
evidence.finding: Registered active-comparator non-inferiority RCT; results not located in PubMed or the registry.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: HCPCS J7328 per 0.1 mg; Medicare Part B (Bioventus 10-K). UnitedHealthcare commercial/exchange 2026-10-01 policy covers Gelsyn-3 after criteria (preferred).
bd.notes: Bioventus competitors named in its 10-K: Ferring, Fidia, Johnson & Johnson, Zimmer Biomet, Arthrex, EmCyte and Channel-Markers Medical.

name: GenVisc 850 (sodium hyaluronate)
ownership_history: PMA P140005 held by Channel-Markers Medical, LLC (approved 2015-09-02); marketed by OrthogenRx. Ownership relationship between the two names not located.
composition: Avian-derived non-cross-linked sodium hyaluronate comparable to Supartz/Supartz FX; 3 to 5 injections.

on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative non-pharmacologic therapy and simple analgesics, e.g., acetaminophen

applications.evidence_summary: FDA approved GenVisc 850 on 'indistinguishable characteristics' with Supartz/Supartz FX: physical/chemical comparability, one GenVisc-vs-Supartz RCT and a Bayesian network meta-analysis showing non-inferiority to Supartz and superiority to saline (Doros 2016).
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Evidence is an indirect network meta-analysis authored with industry ties; a Journal of Rheumatology commentary disputing the ACR knee recommendation disclosed OrthogenRx funding (DOI 10.3899/jrheum.220125, from a search summary).
applications.challenge: The first 'equivalence' PMA route for a Class III device: know that it relied on a predicate-like HA and a network meta-analysis rather than a fresh placebo-controlled pivotal.

evidence.title: A method for establishing class III medical device equivalence: sodium hyaluronate (GenVisc 850) for the treatment of knee osteoarthritis (Doros, Med Devices)
evidence.finding: GenVisc 850 non-inferior to Supartz/Supartz FX and superior to saline in a Bayesian network meta-analysis; safety similar.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill, HCPCS J7320 (per mg). UnitedHealthcare 2026-10-01 policy: typically excluded.
bd.notes: OrthogenRx competes on price against Bioventus and Fidia; Bioventus names Channel-Markers Medical as a competitor.

name: Hyalgan (sodium hyaluronate)
ownership_history: PMA P950027 held by Fidia Farmaceutici S.P.A. (approved 1997-05-28). US sales historically ran through Sanofi (TREAD-20 trial is Sanofi-sponsored); current US entity is Fidia Pharma USA (Hymovis trial listing).
composition: Avian-derived (rooster comb) sodium hyaluronate initially; production switched to bacterial fermentation by supplement S009 (2008-05-01); 5 weekly injections.

on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative nonpharmacologic therapy and to simple analgesics, e.g., acetaminophen
regulatory.hcpcs: J7321 (Hyalgan, Supartz or Visco-3, per dose)

applications.evidence_summary: Altman 1998 (n=495): five weekly injections beat placebo on 50-foot-walk pain at 26 weeks by 8.8 mm (p<0.005), with 56% vs 41% reaching a >=20 mm sustained reduction.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA).

evidence.title: Intraarticular sodium hyaluronate (Hyalgan) in the treatment of patients with osteoarthritis of the knee: a randomized clinical trial (Hyalgan Study Group; Altman, J Rheumatol)
evidence.finding: Hyalgan improved walking pain 8.8 mm more than placebo at week 26; responders 56% vs 41%.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill, HCPCS J7321 per dose. UnitedHealthcare 2026-10-01 policy: typically excluded.
bd.notes: Five-injection regimen is the longest-course product in the class, a convenience disadvantage versus single-injection rivals.

name: Hyaluronic acid viscosupplements as a class: guidelines, Medicare and commercial coverage, OIG
ownership_history: FDA regulates intra-articular HA as a Class III device (product code MOZ, PMA); the Bioventus FY2025 10-K lists reclassification of HA from device to drug in the US as a business risk.
composition: Intra-articular hyaluronan or hylan products, cross-linked or not, avian or bacterial origin; courses of 1 to 5 injections.

on_label_indications: Knee osteoarthritis pain in patients who failed conservative nonpharmacologic therapy and simple analgesics; no HA PMA carries a hip, shoulder or ankle indication (Anika 10-K: labeling limits use to the knee exclusively)

applications.evidence_summary: Class evidence is a small average benefit over saline. Pereira BMJ 2022 (169 trials, n=21,163): pain SMD -0.08, about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale, with higher serious adverse event risk; Rutjes 2012 (89 trials, n=12,667): -0.11 in large blinded trials; Miller 2021 (35 RCTs, n=8,078, DePuy Synthes-affiliated) found no serious-AE difference. AAOS 2013 'strong' against, downgraded in the 2021 third edition to not recommended for routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against HA in the knee and strongly against in the hip.
applications.caveats: Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Payer behavior is outrunning the guideline: coverage now depends on brand contracts, not label.
applications.challenge: Know that the AAOS rating changed (2013 strong, 2021 moderate and 'not recommended for routine use') and that the ACR knee recommendation is conditional, not strong.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for osteoarthritis of the knee: a systematic review and meta-analysis (Rutjes, Ann Intern Med)
evidence.finding: 89 trials; overall effect size -0.37 for pain, but only -0.11 in 18 large blinded-assessment trials, which the authors judged clinically irrelevant; serious adverse event RR 1.41.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for the treatment of osteoarthritis of the knee (Bellamy, Cochrane)
evidence.finding: 76 RCTs of hyaluronan/hylan products of median quality score 3 of 5; Cochrane update that predates the larger-trial meta-analyses (full effect estimates not re-extracted here).

evidence.title: Safety of intra-articular hyaluronic acid for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials involving more than 8,000 patients (Miller, Cartilage)
evidence.finding: 35 RCTs vs saline: no difference in serious adverse events (1.8% vs 1.2%, RR 1.44, 95% CI 0.91-2.26) but more nonserious local reactions (14.5% vs 11.7%); the one safety analysis that argues against the BMJ serious-AE signal.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill under Medicare Part B and commercial medical benefit with HCPCS J7318-J7332 (descriptors per UnitedHealthcare policy 2026D0081M: J7318 Durolane 1 mg; J7320 GenVisc 850 1 mg; J7321 Hyalgan/Supartz/Visco-3 per dose; J7322 Hymovis 1 mg; J7323 Euflexxa per dose; J7324 Orthovisc per dose; J7325 Synvisc 1 mg; J7326 Gel-One per dose; J7327 Monovisc per dose; J7328 Gelsyn-3 0.1 mg; J7329 TriVisc 1 mg; J7331 SynoJoynt 1 mg; J7332 Triluron 1 mg). A third-party list shows J7333 for Visco-3, not reconciled.
bd.notes: MEDICARE: LCD L39260 (Palmetto GBA, JJ/JM, effective 2022-08-21) covers HA for knee OA with radiographic OA, 3 months of failed conservative therapy, failed or contraindicated steroid injection, dose and frequency per FDA label, repeat series no sooner than 6 months and only after response. Medicare Advantage step-therapy programs exist (UnitedHealthcare lists 'Medicare Part B Step Therapy Programs'; CVS Caremark Part B 2026 criteria exist). COMMERCIAL: UnitedHealthcare commercial and exchange policy 2026D0081M effective 2026-10-01 covers only Durolane, Euflexxa and Gelsyn-3 (criteria apply, no prior authorization) and treats Gel-One, GenVisc 850, Hyalgan, Hymovis/Hymovis One, Monovisc, Orthovisc, Supartz, SynoJoynt, Synvisc/Synvisc-One, Triluron, TriVisc and Visco-3 as typically excluded; the June 2024 version required a failed trial of Durolane, Gelsyn-3 or Euflexxa first (search summary). Aetna CPB 0179 covers knee OA only after non-drug therapy plus a 3-month analgesic/steroid trial and treats other joints as not medically necessary (aggregator summary, effective 2026-01-01, unverified). Blue plans: The Rheumatologist reported Blue Cross plans dropping or considering dropping coverage after the 2013 AAOS guideline (dated, unverified); no current Cigna or Blue policy was located. MEDICAID/OTHER: Nebraska Medicaid ended HA coverage for knee OA for dates of service from 2026-01-01; Washington L&I stopped covering HA in March 2024. OIG: work plan project A-07-24-00646 (announced 2024-08-15, active, estimated FY2026 completion) audits whether Medicare paid physicians for HA knee injections properly; no final OIG report exists yet. A 2023 JAMA Internal Medicine study (secondary summary) linked industry payments to HA injection rates. A Part B payment rate of average sales price plus 4.3% appears only in a secondary source (unverified).

name: Hymovis and Hymovis One (HYADD4 hyaluronan hydrogel)
ownership_history: PMA P150010 (Fidia; approved 2015-08-28). Hymovis One (single-injection label) was approved by supplement S005 on 2025-04-09.
composition: HYADD4: hexadecylamide derivative of hyaluronic acid, non-cross-linked, bacterial origin; Hymovis 2 injections one week apart, Hymovis One 1 injection.

regulatory.reference: P150010 (approved 2015-08-28; Hymovis One supplement S005 2025-04-09)
on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative non-pharmacologic therapy or simple analgesics (e.g., acetaminophen)
regulatory.hcpcs: J7322 (Hymovis or Hymovis One, per 1 mg)

applications.evidence_summary: Fidia registered an 800-patient double-blind RCT of Hymovis vs phosphate-buffered saline (NCT01372475) and a 332-patient single-injection HYADD4 study (NCT02187549); neither result set was located, so no brand-level effect estimate is quoted.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Registry-only; Hymovis One approval (2025) means the single-injection data post-date most reviews.

evidence.title: Hymovis versus placebo in knee osteoarthritis: multi-centre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study with open-label extension (Fidia)
evidence.finding: Completed sponsor RCT; results not located in PubMed or posted on the registry.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill, HCPCS J7322 (priced per mg). UnitedHealthcare 2026-10-01 policy: Hymovis and Hymovis One typically excluded.
bd.notes: Hymovis One in 2025 gives Fidia a single-injection answer to Durolane, Monovisc and Synvisc-One.

name: Monovisc (single-injection hyaluronan)
ownership_history: PMA P090031 held by Anika (approved 2014-02-25). US marketing is licensed to J&J MedTech: December 2011 license ran through December 2026, extended on 2025-10-16 to December 2031 (Anika FY2025 10-K). The 10-K also records J&J MedTech's October 2025 plan to divest its orthopaedics business, which would include these products.
composition: Lightly cross-linked sodium hyaluronate; single 4 mL intra-articular injection (volume per the Petterson RCT).

on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative non-pharmacologic therapy and to simple analgesics (e.g., acetaminophen)

applications.evidence_summary: Petterson 2019 (n=369): a single 4 mL Monovisc injection had a higher WOMAC pain success rate through 26 weeks than saline (p=0.043), a barely significant primary result.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Authors' funding not confirmed; Anika-sponsored per its PMA program. Monovisc was also the active reference arm in the Cingal trials.

evidence.title: Single intra-articular injection of lightly cross-linked hyaluronic acid reduces knee pain in symptomatic knee osteoarthritis: a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (Petterson and Plancher, Knee Surg Sports Traumatol Arthrosc)
evidence.finding: Success rate (>=50% and >=20 mm WOMAC pain improvement through week 26) was higher with Monovisc than saline, p=0.043.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill, HCPCS J7327 per dose; J&J MedTech sells and prices Monovisc in the US. Anika FY2025 10-K: J&J MedTech was 50% of Anika revenue; Anika says Monovisc and Orthovisc 'remain market leaders' despite pricing pressure and reduced market access. UnitedHealthcare 2026-10-01 policy: typically excluded.
bd.notes: Concentration risk for Anika: one licensee, one pending divestiture of that licensee's orthopaedics unit, and payer retrenchment.

name: Orthovisc (high molecular weight hyaluronan)
ownership_history: PMA P030019 (approved 2004-02-04) held by Anika. Switched to bacterial-fermentation hyaluronan by supplement S009 (2007-10-26). US marketing licensed to J&J MedTech since December 2003; extended most recently from August 2022 through December 2028 and extendable at J&J MedTech's option (Anika FY2025 10-K). A 2026-08-28 supplement (S028) moved manufacturing to single-use components.
composition: High molecular weight sodium hyaluronate from bacterial fermentation; 3 to 4 injections.

on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative non-pharmacologic therapy and to simple analgesics (e.g., acetaminophen)

applications.evidence_summary: Brandt 2001 (n=226): three weekly 30 mg injections beat saline on WOMAC pain over 27 weeks in the analysis population (patients with low contralateral-knee pain, a restricted subgroup).
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). The positive result is in a post-selected subgroup; Anika-affiliated author (Lavin) on the paper.

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of intraarticular sodium hyaluronate in knee osteoarthritis (ORTHOVISC Study Group; Brandt, Clin Orthop Relat Res)
evidence.finding: In patients completing 15 weeks with low contralateral-knee pain at baseline, hyaluronate improved WOMAC pain, global assessments and standing pain from weeks 7 to 27; 58% vs 40% reached >=5-unit pain improvement.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill, HCPCS J7324 per dose; J&J MedTech sells it. UnitedHealthcare 2026-10-01 policy: typically excluded. Anika 10-K flags a possible CMS change to the reimbursement classification of Orthovisc and Monovisc.
bd.notes: The Anika 10-K says labeling in the US limits both products to the knee exclusively. J&J MedTech's announced orthopaedics divestiture (October 2025) is the contract-continuity question to ask any Anika or DePuy contact.

name: Supartz FX and Visco-3 (sodium hyaluronate)
ownership_history: One PMA (P980044, Seikagaku Corp.) covers both brands: Supartz approved 2001-01-24, renamed Supartz FX by supplement S025 (2015-05-20), Visco-3 added by S027 (2015-12-21). Bioventus distributes Supartz FX (Bioventus/Seikagaku agreement reported extended through May 2028 by a trade-press snippet, not primary-sourced); Zimmer Biomet is reported to distribute Visco-3.
composition: Avian-derived (chicken comb) non-cross-linked sodium hyaluronate; Supartz FX 5 weekly injections, Visco-3 3 injections.

regulatory.reference: P980044 (Supartz 2001-01-24; Visco-3 supplement S027 2015-12-21)
on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative non-pharmacologic therapy and simple analgesics, e.g., acetaminophen
regulatory.course: Supartz FX: 5 injections (UnitedHealthcare lists 3 to 5); Visco-3: 3 injections
regulatory.hcpcs: J7321 (Hyalgan, Supartz or Visco-3, per dose) per UnitedHealthcare 2026 policy; one third-party listing shows a separate J7333 for Visco-3, which was not confirmed

applications.evidence_summary: Five Supartz-vs-saline RCTs (summarized in the GenVisc 850 equivalence paper, Doros 2016) underpin the label; individual trial results were not re-extracted, so the brand claim leans on class meta-analyses that show a small effect.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA).

evidence.title: A method for establishing class III medical device equivalence: sodium hyaluronate (GenVisc 850) for the treatment of knee osteoarthritis (Doros, Med Devices)
evidence.finding: Bayesian network meta-analysis of five Supartz/Supartz FX vs saline RCTs plus three GenVisc 850 studies found GenVisc 850 non-inferior to Supartz and superior to saline.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)
evidence.finding: 169 trials; in 24 large placebo-controlled trials (n=8,997) viscosupplementation lowered pain by SMD -0.08 (about 2 mm on a 100 mm scale), below the 0.37 SMD minimal important difference, with higher serious adverse event risk (RR 1.49) in 15 large trials; authors concluded the findings do not support broad use.

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill; HCPCS J7321 (per dose). Bioventus 10-K lists Supartz FX as a Part B reimbursed product. UnitedHealthcare commercial/exchange 2026-10-01 policy: Supartz and Visco-3 typically excluded.
bd.notes: Seikagaku is the manufacturer and PMA holder; US go-to-market is split across Bioventus (Supartz FX) and Zimmer Biomet (Visco-3, Gel-One) per trade-press snippets, so confirm current agreements before quoting a rep call.

name: Synvisc / Synvisc-One (hylan G-F 20)
ownership_history: PMA holder shown in openFDA as Sanofi Genzyme Corp. (Genzyme Biosurgery heritage); Sanofi US was still running a Synvisc-One specialty-pharmacy program page dated 01/2026. Earlier chain (Biomatrix, Genzyme, Wyeth ex-US/US rights) not re-sourced.
composition: Hylan G-F 20: cross-linked hyaluronan (hylan A and B) derived from avian (chicken comb) sources; Synvisc is 2 mL per injection for 3 injections, Synvisc-One is a single 6 mL injection.

regulatory.reference: P940015 (Synvisc approved 1997-08-08; Synvisc-One added by supplement S012 on 2009-02-26)
on_label_indications: Treatment of pain in osteoarthritis of the knee in patients who have failed to respond adequately to conservative nonpharmacologic therapy and to simple analgesics (e.g., acetaminophen)
regulatory.course: Synvisc: 3 injections one week apart; Synvisc-One: 1 injection (per FDA labeling summary in UnitedHealthcare policy 2026D0081M)

applications.evidence_summary: Chevalier 2010 (n=253): a single 6 mL hylan G-F 20 injection beat saline over 26 weeks on WOMAC A pain but the authors called the margin modest; class meta-analyses find a small, clinically irrelevant average effect.
applications.caveats: Class evidence is weak: Pereira BMJ 2022 and Rutjes 2012 found a clinically irrelevant average effect over saline; AAOS 2021 does not recommend routine use; ACR/AF 2019 conditionally recommends against in the knee. Label is knee-only: hip, shoulder, ankle, thumb CMC and TMJ use is off-label (no US labeling; ACR 2019 strongly recommends against HA in hip OA). Sponsor of the Chevalier RCT not confirmed from the abstract.

evidence.title: Single, intra-articular treatment with 6 ml hylan G-F 20 in patients with symptomatic primary osteoarthritis of the knee: a randomised, multicentre, double-blind, placebo controlled trial (Chevalier, Ann Rheum Dis)
evidence.finding: WOMAC A pain improved more with hylan G-F 20 than saline over 26 weeks; the authors describe the difference as modest.

evidence.title: Viscosupplementation for knee osteoarthritis: systematic review and meta-analysis (Pereira, BMJ)

bd.reimbursement: Buy-and-bill under Medicare Part B/commercial medical benefit with HCPCS J7325 (priced per mg). UnitedHealthcare commercial and exchange policy effective 2026-10-01 lists Synvisc/Synvisc-One as typically excluded (only Durolane, Euflexxa, Gelsyn-3 are covered after criteria).
bd.notes: A separate UnitedHealthcare Individual Exchange policy effective 2026-01-01 (from a search summary, not read) named Synvisc among the products it addressed; the combined policy effective 2026-10-01 treats it as typically excluded, so brand-level coverage is moving fast. Sanofi runs a specialty-pharmacy distribution program for Synvisc-One.

challenge: Synvisc is the category's original brand; a hiring manager will test whether you know the single-injection (Synvisc-One) and three-injection labels, that hip use is off-label, and that PMA supplements (not new PMAs) carried the product forward.

name: Induce XT (Natural Matrix Protein allograft)
ownership_history: Red Rock Regeneration (private); NMP technology also described in a 2026 preclinical paper (PMID 42774656) from an affiliated group.
composition: Human cortical bone fibers and microparticulates processed into Natural Matrix Protein (NMP, a growth-factor-bioavailability-enhanced demineralized allograft) with added cancellous microparticulates

regulatory.reference: No FDA clearance or approval record found: openFDA 510(k) search for applicant 'Red Rock' returns nothing, and no HCT/P determination is public. Product is a human cortical fiber/microparticulate allograft processed into Natural Matrix Protein (NMP); the prospective foot-and-ankle fusion study NCT06662266 (n=60, started May 2025, est. completion 2027-11) is registered as not an FDA-regulated device study.
on_label_indications: No FDA-reviewed indication; homologous bone-graft use (presumed)

applications.evidence_summary: NCT06662266: prospective single-site evaluation of Induce XT in 60 foot and ankle fusions, enrolling by invitation since May 2025, primary completion November 2026.
applications.caveats: Single-arm, single-site; preclinical claim that NMP releases more BMP-7 than conventional DBM comes from the developer.

evidence.title: Prospective evaluation of Induce XT bone graft in foot and ankle fusion
evidence.finding: Enrolling by invitation.

evidence.title: A novel growth factor bioavailability-enhanced allograft for use in craniomaxillofacial bone regeneration
evidence.finding: NMP released more BMP-7 than DBM and was osteoinductive in the rat muscle pouch; competitors OsteoAMP, OsteoFactor and i-FACTOR did not form bone.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Foot/ankle series readout after November 2026 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

bd.reimbursement: No separate payment; bundled or packaged.
bd.notes: Small-company entrant; relevance is as a signal that 'enhanced DBM' claims are being tested in the foot first because the fusion model is small and outpatient.

challenge: Regulatory pathway (510(k) vs 361) is unstated by the sponsor; no FDA record exists, so the atlas should show it as unclassified/investigational rather than as a 361 product.

name: Autologous 'stem cell' clinic treatments (culture-expanded MSCs and adipose SVF) for orthopedic conditions - class record
company: Numerous clinics and clinic networks (FDA actions name Regenerative Sciences, US Stem Cell Clinic, California Stem Cell Treatment Center / Cell Surgical Network, Celltex Therapeutics)
ownership_history: Not a product family; a class of practice. Point-of-care BMAC concentrated in the same procedure is a separate record (bmac); umbilical-cord, exosome and amniotic products are separate class records.
composition: The patient's own adipose stromal vascular fraction or bone-marrow/adipose MSCs, often culture-expanded off-site, injected into joints, discs, tendons or nonunions.

regulatory.reference: 351 HCT/Ps (more than minimally manipulated and/or non-homologous) that need an IND to study and a BLA to sell; none is licensed for any orthopedic indication. Courts have sided with FDA: US v. Regenerative Sciences (D.C. Cir. 2014; cultured autologous MSCs for orthopedic use are drugs/biologics), US v. US Stem Cell Clinic (11th Cir. 2021; SVF), and US v. California Stem Cell Treatment Center / Cell Surgical Network (9th Cir. 2024-09-27, reversing the district court; rehearing denied 2024-12-20; cert petition 24-1189 filed 2025-05-19, disposition not confirmed). FDA warning letter to Celltex dated 2012-09-24 (unlicensed biologic, more than minimally manipulated, CGMP failures). Celltex now registers trials under IND, e.g., knee OA Phase 2 NCT04448106 (status unknown). The 2014 and 2021 appellate citations were not read from primary court documents in this sweep.
on_label_indications: None. Not a choice outside an FDA-cleared IND.

challenge: A rep or distributor who supplies, labels or promotes these services can be treated as a manufacturer; the appellate record is uniformly in FDA's favor.

applications.evidence_summary: No controlled trial of any clinic's own product located; the regulated analog (JointStem, separate record) has a Korean Phase 3. Celltex's IND trial NCT04448106 (n=300 planned) has posted no results.
