applications.caveats: Clinic marketing claims are not evidence; outcomes are self-reported and unaudited.

applications.evidence_summary: No product-specific controlled study located for clinic-prepared cells (PubMed search 2026-10-23); the regulated disc programs are rexlemestrocel-L and IDCT (existing records).
applications.caveats: Unlicensed.

applications.evidence_summary: No product-specific controlled study located for clinic-prepared cells.
applications.caveats: Unlicensed.

applications.evidence_summary: No product-specific controlled study located; FDA's position is that culture-expanded cells for nonunion require an IND.
applications.caveats: Unlicensed.

evidence.title: Autologous Adipose Tissue-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells (AdMSCs) for Osteoarthritis (Celltex, Phase 2)
evidence.finding: Registry status unknown; no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered; cash-pay.
bd.notes: Compliance red flag. Hiring managers will ask how a rep separates legitimate same-day BMAC (device-processed, 361 exception debates aside) from culture-expanded cells and SVF.

name: BRTX-100 (autologous hypoxia-cultured bone marrow MSCs)
ownership_history: Nasdaq: BRTX; public offering (Form 424B4) in 2026.
composition: Autologous bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells culture-expanded under hypoxic conditions, single intradiscal injection in a carrier

regulatory.reference: IND; Fast Track designation for chronic lumbar disc disease (company). Separate IND cleared for chronic cervical discogenic pain (company boilerplate).

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2 (NCT04042844, n=99 planned, saline-controlled) remains blinded; company presented pooled blinded data at ISCT May 2026 showing 52% of 25 evaluable patients with at least 50% improvement in both VAS and ODI at 52 weeks and no dose-limiting toxicity.
applications.caveats: Blinded, pooled, company-reported interim data from 25 patients cannot show efficacy; no unblinded topline yet; evidence grade will be I only after unblinding of the randomized comparison.

evidence.title: Phase 2, double-blind, randomized, saline-controlled study of a single intradiscal injection of BRTX-100 in chronic lumbar disc disease
evidence.finding: Recruiting/enrolling at 19 sites since June 2022; primary completion Dec 2026; enrollment reported complete (trade press).

pipeline.expected_milestone: Unblinded topline analysis after primary completion (Dec 2026 per registry); company targets a Phase 3 IND submission in late 2026 after a February 2026 Type B meeting (company).

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational. Autologous manufacturing implies per-patient logistics cost.
bd.notes: Microcap sponsor; financing risk is the main schedule variable.

name: EpiBone-CMF (EB-CMF) engineered living bone graft
composition: Patient-specific, CT-shaped decellularized bone scaffold seeded with the patient's adipose-derived stem cells and matured in a perfusion bioreactor

regulatory.reference: IND cleared May 2019 for a Phase 1/2 first-in-human study (NCT03678467); no BLA

applications.evidence_summary: Open-label, single-arm, six-patient first-in-human study of EB-CMF for mandibular ramus reconstruction (three US sites) registered with a 2021 start and August 2023 primary completion; the record was last updated May 2022 with status unknown, and no results have been published or presented in sources located as of 2026-10-22.
applications.caveats: Autologous cell-based combination product under FDA's cellular therapy pathway; funding rounds (Hackensack Meridian 2020, NetScientific) but no clinical readout; treat as stalled until a status update appears.

evidence.title: Open-label first-in-human single intervention study of EpiBone-CMF engineered living bone graft for mandibular ramus reconstruction
evidence.finding: Phase 1/2, status unknown since May 2022; no results posted.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No public milestone; ClinicalTrials.gov status unknown (record last verified May 2022).

bd.reimbursement: n/a
bd.notes: Only US tissue-engineered mandible construct to reach an IND; related academic programs (axially vascularized ceramic in Alexandria NCT04001842; ovine patient-matched permanent scaffolds, Nat Commun 2025) remain preclinical or non-US.

name: IDCT (rebonuputemcel; Injectable Discogenic Cell Therapy)
ownership_history: Private (Salt Lake City). Co-founder/CEO Flagg Flanagan announced retirement Oct 5, 2026 after 18 years; successor not named in release.
composition: Allogeneic, manufactured progenitor cell population derived from donated adult human disc tissue, delivered in a viscous (sodium hyaluronate) carrier by single intradiscal injection

regulatory.reference: IND; RMAT and Fast Track designations (company). FDA accepted Phase 3 protocols and manufacturing plan July 2024 (company). Not approved anywhere.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 1/2 US trial (NCT03347708, n=60, 14 sites, saline- and vehicle-controlled) and a Japanese Phase 1/2 (NCT03955315, n=38, sham-controlled) completed Feb 2022; company reports favorable safety and pain/function signals. Pivotal Phase 3 DGX-A02 (NCT07254806, n=162, sham-controlled) dosing began Dec 2025/Jan 2026.
applications.caveats: Peer-reviewed publication of the Phase 1/2 efficacy data could not be located on PubMed during this review (unverified); early-phase trials were small; Phase 3 readout not before late 2027.

evidence.title: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle- and placebo-controlled Phase 1 of IDCT in single-level symptomatic lumbar disc degeneration (US)
evidence.finding: Completed (primary completion Feb 2022); 14 US sites; results not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov at review.

evidence.title: Randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled Phase 1/2 of IDCT in lumbar DDD (Japan)
evidence.finding: Completed Feb 2022; 6 sites.

evidence.title: DGX-A02: prospective, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, multicenter Phase 3 of IDCT in single-level mild-to-moderate lumbar disc degeneration
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 31 sites; started Dec 23, 2025; first patient treated Jan 2026; DSMB recommended continuation without modification June 9, 2026; primary completion Nov 2027 (52-week primary period, 104-week total).

pipeline.expected_milestone: Phase 3 primary completion Nov 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov); no company guidance on BLA timing.

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational.
bd.notes: Private company; leadership transition Oct 2026 framed as preparation for late-stage development and potential commercialization.

name: InGeneron Transpose RT System (point-of-care adipose-derived regenerative cell isolation) and SmartGraft
composition: Transpose RT is a benchtop device and enzymatic reagent kit that digests lipoaspirate to isolate fresh uncultured, unmodified adipose-derived regenerative cells (UA-ADRCs, stromal vascular fraction) in under about 90 minutes for same-day injection. SmartGraft 30 and 200 are separate fat-concentration devices cleared in 2014.

regulatory.reference: Transpose RT: no marketing authorization; used in IDE trials NCT03752827 (rotator cuff, 168 enrolled), NCT03513731 (facet OA, 40), NCT03503305 (wrist OA, 40). SmartGraft 30 (K141591, 2014-09-24) and SmartGraft 200 (K141713, 2014-10-28), product code MUU, cover fat transfer only.
on_label_indications: Transpose RT: none; investigational only. SmartGraft: concentrating adipose tissue for aesthetic body contouring and listed surgical specialties (not ADRC isolation). Enzymatic digestion makes the product a 351 drug under FDA's 2017/2020 guidance (US v. US Stem Cell Clinic, 11th Cir. 2021; US v. California Stem Cell Treatment Center, 9th Cir. 2024).

challenge: A pivotal-scale trial exists but results are unposted; the independent rotator cuff evidence is a 16-patient company-sponsored pilot.

applications.evidence_summary: First-in-human pilot RCT (Hurd 2020, 11 UA-ADRC vs 5 corticosteroid patients, mITT): ASES total significantly higher with cells at 24 and 52 weeks (p<0.05) in partial-thickness tears. Pivotal-scale IDE trial NCT03752827 (168 enrolled, active not recruiting) has no posted results.
applications.caveats: Company-sponsored, tiny n, injection into tendon not repair augmentation; company press releases overstate (not independently verified); 3.4-year follow-up reported by the company, not read here. Enzymatic SVF/ADRC isolation is a 351 drug per FDA's 2017 and 2020 guidance; not a 361-exempt point-of-care product.

evidence.title: Safety and efficacy of treating symptomatic, partial-thickness rotator cuff tears with fresh, uncultured, unmodified, autologous adipose-derived regenerative cells (UA-ADRCs) isolated at the point of care: a prospective, randomized, controlled first-in-human pilot study
evidence.finding: Pilot: 11 UA-ADRC vs 5 corticosteroid patients (mITT); ASES total higher with cells at 24 and 52 weeks (p<0.05); company-sponsored, tiny n.

evidence.title: Autologous Adult Adipose-Derived Regenerative Cell Injection Into Chronic Partial-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears
evidence.finding: InGeneron IDE trial vs corticosteroid, primary pain VAS; 168 enrolled, active not recruiting; no results posted as of 2026-10-23.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Pivotal rotator cuff trial active, not recruiting (168 enrolled); a BLA/IND pathway would be required for enzymatic SVF; no filing located.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable: investigational.
bd.notes: Enzymatic ADRC systems sit on the wrong side of the FDA 361/351 line unless approved as a drug; Ingeneron is the cleanest ortho example because it runs IDEs rather than selling.

name: Intradiscal / degenerative disc biologics (rexlemestrocel-L, IDCT, VIA Disc NP) - not fusion products
ownership_history: Mesoblast (ASX/NASDAQ: MESO), DiscGenics (private, Salt Lake City), VIVEX Biologics (private, Miami; VIA Disc NP is a 361 HCT/P nucleus pulposus allograft).
composition: Rexlemestrocel-L: allogeneic STRO-3+ mesenchymal precursor cells, 6 million cells with hyaluronic acid, single intradiscal injection. IDCT (rebonuputemcel): allogeneic discogenic progenitor cells in a viscous carrier. VIA Disc NP: processed allogeneic nucleus pulposus tissue reconstituted with saline.

regulatory.reference: Mesoblast: FDA IND, RMAT designation, BLA planned Q3 2027 after MSB-DR004 (NCT06325566). DiscGenics: Fast Track; phase 3 NCT07254806 started December 2025. VIVEX: VIA Disc NP marketed as a 361 HCT/P (not an approved therapy) while running an IND-stage RCT (NCT06778447).

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells with and without hyaluronic acid for chronic low back pain: randomized, double-blind, concurrent-controlled 36-month study (MSB-DR003)
evidence.finding: Primary composite responder endpoint at 12 and 24 months not met in all subjects; MPC+HA reduced LS-mean pain vs saline at 12 and 24 months, with larger effects in patients with CLBP under 68 months; no treatment-related SAEs.

evidence.title: Rexlemestrocel-L + HA vs saline in moderate to severe chronic low back pain (MSB-DR004)
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; primary completion July 2027; company guides top-line mid-2027 and BLA Q3 2027.

evidence.title: IDCT (rebonuputemcel) vs sham in single-level mild-to-moderate lumbar disc degeneration (phase 3)
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 31 sites; primary completion November 2027; follows completed phase 1/2 NCT03347708 (n=60).

evidence.title: Nucleus pulposus allograft (VIA Disc NP) vs sham for lumbar discogenic pain
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 19 sites; primary completion October 2027; the earlier VIA Disc NP registry (NCT04652687) was terminated and a 500-patient registry 3.0 (NCT06345690) is active.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Mesoblast BLA Q3 2027 if MSB-DR004 succeeds; DiscGenics and VIVEX phase 3 readouts late 2027

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable; VIA Disc NP is billed today as a 361 tissue product in office/ASC settings with no established coverage.
bd.notes: Included only as context: these are injectables aimed at avoiding fusion, not fusion biologics. The first MSB-DR003 phase 3 missed its primary endpoint, which is why Mesoblast is running a second phase 3; VIA Disc NP's commercialization under 361 while in an RCT is a regulatory grey zone FDA has scrutinized for other 'structural tissue' allografts.

name: JointStem (autologous adipose-derived MSCs, intra-articular, knee OA)
ownership_history: Nature Cell Co., Ltd. (Korea) with affiliate R-Bio (sponsor of the Korean trials). Korea's MFDS rejected the product license in April 2023 and again after the Korean Phase 3 (reported in Korean press); FDA granted RMAT (October 2024) and Breakthrough Therapy designation (March 2025), per company releases. Out of the bone scope; knee OA injection, recorded because the brief asked and flagged for the cartilage/injection slice.
composition: Autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells, culture-expanded, single intra-articular injection.

regulatory.reference: US IND (number not public). US Phase 2b/3a NCT04368806 (Nature Cell, n=173, active not recruiting, primary completion 2027-08-06). Company says it sought a pre-BLA meeting in 2026 on the strength of the Korean Phase 3; FDA position on that request not public. RMAT and Breakthrough designations are from company releases, not an FDA list.
on_label_indications: None in the US

applications.evidence_summary: Kim 2023 Korean Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (261 K-L grade 3 patients; 125 vs 127 analyzed; matches NCT03990805): 6-month VAS improvement 25.2 vs 15.5 mm (p=.004) and WOMAC 21.7 vs 14.3 (p=.002) favored ADMSC.
applications.caveats: Six-month primary endpoint; the paper does not name the product (attribution via the R-Bio registry record); Korea's regulator judged the effect not clinically meaningful and refused approval.
applications.challenge: Positive p-values but a regulator rejection on clinical meaningfulness; cite both.

evidence.title: Clinical efficacy and safety of the intra-articular injection of autologous adipose-derived MSCs for knee osteoarthritis: a Phase III, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
evidence.finding: VAS and WOMAC improved more than placebo at 6 months.

evidence.title: A Phase 3 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of JointStem in Treatment of Osteoarthritis (Korea)
evidence.finding: Completed 2020.

evidence.title: A Phase 2b/3a Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of JointStem in Patients Diagnosed as Knee Osteoarthritis (US)
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; primary completion 2027-08.

evidence.title: A Phase 2 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of JointStem in Treatment of Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Completed 2018; results posted.

pipeline.expected_milestone: US Phase 2b/3a primary completion 2027-08; company is pressing for a BLA path.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable in the US.
bd.notes: Autologous culture-expanded MSCs are exactly what US clinics sell without an IND; JointStem is the regulated version of that product.

name: NVD-003 (autologous adipose-derived osteogenic 3D graft)
ownership_history: Spun out of UCLouvain (2013); FDA Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations for congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (December 2020), RMAT designation, IND (March 2021); Phase 3 in CPT started September 2025.
composition: Autologous adipose-derived stem cells differentiated into a scaffold-free 3D osteogenic implant with HA/beta-TCP particles (3M3 platform); manufactured per patient

regulatory.reference: IND (2021); Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations (2020); RMAT; eligible for a priority review voucher if approved
on_label_indications: Investigational: congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (pediatric, Paley type 3-4 diaphyseal); recalcitrant lower-limb nonunion in adults

applications.evidence_summary: Adult phase 1/2 in recalcitrant lower-limb nonunion (NCT06335394, n=11 enrolled, company reported 9 treated): clinical healing in 8/9 at 2 years, median 6 months, no implant-related complications (company release, December 2022). Pediatric CPT Phase 3 vs ICBG (NCT07112443, n=12, 7 sites US/EU, primary completion October 2026) is recruiting.
applications.caveats: Tiny uncontrolled adult series; company-reported; the Phase 3 is powered as an orphan study (n=12). Manufacturing is autologous and weeks-long, unsuited to acute trauma.
applications.challenge: Orphan CPT is a route to a BLA, not a trauma market; the adult nonunion path would need a separate pivotal.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 1b/2a (NCT05693558; 17 patients: 9 adults with bone nonunion, 8 children with CPT) reported 88% healing at 12 months (100% where mechanical stability was achieved) in a January 2025 company release; a 12-patient randomized Phase 3 vs ICBG (NCT07112443) began Sept 2025 with the first two children implanted Feb-Mar 2026.
applications.caveats: Company-reported, not peer-reviewed; tiny n; Phase 3 is n=12 with a composite mRUST/clinical/no-secondary-intervention endpoint, acceptable only because the disease is rare.

applications.evidence_summary: Adult lower-limb nonunion cohort of the Phase 1/2: company reports 89% union at 24 months and no refractures at 5 years (April 2025 release). Adult critical-size-bone-defect Phase 3 in start-up (Sept 2026).
applications.caveats: Open-label, company-reported, small cohort; adult approval targeted 2031.

evidence.title: Phase 3 randomized controlled study of NVD003 vs iliac crest bone graft in pediatric congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia
evidence.finding: Recruiting at Phoenix Children's, Loma Linda, Sinai Baltimore, Mayo, Brussels, Amiens, Barcelona; primary endpoint overall healing at 12 months (mRUST 13 or more, no pain on weight bearing, no secondary intervention).

evidence.title: Single-arm study of NVD-003 for recalcitrant lower limb nonunion in adults
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; company reported 8/9 clinical healing at 2 years.

evidence.title: NVD-003 in the treatment of congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (Phase 1b/2a, US/EU)
evidence.finding: Open-label; 12-month 'efficacy' 88% across 17 patients (9 adult nonunion, 8 pediatric CPT) per company release Jan 31, 2025; registry entry last verified Jan 2024.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Phase 3 primary completion October 2026, study completion July 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov); BLA timing not public.

bd.reimbursement: Would be a biologic (BLA) with potential for separate payment; none today.
bd.notes: Sister product NVD-X3 (allogeneic) has an IND for cervical fusion (2024). The priority review voucher is the financial story.

name: NVDX3 (allogeneic adipose-derived osteogenic graft)
ownership_history: Same sponsor as NVD-003.
composition: Off-the-shelf allogeneic version of the Novadip 3M3 platform: adipose-derived cells differentiated into an osteogenic graft (details from company; scaffold composition not confirmed)

regulatory.reference: US IND for a Phase 2b/3 cervical spine fusion study cleared 2024-11-22 (company release). ClinicalTrials.gov lists three Novadip NVDX3 trials: NCT05961956 (low-grade degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis, active not recruiting), NCT05987033 (distal radius fracture proof of concept, completed), NCT06532253 (long-term safety, recruiting, Luxembourg). No NCT for the US cervical Phase 2b/3 study was found.

applications.evidence_summary: Company reported 12-month Phase 1b/2a trauma results (Feb 20, 2025): durable bone union in 100% of distal radius fracture participants, no related adverse events.
applications.caveats: Company-reported, small open-label cohort; no NCT or publication located for the trauma or spine Phase 1b/2a studies during this review.

applications.evidence_summary: Interim first-in-human lumbar fusion data (Oct 2024, company): 90% of patients healing or progressing toward healing at 6 months. Phase 2b/3 in cervical fusion planned to enroll in the US from H2 2025.
applications.caveats: Interim, company-reported, no comparator; no registry entry located.

pipeline.expected_milestone: US cervical Phase 2b/3 start (IND cleared Nov 2024; enrollment target Nov 2025 per April 2025 release) not confirmed in any registry as of 2026-10-22.

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational.
bd.notes: An allogeneic, off-the-shelf osteogenic cell graft would compete directly with 361 cellular bone allografts but with a BLA and labeled claims; this is the strategically interesting asset in the Novadip portfolio.

challenge: No 2026 NVDX3 update or US cervical-study registration found.

name: NeoFuse (allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells) for spinal fusion - no Phase 3
ownership_history: Mesoblast Ltd (Melbourne; Nasdaq/ASX: MESO). Same STRO-3+ MPC platform as rexlemestrocel-L (existing disc record).
composition: Allogeneic STRO-3-selected mesenchymal precursor cells (25 or 75 million per level), loaded on MasterGraft granules in the posterolateral study; carrier for the interbody and cervical studies not stated in the registry titles.

regulatory.reference: US IND (number not public). NCT00996073 (lumbar interbody, Phase 2, n=24), NCT00549913 (PLF with MasterGraft, Phase 1/2, n=6), NCT00810212 (PLF, withdrawn), NCT01097486 (multilevel ACDF, Phase 2, n=24), NCT01106417 (multilevel ACDF, Phase 1/2, n=12). In January 2013 Mesoblast said the interbody data supported a Phase 3; none is registered.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2 randomized trial (NCT00996073, n=24, 8 per arm, posterior interbody approach): 12-month fusion 85.7% with 25M MPC vs 62.5% with 75M and 75% with autograft, no cell-related serious adverse events, per the company's January 2013 release; never published (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Grade I by design only: 8 patients per arm, sponsor press release, no dose response (higher dose did worse), no publication.

applications.evidence_summary: Two multilevel ACDF studies (NCT01097486 n=24; NCT01106417 n=12) completed 2012-2013 with no results posted or published; supporting data are ovine cervical fusion studies.
applications.caveats: No human data available.

applications.evidence_summary: Six-patient dose study with MasterGraft (NCT00549913) completed 2013; no results posted.
applications.caveats: No human data available.

evidence.title: Safety and Preliminary Efficacy Study of NeoFuse in Subjects Requiring Lumbar Interbody Fusion
evidence.finding: Completed; sponsor-reported 12-month fusion 85.7% (25M) vs 62.5% (75M) vs 75% (autograft); no registry results.

evidence.title: Safety and Preliminary Efficacy Study of NeoFuse in Multi-Level ACDF
evidence.finding: Completed 2013; no results posted.

evidence.title: Cervical interbody fusion is enhanced by allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells in an ovine model
evidence.finding: Ovine model supporting the ACDF program.

evidence.title: Allogeneic mesenchymal progenitor cells for posterolateral lumbar spine fusion in sheep
evidence.finding: Ovine PLF model.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No Phase 3 registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (search 2026-10-23); the program appears inactive but Mesoblast has not been confirmed to have discontinued it.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Allogeneic cells as a fusion graft remain unlicensed; this is the most-cited industry attempt and it never reached a pivotal trial.

name: OSSGROW / OSSRON (autologous adult live cultured osteoblasts, India) - not US-marketed
ownership_history: Regrow Biosciences Pvt. Ltd. (Mumbai; also styled RMS Regrow), private; hospital partnership with Apollo Hospitals to offer Ossron and the cartilage product Chondron (press release).
composition: Autologous osteoblasts cultured from the patient's bone marrow and implanted into the necrotic femoral head after core decompression.

regulatory.reference: No FDA status. Conditional marketing approval in India in March 2017 (per Palekar 2021; the CDSCO/DCGI approval document was not seen). Indian Phase 3 CTRI/2015/04/005662 (n=12, completed; results not located).

applications.evidence_summary: Palekar 2021 retrospective multicenter series (64 patients, 101 hips, mean 6.3-year follow-up): VAS 58.8 to 32.2, Harris hip score 47.1 to 63.7; 28.7% of hips went to THA; 37.6% progressed.
applications.caveats: Uncontrolled retrospective series by users of the product; no comparison with core decompression alone, and the double-blind European RCT of a similar product (PREOB) was negative.

evidence.title: Retrospective study on implantation of autologous-cultured osteoblasts for the treatment of patients with avascular necrosis of the femoral head
evidence.finding: Pain and function improved; 28.7% of hips required THA at mean 6.3 years; no control group.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable in the US.
bd.notes: Ex-US cultured-cell product; any US use would require an IND.

name: PLX-PAD (placental expanded stromal cells) for recovery after hip fracture arthroplasty - Phase 3 missed primary endpoint
ownership_history: Pluristem Therapeutics (Haifa, Israel; Nasdaq: PLUR) renamed itself Pluri Inc. in 2022. HIPGEN was funded in part by the EU Horizon 2020 program (CORDIS project 779293) with Charite Berlin as a lead academic partner.
composition: Allogeneic placenta-derived mesenchymal-like adherent stromal cells (PLX-PAD) injected into the gluteal muscles during arthroplasty for hip fracture; targets muscle recovery, not bone healing.

regulatory.reference: US IND (number not public; the trial enrolled in the US, Europe and Israel); EU CT 2017-005165-49; NCT03451916. Not licensed for any indication.

applications.evidence_summary: HIPGEN Phase 3 double-blind RCT (n=240, NCT03451916): primary endpoint SPPB at week 26 not met (6.873 PLX-PAD vs 7.039 placebo, per the EU/UK registry summary); sponsor reported a secondary-endpoint gain in hip abduction strength (p=0.047 at week 26, p=0.0022 at week 52, injured leg). No peer-reviewed results paper located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Failed primary endpoint; the positive result is a sponsor-highlighted secondary endpoint; results only in registries and a press release. Muscle-recovery adjunct, not a bone biologic.
applications.challenge: Pluri still features the strength result; the trial was negative on its prespecified primary endpoint.

evidence.title: Treatment of Muscle Injury Following Arthroplasty for Hip Fracture (HIPGEN)
evidence.finding: Completed 2022; primary SPPB endpoint not met; secondary hip abduction strength better with PLX-PAD per sponsor.

evidence.title: HIPGEN: a randomized, multicentre phase III study using intramuscular placenta-expanded stromal cells therapy for recovery following hip fracture arthroplasty: a study design
evidence.finding: Design paper: SPPB at week 26 primary; 240 patients for 88% power to detect a 1-point SPPB difference.

evidence.title: Immunomodulatory placental-expanded, mesenchymal stromal cells improve muscle function following hip arthroplasty
evidence.finding: Phase 1/2a in elective THA: low dose improved gluteus medius strength vs placebo at week 26 (p=0.007); no relevant cell-related adverse events.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No follow-on orthopedic trial registered (ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23); stage set to phase-2 because the schema has no 'failed phase 3' value.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Example of a large, well-run cell trial in hip fracture that missed; relevant when a cell company pitches 'regeneration' in geriatric trauma.

name: Rexlemestrocel-L (MPC-06-ID; allogeneic STRO-3+ mesenchymal precursor cells with hyaluronic acid)
ownership_history: Developed by Mesoblast (Australia/US) since the 2011 Phase 2; no partner announced for the disc program as of Oct 2026.
composition: Immunoselected, culture-expanded allogeneic bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal precursor cells (6 million cells) mixed with hyaluronic acid carrier, single intradiscal injection

regulatory.reference: IND (number not public); RMAT designation for chronic low back pain due to DDD (company statements). No BLA filed as of Oct 2026.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 3 MSB-DR003 (NCT02412735, n=404, 48 sites) did not meet its composite primary endpoint (50% VAS reduction plus 15-point ODI reduction at both 12 and 24 months without intervention); 36-month results published Spine J 2025 report pain and function improvements favoring cells over saline on secondary analyses. FDA's January 2026 Type B feedback (company account) is that pain-intensity effects favored rexlemestrocel-L and that a clinically meaningful 12-month pain reduction in the confirmatory trial could support efficacy.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; primary endpoint of DR003 was missed; the BLA case rests on a single confirmatory trial (MSB-DR004, n=300, topline expected mid-2027). Bayesian responder analyses in DR003.

evidence.title: MSB-DR003: placebo-controlled Phase 3 of rexlemestrocel-L alone or with HA in chronic low back pain
evidence.finding: Primary composite responder endpoint (both 12 and 24 months) not met; results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; 48 sites (47 US, 1 Australia), primary completion May 2020.

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells with and without hyaluronic acid for treatment of chronic low back pain: a prospective, randomized, double blind, concurrent-controlled 36-month study (Spine J 2025; DOI 10.1016/j.spinee.2025.03.015)
evidence.finding: 36-month follow-up of the Phase 3; authors report durable reductions in pain and disability versus saline on secondary analyses (abstract truncated in retrieval; see notes).

evidence.title: Allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells treatment for chronic low back pain associated with degenerative disc disease: a prospective randomized, placebo-controlled 36-month study (Spine J 2020; DOI 10.1016/j.spinee.2020.10.004)
evidence.finding: Phase 2 (NCT01290367): 6M and 18M MPC+HA vs HA vehicle vs saline at 13 sites, 3:3:2:2; safety and preliminary efficacy through 36 months supported the Phase 3 dose of 6 million cells.

evidence.title: MSB-DR004: randomized, double-blind, saline-controlled Phase 3 of rexlemestrocel-L + HA in moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain
evidence.finding: Started July 2024; 40 sites; recruitment target reached April 2026 and all 300 patients treated by August 2026 (company); 12-month pain endpoint; primary completion July 2027.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Topline from MSB-DR004 expected mid-CY2027; BLA filing targeted Q3 CY2027 if positive (Mesoblast releases Apr 29 and Aug 17, 2026). RMAT allows rolling review.

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational. Would be a physician-administered biologic (likely J-code) if licensed.
bd.notes: Mesoblast already holds a BLA for remestemcel-L (Ryoncil, pediatric GVHD, 2024), so it has a licensed MSC manufacturing platform. Commercial-scale manufacturing for the disc product is reportedly proceeding in parallel with DR004 (company).

name: Umbilical cord / Wharton's jelly / cord-blood injectables marketed for orthopedic use
company: Numerous; public FDA letters name New Life Medical Services (Restor+, Regain, Renyte), R3 Medical / Bello Bio / Regen Suppliers (ReBellaWJ, ReBellaCB), Dynamic Stem Cell Therapy; BioStem Life Sciences (Jan 2025, CGMP) per search results
ownership_history: Not applicable (class record).
composition: Minced, micronized or enzymatically processed umbilical cord tissue (Wharton's jelly) or cord blood, cryopreserved, sold as 'stem cell' injections; cell viability after processing is frequently near zero

regulatory.reference: FDA position: umbilical cord's basic function in the donor is a conduit between mother and fetus, so injection into a joint, disc or tendon is non-homologous (fails 1271.10(a)(2)); processing that disrupts the cord's tubular structure is more than minimal manipulation; allogeneic cord blood that depends on living cells fails criterion (a)(4). Products are unapproved new drugs (FD&C 505(a)) and unlicensed biologics (PHS 351(a)(1)). The only licensed cord-blood products are HPC, Cord Blood for hematopoietic reconstitution.

applications.evidence_summary: No controlled trial of any marketed umbilical cord injectable for bone healing; the New Life letter documents marketing for 'non-union fractures' and 'bone spurs' with no data.
applications.caveats: Sterility failures documented in multiple letters; CDC-investigated bacterial infections after cord-blood product injections (2018, Liveyon) are the safety precedent (not re-verified here).

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to New Life Medical Services, LLC (CBER 25-711102)
evidence.finding: Wharton's jelly products fail minimal manipulation and homologous use; marketed for orthopedic procedures, bone spurs and non-union fractures.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Dynamic Stem Cell Therapy (CBER 25-712579)
evidence.finding: Umbilical-cord product marketed for sports injuries, arthritis and joint pain; misbranded drug, unlicensed biologic, fails 1271.10(a).

pipeline.expected_milestone: None; legitimate allogeneic cord-derived MSC products (e.g., Korean Cartistem for cartilage) have not entered US pivotal trials for bone.

bd.reimbursement: None; cash-pay.
bd.notes: Compliance red flag for any orthopedic distributor; FDA treats the distributor as a manufacturer when it labels or approves product (R3 letter: Regen Suppliers subject to CGMP under 21 CFR 210.3(b)(12)).

name: nSTRIDE Autologous Protein Solution (APS) Kit
ownership_history: Biomet Biologics; Zimmer Biomet since 2015.
composition: Point-of-care blood processing kit (two devices, a few mL of whole blood) that concentrates white cells, platelets and anti-inflammatory proteins such as IL-1Ra into a cell-free solution for intra-articular injection. Not cleared or approved in the US for any use.

regulatory.reference: Investigational device under IDE (PROGRESS IV NCT02905240 and the HA-comparator trial NCT03182374 ran as unapproved-device studies); no 510(k) or PMA located as of 2026-10-23. IDE number not confirmed from a primary source.
on_label_indications: No US marketing authorization. Sponsor intent: single intra-articular injection for knee osteoarthritis (investigational). Unlike cleared PRP kits (ORG: PRP to be mixed with bone graft), this is a cell-free blood-derived injectate with no cleared claim; injecting any autologous blood concentrate into a joint is off-label for a cleared device.

challenge: The saline-controlled pivotal trial and an independent saline-controlled RCT were both negative; a hiring manager will ask why APS is still discussed.

applications.evidence_summary: Zimmer Biomet's saline-controlled PROGRESS IV (n=332) posted WOMAC pain change -5.6 (APS) vs -5.4 (saline) at 12 months, and an independent double-blind RCT (n=40) found no difference from saline and worse VAS pain with APS at 12 months (Ross 2024). The APS-vs-Synvisc-One trial (n=252) posted pain falling 11.5 to 6.7 vs 11.9 to 7.2.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-run trials; the HA-comparator posting does not state a clean between-arm contrast; independent trial is small. Early open-label data (van Drumpt 2016, n=11) was positive and is the source of much marketing. Off-label use of the device; FDA treats the autologous product as 361-exempt (same-surgical-procedure rule) only when minimally manipulated.

evidence.title: Saline-Controlled Study of nSTRIDE APS for Knee Osteoarthritis (PROGRESS IV)
evidence.finding: Posted results: 12-month change in WOMAC LK3.1 pain -5.6 with APS vs -5.4 with saline, i.e. no meaningful difference on the primary endpoint.

evidence.title: nSTRIDE APS Versus Hyaluronic Acid (Synvisc-One) for Knee Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Posted results: WOMAC LK3.1 pain 11.5 to 6.7 (APS) vs 11.9 to 7.2 (Synvisc-One) at 12 months; the registry lists a within/between p<0.0001 without stating the contrast, so superiority is not established from the posting.

evidence.title: The effect of intra-articular autologous protein solution on knee osteoarthritis symptoms
evidence.finding: nSTRIDE APS vs saline, 21 and 19 analyzed, KL 2-3: no difference in WOMAC or KOOS at 12 months, and VAS pain at 12 months was worse with APS than saline.

evidence.title: Safety and Treatment Effectiveness of a Single Autologous Protein Solution Injection in Patients with Knee Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: 11 patients with early to moderate OA: no serious adverse events and WOMAC improvement from 2 weeks to 6 months; Zimmer Biomet-linked open-label study.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Both large trials completed (2020-06 and 2023-01); no US submission located. Treat as stalled.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable: unapproved in the US.
bd.notes: The APS pivotal completed in mid-2020 with no difference from saline on the posted primary outcome; no regulatory filing was found. Zimmer Biomet has not publicly reconciled this in the sources read.

name: Amniotic and placental tissue products (dHACM injectables, amnion sheets and tendon wraps; e.g., MiMedx AmnioFix/EpiFix, Organogenesis, Integra and others)
company: Multiple (MiMedx, Organogenesis, Integra, Smith+Nephew, BioTissue and many tissue banks)
ownership_history: Fragmented; MiMedx is the largest US amnion processor.
composition: Dehydrated or cryopreserved human amnion/chorion membrane, as sheets (wraps/barriers) or micronized powder reconstituted for injection; some products are flowable amniotic fluid or umbilical-cord derived

regulatory.reference: Sheet forms used as a covering or barrier are regulated as 361 HCT/Ps when minimally manipulated and homologous. Micronized or injectable forms used to treat tendinopathy, fasciitis or arthritis do not meet the 361 criteria and require a BLA; FDA's enforcement-discretion period for such products ended 2021-05-31, and MiMedx stated that AmnioFix Injectable, EpiFix Micronized and AmnioFill were affected while its sheet products were not.
on_label_indications: Sheet products: homologous use as a wound covering or barrier (no FDA-reviewed therapeutic indication)
Injectable/micronized products for plantar fasciitis or tendinopathy: no FDA approval; investigational (IND/BLA) only after 2021

applications.evidence_summary: Plantar fasciitis injection, not bone healing: Cazzell 2018 (PMID 30058377) 14-site RCT, 145 patients, single micronized dHACM injection vs saline; VAS fell 76% vs 45% at 3 months (p<0.0001). Zelen 2013 (PMID 23945520) 45-patient RCT positive at 8 weeks; Hanselman 2014 (PMID 25249320) cryopreserved amnion vs corticosteroid, 23 patients, mostly no difference. Network meta-analysis of 22 injection RCTs (PMID 27143138) found dHACM superior to corticosteroid only in the short term with no data beyond 2 months.
applications.caveats: MiMedx-funded trials with company authors; the injectable products studied are no longer lawfully marketed without a BLA; no evidence for bone healing in the foot. Tendon-wrap use (Achilles, peroneal) rests on case series. Tiered investigational per FDA position.

applications.evidence_summary: No controlled trial of any amniotic product for bone healing, fracture or fusion; orthopedic marketing is for osteoarthritis, tendinopathy, plantar fasciitis and 'inflammation', which FDA treats as non-homologous.
applications.caveats: The wound-care evidence base for 361 amniotic sheets (DFU/VLU) does not transfer to injection or bone indications.

evidence.title: Randomized controlled trial of micronized dehydrated human amnion/chorion membrane (dHACM) injection compared to placebo for the treatment of plantar fasciitis
evidence.finding: 76% VAS reduction vs 45% placebo at 3 months; FFI-R improved 60% vs 40%.

evidence.title: Prospective, randomized, blinded, comparative study of injectable micronized dehydrated amniotic/chorionic membrane allograft for plantar fasciitis
evidence.finding: AOFAS hindfoot score improved 51-53 points with mDHACM vs 13 points with saline at 8 weeks.

evidence.title: Cryopreserved human amniotic membrane injection for plantar fasciitis: a randomized, controlled, double-blind pilot study
evidence.finding: Mostly no difference vs corticosteroid; pilot.

evidence.title: Injection therapies for plantar fasciopathy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of 22 randomised controlled trials
evidence.finding: Dehydrated amniotic membrane superior to corticosteroid at 0-2 months; no data beyond 2 months.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Frontier Biologics LLC (CBER 25-686059)
evidence.finding: Amniotic-fluid injectable marketed for osteoarthritis, joint pain and soft-tissue injury is not an HCT/P; amniotic membrane marketed for healing/anti-inflammation fails homologous use; CGMP violations.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Celularity Inc. (CBER 25-681480)
evidence.finding: Interfyl decellularized placental matrix marketed (via Arthrex) for orthopedic soft-tissue healing fails homologous use; unapproved drug and unlicensed biologic; 483 responses found inadequate.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to BioXtek LLC (CBER 26-715478)
evidence.finding: Amniotic membrane products marketed for wound healing and orthopedic tendon repair fail homologous use (1271.10(a)(2)).

bd.reimbursement: Facility use (wraps in surgery) is packaged with no separate payment. Office injections billed under product-specific Q-codes have been targeted by Medicare contractors with overpayment demands since 2022; Medicare treats non-wound orthopedic amniotic injections as not reasonable and necessary, and CMS's CY2026 physician fee schedule overhauled skin-substitute payment (details not verified in this sweep). Commercial payers largely exclude amniotic injections as experimental.
bd.notes: Sold by wound-care and podiatry reps; the post-2021 market is sheet products for wounds and surgical wraps. Any BD plan treating injectable amnion as an orthopedic product must assume BLA-level development; MiMedx has pursued IND-based trials for its injectable.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None for bone. Adjacent context: CMS CY2026 PFS final rule (Oct 31, 2025) set skin-substitute payment at $127.28/cm2 from Jan 1, 2026, exempting 351-licensed products, after a ~40-fold rise in Medicare spending over five years; this reprices the Q-code economy that funds many amniotic tissue banks.

name: ReNu (cryopreserved amniotic suspension allograft, ASA)
ownership_history: Developed by NuTech Medical (Birmingham, AL), acquired by Organogenesis in 2017. Sold commercially as a 361 product until FDA's enforcement-discretion window closed; Organogenesis ceased commercial distribution of ReNu on 31 May 2021 and ran it as an IND/BLA program (RMAT designation for knee OA, 2021).
composition: Cryopreserved suspension of micronized amniotic membrane plus cells derived from amniotic fluid, injected intra-articularly.

regulatory.reference: BLA accepted for review 6 July 2026 (BLA number not disclosed); PDUFA target date 24 April 2027; RMAT designation 2021
on_label_indications: None yet. Proposed indication: management of symptoms (pain) of knee osteoarthritis. Not approved as of 2026-10-23.

challenge: Organogenesis is filing on one positive Phase 3 (one-sided p=0.0177 vs a 0.023 threshold, WOMAC pain -0.7 vs saline) and one that missed (p=0.0393, -0.5), plus a pooled analysis. Expect an FDA advisory-committee-style debate over whether a sub-1-point WOMAC difference is clinically meaningful.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 3 #1 (NCT04636229, n=516): WOMAC pain -0.72 vs saline at 6 months, one-sided p=0.0177 (met). Phase 3 #2 (NCT06000410, n=594, topline 25 Sept 2025): -0.51, one-sided p=0.0393, missed the 0.023 threshold. Earlier Phase 2 single-blind RCT (n=200, ASA vs HA vs saline; Farr 2019, Gomoll 2021) favored ASA on KOOS/VAS to 12 months. 2025-2026 systematic reviews pool mostly these sponsor trials.
applications.caveats: All trials sponsor-funded with Organogenesis-paid investigators; effect sizes are small on a 0-20 or 0-10 WOMAC pain scale (scale not stated in releases); Phase 3 results are press releases and 10-K text, not peer-reviewed papers yet.
applications.challenge: Under BLA review, not approved; cannot be offered as a 'choice' today.

applications.evidence_summary: A 150-patient ReNu vs corticosteroid plantar fasciitis trial (NCT02982226) is listed with unknown status and no results; no published tendinopathy data located (2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Not studied to completion.

evidence.title: A Randomized Controlled Single-Blind Study Demonstrating Superiority of Amniotic Suspension Allograft Injection Over Hyaluronic Acid and Saline Control for Modification of Knee Osteoarthritis Symptoms
evidence.finding: 1:1:1 ASA vs HA vs saline; at 3 months 13.2% of ASA patients reported unacceptable pain vs 68.8% HA and 75% saline; KOOS and VAS favored ASA.

evidence.title: Safety and Efficacy of an Amniotic Suspension Allograft Injection Over 12 Months in a Single-Blinded, Randomized Controlled Trial for Symptomatic Osteoarthritis of the Knee
evidence.finding: 12-month follow-up of the same trial: ASA kept significant KOOS and VAS improvements over HA and saline.

evidence.title: Efficacy of Amniotic Suspension Allograft in Patients With Osteoarthritis of the Knee (Phase 3 #1)
evidence.finding: Company-reported: WOMAC pain -0.72 vs saline at 6 months, one-sided p=0.0177 against a 0.023 threshold.

evidence.title: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy of Amniotic Suspension Allograft in Patients With Osteoarthritis of the Knee (Phase 3 #2)
evidence.finding: Company-reported 25 Sept 2025: WOMAC pain -0.51 vs saline, one-sided p=0.0393; missed the primary endpoint.

evidence.title: Evaluating the efficacy of intra-articular human amniotic suspension allografts for knee osteoarthritis management: A systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: 5 studies (3 RCTs): pooled KOOS MD +10.9 and large VAS reductions; authors call for larger independent RCTs.

evidence.title: Efficacy of Amniotic Suspension Allografts in the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review
evidence.finding: 9 studies, narrative synthesis: ASA generally outperformed HA and saline on pain; mild transient adverse events.

pipeline.expected_milestone: PDUFA target action date 24 April 2027 (Organogenesis release, 6 July 2026). Hip OA studies in planning.

bd.reimbursement: None until approved. If licensed under Section 351 it would be a biologic (J-code/ASP pathway), outside the flat skin-substitute rate.
bd.notes: Would be the first licensed amniotic injectable for any orthopedic indication in the US.

name: TTAX03 (lyophilized micronized amniotic membrane and umbilical cord, investigational injectable)
ownership_history: BioTissue Holdings (formerly TissueTech), Miami; retained pipeline after the January 2026 sale of surgical/wound brands to BioStem.
composition: Lyophilized and micronized particulate human amniotic membrane and umbilical cord, reconstituted for intra-articular injection.

regulatory.reference: IND (number not public); Phase 2 NCT05079035
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2, 52-week, single injection TTAX03 vs saline in KL 3-4 knee OA (NCT05079035, n=90) completed March 2025; no results posted or published as of 2026-10-23. A facet-joint Phase 1 (NCT06236308) was withdrawn.
applications.caveats: Results unknown.

evidence.title: A Phase 2, 52-Week Trial of TTAX03 vs. Saline as a Single Intra-articular Injection in Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3-4 Knee OA
evidence.finding: Completed 2025-03-07; no results posted.

evidence.title: TTAX03 for the Treatment of Lumbosacral Facet Joint Pain
evidence.finding: Withdrawn before enrollment.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Phase 2 readout not public as of 2026-10-23.

bd.reimbursement: None (investigational).
bd.notes: The proper 351 path for the same tissue BioTissue also sold as Clarix Flo.

name: AlloJoin (allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal progenitor cells)
ownership_history: Developed by Cellular Biomedicine Group (Shanghai/Cupertino); ClinicalTrials.gov lists Shanghai AbelZeta Ltd. as sponsor of the Phase II. Corporate chain (CBMG to AbelZeta) not verified.
composition: Allogeneic human adipose-derived mesenchymal progenitor cells (haMPC) injected intra-articularly (two injections three weeks apart in the Phase I).

regulatory.reference: China NMPA IND (reported as the first stem-cell drug application approved for Phase II in China, 2019, per a BioSpace headline); no marketing authorization
on_label_indications: None (investigational)

applications.evidence_summary: Randomized, double-blind Phase II (NCT04208646, n=106, China, 2020-2021) is complete without published results located; the earlier randomized dose-ranging Phase I pilot (n=22, 19 completed) reported transient injection-site pain and improved WOMAC/VAS secondary endpoints with slight MRI cartilage gains in the low-dose group.
applications.caveats: Unpublished Phase II; tiny Phase I; knee-OA injectable MSC class likely covered in another slice.

evidence.title: Intra-articular injections of allogeneic human adipose-derived mesenchymal progenitor cells in patients with symptomatic bilateral knee osteoarthritis: a Phase I pilot study
evidence.finding: Safe; transient AEs; secondary pain/function endpoints improved at 48 weeks; MRI slight gains in low dose.

evidence.title: Allogenic adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal progenitor cells (AlloJoin) for knee osteoarthritis (Phase II)
evidence.finding: Completed 2021-06-30 per registry; no results located.

evidence.title: Allogenic adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells for the treatment of knee osteoarthritis (phase 3)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion estimated December 2026; no results.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No Phase III plan located.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed.
bd.notes: Overlap risk with MSC/knee OA slice; included because named in the cartilage slice brief.

name: CARTISTEM
ownership_history: Medipost Co., Ltd. (Seongnam, Korea; US subsidiary Medipost, Inc.). Korean MFDS approval 2012 is widely reported but not verified here.
composition: Allogeneic umbilical cord blood-derived mesenchymal stem cells in sodium hyaluronate hydrogel, implanted into the defect after marrow-stimulating drilling (mini-arthrotomy).

regulatory.reference: US IND; FDA agreed to a single pivotal Phase 3 plus confirmatory evidence BLA strategy (June 2026 company release). Korea: marketed (approval year not verified)
on_label_indications: US: none (investigational). Korea: repair of knee cartilage defects (labeling not read).

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 3 in Korea (n=114, large ICRS grade-4 defects, mean age 56): 97.7% vs 71.7% improved >=1 ICRS grade at 48-week second-look (P=.001) vs microfracture; VAS/WOMAC/IKDC not different at 48 weeks but better to 5 years. US pivotal NCT07339111 (n=300, ~70 US/Canadian sites, vs surgical debridement) started March 2026.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; ICRS second-look arthroscopy endpoint is a structural surrogate; older, large-defect Korean population; US trial comparator is debridement.

applications.evidence_summary: Hyundai Bioland Phase III (NCT04310215, n=102, single-blind, adding CARTISTEM to microfracture in talar chondral lesions) completed June 2022; no publication located.
applications.caveats: Unpublished; different sponsor/licensee.

evidence.title: Allogeneic Umbilical Cord Blood-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cell Implantation Versus Microfracture for Large, Full-Thickness Cartilage Defects in Older Patients
evidence.finding: 97.7% vs 71.7% improved >=1 ICRS grade at 48 weeks (P=.001); clinical scores superior over 5 years.

evidence.title: Phase 3 pivotal trial comparing CARTISTEM and surgical comparator for knee cartilage lesions and osteoarthritis (US/Canada)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion estimated June 2029.

evidence.title: Phase III trial of adding CARTISTEM to microfracture in talar chondral lesions
evidence.finding: Completed June 2022; no results located.

evidence.title: Cartilage regeneration in osteoarthritic patients by a composite of allogeneic UCB-MSCs and hyaluronate hydrogel: results from a clinical trial for safety and proof-of-concept with 7 years of extended follow-up
evidence.finding: Seven patients; hyaline-like repair at 1 year, stable scores over 7 years, no tumorigenesis.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Safety and Exploratory Efficacy of CARTISTEM for Articular Cartilage Defects (US Phase 1/2)
evidence.finding: Completed 2017; results posted.

pipeline.expected_milestone: US Phase 3 primary completion est. 2029-06 (ClinicalTrials.gov); company release June 2026 on FDA alignment.

bd.reimbursement: Korea reimbursement not verified; US not marketed.
bd.notes: One of the few allogeneic MSC scaffolds with an FDA-agreed pivotal design; first patient dosed July 2026 per Edaily summary.

challenge: Licensed in Korea but not in the US; in the US it is an investigational 351 biologic and cannot be offered outside the IND.

name: CartiLife
ownership_history: Biosolution Co., Ltd. (Korea). Korean distribution partner: Mundipharma exclusive commercialization/distribution agreement (headline only; terms not read). Korean approval date conflicts across sources (a 2026 Korean report cites April 2025 MFDS approval).
composition: Autologous chondrocytes grown as extracellular matrix-associated pellets (beads) from the patient's cartilage biopsy, implanted into the defect (registry description: 'pellet-type extracellular matrix-associated autologous chondrocytes').

regulatory.reference: US: IND, Phase 2 (NCT04744402, n=25, FDA IND cleared Nov 2019 per a 2020 brokerage report); company requested a Type C meeting for a US Phase 3 (2026 Korean report). Korea: MFDS product approval reported April 2025 (unverified); Hainan (China) sales approval reported
on_label_indications: US: none (investigational). Korea: autologous cartilage defect repair of the knee (label not read).

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed study of this product located in PubMed (search 2026-10-23, 'CartiLife'). Registered studies: Korean Phase 3, active-controlled (NCT05051332, n=104, status unknown, primary completion estimated 2023-09), US Phase 2 single-arm (NCT04744402, n=25), earlier Korean study (NCT03545269, n=30, completed).
applications.caveats: No published efficacy data; status of US Phase 2 uncertain (registry not updated since 2023).

evidence.title: Active-controlled Phase III trial of CartiLife in Korea (comparator named in the truncated registry title as autologous chondrocyte implantation)
evidence.finding: Registry only; status unknown, no results located.

evidence.title: Phase 2 trial of CartiLife for articular cartilage defects of the knee (United States)
evidence.finding: Single-arm open-label US Phase 2; listed as recruiting but registry last updated 2023; no results located.

pipeline.expected_milestone: US Phase 3 planning after FDA Type C meeting request (2026 Korean press, unverified).

bd.reimbursement: Korea/China only.
bd.notes: Mundipharma Korea distribution headline; Biosolution seeking global partners at BIO USA (2026 Korean press).

name: Chondro-Gide (AMIC) collagen membrane
ownership_history: Geistlich Pharma AG (Wolhusen, Switzerland), private. Two US-registered knee studies (NCT04537013 SECURE, n=82; NCT05785949, n=75) were both terminated early for a change in business strategy (registry/summary).
composition: Bilayer resorbable porcine type I/III collagen membrane laid over a microfractured defect (AMIC, autologous matrix-induced chondrogenesis) and glued or sutured.

regulatory.reference: US: FDA Breakthrough Device Designation granted February 2021 for Chondro-Gide articular cartilage cover; no clearance/approval located. Geistlich dental collagen membranes (e.g., K212463 Bio-Gide) are different products
on_label_indications: No US cartilage indication. Used ex-US (AMIC) for knee and ankle defects; CE labeling not read.

applications.evidence_summary: Int Orthop 2017 RCT ( n=47 randomized to microfracture or sutured/glued AMIC): AMIC scores stable over 5 years while microfracture scores declined; MRI fill better with AMIC. A 2021 meta-analysis (12 studies, 375 patients) found significant pain and function gains, mostly uncontrolled. A 67-patient Geistlich RCT of microfracture plus Chondro-Gide vs microfracture alone (NCT02993510) is completed, with no publication located.
applications.caveats: Small RCT; sponsor-linked; US trials terminated; AMIC is a surgeon technique that adds a membrane, not a new biology.
applications.challenge: US regulatory status is the question: BDD is a review-speed designation, not an authorization.

applications.evidence_summary: A 5-year prospective cohort (n=19) of AMIC with cancellous graft via malleolar osteotomy showed FFI -22.5% and AOFAS +17.2% at 24 months, stable at 60 months (BMC Musculoskelet Disord 2021, Level II). Geistlich ankle RCT (NCT05741983) withdrawn.
applications.caveats: Small single-center cohort; osteotomy needed.

evidence.title: A randomized controlled trial demonstrating sustained benefit of Autologous Matrix-Induced Chondrogenesis over microfracture at five years
evidence.finding: AMIC groups stayed stable over 5 years while microfracture scores progressively deteriorated; MRI defect fill better with AMIC.

evidence.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Clinical Evidence on the Use of Autologous Matrix-Induced Chondrogenesis in the Knee
evidence.finding: 12 studies: pain VAS improved by 4.0 points at 1-2 years, sustained beyond 3 years; study quality suboptimal.

evidence.title: AMIC for traumatic focal osteochondral defect of the talar shoulder: a 5 years follow-up prospective cohort study
evidence.finding: FFI fell 22.5% and AOFAS rose 17.2% at 24 months with no further change at 60 months.

evidence.title: Randomised multi-center study: microfracturing with Chondro-Gide for isolated cartilage defects in the knee
evidence.finding: Completed December 2015; results not located.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed for cartilage in the US.
bd.notes: Breakthrough designation 2021 followed by US trial terminations suggests the US plan stalled.

name: Hyalofast cartilage repair scaffold
ownership_history: Hyaluronic acid-ester (HYAFF-11) scaffold from Fidia Advanced Biopolymers (Italy); Anika Therapeutics owns the product (the 2009 Fidia Advanced Biopolymers acquisition is general knowledge, not read in this sweep). FDA Breakthrough Device Designation.
composition: Non-woven scaffold of HYAFF-11 (esterified hyaluronic acid fibers), implanted over microfracture or soaked with autologous bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) in a one-step procedure.

regulatory.reference: US: PMA under review - third and final PMA module filed 2025-10-31 (Anika release 2025-11-05); no approval or panel found. Ex-US: marketed in over 35 countries (company); CE marking not independently verified
on_label_indications: No US indication (investigational in the US). Ex-US labeling for knee cartilage lesions per company; not read.

applications.evidence_summary: FastTRACK (NCT02659215, n=200, US randomized, evaluator-blinded, Hyalofast plus BMAC vs microfracture, 24 months) missed both co-primary endpoints: KOOS Pain 8.11% difference favoring microfracture (p=0.81) and IKDC function 4.84% favoring Hyalofast (p=0.34). Secondary KOOS sports (+12.19, p=0.01), QoL and total KOOS favored Hyalofast; responder and observed-data analyses were post-hoc.
applications.caveats: The primary endpoints were not met under the pre-specified analysis; Anika's explanation (COVID disruptions, microfracture dropouts, shift in standard of care) is the sponsor's. Results in press release, not peer-reviewed; n is not given in the release (200 from the registry).
applications.challenge: A hiring manager will ask how a PMA can succeed after missed co-primaries; Anika's argument leans on Breakthrough designation, secondary endpoints and 35,000 ex-US patients.

applications.evidence_summary: Ex-US case reports use Hyalofast in the talus (e.g., Cureus 2021); no published study of this product in this application beyond case reports located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Case-report level only.

evidence.title: HyaloFAST Trial for Repair of Articular Cartilage in the Knee (FastTRACK)
evidence.finding: Co-primary endpoints missed at 24 months (KOOS Pain -8.11% vs microfracture, p=0.81; IKDC +4.84%, p=0.34); secondary KOOS sports/QoL/total favored Hyalofast. Source: sponsor press release 2025-11-05.

evidence.title: Osteochondral Injury of the Talus Treated With Cell-Free Hyaluronic Acid-Based Scaffold (Hyalofast) - A Reliable Solution
evidence.finding: Case report-level data on talar use ex-US.

pipeline.expected_milestone: PMA complete 2025-10-31 (final module); FDA decision date not disclosed. Anika's investor release lists review timing as uncertain.

bd.reimbursement: US not yet marketed; ex-US hospital procurement.
bd.notes: Anika's key cartilage asset; Anika also sells Integrity Implant (rotator cuff). Over 35,000 patients treated globally since 2009 (company).

name: NOVOCART 3D (and NOVOCART 3D Plus)
ownership_history: Developed by TETEC AG (Reutlingen, Germany); US sponsor Aesculap Biologics, LLC (B. Braun group). Corporate linkage between TETEC and B. Braun not verified in this sweep.
composition: Autologous chondrocytes cultured in a three-dimensional collagen-based biphasic matrix (per publication titles; detailed composition not verified); implanted by mini-arthrotomy with a cartilage biopsy first.

regulatory.reference: US BLA-track under IND; Phase 3 NCT01957722 active. EU: used in Germany (non-interventional studies); EMA authorization not located
on_label_indications: None in the US (investigational). Aesculap's US trial page describes it as investigational and not available outside the trial (via secondary search summary).

applications.evidence_summary: Two randomized Phase 3 programs vs microfracture: US NCT01957722 (n=233, primary completion est. Dec 2025, active-not-recruiting) and EU NCT01656902 (n=263, completed March 2020, results not published in PubMed). Non-interventional NISANIK registry (n=80, 36 months) reported IKDC improvement (Level IV).
applications.caveats: No published randomized results located; BLA filing status unknown; sponsor-funded; microfracture control.

evidence.title: NOVOCART 3D vs microfracture in articular cartilage defects of the knee (US Phase 3)
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; no results posted.

evidence.title: NOVOCART 3D Plus vs microfracture in knee cartilage defects (EU Phase III)
evidence.finding: Completed March 2020; no results posted or located in PubMed.

evidence.title: A non-interventional study to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a biphasic, chondrocyte-containing biomaterial (NOVOCART 3D) in the treatment of localized full-thickness cartilage defects or osteochondral lesions of the knee joint (NISANIK)
evidence.finding: Single-arm, 8 centers, 36 months; IKDC 2000 used for effectiveness (details not read).

pipeline.expected_milestone: US Phase 3 primary completion est. 2025-12 per registry; no BLA filing located.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed in the US.
bd.notes: A US BLA for an autologous cell product would compete with MACI; Aesculap has run the trial since 2013 (>12 years).

name: NeoCart
ownership_history: Developed by Advanced Tissue Sciences/Histogenics (Waltham, MA). Histogenics' Phase 3 missed in 2018, FDA said another trial was needed, and Histogenics reverse-merged into Ocugen in 2019 (reported). Ocugen later pursued RMAT status (May 2022) and an FDA-agreed Phase 3 design (Dec 2022); NeoCart sits in OrthoCellix, an Ocugen subsidiary formed after a 2025 Carisma merger (search summary of Ocugen filings; unverified).
composition: Autologous chondrocytes expanded and grown on a bovine type I collagen scaffold under hypoxia and hydrostatic pressure in a bioreactor to form a cartilage-like tissue implant.

regulatory.reference: BLA-track biologic; RMAT designation (May 2022); FDA agreed Phase 3 design December 2022 (compare NeoCart with chondroplasty, 1-3 cm2 lesions)
on_label_indications: None (investigational)

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2 (JBJS 2012, n=30, 2:1 vs microfracture): NeoCart safe and associated with greater clinical efficacy at 2 years. Phase 3 (NCT01066702, n=245 randomized) missed its primary endpoint: pain and function improved in 74.2% vs 62% of patients at 1 year (p=0.0714) per Histogenics; FDA required a further trial before accepting a BLA.
applications.caveats: Phase 3 results are from company statements and trade coverage, not a peer-reviewed paper; registry lists the Phase 3 as terminated.

evidence.title: NeoCart, an autologous cartilage tissue implant, compared with microfracture for treatment of distal femoral cartilage lesions: an FDA phase-II prospective, randomized clinical trial after two years
evidence.finding: NeoCart group (n=21) vs microfracture (n=9): similar safety and greater clinical efficacy at 2 years.

evidence.title: Confirmatory Study of NeoCart in Knee Cartilage Repair (Phase 3)
evidence.finding: Terminated; sponsor reported 74.2% vs 62% responders (p=0.0714), missing the primary endpoint.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Ocugen planned a Phase 3 start by end of 2025; no new registration or 2026 update located (search summary).

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed.
bd.notes: A cautionary tale for the category: single-pivotal cell-therapy programs can fail by a few points; Ocugen's priority is ophthalmology gene therapy.

name: ReNew Hip Implant (cartilage defect repair, early feasibility)
ownership_history: Cytex Therapeutics, Inc. is the ClinicalTrials.gov sponsor; no further corporate details found.
composition: Registry lists only 'ReNew Hip Implant' (device); composition not read.

regulatory.reference: Early feasibility study NCT06823089 (US, n=15 estimated, start 2025-11-06, active not recruiting)
on_label_indications: None (investigational). Population: ages 14-64 with hip disease causing loss of articular cartilage integrity on the femoral head (e.g., FAI), failed conservative care.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Early feasibility IDE study only.
applications.caveats: Pre-pivotal; details unverified.

evidence.title: Early Feasibility Study of Cartilage Defect Repair (ReNew Hip Implant)
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; primary completion estimated 2031-10.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Primary completion est. 2031-10 (registry).

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed.
bd.notes: Included because the sweep brief named Cytex; scope limited to the registry.

name: Exosome / extracellular-vesicle / 'secretome' products marketed to orthopedic and pain clinics
company: Numerous; public FDA letters name Kimera Labs (XoGlo, XoGlo Pro), New Life Medical Services (Rexo), R3 Medical / Regen Suppliers (ReBellaXO, ReBellaXOL), Dynamic Stem Cell Therapy (exosome marketing); Invitrx (2022), Evolutionary Biologics (2024) and Chara Biologics (2025) are reported in secondary sources
ownership_history: Not applicable (class record).
composition: Vesicle-containing conditioned media or lyophilized fractions derived from cultured MSCs, amniotic fluid or umbilical cord tissue; FDA has found in at least one case (R3, 2026) that the process 'does not appear to isolate exosomes' at all

regulatory.reference: No FDA-approved exosome product for any indication (FDA Public Safety Notification Dec 6, 2019; Consumer Alert July 22, 2020, updated Apr 9, 2024; Approved CGT Products list as of Sept 17, 2026). Exosomes intended to treat disease are drugs and biologics requiring an IND and BLA; they are not HCT/Ps (no cells or tissue) so the 361 lane is unavailable. Kimera Labs held an IND (26535) but was cited for commercial distribution under it (21 CFR 312.7(b)).

applications.evidence_summary: No human trial of an exosome product for bone healing, fusion or fracture has been published; the field is preclinical (MSC-derived EVs loaded on scaffolds in rodent calvarial and femoral defect models) and reviews through 2026 identify manufacturing standardization, potency assays and dosing as unsolved prerequisites for an IND.
applications.caveats: Commercial 'exosome' injections for joints, discs and tendons are sold without any controlled data; FDA documented serious adverse events (Nebraska, 2019) and sterility failures (Kimera lot with positive sterility test fully distributed).

evidence.title: FDA Public Safety Notification on Exosome Products
evidence.finding: Serious adverse events in Nebraska patients treated with unapproved products marketed as exosomes; 'there are currently no FDA-approved exosome products'.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Kimera Labs, Inc. (CBER 23-649343)
evidence.finding: XoGlo/XoGlo Pro/Amnio2X are unapproved drugs and unlicensed biologics; ~37,000 vials made under deficient CGMP; closeout June 12, 2026 after the company ceased the products.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to R3 Medical Companies (CBER 26-726330)
evidence.finding: Products marketed as exosomes (ReBellaXO/XOL) made by a process that does not appear to isolate exosomes; umbilical-cord products fail homologous use; CGMP failures; orthopedic claims (arthritis, cartilage repair, tendonitis).

pipeline.expected_milestone: No orthopedic exosome IND with public efficacy data as of Oct 2026.

bd.reimbursement: None; cash-pay. Billing Medicare for these injections has been the basis of fraud prosecutions (secondary reports; not verified here).
bd.notes: A legitimate company cannot touch this category in the US without an IND; any distributor relationship with an exosome supplier is a compliance liability (see Arthrex named as distributor in the Celularity letter for the analogous amniotic case).

name: Arthrosamid (2.5% polyacrylamide hydrogel, PAAG)
ownership_history: Contura (Denmark); US trials registered under Contura.
composition: 2.5% cross-linked polyacrylamide, 97.5% water, non-absorbable, biocompatible hydrogel injected once into the knee.

regulatory.reference: none; not FDA authorized (a 2025 ISAKOS poster describes US use as off-label); CE mark ex-US (Contura lists 20 May 2020; a secondary source says 2021)
on_label_indications: None in the US. Ex-US (CE mark): symptomatic knee osteoarthritis

applications.evidence_summary: A 238-patient randomized, double-blind Contura trial (NCT04045431) completed March 2025 but results were not located; a 2026 review (Knee) says one RCT showed no significant difference from hyaluronic acid, four case series improved WOMAC pain by 15.7 to 20.8 points, and a retrospective cohort found PAAG beat corticosteroid at 6 months but not HA at 3 months.
applications.caveats: Mostly open-label series and sponsor-linked authors (Snow has Contura research funding); a non-absorbable injectable with limited long-term imaging data. The reviewing authors advise caution for routine use.

evidence.title: Efficacy of novel polyacrylamide hydrogel injection for osteoarthritis (Farhan-Alanie, Knee)
evidence.finding: Narrative review: case series show WOMAC improvement, one RCT found no significant difference from HA, no serious complications, but study quality limits routine recommendation.

evidence.title: Multi-centre randomized controlled double-blind investigation of intra-articular polyacrylamide hydrogel in subjects with knee osteoarthritis followed by open-label extension (Contura)
evidence.finding: Completed 2025-03-10; no results posted or found.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered in the US because it is not FDA authorized; no HCPCS.
bd.notes: Contura runs a US observational study (NCT05057559, LUNA, n=201, active not recruiting); a randomized Arthrosamid-vs-steroid trial is recruiting in Ireland (NCT07489521).

pipeline.expected_milestone: No US PMA submission or IDE pivotal located; LUNA observational completion estimated 2029 (search summary)

name: Bone Healing Accelerant (BHA, CT-101) plasma-based bioactive material
company: Longevity Health Holdings (formerly Carmell Corporation / Carmell Therapeutics)
ownership_history: Carmell Therapeutics (Pittsburgh; Carnegie Mellon University license) went public via SPAC with Alpha Healthcare Acquisition Corp. III in July 2023 as Carmell Corporation; repositioned to bio-aesthetics from late 2023, sold the AxoBio tissue-graft subsidiary in 2024 and renamed itself Longevity Health Holdings in March 2025.
composition: Allogeneic platelet-enriched plasma plasticized and crosslinked with genipin, combined with beta-tricalcium phosphate as a putty; FDA designated it a biologic-led combination product (FY2025 10-K). Acellular; listed here because the brief asked for Carmell.

regulatory.reference: IND for severe open tibia fractures with FDA agreement to a Phase 2 trial; Fast Track designation (2020); development deprioritized and clinical studies ceased (Longevity Health FY2025 10-K)
on_label_indications: None (investigational biologic; no BLA)

challenge: A BLA-path bone biologic abandoned for cosmetics; the company's earlier Phase II open-tibia results were company-reported and no peer-reviewed publication was located.

applications.evidence_summary: Company-reported Phase II in open tibia fractures (fewer infections, faster healing); no publication located (PubMed search 'plasma-based genipin bone healing tibia fracture' 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Program paused; no active trial.

applications.evidence_summary: Planned Phase 2 vs autograft (NCT06258499) withdrawn, never started.
applications.caveats: No data.

evidence.title: Bone Healing Accelerant Versus Standard of Care for Open Tibia Fractures
evidence.finding: Withdrawn; combined into an international study that also never started.

evidence.title: Multiregion BHA in Open Tibia Fractures
evidence.finding: Withdrawn; never started, delayed until further notice.

evidence.title: Bone Healing Accelerant vs Autologous Bone Grafting for Hindfoot or Ankle Arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Withdrawn; never started.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None: 'we have deprioritized further research and development of these product candidates and ceased clinical studies' (FY2025 10-K, filed March 2026)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable (investigational).
bd.notes: Candidate for out-licensing if anyone wants an IND-stage plasma biologic with Fast Track history.

name: Gene therapy for bone regeneration (BMP-2/BMP-7/VEGF via adenoviral, AAV or non-viral vectors) - preclinical only
company: Academic groups (e.g., Mayo, UCLA, Pittsburgh, Jerusalem; Kolon TissueGene for cartilage)
ownership_history: Not applicable.
composition: Regional gene therapy: osteogenic transgenes delivered by viral vectors or transduced cells on scaffolds to critical-size defects, fractures or fusion beds

regulatory.reference: No US IND for a bone-healing gene therapy identified; no gene therapy on FDA's approved CGT list is for bone (list current Sept 17, 2026).

applications.evidence_summary: Rodent and large-animal models show adenoviral or cell-based BMP-2 delivery can heal critical-size defects; immunogenicity, dose control and ectopic bone have kept the field preclinical for 25 years.
applications.caveats: One-line record by design; no clinical data.

evidence.title: Constructing Gene-Enhanced Tissue Engineering for Regeneration and Repair of Osteochondral Defects (Adv Biosyst 2019; DOI 10.1002/adbi.201900004)
evidence.finding: Example of adenovirus-vector growth-factor gene delivery combined with scaffolds achieving osteochondral repair in an animal model.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Placeholder so the app can state plainly that no gene therapy for bone is in US clinical testing.

name: Intradiscal rhGDF-5 for early lumbar disc degeneration - not advanced past Phase 2
ownership_history: Sponsor of record DePuy Spine (now DePuy Synthes). rhGDF-5 (also called BMP-14 / MP52) is a BMP-family growth factor; its origin at Biopharm GmbH (Heidelberg) is from general knowledge and was not confirmed in a source read.
composition: Recombinant human growth and differentiation factor-5 (a BMP-family protein) given as a single intradiscal injection; two doses tested.

regulatory.reference: US IND (number not public). Four DePuy Spine trials, all completed with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00813813 (Phase 1/2, n=32), NCT01124006 (Phase 2 randomized placebo-controlled, n=24), NCT01182337 (Phase 1/2, n=31), NCT01158924 (Phase 1/2, n=40). No Phase 3 registered.

applications.evidence_summary: Largest controlled study is NCT01124006 (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, n=24, two doses); the primary outcome was neurological safety at 12 months with ODI and VAS as secondary measures. Results are posted only on ClinicalTrials.gov; no peer-reviewed publication located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Grade I by design only: n=24, safety-primary, sponsor-only registry results. No later-phase trial was registered, which suggests the program was dropped (not confirmed by J&J).

evidence.title: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 2 doses of intradiscal rhGDF-5 for early-stage lumbar disc degeneration
evidence.finding: Completed 2014; results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (safety primary); no publication.

evidence.title: Intradiscal rhGDF-5 Phase I/II Clinical Trial
evidence.finding: Completed 2013; results posted; no publication.

evidence.title: Single administration intradiscal rhGDF-5 for early-stage lumbar disc degeneration
evidence.finding: Completed 2014; results posted; no publication.

evidence.title: Single administration intradiscal rhGDF-5 for early-stage lumbar disc degeneration
evidence.finding: Completed 2014; results posted; no publication.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None; no activity registered since 2014.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: A big-strategic intradiscal biologic that went quiet after Phase 2; relevant precedent for Mesoblast and DiscGenics.

name: NB1 (rhNELL-1 with DBM)
ownership_history: Bone Biologics Corp (NASDAQ: BBLG), Burlington, MA; exclusive worldwide license from UCLA for NELL-1 in spine fusion, trauma and osteoporosis; historically MTF Biologics was a major shareholder and the DBM carrier partner (not confirmed in sources fetched here).
composition: Recombinant human NEL-like molecule-1 (NELL-1) osteoinductive protein combined with demineralized bone matrix; proposed as a more bone-specific signal than BMP-2 with less ectopic bone and inflammation

regulatory.reference: No US IDE yet; pilot study design reviewed by FDA Division of Orthopedic Devices in a Pre-Submission; pilot run under Australian HREC approval

applications.evidence_summary: NCT03810573: multicenter randomized pilot in up to 30 adults with single-level DDD (L2-S1, up to Grade 1 listhesis) undergoing TLIF in Australia; first two patients treated June 2024; expanded to six Australian sites September 2026 with enrollment targeted to finish by end of 2026; primary endpoints fusion at 12 and 24 months and ODI change; 12-month data expected Q4 2027. Only preclinical efficacy data exist.
applications.caveats: Comparator not specified in public materials; company reports cash runway only through Q2 2027.

evidence.title: Multi-center, prospective, parallel group, randomized pilot study of NB1 bone graft device in DDD patients undergoing TLIF
evidence.finding: Recruiting (Australia); primary completion December 2026.

evidence.title: Nell-1 protein promotes bone formation in a sheep spinal fusion model (Tissue Eng Part A 2011; DOI 10.1089/ten.TEA.2010.0486)
evidence.finding: NELL-1 at 0.3 or 0.6 mg/mL with DBM (n=8/group) or heat-inactivated DBM (n=4/group) increased interbody bone formation vs DBM alone in sheep.
