pipeline.expected_milestone: Pilot 12-month data Q4 2027, then US IDE pivotal and PMA (company statements, Sept 2026)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Micro-cap with a single asset; the 'hard healers' (smokers, diabetics, obese) positioning overlaps directly with PearlMatrix's high-risk subgroup claims.

name: Osteogrow (rhBMP6 in autologous blood coagulum) / Osteogrow-C
ownership_history: Genera Research Ltd (Zagreb, Croatia; Slobodan Vukicevic), EU FP7-funded OSTEOGROW project; a related rhBMP6 product (AGA111, Angitia Biopharmaceuticals) was tested in a US/China TLIF RCT, relationship to Genera unverified.
composition: Recombinant human BMP-6 delivered in an autologous blood coagulum carrier, mixed with cancellous allograft (Osteogrow-A) or synthetic calcium phosphate ceramics (Osteogrow-C)

regulatory.reference: EU clinical trials only: EudraCT 2017-000860-14 (Osteogrow-A, PLIF, 143 randomized in Austria, ended 13 Mar 2023, results posted 11 Feb 2026) and a TLIF trial; no US IDE/IND found
on_label_indications: Investigational: fracture nonunion, HTO gap healing, distal radius fracture, dental (company list)

applications.evidence_summary: Osteogrow-A phase II (EudraCT 2017-000860-14): randomized, double-blind, n=143 at three Austrian centers (62 ICBG standard of care, 61 high-dose 2 mg rhBMP6, 20 low-dose 1 mg) in PLIF for L3-S1 DDD; 20-month composite 'overall clinical success' was very low in every arm, bilateral bridging was observed in only 4-6% of subjects in any arm, and the sponsor concluded the success definition was overly strict; fewer serious AEs with Osteogrow (31.1% HD vs 54.1% SoC); results posted February 2026. A separate 63-patient placebo-controlled rhBMP6 (AGA111) TLIF RCT was presented at AAOS 2025. Earlier Genera trials were in distal radius fracture and high tibial osteotomy.
applications.caveats: The posted PLIF fusion numbers are implausibly low for any arm and should be read from the EU register directly before being quoted; no peer-reviewed spine publication retrieved.

applications.evidence_summary: Preclinical only: rabbit and sheep posterolateral fusion with rhBMP6/ABC plus ceramics (PMID 38086987).
applications.caveats: No human PLF data.

applications.evidence_summary: EU-funded phase I/II in HTO distraction-gap healing and distal radius fractures (CORDIS project page describes plans; peer-reviewed phase II results were not retrieved in this sweep). ClinicalTrials.gov search for OSTEOGROW/rhBMP6 returned nothing.
applications.caveats: Company-reported status only; no registry or FDA footprint found.
applications.challenge: Verify any trial claim against EU CTIS before citing.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase III in nonunion is a stated plan, not a registered trial.
applications.caveats: Unverified.

applications.evidence_summary: Randomized, double-blind Phase 1 (n=32) in closed distal radius fractures treated with K-wires: 250 ug rhBMP6/mL coagulum injected at the fracture accelerated CT/radiographic healing vs placebo coagulum and standard of care at 5 and 9 weeks (p=0.027), with no difference by 13 weeks; no anti-BMP6 antibodies; no serious adverse reactions (Bone 2020).
applications.caveats: Tiny n, short-term radiographic surrogate, sponsor-affiliated authors; effect disappeared by 13 weeks.

evidence.title: Patient- and evaluator-blinded non-inferiority study of Osteogrow in adults undergoing PLIF for degenerative disc disease (Osteogrow-A)
evidence.finding: Non-inferiority claimed on a composite endpoint with very low success in all arms; fewer SAEs with rhBMP6; trial ended March 2023, results posted February 2026.

evidence.title: Calcium phosphate ceramics combined with rhBMP6 within autologous blood coagulum promote posterolateral lumbar fusion in sheep
evidence.finding: Osteogrow-C produced radiographic fusion with complete integration to transverse processes in sheep.

evidence.title: A novel autologous bone graft substitute comprised of rhBMP6 blood coagulum as carrier tested in a randomized and controlled Phase I trial in patients with distal radial fractures (Bone 2020; DOI 10.1016/j.bone.2020.115551)
evidence.finding: Accelerated trabecular healing at 5 and 9 weeks vs placebo and standard of care; equivalent by 13 weeks; good tolerability.

evidence.title: Recombinant Human BMP6 Applied Within Autologous Blood Coagulum Accelerates Bone Healing: Randomized Controlled Trial in High Tibial Osteotomy Patients (J Bone Miner Res 2020; DOI 10.1002/jbmr.4107)
evidence.finding: First placebo-controlled BMP trial on a trabecular bone surface; CT BMD in the wedge defect roughly doubled vs placebo at 9 and 14 weeks.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No US filing announced; next step unclear (company website undated)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Academic-origin program; the autologous-blood-carrier concept avoids collagen sponge and is pitched as lower-dose, lower-inflammation BMP.

challenge: EU CTR results page read directly on 2026-10-22. As posted: arms Standard of Care n=62 (55 mITT), HD Osteogrow n=61 (56 mITT), LD Osteogrow n=20 (19 mITT); primary 'overall clinical success' at 20 months 1.9% SoC vs 0.2% HD (LD none), difference -1.7 points, one-sided 95% lower limit -5.2 against a -10 margin, reported as non-inferior; radiographic fusion 3.8/5.6% at 6 months, 4.4/6.0% at 12 months, 6.2% SoC vs 4.2% HD at 20 months (difference -2, lower limit -9.5); serious TEAEs 54.1% SoC, 31.1% HD, 25.0% LD; 3 deaths in SoC. These success and fusion proportions are implausibly low for PLIF and almost certainly reflect a unit or data-entry error in the register posting (e.g. fractions mislabeled as percent); the extraction is verified but the numbers should not be quoted as fusion rates without the sponsor's publication.

name: PCRX-201 (enekinragene inzadenovec, intra-articular IL-1Ra gene therapy)
ownership_history: Pacira program.
composition: Helper-dependent adenoviral vector encoding interleukin-1 receptor antagonist injected once into the knee.

regulatory.reference: phase 2 ASCEND NCT06884865 (recruiting); RMAT designation reported by Pacira
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: Two-year phase 1 data (Ann Rheum Dis, August 2026 per Pacira release) reported exploratory improvements in pain, stiffness and function; the phase 2 ASCEND study (n=135, Part A enrollment closed June 2026) has no results, with topline expected by end of 2026.
applications.caveats: Open-label exploratory phase 1; gene therapy durability and safety unknown at scale.

evidence.title: Safety and tolerability of PCRX-201 in subjects with painful osteoarthritis of the knee (phase 2)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; topline expected by end of 2026; no results yet.

bd.reimbursement: Not approved.
bd.notes: Pacira's follow-on to Zilretta in knee OA; RMAT designation per company releases.

pipeline.expected_milestone: ASCEND topline by end of 2026 (Pacira release via search)

name: Regenexx (clinic-network bone marrow concentrate and PRP procedures for knee OA)
company: Regenexx / Centeno-Schultz Clinic (Regenerative Sciences, LLC heritage)
ownership_history: Procedure brand licensed to a clinic network; Regenerative Sciences, LLC was the defendant in the FDA case below.
composition: Not a product: point-of-care autologous bone marrow concentrate and PRP injections (own-clinic protocols); the historical Regenexx-C was a culture-expanded autologous cell product.

regulatory.reference: none; FDA position: Regenexx-C (cultured, expanded cells) was held a drug in United States v. Regenerative Sciences (D.D.C. 2012, aff'd D.C. Cir. 2014, No. 12-5254), requiring BLA/IND; point-of-care concentrates are treated through the BMAC and PRP device-kit pathways (see those records)
on_label_indications: None; cash-pay clinic procedures

applications.evidence_summary: Centeno's own dose-response series (PMID 26385099) and registry-style papers report symptomatic improvement after BMAC for knee OA; no randomized, independent trial of the Regenexx protocol was located. For PRP and BMAC comparators in knee OA see the prp-bmac-adipose slice, not this record.
applications.caveats: Network-authored, uncontrolled data; cash-pay. The 2014 court decision applies to culture-expanded cells, not to same-visit concentrates.

evidence.title: A dose response analysis of a specific bone marrow concentrate treatment protocol for knee osteoarthritis (Centeno, BMC Musculoskelet Disord)
evidence.finding: Registry analysis relating nucleated-cell dose to patient-reported outcomes after one BMAC protocol; uncontrolled.

bd.reimbursement: Not covered; patient pays cash.
bd.notes: Included only as a class record with the FDA position; PRP knee-OA comparators are in the prp-bmac-adipose slice.

name: TETRANITE regenerative bone adhesive (cranial flap fixation)
composition: Synthetic, injectable, self-setting calcium phosphate and phosphoserine-based bone adhesive that resorbs and is replaced by bone; derived from sandcastle-worm chemistry (LaunchPad Medical origin)

regulatory.reference: FDA IDE approval December 2023 for a 20-patient pilot of stand-alone cranial flap fixation; NIH NINDS Phase II SBIR $2.4M September 2024; sites Semmes Murphey (Memphis) and Brigham and Women's (Boston)

applications.evidence_summary: First five patients enrolled by September 2024 with company-reported radiographic adhesion and no complications at over three months in the first patient; no peer-reviewed results or NCT number located as of 2026-10-22.
applications.caveats: Company statements only; would replace plates and screws rather than a biologic; a De Novo or PMA is the likely path.

evidence.title: RevBio receives $2.4 million NIH grant for first-in-human trial of regenerative bone adhesive for cranial flap fixation and enrolls first five patients
evidence.finding: 20-patient pilot under an FDA-approved IDE; five enrolled; early radiographs reported as showing continued adhesion of the flap with no complications.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Completion of the 20-patient pilot and a pivotal design; no date published (RevBio press releases 2023 and 2024).

bd.reimbursement: n/a
bd.notes: If it works, it competes with cranial fixation plates (hardware) and with Montage Flowable's registered flap-fixation study, not with void fillers.

name: TG-C (TissueGene-C; Invossa) - adjacent, knee osteoarthritis
company: Kolon TissueGene, Inc. (US subsidiary of Kolon Life Science, Korea)
ownership_history: Invossa-K was approved by Korea's MFDS in 2017 and the license was revoked in 2019 after the second cell component proved to be kidney-derived (GP2-293) rather than chondrocyte-derived; FDA placed the US Phase 3 on clinical hold in May 2019 and lifted it in April 2020, with broader recruitment resuming November 2021 (CGTLive 2026-07-23).
composition: Allogeneic human chondrocytes mixed 3:1 with irradiated, TGF-beta1-transduced cells (GP2-293 derived), single intra-articular injection; a cell-mediated gene therapy

regulatory.reference: US IND; two Phase 3 trials (ACTiVION-I NCT03203330, n=535; ACTiVION-II NCT03291470). Not approved anywhere after the Korean revocation.
on_label_indications: None in the US (investigational)

challenge: Adjacent (cartilage/OA, not bone); kept as a live example of cell-therapy risk: ACTiVION-II missed its co-primary endpoints on 2026-07-20 (between-group VAS difference 0.5 points, p=0.83).

applications.evidence_summary: Korean Phase III (n=163, K-L 3, intra-articular TG-C vs placebo, 52 weeks): significant improvement in IKDC and VAS at 26, 39 and 52 weeks (published 2018). US Phase 3 (NCT03203330/NCT03291470, K-L 2-3) readout reported negative in mid-2026 by an aggregator (unverified).
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; Korean trial population and endpoint differ from US; cell/gene therapy safety scrutiny; a post-hoc structure-modification claim is unproven.
applications.challenge: Primary-source confirmation of the 2026 US Phase 3 topline is missing; treat the 'missed primary endpoint' line as unverified.

evidence.title: ACTiVION-II: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 of TG-C in knee OA
evidence.finding: Missed co-primary endpoints (company release, July 2026, via CGTLive).

evidence.title: ACTiVION-I: Phase 3 of TG-C in KL grade 2-3 knee OA
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; 44 sites; primary completion July 2024; topline expected Oct 2026.

evidence.title: A Multicenter, Double-Blind, Phase III Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of a Cell and Gene Therapy in Knee Osteoarthritis Patients
evidence.finding: TG-C beat placebo on IKDC and VAS at 26, 39 and 52 weeks; WOMAC and KOOS also favored TG-C.

pipeline.expected_milestone: ACTiVION-II (NCT03291470) read out 2026-07-20 and missed both co-primary endpoints (VAS and WOMAC at month 12; placebo response high); ACTiVION-I (NCT03203330, n=535) topline was guided for October 2026 and had not been found as of 2026-10-22. A Phase 1 in discogenic back pain (NCT06144970) is registered as not yet recruiting.

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Benchmark for the cost of a two-trial US Phase 3 program in a cell therapy; parent company exposure to Korean regulatory and legal history.

name: VIA Disc NP (nucleus pulposus allograft)
ownership_history: VIVEX Biologics (Miami; formerly VIVEX Biomedical). Product earlier marketed as VIA Disc Matrix.
composition: Micronized, processed human nucleus pulposus allograft (with cells, viability not claimed as mechanism) reconstituted with saline and injected intradiscally

regulatory.reference: Marketed on the manufacturer's determination that supplementation of nucleus pulposus tissue is a minimally manipulated, homologous use; no FDA premarket review. ClinicalTrials.gov: ASCEND NCT06615505 (Vivex; n=121 actual; active not recruiting; primary completion 2026-02-06) and a sham-controlled pivotal-size trial NCT06778447 (n=325 estimated; recruiting; primary completion est. 2027-10); the sponsor's regulatory intent (361 versus BLA) is still not public.
on_label_indications: Supplementation of degenerated nucleus pulposus tissue (361 homologous-use positioning; not an FDA-approved indication)

challenge: Trial records re-checked on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06615505 active not recruiting, NCT06778447 recruiting). No FDA letter, RFD or BLA statement about VIA Disc NP was found in FDA letters or web search, so the 361-versus-BLA tension remains an open question; the 2018 market year is still secondary-source.

applications.evidence_summary: VAST trial (NCT03709901; 218 enrolled, 13 US sites) randomized 3.5:1:1 to allograft, saline, or nonsurgical management; the published interim report (Beall 2020, n=24) was descriptive and not powered; sponsor-reported 12-month data in the larger cohort showed VAS improvement with no separation from saline until after 3 months. A 2:1 sham-controlled 325-patient trial began Feb 2025.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; published data are a 24-subject interim with 4 placebo patients; full VAST results not peer-reviewed in PubMed at review; VA Office of Community Care review notes conflicts of interest not disclosed in the journal article.

evidence.title: VAST Clinical Trial: Safely Supplementing Tissue Lost to Degenerative Disc Disease (Int J Spine Surg 2020; DOI 10.14444/7033)
evidence.finding: Interim analysis of the first 24 subjects (16 allograft, 4 saline, 4 NSM crossover): VAS fell from 54.8 to 12.3 (allograft) and 55.3 to 19.7 (saline) at 12 months; adverse events transient; not powered for significance.

evidence.title: Randomized, sham-controlled, double-blind trial of nucleus pulposus allograft in lumbar discogenic pain
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 19 sites; started Feb 17, 2025; 2:1 randomization vs sham; primary completion Oct 2027.

evidence.title: ASCEND: randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled Phase I/II of VIA Disc NP
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; 5 sites; primary completion Feb 2026; results not posted.

evidence.title: VIA Disc NP Registry 3.0
evidence.finding: Observational registry at 24 sites; primary completion Jan 2027. Prior registry (NCT04652687, n=83) terminated.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Pivotal sham-controlled trial primary completion Oct 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov); regulatory intent (361 vs BLA) not publicly stated.

bd.reimbursement: Sold today as a 361 tissue through pain-management and spine practices; CPT 0627T-0630T (intradiscal allogeneic disc tissue injection) exist as Category III codes; most commercial payers deem it investigational (e.g., VA review cites non-coverage).
bd.notes: Commercial exposure: if FDA concluded the product fails homologous use, current sales would be of an unlicensed biologic. Regenexx (a competitor) publicly critiques the VAST data.

name: rhFGF-2 (trafermin) gelatin hydrogel for fracture healing - Japanese program, not approved for fracture
ownership_history: Trafermin (recombinant human basic FGF) is Kaken Pharmaceutical's molecule (marketed in Japan for other uses: Fiblast skin-ulcer spray; Regroth for periodontal regeneration, per general knowledge, unverified here). The tibial fracture RCT was run by the TESK Group led by the University of Tokyo; Kaken sponsorship of the fracture trials was not confirmed.
composition: rhFGF-2 (0.8 or 2.4 mg) in a gelatin hydrogel injected into the fracture gap after IM nailing; a separate Japanese series mixed rhFGF-2 with beta-TCP granules and hyaluronate as an injectable paste.

regulatory.reference: Not approved for fracture in Japan or the US; no US IND or ClinicalTrials.gov fracture trial located (search 2026-10-23).

applications.evidence_summary: Kawaguchi 2010 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (70 completers; 24 placebo, 23 low, 23 high dose): faster cumulative radiographic union with rhFGF-2 (p=.031 low, p=.009 high vs placebo); delayed union at 24 weeks in 4, 1 and 0 patients.
applications.caveats: Small trial (85 eligible of 194 screened), radiographic surrogate endpoint, no secondary interventions in any arm; not replicated and no approval followed.

applications.evidence_summary: Tanaka 2012 case series (n=25, AO 31.A2, ages 76-91): rhFGF-2/beta-TCP/hyaluronate paste with IM nail; all fractures united and the lesser trochanter united in 24 of 25 by 12 weeks.
applications.caveats: No control group; single center.

evidence.title: A local application of recombinant human fibroblast growth factor 2 for tibial shaft fractures: a randomized, placebo-controlled trial
evidence.finding: rhFGF-2 groups reached radiographic union sooner than placebo; no dose response between 0.8 and 2.4 mg.

evidence.title: Local application of rhFGF-2 on bone repair: a dose-escalation prospective trial on patients with osteotomy
evidence.finding: Dose-escalation safety study preceding the tibial RCT.

evidence.title: Use of an injectable complex of beta-TCP granules, hyaluronate, and FGF-2 on repair of unstable intertrochanteric fractures
evidence.finding: All 25 unions; marked new bone around the lesser trochanter; uncontrolled.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Ex-US historical program; the only growth factor besides BMP and PDGF with a positive fracture RCT.

name: AMPLEX (B2A peptide on HA/beta-TCP granules)
company: Ferring Pharmaceuticals (sponsor of pivotal); originally BioSET Inc
ownership_history: BioSET (Texas) developed the B2A synthetic BMP-2 receptor-targeting peptide; Ferring sponsored the hindfoot/ankle pivotal (NCT03028415) after licensing; commercial status after 2020 completion not public.
composition: Synthetic peptide B2A that augments BMP-2 receptor signaling, coated on hydroxyapatite/beta-TCP ceramic granules

regulatory.reference: Pivotal IDE study NCT03028415 (Ferring; ankle fusion and hindfoot; n=56; completed, primary completion 2020-01-09); no PMA exists: openFDA PMA search for trade name AMPLEX returns nothing and Ferring's only PMAs are Euflexxa (P010029) and Nuxflexxa
on_label_indications: Investigational: supplemental graft in single, double or triple hindfoot or ankle arthrodesis (not trauma)

applications.evidence_summary: Included because the brief asked; AMPLEX has no trauma program. The pivotal (n=56 randomized vs autograft, 38 US/Canada sites, completed July 2020) has results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov but the outcome was not retrieved and no PMA has been announced, which suggests the program stalled.
applications.caveats: No trauma relevance; elective fusion only.

applications.evidence_summary: NCT03028415: multicenter randomized pivotal study of AMPLEX vs autogenous bone graft in hindfoot or ankle arthrodesis, 36 sites, listed enrollment 56, completed January 2020; no results posted and no FDA decision or publication found. Pilot NCT01224119 (24 patients, 2011-2012).
applications.caveats: A 56-patient enrollment at 36 sites suggests the pivotal trial was stopped or under-enrolled; program status unknown.

evidence.title: Multi-center randomized pivotal study evaluating AMPLEX compared to autogenous bone graft in hindfoot or ankle arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Completed; primary endpoint a 5-part composite at 52 weeks; results posted; no publication or PMA found.

evidence.title: Multi-center randomized pilot study evaluating Amplex compared to autograft bone in foot and ankle fusion surgery
evidence.finding: Pilot; status unknown.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Unknown; no public update since 2020.

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Peptide-on-ceramic is the same construct class as i-Factor (P-15); that is the comparator a hiring manager will raise.

name: KUR-113 / Fibrin-PTH (TGplPTH1-34 in fibrin)
ownership_history: Originated at Kuros Biosurgery AG (Zurich); Kuros merged with Xpand Biotechnology (2016), later acquired by... (no; Kuros remains independent, SIX: KURN) and now markets MagnetOs synthetic bone graft; Fibrin-PTH was discontinued per the company's FY2023 report (March 13, 2024).
composition: Engineered PTH(1-34) fragment with a transglutaminase substrate and plasmin-cleavable linker, covalently bound into a fibrin matrix applied at the fracture or fusion site

regulatory.reference: US IND for the STRUCTURE Phase 2 TLIF trial NCT04294004 (Kuros Biosurgery AG; n=50 actual; start 2020-08-27; ClinicalTrials.gov status UNKNOWN, last updated 2023-08-09; flagged FDA-regulated drug). Discontinuation after Phase 2 is reported only in the Synapse summary of Kuros releases; no Kuros primary document was retrieved.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2 randomized, open-label (dose-blinded) trial in 200 open tibial shaft fractures (NCT00533793; JBJS 2022): 6-month healing 76%, 80% and 69% for low, mid and high dose plus standard of care vs 65% for standard of care alone; the mid-dose met the prespecified primary endpoint.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; open-label; non-monotonic dose response; no Phase 3 followed in fracture.

applications.evidence_summary: STRUCTURE Phase 2 (NCT04294004, n=50, two dose levels vs local autograft in single-level TLIF) completed enrollment July 2023; results were not published and the company elected not to proceed to Phase 3.
applications.caveats: Registry status 'unknown' (last verified Aug 2023); the only public efficacy signal is the company's decision to stop.

evidence.title: Novel Parathyroid Hormone-Based Bone Graft, KUR-113, in Treatment of Acute Open Tibial Shaft Fracture: A Phase-2 Randomized Controlled Trial (J Bone Joint Surg Am 2022; DOI 10.2106/JBJS.20.02109; erratum PMID 35442252)
evidence.finding: Four arms (SoC; SoC + 4 mL KUR-113 at 0.133, 0.4 or 1.0 mg/mL); mid-dose met the primary healing endpoint at 6 months (80% vs 65%).

evidence.title: STRUCTURE: KUR-113 bone graft vs local autograft in single-level TLIF (Phase 2)
evidence.finding: Enrollment completed July 2023 (company); results not posted; program discontinued Dec 2023.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None; discontinued (company FY2023 results, March 2024, as summarized by Synapse; primary Kuros document not retrieved).

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Kuros redeployed capital to MagnetOs (510(k) synthetic), which is now running RCTs vs Trinity Elite (NCT05037968) and vs DBM (NCT04679844). A PTH-in-fibrin asset could be licensed.

challenge: Registry record confirms the Phase 2 (NCT04294004, n=50, status UNKNOWN since 2023). The discontinuation decision still rests on a secondary summary; Kuros IR pages return 403, so the primary document was not read.

name: Lorecivivint (SM04690, Wnt pathway modulator)
ownership_history: Developed by Samumed (now Biosplice).
composition: Small-molecule CLK/DYRK inhibitor suspension for intra-articular injection once or twice a year.

regulatory.reference: NDA submitted to FDA, announced 2026-01-06 (Biosplice release via press coverage); acceptance and PDUFA date not located
on_label_indications: None yet; sponsor seeks a knee osteoarthritis indication

applications.evidence_summary: Three phase 3 trials missed their primary pain endpoints: STRIDES (NCT05603754, n=499) change in knee pain at week 12 was -3.64 with lorecivivint vs -3.54 with vehicle (p=0.543); OA-10 (NCT04385303, 28 weeks) -2.15 vs -2.22 (p=0.703); OA-11 (NCT03928184, 56 weeks) -2.24 vs -2.49 (p=0.185). Biosplice says the NDA rests on 11 trials including OA-07 (NCT04520607 long-term extension, terminated, n=276), where it reports gains at 6 and 12 months.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; the sponsor's positive claims come from extension and post-hoc timepoints, not from a prespecified primary win; the NDA's clinical package is exactly what an FDA reviewer will question.
applications.challenge: Be able to say that three phase 3 primary endpoints failed (STRIDES, OA-10, OA-11) and that the NDA is built on a different trial and structural (joint space width) secondaries.

evidence.title: STRIDES: safety and efficacy of lorecivivint (SM04690) for knee osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Primary endpoint (week-12 pain NRS) not met: -3.64 lorecivivint vs -3.54 vehicle, difference -0.12 (95% CI -0.53 to 0.28), p=0.543; WOMAC function also null.

evidence.title: A phase 3, 28-week, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (OA-10) of a single lorecivivint injection (Yazici, Clin Exp Rheumatol)
evidence.finding: Primary pain endpoint not met (registry: -2.15 vs -2.22, p=0.703).

evidence.title: A phase 3, 56-week randomised placebo-controlled study (OA-11) with patient-reported and radiographic outcomes (Yazici, Clin Exp Rheumatol)
evidence.finding: Primary pain endpoint not met (registry: -2.24 vs -2.49, p=0.185).

bd.reimbursement: Not approved; no reimbursement pathway yet.
bd.notes: Biosplice is private; an approval would be the first DMOAD-style small molecule for knee OA, but the filing's efficacy support is contested.

pipeline.expected_milestone: NDA submitted January 2026; FDA filing acceptance and action date not located

name: RTX-GRT7039 (resiniferatoxin, intra-articular)
ownership_history: Licensed from Sorrento Therapeutics, whose own phase 3 trials were withdrawn (registry); the license chain was not sourced.
composition: Ultrapotent TRPV1 agonist injected into the knee to silence pain-sensing nerve endings, a non-steroid, non-HA analgesic.

regulatory.reference: phase 3 NCT05248386, NCT05449132, NCT05377489; Breakthrough Therapy designation reported by Grünenthal (search summary); no filing located
on_label_indications: None yet

applications.evidence_summary: Three phase 3 trials are complete (about 466-714 patients each). Registry-posted LS-mean WOMAC pain change at week 12 was -3.25 vs -2.99 (single injection, NCT05449132) and -2.96 vs -2.85 (repeat injections, NCT05248386), and week-26 values were near-equal in the repeat study; no p-values are posted and no topline press release was located.
applications.caveats: Registry numbers only; effect over placebo appears small. Do not infer a pass or fail.

evidence.title: Comparison of a single RTX-GRT7039 and placebo intra-articular injection for pain associated with osteoarthritis of the knee
evidence.finding: Posted week-12 WOMAC pain LS-mean change -3.25 RTX vs -2.99 placebo; week 26 -3.27 vs -2.82; no p-values posted.

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of repeated RTX-GRT7039 injections in knee osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Posted week-12 WOMAC pain LS-mean change -2.959 RTX vs -2.847 placebo; week 26 -2.564 vs -2.597; no p-values posted.

bd.reimbursement: Not approved.
bd.notes: Grünenthal is private; a filing decision was expected in 2025 per its 2023 annual results, outcome not located.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Submission decision expected 2025 per sponsor; status not located

name: Sprifermin (rhFGF-18)
company: Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany (EMD Serono in the US)
ownership_history: Merck KGaA (EMD Serono is its US healthcare business; the FORWARD sponsor is listed as EMD Serono R&D Institute).
composition: Recombinant truncated human fibroblast growth factor 18, given as three weekly intra-articular injections per cycle.

regulatory.reference: phase 2 FORWARD (NCT01919164); no phase 3 or filing located
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: FORWARD (n=549, 2-year primary): 100 µg every 6 months increased total femorotibial cartilage thickness by about 0.05 mm over placebo, and WOMAC differences from placebo were not statistically significant; the 5-year follow-up is Eckstein 2021 (PMID 33962962; its abstract was not extracted here).
applications.caveats: A structural MRI surrogate with sub-millimeter effect; no phase 3 located; sponsor-funded. Whether Merck KGaA retains the asset was not confirmed.

evidence.title: Effect of intra-articular sprifermin vs placebo on femorotibial joint cartilage thickness in patients with osteoarthritis: the FORWARD randomized clinical trial (Hochberg, JAMA)
evidence.finding: 100 µg every 6 months raised 2-year cartilage thickness by 0.05 mm versus placebo; no significant WOMAC difference.

evidence.title: Long-term structural and symptomatic effects of intra-articular sprifermin in patients with knee osteoarthritis: 5-year results from the FORWARD study (Eckstein, Ann Rheum Dis)
evidence.finding: Five-year follow-up of FORWARD reporting structural and symptomatic outcomes (abstract not extracted here).

bd.reimbursement: Not approved.
bd.notes: Frequently cited as the proof that cartilage thickness can be moved without proof that symptoms follow.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No phase 3 start located (searched 2026-10-23)

name: Bioventus BMP portfolio (next-generation BMP licensed from Pfizer, 2013) - status not disclosed
ownership_history: On 2013-07-01 Bioventus took an exclusive worldwide license to Pfizer's BMP development portfolio: an unnamed next-generation BMP, rights to rhBMP-2 in fields previously reserved to Pfizer, and an option on a soft-tissue BMP program; Pfizer to manufacture and supply rhBMP-2. Bioventus retained former Wyeth BMP scientists and planned a Boston lab.
composition: Not disclosed (next-generation BMP; rhBMP-2).

regulatory.reference: No IND, IDE or ClinicalTrials.gov registration located for a Bioventus BMP product (ClinicalTrials.gov search 2026-10-23).

pipeline.expected_milestone: None public; whether the program continues was not confirmed from Bioventus filings (EDGAR full-text search was blocked).

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Bioventus's marketed biologics (OSTEOAMP, SIGNAFUSE, EXOGEN) are separate records; this entry only documents where Pfizer's rhBMP-2 rights went.

name: Gu You Dao rhBMP-2 bone repair material (China; plus other NMPA-registered Chinese rhBMP-2 products) - not US-marketed
ownership_history: Hangzhou Jiuyuan Gene Engineering Co. listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange main board on 2024-11-28 (2566.HK); listing coverage describes Gu You Dao as China's first rhBMP-2 bone repair material and the top-selling bone repair material in China by 2023 revenue (a company/prospectus claim, not independently verified). Shanghai Rebone Biomaterials holds a US patent on E. coli rhBMP-2 production (US7947821), but no Rebone-branded finished product or NMPA registration was confirmed.
composition: rhBMP-2 on a bone repair carrier; carrier, dose and expression system not confirmed from a primary source.

regulatory.reference: No FDA submission. NMPA (China) registration claimed in company materials; registration number, year and labeled indications not verified (NMPA database not accessed).

challenge: Established in China by company account, but has no US status; cannot be imported for clinical use outside an IDE. Novosis (Korea) is the separate record for CGBio/Daewoong.

applications.evidence_summary: No study naming Gu You Dao located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Chinese rhBMP-2 interbody data exist without product attribution, e.g., Chen 2024 randomized PE-PLIF study (n=102): 12-month fusion 86.3% rhBMP-2 vs 54.9% autograft, product not named.
applications.caveats: Product attribution missing; single-center Chinese data; 54.9% autograft fusion at 12 months is unusually low.

evidence.title: Application of rhBMP-2 in percutaneous endoscopic posterior lumbar interbody fusion
evidence.finding: Fusion 86.27% vs 54.90% at 12 months and less cage displacement with rhBMP-2; product not identified.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable in the US.
bd.notes: Context for the global rhBMP-2 market: Korea (Novosis) and China have domestic rhBMP-2 grafts; the US has only Infuse.

name: LDGraft (low-dose encapsulated rhBMP-2)
ownership_history: Locate Bio Ltd (Nottingham, UK), private; raised GBP 9.2 million in April 2024 to fund the RESTORE study; US subsidiary Locate Bio Pty/Inc.
composition: rhBMP-2 pre-encapsulated in a resorbable polymer (dose-shielding microparticles) within a bone graft substitute carrier, designed for sustained 28-day release at doses well below Infuse

regulatory.reference: Breakthrough Device designation May 2023 (single-level ALIF, L3-S1, DDD); FDA IDE approval announced 2025-09-08. ClinicalTrials.gov has two LDGraft records: NCT06462729 (Locate Bio Pty Ltd; Phase 1/2, ALIF, n=40 estimated; IDE-flagged unapproved device; recruiting since 2024-11-12; sites in Newcastle, Australia and Fort Wayne, Nashville and Pinehurst, US; last update 2026-08-26) and NCT07858643 (Locate Bio Ltd; 'AMBITION', n=25, sites in Tbilisi, Georgia; started 2026-04-08). NCT06462729 is the registration that matches the Australia-plus-US IDE study.
on_label_indications: Investigational: single-level ALIF for degenerative disc disease (spine); no trauma indication proposed

applications.evidence_summary: RESTORE (NCT06462729): first-in-human, randomized 3:3:2 dose-finding, single-blind, two LDGraft doses vs 100% allograft in single-level ALIF (L3-S1) with cage and plate; n=40; sites in Australia (Newcastle) and US (Fort Wayne, Pinehurst, Nashville); started November 2024, primary completion December 2027. Preclinical: 120-sheep study reported all three doses equivalent to ICBG at 6 months.
applications.caveats: No human efficacy data; the brief's description of a TLIF/PLF trial was wrong, the trial is ALIF only.

applications.evidence_summary: No trauma program announced; included because a controlled-release BMP-2 would be the natural successor to Infuse in open fractures and nonunion if the spine study succeeds.
applications.caveats: Spine-only development; no trauma data.

evidence.title: A randomized study of LDGraft in single-level ALIF (RESTORE)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary endpoints CT fusion, no secondary surgery, ODI 15-point improvement, neuro status and no device-related SAE at 12 and 24 months.

evidence.title: AMBITION: a study of LDGraft in single-level lumbar interbody fusion (Phase 1/2, single group)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; start April 8, 2026; primary completion Oct 2027; two sites in Tbilisi, Georgia; excludes smokers, BMI > 40, osteoporosis.

pipeline.expected_milestone: RESTORE primary completion December 2027; pivotal IDE would follow (company statements)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable; would be bundled like Infuse if approved.
bd.notes: Positioned as 'Infuse efficacy at a fraction of the dose' to neutralize the YODA safety narrative; small company likely to need a commercial partner.

challenge: Two separate registrations exist; the Australia-plus-US IDE study is NCT06462729. The sponsor's 'RESTORE' name was not seen on either record.

name: Novosis / Novosis Putty (rhBMP-2 bone graft, Korea) - not US-marketed
company: CGBio (Korea); rhBMP-2 manufactured by Daewoong Pharmaceutical
ownership_history: Approved by Korea's MFDS as the country's first rhBMP-2 bone graft (year not confirmed); second-generation Novosis Putty received FDA Breakthrough Device designation in January 2024 (trade press). J&J and CGBIO signed an exclusive Asia-Pacific distribution and promotion deal in February 2025 (Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, India, Hong Kong, Macau; later expanded). On 2026-05-26 DePuy Synthes announced an exclusive distribution agreement with CGBIO for the US, Canada and Australia covering spine, CMF and trauma, with rights of first negotiation for other markets; CGBIO's release (2026-05-27) adds joint clinical development and regulatory steps including FDA IDE and PMA and a steering committee. No financial terms disclosed.
composition: E. coli-derived rhBMP-2 on a hydroxyapatite/calcium phosphate carrier (Novosis) or putty formulation (Novosis Putty)

regulatory.reference: Not cleared or approved in the US; FDA Breakthrough Device designation (Jan 2024, trade press). J&J MedTech's 2026-05-26 release says a US IDE study for spine procedures is approved and 'actively enrolling'; CGBIO's 2026-05-27 release says the IDE study is being prepared with a target start in the second half of 2026. The two statements conflict; no NCT number located.

applications.evidence_summary: Korean clinical data exist (e.g., Korea University publications on efficacy and safety of rhBMP-2) but no US trial; Breakthrough designation does not imply efficacy.
applications.caveats: Non-US product; included as the most credible 'second rhBMP-2' attempt and as a reminder that no rhBMP-2 generic or biosimilar pathway exists for a PMA combination product (Infuse is a device, so the biosimilar statute does not apply).

pipeline.expected_milestone: US spine IDE study (type not stated): J&J says approved and enrolling; CGBIO says start targeted for H2 2026. No PMA submission announced.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable in US.
bd.notes: A Chinese rhBMP-2 bone repair material (Hangzhou Jiuyuan) is listed as an implanted device registered in China; NMPA details not verified. Neither product can be imported for US clinical use outside an IDE.

challenge: The two companies' releases disagree on whether the US IDE has started enrolling; treat enrollment as unconfirmed until an NCT/IDE listing appears.

name: OsteoAdapt SP (spine) and OsteoAdapt DE (dental) - AMP2 ceramic-binding rhBMP-2 variant
ownership_history: Theradaptive, Inc. (Frederick, MD), privately held; work supported by a Department of Defense Peer Reviewed Medical Research Program award and technology licensed from the DHA Office of Medical Technology Transfer (per the April 2026 release).
composition: AMP2, a modified rhBMP-2 engineered to bind a tricalcium phosphate-containing carrier, so the protein stays tethered to the graft rather than diffusing (the stated rationale against rhBMP-2 off-target effects).

regulatory.reference: FDA IDE (number not public): feasibility OASIS trial in TLIF approved early 2024; expanded to ALIF and LLIF December 2024; FDA authorized the pivotal phase on 2026-04-30, with PMA named as the route to market. Company reports three FDA Breakthrough Device designations (count from secondary coverage, not the FDA list). No ClinicalTrials.gov record for the spine trial located; enrollment includes Australia and Israel. Dental: OsteoAdapt DE Phase 1/2 NCT07078331 (n=45, alveolar ridge).

applications.evidence_summary: No human results published; sheep lateral interbody study (43 OsteoAdapt vs 21 ICBG animals) showed fusion at 26 weeks with no systemic toxicity. About 100 patients treated in feasibility per the company; results not released.
applications.caveats: Preclinical and sponsor statements only; FDA IDE device, not authorized.

applications.evidence_summary: Added to the IDE in December 2024; no human data published (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Investigational.

applications.evidence_summary: Added to the IDE in December 2024; supporting data are the ovine lateral fusion study only.
applications.caveats: Investigational.

applications.evidence_summary: OsteoAdapt DE Phase 1/2 dose study in localized alveolar ridge augmentation (NCT07078331, n=45, active not recruiting, primary completion 2026-04); no results posted.
applications.caveats: Investigational.

evidence.title: In vivo assessment of AMP2, a novel ceramic-binding BMP-2, in ovine lumbar interbody fusion
evidence.finding: Both doses fused all levels by palpation at 26 weeks in sheep, comparable to ICBG; no systemic toxicity.

evidence.title: Safety and Performance, and Dose, of OsteoAdapt DE in Localized Alveolar Ridge Augmentations
evidence.finding: Phase 1/2; active, not recruiting; no results posted.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Pivotal OASIS (single-level TLIF, ALIF, LLIF) authorized 2026-04-30; PMA would follow; no timeline given.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable until approved; as a PMA bone graft it would be bundled in fusion MS-DRGs unless it wins NTAP.
bd.notes: The most advanced US rhBMP-2 challenger besides CGBio/DePuy Synthes Novosis; watch for a partner announcement.

name: Augment Rotator Cuff (rhPDGF-BB on type I collagen matrix) - development not continued
ownership_history: BioMimetic Therapeutics (Franklin, TN) ran the pilot; Wright Medical acquired BioMimetic in 2013 and Stryker acquired Wright in 2020 (same chain as Augment Bone Graft, P100006). GEM 21S dental rights sit with Lynch Biologics (existing record).
composition: Recombinant human PDGF-BB delivered on a type I bovine collagen matrix placed at the tendon-bone interface during rotator cuff repair.

regulatory.reference: Canadian pilot study NCT01256242 (n=31; London, Ottawa and Toronto sites; completed 2012-11). No US IDE or PMA located (openFDA PMA search for BioMimetic returns only P100006 Augment Bone Graft/Injectable).

applications.evidence_summary: Pilot results never posted or published (PubMed search 2026-10-23); support is an ovine rotator cuff study (rhPDGF-BB on collagen matrix improved early repair biomechanics).
applications.caveats: Preclinical only; no activity registered since 2012.

evidence.title: Pilot Study of Augment Rotator Cuff for Surgical Treatment of Full Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears
evidence.finding: Completed 2012; no results posted.

evidence.title: Augmentation of a rotator cuff suture repair using rhPDGF-BB and a type I bovine collagen matrix in an ovine model
evidence.finding: Ovine model of the product concept.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Historical; Stryker's only rhPDGF products on the market are Augment Bone Graft and Augment Injectable (foot and ankle fusion).

name: Actifit polyurethane meniscal scaffold
ownership_history: Orteq Sports Medicine; ownership/investors not verified. CE-marked and approved in Korea; FDA Breakthrough Device Designation reported; a US IDE has not been confirmed.
composition: Biodegradable, porous polyurethane scaffold fixed to the meniscal rim; designed for partial meniscus defects.

regulatory.reference: No FDA clearance/approval located; Breakthrough Device Designation reported (search summary); Orteq said it expected to present European clinical data to FDA
on_label_indications: Ex-US: partial meniscus defect scaffold (labeling not read). US: none.

applications.evidence_summary: Meta-analysis (37 studies, 1,276 patients incl. 804 Actifit): significant improvement and failure risk 9%; quality low, long-term Actifit data limited. French 5-year MRI/function study (n not recoverable) and a 54-patient multicenter series (VAS 5.5 to 2.9 at 24 months) are case-series level. Orteq reports >4,000 implants in 30 countries (company).
applications.caveats: Mostly case series; one independent RCT not found; Orteq-funded long-term follow-up planned (NCT07800923, n=120).

evidence.title: No differences in clinical outcome between CMI and Actifit meniscal scaffolds: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Both scaffolds improved symptoms and function; failure risk 7% CMI vs 9% Actifit.

evidence.title: Actifit polyurethane meniscal scaffold: MRI and functional outcomes after a minimum follow-up of 5 years
evidence.finding: 5-year MRI and function outcomes (abstract not indexed; findings not read).

evidence.title: Long-term follow-up of Actifit meniscal scaffold patients
evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting; primary completion estimated 2028-09.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None found for FDA submission.

bd.reimbursement: Ex-US only.
bd.notes: Ex-US hospital procurement; US entry blocked pending FDA data.

name: NUsurface Meniscus Implant
ownership_history: Active Implants LLC (Memphis, TN per FDA panel minutes); CE-marked in Europe (2008) and used in Israel since 2011 (search summary). US trial sponsor on CT.gov: Phoenix Kinetics.
composition: Free-floating polycarbonate-urethane (Bionate) disc implanted in the medial compartment after a near-total medial meniscectomy; no fixation to bone or soft tissue.

regulatory.reference: US De Novo request (not PMA; the brief's 'PMA' is incorrect). FDA Orthopaedic and Rehabilitation Devices Panel, 2023-04-20, voted 2 yes / 6 no / 1 abstain on benefit outweighing risk. FDA Breakthrough designation (2019). A final De Novo decision was not located (no authorization found as of 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: Proposed (De Novo): improve pain and function in the medial compartment of a knee in which the medial meniscus has been resected, in patients with mild to moderate arthritis, mild or greater knee pain, and cartilage present on the load-bearing surfaces (FDA panel minutes)

challenge: The sponsor's case rested on a post-hoc modified dataset (extrusion <5 mm and tibial spine height >=11 mm; 74 implanted vs 35 controls) after the full VENUS population; FDA reviewers noted a 34% automatic surgical failure rate falling to 17% in the subset and retrieval evidence of abrasion and fracture.

applications.evidence_summary: VENUS RCT (n=127 treated; NUsurface 61 vs non-surgical care 66): at 1 year KOOS Pain (P=.013) and KOOS Overall (P=.027) improved more with the implant. The sponsor's De Novo used pooled VENUS plus single-arm SUN (n=115): FDA panel voted against benefit-risk (2 yes, 6 no, 1 abstain) citing high failure rate, subgroup selection, and 2-year follow-up with sparse 60-month data.
applications.caveats: Randomized against non-surgical care (not against meniscus transplant or scaffolds); sponsor-funded; open-label; failure and removal rates high; 1-year paper above (2-year primary in the De Novo).

evidence.title: Treatment of post-meniscectomy knee symptoms with medial meniscus replacement results in greater pain reduction and functional improvement than non-surgical management: 1-year results of the VENUS RCT
evidence.finding: KOOS Pain and Overall improved more with NUsurface than non-surgical care at 1 year (P=.013, .027); treatment cessation 4.9% vs 14.5%.

evidence.title: Preliminary Results From a US Clinical Trial of a Novel Synthetic Polymer Meniscal Implant
evidence.finding: First 100 patients across VENUS and SUN at 12 months: greater KOOS gains than controls (119%-177% greater improvement), similar adverse event rates (16.9% vs 14.3%).

evidence.title: SUN: Safety utilizing NUsurface meniscus implant (single-arm)
evidence.finding: Completed June 2020; pooled with VENUS in the De Novo (Mercury dataset).

evidence.title: VENUS: Verifying the Effectiveness of the NUsurface System (randomized superiority study)
evidence.finding: Completed; registry n=34 differs from the 127 treated in the 1-year paper and the FDA minutes.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No FDA decision found; post-panel path unknown. NUsurface Implant Registry (NCT03953846) terminated 2023-11.

bd.reimbursement: Not authorized in the US.
bd.notes: Fifth FDA attempt per trade coverage; a US launch looks unlikely without a new study.

name: Ortho-R (chitosan-based implant for rotator cuff repair)
ownership_history: Ortho Regenerative Technologies Inc. ('Ortho RTi'); the ClinicalTrials.gov sponsor is ChitogenX Inc. Entity relationship not verified.
composition: Lyophilized chitosan-based polymer solubilized with the patient's own PRP and applied at the rotator cuff repair site (company description; not verified).

regulatory.reference: US IND for a Phase I/II rotator cuff trial submitted 2021, FDA clinical hold August 2021 (CMC information), hold lifted December 2021. Registered randomized safety study NCT05333211 (n=78) status UNKNOWN
on_label_indications: None (investigational)

applications.evidence_summary: No published human study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23, 'Ortho-R'). Registered blinded randomized safety study NCT05333211 (n=78, started 2022-07, primary completion 2023-12, status unknown).
applications.caveats: Early stage; status unknown; sponsor claims unverified.

evidence.title: A blinded randomized controlled study investigating the safety of Ortho-R for rotator cuff repair compared with standard of care
evidence.finding: Registry status UNKNOWN; no results.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None located; registry last verified date old.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed.
bd.notes: Small-cap biologic-polymer player; no 2026 update found.

name: CERAMENT V (vancomycin-eluting)
composition: Cerament biphasic ceramic premixed with vancomycin; CE-marked in Europe.

regulatory.reference: No US authorization as of 2026-10-22. The submission was moved from 510(k) to the De Novo process on 2025-12-02 (company release); BONESUPPORT's Q3 2026 interim report (2026-10-22) says it submitted the supplemental data package FDA requested under De Novo and the dialogue is 'constructive'. FDA granted Breakthrough Device designation (bone infection). CMS's FY2027 final rule creates a code for vancomycin-eluting bone void fillers effective 2026-10-01 and would assign CERAMENT V to it only if FDA grants De Novo classification. BONESUPPORT's US portfolio page lists only CERAMENT G and CERAMENT Bone Void Filler.
on_label_indications: Proposed: adjunct to systemic antibiotics and debridement in the treatment of bone infection in extremity defects (vancomycin for gram-positive/MRSA coverage); not yet authorized in the US

challenge: Ex-US only today (CE-marked); US De Novo still under review as of 2026-10-22.

applications.evidence_summary: European use in infected nonunion and Masquelet reconstructions (e.g., Lyon cohort NCT03970941, n=8); no US data.
applications.caveats: Not available in the US.

applications.evidence_summary: European use in osteomyelitis, PJI and diabetic foot; UK post-market study of CERAMENT V/G in foot osteomyelitis (NCT06628115, n=25) and Italian revision-arthroplasty study (NCT03389646); no US data.
applications.caveats: Not authorized in the US as of this review; evidence is observational.

evidence.title: Post-market study of CERAMENT V/G in foot osteomyelitis (Mid and South Essex NHS)
evidence.finding: Completed August 2026; results not yet public.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable in the US.
bd.notes: Relevant only as pipeline for the US; its vancomycin loading targets MRSA where gentamicin resistance limits Cerament G.

pipeline.expected_milestone: FDA De Novo decision pending (no date given; supplemental data package submitted per the 2026-10-22 Q3 report).

ownership_history: CE-marked 2015; FDA Breakthrough Device designation for bone infection; US submission planned as 510(k) with CERAMENT G as predicate (July 2024 announcement), transferred to De Novo in December 2025; complete additional data package submitted 2026-09-21.

name: EP Granules + Tobramycin (Elute antibiotic-eluting graft)
composition: Investigational combination of Elute's resorbable calcium-salt/polymer granules with tobramycin for roughly eight weeks of local release (per company and trial descriptions).

regulatory.reference: NCT05361941 (FDA-authorized pivotal IDE trial)
on_label_indications: Investigational; no marketing authorization. Study treats periprosthetic joint infection in the first stage of staged revision

applications.evidence_summary: No published efficacy data located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Elute antibiotic EP Granules tobramycin); the pivotal trial is randomized, blinded, 204 planned.
applications.caveats: Investigational combination device; the trial is in periprosthetic joint infection, a population close to but not identical to long-bone osteomyelitis.

evidence.title: Multicenter Trial of Antibiotic Eluting Graft for Promoting New Bone Growth in/Near Infected Bone Cavities
evidence.finding: Pivotal prospective, multicenter, randomized, blinded trial of EP Granules + tobramycin versus standard-of-care revision in staged PJI; recruiting, estimated primary completion December 2029.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Primary completion estimated 2029-12 (ClinicalTrials.gov)

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable (investigational).
bd.notes: Direct competitors for antibiotic carriers: CERAMENT G/V, STIMULAN VG (all in the atlas).

name: Cingal (cross-linked hyaluronate plus triamcinolone hexacetonide)
ownership_history: Anika Therapeutics (Bedford, MA) owns the product; Anika bought the Aristospan (triamcinolone hexacetonide) NDA in September 2024 and sold it in April 2025 to a manufacturer that will supply the reference drug for the bioequivalence study (FY2025 10-K).
composition: Monovisc-type cross-linked sodium hyaluronate combined with triamcinolone hexacetonide (steroid dose not re-sourced); single injection; a drug-device combination in the US.

regulatory.reference: none (not approved in the US; Anika is pursuing an NDA per its FY2025 10-K); CE marked and sold in more than 50 countries
on_label_indications: None in the US. Ex-US (CE mark): symptomatic relief of knee osteoarthritis; hip, shoulder and ankle studies exist (NCT04640298, NCT04640961, NCT04640974)

applications.evidence_summary: Hangody 2018 (n=368): Cingal beat saline on WOMAC pain through 26 weeks (p=0.0099 at 12 weeks) and was similar to Monovisc from week 6; the 526-patient Cingal 16-02 extension (NCT03390036) found OMERACT-OARSI responder rates at 39 weeks of 91.2% Cingal, 92.4% Monovisc and 93.2% triamcinolone hexacetonide (p=0.81), i.e. no separation among arms at 39 weeks.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; authors were Anika consultants. The steroid component, not the HA, likely drives early relief. US marketing needs an NDA; none submitted as of the FY2025 10-K.

evidence.title: Intraarticular injection of a cross-linked sodium hyaluronate combined with triamcinolone hexacetonide (Cingal) to provide symptomatic relief of osteoarthritis of the knee: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter clinical trial (Hangody, Cartilage)
evidence.finding: Cingal improved on saline through 26 weeks (p=0.0099 at 12 weeks); against HA alone (Monovisc) it showed an early advantage with comparable benefit from about 6 weeks.

evidence.title: Cingal 16-02 trial extension: 39-week follow-up of Cingal vs Monovisc vs triamcinolone hexacetonide
evidence.finding: Registry results: OMERACT-OARSI responder rate at 39 weeks 91.2% Cingal, 92.4% Monovisc, 93.2% triamcinolone hexacetonide, p=0.8106.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed in the US; no HCPCS code.
bd.notes: Anika FY2025 10-K cites a roughly $1 billion US addressable market, a bioequivalence study started in December 2025 and a Type C meeting in February 2025; no NDA filing or approval date is stated. Cingal is why Anika bought and sold the Aristospan NDA.

pipeline.expected_milestone: NDA submission pending completion of a bioequivalence study initiated December 2025 (Anika FY2025 10-K); no approval timeline stated

challenge: FDA treats HA plus steroid as a combination product needing an NDA, not a PMA; the BE study against Aristospan is the gating item.

name: ALLOB (allogeneic osteoblastic cell therapy) - failed
ownership_history: Bone Therapeutics (Gosselies) developed ALLOB and PREOB; reverse merger with Medsenic created BioSenic (2022); ALLOB Phase IIb in tibial fracture failed (June 2023); company pivoted to oral arsenic trioxide and later licensed/returned ALLOB rights amid a terminated Pregene license (2023).
composition: Allogeneic bone-marrow MSCs differentiated to osteoblastic lineage, cryopreserved, injected percutaneously

regulatory.reference: EU ATMP trials (EudraCT 2018-001054-96); no US IND found
on_label_indications: None; development discontinued

applications.evidence_summary: Phase IIb (n=57 treated) in acute tibial fractures at risk of delayed union gave ALLOB days after injury; it failed to accelerate healing and BioSenic suspended the program (June 2023), concluding MSCs should not be given in the acute inflammatory window. An earlier mid-phase delayed-union study had been positive.
applications.caveats: Negative RCT; informative for anyone proposing early cell therapy in acute fracture.
applications.challenge: Cited as the reason cell therapy in acute trauma is out of favor.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2b randomized 1:1 placebo-controlled trial in high-risk tibial fractures (NCT04432389, n=57) showed no acceleration of fracture healing on the primary efficacy endpoint; no treatment-related serious adverse events (BioSenic, June 2023).
applications.caveats: Underpowered after restructuring; endpoint reclassified during the trial (July 2022); results not located in a peer-reviewed journal during this review.

evidence.title: Bone Therapeutics' final asset buried after failure in phase 2 fracture study (Fierce Biotech)
evidence.finding: ALLOB did not accelerate fracture healing in the Phase IIb; safety acceptable; program suspended.

evidence.title: Phase 2b of ALLOB in patients with high-risk tibial fractures
evidence.finding: Negative on the primary efficacy endpoint; sponsor paused development and redirected resources (CGTLive, June 19, 2023).

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Case study for diligence: a cell therapy with positive delayed-union signal that failed when moved to acute fracture.

challenge: The assignment brief described this as a failed Phase 3; the trial was a Phase 2b (n=57 analyzed after a mid-study amendment reduced the target from 178 to 132 evaluable). It is the clearest randomized negative result for an allogeneic MSC product in fracture healing and belongs in the atlas as a cautionary comparator.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None announced; development paused June 2023, company has stated it would consider later-timepoint dosing but has no active trial.

name: Cytori Celution System and Puregraft (adipose-derived regenerative cells)
company: Plus Therapeutics (successor name of Cytori Therapeutics); Puregraft later sold on
ownership_history: Cytori Therapeutics renamed Plus Therapeutics in 2019 (per the brief; not re-verified) and moved away from the Celution cell-therapy business; Puregraft LLC and Bimini Health Tech appear as later applicants/labelers (Dermapose Refresh K193363, PUREGRAFT SYNC BK251296).
composition: Celution is an automated closed system that digests lipoaspirate with Celase enzyme to isolate adipose-derived regenerative cells (a stromal vascular fraction product). Puregraft (50, 250, 850) is a washing/filtering fat-graft device without enzymes.

regulatory.reference: Celution Cell Concentration Device K060482 (2006-09-28, product code CAC, autotransfusion/cell washing) and Cytori Lipoplasty System with Celase K063235 (2007-01-24, QPB, fat emulsification; Celase reagent) cover tissue/cell handling, not therapy. Puregraft 250/850/50: K092923, K113255, K132815 (MUU) for aesthetic fat grafting. Orthopedic ADRC use only in IDE trials such as NCT02326961.
on_label_indications: K060482: collection, concentration, washing and reinfusion of autologous cells collected intra- or postoperatively (general, orthopedic and other surgery); K063235: fragmentation, emulsification and aspiration of soft tissue and aesthetic body contouring. Neither authorizes ADRC injection for osteoarthritis. Enzymatic ADRC/SVF is a 351 drug under FDA's 2017 and 2020 guidance, so injection outside an IND is off-label/unapproved (US v. US Stem Cell Clinic, 11th Cir. 2021).

applications.evidence_summary: Cytori's placebo-controlled phase 2 knee OA trial of Celution-prepared ADRCs (NCT02326961, 94 enrolled, primary KOOS pain on walking) completed with no results posted and no peer-reviewed report located.
applications.caveats: Registry-only evidence; Cytori exited the program. Commercial status of Celution in 2026 not confirmed. Enzymatic SVF/ADRC isolation is a 351 drug per FDA's 2017 and 2020 guidance; not a 361-exempt point-of-care product.

evidence.title: Celution Prepared Adipose Derived Regenerative Cells in the Treatment of Osteoarthritis of the Knee
evidence.finding: Cytori phase 2 placebo-controlled trial, primary KOOS pain on walking; completed with 94 enrolled; no results posted and no peer-reviewed report located.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None: program completed/withdrawn; no sponsor activity located.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable: investigational; Puregraft fat grafting is cash-pay.
bd.notes: Historical cautionary tale for enzymatic ADRC devices: strong early press, a completed knee OA phase 2 with no public result, and corporate renaming.

name: AmnioCyte and AmnioCyte Plus (amniotic fluid)
ownership_history: Predictive Biotech, subsidiary of Predictive Technology Group (Salt Lake City). Sister Wharton's-jelly product CoreCyte drew FDA Warning Letter CBER-20-04 (17 Aug 2020) for COVID-19 and intra-articular 'cushioning' promotion; the company later stopped selling CoreCyte.
composition: Amniotic-fluid-derived allografts (company 10-K); CoreCyte and PolyCyte are Wharton's jelly products.

regulatory.reference: None. Amniotic fluid is not an HCT/P, so injectable AmnioCyte would need a BLA. No FDA letter naming AmnioCyte located.
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: No published study located (PubMed 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Company status uncertain after 2020.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Predictive Biotech (CBER-20-04) on CoreCyte
evidence.finding: Wharton's jelly product failed homologous use and appeared to fail minimal manipulation; intra-articular 'cushioning and protection' use cited.

bd.reimbursement: Q4242 ('AmnioCyte Plus, per 0.5 cc') remains in HCPCS.
bd.notes: Note the warning letter names CoreCyte, not AmnioCyte; the brief's 'AmnioCyte warning letter' could not be confirmed.

name: BioDRestore (amniotic tissue particulate)
ownership_history: BioD LLC / Integra. Not named in Integra's FY2025 10-K, so current availability is unconfirmed.
composition: Particulate (injectable) amniotic tissue allograft.

regulatory.reference: None. Particulate amniotic tissue injected into a joint for osteoarthritis pain is outside 361 homologous use per FDA's 2017/2020 HCT/P guidance and letters; no BLA.
on_label_indications: None for intra-articular use

applications.evidence_summary: Double-blind RCT (n=81, severe knee OA): single BioDRestore injection vs triamcinolone; no difference at 6 weeks, but more amnion patients kept pain relief and function to 1 year (MCID met for Lysholm, KOOS ADL and pain).
applications.caveats: Small; corticosteroid comparator, not saline; non-homologous use without a BLA.

evidence.title: Amniotic Tissue Injections Are an Effective Alternative to Corticosteroid Injections for Pain Relief and Function in Patients With Severe Knee Osteoarthritis: A Double-Blind, Randomized, Prospective Study
evidence.finding: BioDRestore (n=39) vs triamcinolone (n=42): equal at 6 weeks; amnion group kept improvement to 1 year on SANE, Lysholm and KOOS subscales.

bd.reimbursement: Not separately payable for joint injection; no Q-code located for BioDRestore.
bd.notes: Status 'off-market' inferred from absence in the FY2025 10-K; confirm with Integra.

name: BioECM (umbilical-cord placental connective tissue matrix) and BioRenew
ownership_history: Skye Biologics Holdings LLC (El Segundo, CA). FDA Warning Letter CBER-24-654466 (16 Dec 2024) after a Nov-Dec 2022 inspection; the letter also questioned BioRenew and 'HRT' BioPower-A, BioPower-C and NX amnion/chorion/cord products.
composition: Flowable umbilical-cord-derived matrix (BioECM variants ActiveMatrix, BurnMatrix, CryoMatrix, MX, NX, RX, WoundEx).

regulatory.reference: FDA Warning Letter CBER-24-654466 (16 Dec 2024): unapproved new drugs/unlicensed biologics; fails minimal manipulation (flowable processing altered cord integrity) and homologous use (anti-inflammatory, void-filling claims); 7 CGMP findings.
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: No published study located; FDA cited anti-inflammatory and void-filling claims rather than named orthopedic uses.
applications.caveats: Warning letter; status unknown.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Skye Biologics Holdings LLC (CBER-24-654466)
evidence.finding: Flowable umbilical cord products are more than minimally manipulated and non-homologous; no endotoxin testing or stability data.

bd.reimbursement: No Q-code located for BioECM.
bd.notes: 'OrthoFlo' (named in the brief under Skye) is a MiMedx amniotic-fluid product; no Skye OrthoFlo or OrthoFlo FDA letter was found.

name: Fluid Flow, Fluid GF, Restore GF, Amnio Restore (amniotic fluid) and Membrane Wrap
ownership_history: BioLab Sciences, Inc. (Scottsdale, AZ). Distributed through third parties, some private label. The brief links Fluid Flow / Fluid GF to 'Human Regenerative Technologies'; FDA's letter names BioLab Sciences as manufacturer and does not mention that company.
composition: Injectable amniotic fluid products (Fluid Flow, Fluid GF, Restore GF, Amnio Restore, Stimuleyes) and amniotic membrane sheets (Membrane Wrap family).

regulatory.reference: FDA Warning Letter OBPO 621465 (23 Aug 2022): amniotic fluid is not an HCT/P; the fluid products are unapproved drugs/unlicensed biologics intended for injection; unvalidated aseptic processing; Membrane Wrap marketed for pain and scarring fails homologous use (footnote).
on_label_indications: None for fluid products; Membrane Wrap sheets only as a barrier

applications.evidence_summary: No published study located; FDA did not cite orthopedic uses specifically.
applications.caveats: Unlicensed biologic.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to BioLab Sciences, Inc. (OBPO 621465)
evidence.finding: Amniotic fluid injectables are drugs/biologics, not HCT/Ps; ~90% of cleanroom excursions uninvestigated.

bd.reimbursement: Q4206 ('Fluid Flow or Fluid GF, 1 cc') still in HCPCS; Membrane Wrap sheets Q4205, Q4290, Q4344, Q4373; newer 'BioLab Wrap' codes Q4418-Q4423.
bd.notes: A live Q-code for an injectable FDA has called an unlicensed biologic is the billing-risk pattern OIG and DOJ have pursued.

name: FlōGraft (cryopreserved amniotic fluid / micronized amnion allograft)
ownership_history: Applied Biologics, LLC; not listed on the company's current website.
composition: Cryopreserved injectable allograft of chorion-free amnion and amniotic fluid (also described as micronized human amnion chorion membrane in its knee OA IND trial).

regulatory.reference: Phase 2 IND trial NCT03441607 (IND number not public). Amniotic-fluid injectables need a BLA per FDA.
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2 placebo-controlled trial (NCT03441607, target n=320) has unknown status since 2018 and no results.
applications.caveats: Abandoned or unreported.

applications.evidence_summary: Randomized rotator cuff repair study with and without FlōGraft (NCT03379324, target n=260) has unknown status and no results.
applications.caveats: Unreported.

evidence.title: Safety & Efficacy of FloGraft (mHACMb) in Adults With Pain Due to OA of the Knee
evidence.finding: Phase 2; status unknown; no results.

evidence.title: Arthroscopic double-row rotator cuff repair with and without a cryopreserved, liquid, injectable amnion allograft
evidence.finding: Status unknown; no results.

bd.reimbursement: None.
bd.notes: Off-market status inferred from its absence on appliedbiologics.com (2026-10-23).

name: Purified Fluid Allograft (amniotic fluid) and Allograft Matrix
ownership_history: Frontier Biologics, LLC (Waco, TX). FDA Warning Letter CBER 25-686059 (1 Nov 2024) after a Feb-Mar 2024 inspection.
composition: Amniotic-fluid injectable (also sold as Purified Amniotic Fluid Allograft, Evexcell Purified Nanoparticle Fluid) and an amniotic membrane matrix/patch.

regulatory.reference: FDA Warning Letter CBER 25-686059 (1 Nov 2024): amniotic fluid not an HCT/P; Allograft Matrix fails 1271.10(a) (wound-healing, anti-inflammatory claims); no BLA or IND; 6 CGMP findings including uninvestigated sterility failures.
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: Promoted for osteoarthritis and joint injuries/pain by injection per FDA; no published study located.
applications.caveats: Unlicensed biologic.

applications.evidence_summary: Promoted for muscle tears and soft-tissue injuries per FDA; no study located.
applications.caveats: Unlicensed biologic.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Frontier Biologics, LLC (CBER 25-686059)
evidence.finding: Injectable amniotic fluid marketed for osteoarthritis and joint pain is an unapproved drug/unlicensed biologic.

bd.reimbursement: None located.
bd.notes: Clearest FDA statement that orthopedic amniotic-fluid injections are 351 products.

name: BoneSource Hydroxyapatite Cement (HAC), Fast Setting and Rapid Setting
company: Stryker (originally Osteogenics; Leibinger; Howmedica Osteonics / Stryker Instruments)
ownership_history: Developed at the American Dental Association Paffenbarger Research Center (Chow and Takagi); cleared to Osteogenics in 1996 and 1997 (K953339, K964537), then Stryker Leibinger (K991398, 1999), Stryker Instruments (K021440 2002, K032366 Fast Setting 2003, K043334 Rapid Setting 2005) and a BoneSource BVF orthopedic version to Howmedica Osteonics (K031435, MQV, 2003). Stryker's current US CMF catalog does not list BoneSource; HydroSet (2006) and DirectInject (2015) appear to have replaced it.
composition: Tetracalcium phosphate and dicalcium phosphate powder mixed with a sodium phosphate solution, setting to carbonated hydroxyapatite

on_label_indications: Self-setting calcium phosphate cement intended for repairing neurosurgical burr holes and cranial defects and for restoring bony contour in the craniofacial skeleton (per the 2002 to 2005 510(k) summaries; no clinical data provided, bench testing only)

challenge: Current US availability could not be confirmed either way: no discontinuation notice was found, but BoneSource is absent from Stryker's CMF product pages and no 510(k) activity since 2005. Treat as legacy; the clinical literature (Friedman, Costantino, Kveton) is the origin of the HA cement evidence base now claimed by HydroSet.

applications.evidence_summary: Friedman 2000 three-center controlled cohort of 40 patients with frontal sinus and frontofacial defects up to 25 cm2: 82 percent successful reconstruction at 24 months and about 5 percent infection-related removal versus historical methyl methacrylate controls; Costantino 2001 sealed 21 of 21 sphenoethmoid CSF leaks.
applications.caveats: Nonrandomized, historical controls, investigator-developed material (ADA Paffenbarger and NIST patents).

applications.evidence_summary: Reinforced BoneSource with tantalum mesh for nine cranioplasties over 25 cm2 (mean 128 cm2): two constructs removed for infection within three months; pediatric series of 78 children (Mimix or BoneSource) with 7 complications and 6 removals.
applications.caveats: Off-label when reinforced above 25 cm2; infection when contiguous with sinus mucosa.

applications.evidence_summary: Secondary contour cranioplasty in 48 patients with fast-setting HAC: five complications including two infections, 38 good results (Magee 2004).
applications.caveats: Single surgeon, no comparator.

evidence.title: Reconstruction of the frontal sinus and frontofacial skeleton with hydroxyapatite cement
evidence.finding: 82 percent successful reconstruction of frontal-cranial defects up to 25 cm2 at 24 months; two implants (about 5 percent) removed for infection; osseointegration confirmed on explant biopsy.

evidence.title: Sphenoethmoid cerebrospinal fluid leak repair with hydroxyapatite cement
evidence.finding: All 21 sphenoethmoid CSF leaks sealed on first application with no recurrence at mean 36 months; extrusion when placed transnasally in the ethmoid region.

evidence.title: Correction of large (over 25 cm2) cranial defects with reinforced hydroxyapatite cement
evidence.finding: Nine cranioplasties of 40 to 196 cm2 using HAC over tantalum mesh and titanium bars; two constructs removed for infection at one and three months.

evidence.title: Use of fast-setting hydroxyapatite cement for secondary craniofacial contouring
evidence.finding: Five complications (two infections, one seroma, one persistent swelling, one retained drain); 38 good and 7 acceptable results, 3 reoperations for contour.

evidence.title: Use of hydroxyapatite cement in pediatric craniofacial reconstructive surgery: strategies for avoiding complications
evidence.finding: 78 children reconstructed with Mimix or BoneSource (mean 57 g): 7 complications (trauma, infection, exposure), 6 requiring removal; every complication followed a traumatic event.

evidence.title: BoneSource hydroxyapatite cement: a novel biomaterial for craniofacial skeletal tissue engineering and reconstruction
evidence.finding: Review of material chemistry and clinical use guidelines by the developers; sets the 25 cm2 and no-sinus-contact rules later written into labels.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled (see hydroset).
bd.notes: Legacy brand; evidence base inherited by HydroSet in Stryker marketing.

name: Cementek, Cementek LV, TriHA+ and Ceraform (Teknimed calcium phosphate)
composition: Cementek: apatitic calcium phosphate cement putty (solid plus liquid phase, athermic setting); TriHA+ and Ceraform: calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite/TCP) scaffolds.

regulatory.reference: K041493 (Cementek, Aug 2004); K042911 (Cementek LV, Dec 2004); K031826 (TriHA+, Nov 2003); K040669 (Ceraform, May 2004)
on_label_indications: Cementek (K041493): bone void filler only, for voids or gaps not intrinsic to stability; putty molded into the 'extremities, spine, and pelvis'; calcium phosphate scaffold resorbs and is replaced with bone
TriHA+ and Ceraform: gently packed into voids in the extremities, spine and pelvis; not for large defects that would not heal spontaneously

challenge: Status 'off-market' inferred from age of clearances and absence of US catalogs; not confirmed.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Cementek Teknimed). A minipig study compared Bone Source and Cementek with Endobon (PMID 21337309).
applications.caveats: Preclinical only.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Teknimed is better known for vertebroplasty cements; US marketing of these 2003 to 2004 clearances was not confirmed.

name: MIIG injectable calcium sulfate (MIIG, MIIG X3, MIIG SR)
ownership_history: Wright Medical Technology (Arlington, TN); acquired by Stryker in November 2020 (as for OSTEOSET in the atlas).
composition: Injectable calcium sulfate paste that cures in situ (MIIG SR adds calcium phosphate and can be molded into pellets).

regulatory.reference: K024336 (MIIG II, March 2003); K060011 (MIIG SR, Feb 2006)
on_label_indications: MIIG paste: injected into open bone voids/gaps not intrinsic to stability of the skeletal system (extremities, spine and pelvis), cures in situ, can augment provisional hardware such as K-wires (K024336)
MIIG SR: injected or molded pellets for the same regions (K060011)

challenge: Off-market inferred; included so the Wright calcium sulfate history is complete.

applications.evidence_summary: Fifteen patients with benign bone lesions were curetted and grafted with injectable calcium sulfate (MIIG): 14 of 15 showed complete graft incorporation at an average 8 weeks, one deep infection, mean MSTS function 83% at 6 months (PMID 14763545).
applications.caveats: Single-center case series with 6-month average follow-up; 2004.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: MIIG tibial plateau).
applications.caveats: Extremities named.

evidence.title: Treatment of benign bone lesions with an injectable calcium sulfate-based bone graft substitute
evidence.finding: Fourteen of 15 benign-lesion defects incorporated the injectable calcium sulfate graft by about 8 weeks; one deep infection.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Older Wright calcium sulfate line; current Stryker catalog status not checked. Also unreviewed from Wright: IGNITE Bone Void Filler (K190482, 'extremities and pelvis'; composition not stated in the text read).

name: AlloStem Cellular Bone Allograft
ownership_history: AlloSource product (trade press reports a US patent in 4Q 2015; not read directly). Commercial status in 2026 unconfirmed.
composition: Partially demineralized allograft bone combined with allogeneic adult adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (Aetna CPB 0411 background section).

regulatory.reference: none (marketed as a 361 HCT/P by AlloSource; no 510(k) in openFDA for 'allostem', searched 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: Marketed as a bone graft alternative to autograft for fusion and nonunion (361 homologous use claimed); IFU not located

challenge: The hardest 361 case in the category: the cells come from fat, not bone, and are combined with a bone scaffold, which strains both the homologous-use criterion and the 'no combination with another article' criterion of 21 CFR 1271.10(a). No public FDA letter to AlloSource about AlloStem was found in the sources read. Status set to off-market on weak evidence (no current product page reachable; payer policies still list it by name in 2026); treat as unverified.

applications.evidence_summary: AlloSource ran a 140-patient randomized trial against autograft in subtalar fusion (NCT01413061, completed 2017) but no results are posted or published; the only literature is a narrative review chapter (Foot Ankle Clin 2016, PMID 27871419). PubMed searches 2026-10-23.
applications.caveats: Unreported sponsor RCT: possible publication bias.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23). Buttermann 2026 randomized an adipose-MSC-plus-allograft arm (64% posterior fusion vs 98% iliac crest), but the paper's abstract does not name the commercial product.
applications.caveats: Aetna CPB 0411 names AlloStem as experimental for all orthopedic applications including spinal fusion.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in nonunion located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Nonunion marketing would sharpen the 'living cells do the work' problem under criterion 4.

evidence.title: Study of Subtalar Arthrodesis Using AlloStem Versus Autologous Bone Graft
