evidence.finding: AlloSource-sponsored open-label randomized trial of AlloStem vs autologous graft in subtalar arthrodesis (primary endpoint CT fusion at 24 weeks); completed February 2017 with 140 enrolled, but no results posted and no peer-reviewed report located.

evidence.title: Comparison of posterior cellular bonegraft options for single-level lumbar spinal fusion: a randomized trial
evidence.finding: Single-blinded six-arm randomized study with historical allograft control in anterior/posterior fusion: posterior fusion 98% iliac crest, 94% BMP, 85% marrow aspirate, 67% bone-marrow-MSC allograft, 64% adipose-MSC allograft, 62% amnion-MSC allograft, 50% plain allograft; clinical outcomes similar when the interbody fusion was solid. Registered retrospectively as NCT07187362 (119 actual enrollment, 2015-2019) versus 175 in the paper; commercial products not named in the abstract.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG when used; named as experimental for all orthopedic applications by Aetna (CPB 0411).
bd.notes: If it is still sold, expect payer friction by name. Commercial status should be confirmed with AlloSource before citing.

name: Cellentra VCBM (Viable Cell Bone Matrix)
company: Highridge Medical (heritage Biomet, then Zimmer Biomet and ZimVie spine)
ownership_history: Biomet Spine/Biologics product by 2012 (Biomet 10-Q, October 2012: 'an allogenic stem cell offering' contributing to growth); Biomet merged with Zimmer in 2015; spine moved to ZimVie (2022) and Highridge Medical (2024). Appears superseded by PrimaGen Advanced (2016); current availability not confirmed.
composition: Cryopreserved cancellous bone with naturally occurring viable cells combined with demineralized cortical bone matrix; Biomet claimed at least 250,000 viable cells per cc including MSCs, osteoprogenitor cells and pre-osteoblasts, and growth factors (BMP-2, 4, 7, VEGF, TGF-beta, PDGF, IGF-1, FGF) in the demineralized component (Biomet FY2013 10-K).

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P); no 510(k) in openFDA for 'cellentra' (searched 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: Repair, replacement, reconstruction or supplementation of recipient tissue in surgically created or traumatic musculoskeletal defects (per trial and filing descriptions; IFU not read)

challenge: In the Orthofix/MTF-funded athymic rat PLF comparison, Cellentra fused 11 of 15 rats (best of six commercial CBMs, ahead of Trinity Elite at 8 of 15), yet its 81-patient ACDF study (NCT02182843, completed 2018) has no posted or published results located.

applications.evidence_summary: Zimmer Biomet's single-arm ACDF outcomes study (NCT02182843, 81 enrolled, completed January 2018) has no results located on ClinicalTrials.gov or PubMed (search 'Cellentra' 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Unpublished sponsor study; possible publication bias.

applications.evidence_summary: Only preclinical: athymic rat PLF, 11 of 15 fused by palpation and 73% bone-volume increase on micro-CT at 6 weeks (Lin 2020). No human PLF study located.
applications.caveats: Rat xenograft model funded by competitors Orthofix and MTF; not a clinical endpoint.

applications.evidence_summary: A Zimmer Biomet video presents a trauma case series (branded 'Bonus Triad'); no published trauma or nonunion study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Video not reviewed; claim unverified.

evidence.title: Cellentra Viable Cell Bone Matrix (VCBM) Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion Outcomes Study (VCBM/MaxAn)
evidence.finding: Completed (primary completion January 2018); no results posted or published as of 2026-10-23.

evidence.title: Comparing cellular bone matrices for posterolateral spinal fusion in a rat model
evidence.finding: Six commercial CBMs (15 rats each) in athymic rat PLF: fusion by palpation Cellentra 11/15, Trinity Elite 8/15, ViviGen 2/15, Osteocel Pro, Bio4 and map3 0/15; syngeneic bone 5/15.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Useful history for a hiring conversation: the best-performing CBM in the competitor-funded rat study is one its owner stopped promoting. No FDA letter about Cellentra found in the sources read.

name: HEALOS and HEALOS Fx (collagen-hydroxyapatite sponge)
ownership_history: Orquest, Inc. originated HEALOS; acquired by DePuy Spine (J&J) and now under DePuy Synthes. Acquisition date not sourced.
composition: Collagen-ceramic composite: bovine Type I collagen fibers coated with hydroxyapatite (about 30% mineral by weight); soaked in the patient's bone marrow aspirate; Fx is an injectable form with a mixing and delivery system.

regulatory.reference: K081758 (HEALOS Fx, Sept 2008); K062495 (Fx, 2006); K043308 (modification, 2005); K012751 (HEALOS, Nov 2001, Orquest)
on_label_indications: HEALOS Fx combined with autogenous bone marrow: filling bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system 'extremities, spine, and pelvis' not intrinsic to stability; surgically created or traumatic defects; resorbed and remodeled into new bone (K081758)
Separate dental and Healos II clearances exist (K081432, K093390; product code LYC)

challenge: Off-market status is inferred, not confirmed; the interbody RCT NCT00316121 is unpublished.

applications.evidence_summary: Neen 2006 (PMID 16915079): Healos plus bone marrow aspirate in 50 matched lumbar fusions versus historical iliac autograft controls: equivalent radiographic and clinical results in posterolateral fusion, no persisting donor-site complications versus 14% in autograft. Counterpoints: Ploumis 2010 (PMID 20672956; n=28 degenerative scoliosis) found equal clinical outcome but slower fusion than allograft, and a Thai intrapatient series (PMID 23991599; n=27) found 2-year radiographic fusion 29.6% with Healos/BMA versus 63.0% with local graft.
applications.caveats: Mixed evidence; historical controls in Neen; older 2000s imaging standards; outcomes depend on bone marrow aspirate quality.

applications.evidence_summary: Neen 2006: radiographic fusion rate was significantly lower with Healos in interbody fusions despite similar clinical outcomes. Case series of 20 TLIF/PLF patients: 95% fusion at 27 months (PMID 19111510). DePuy-linked randomized TLIF trial of Healos versus autograft (NCT00316121, n=138, completed, results posted) has no peer-reviewed report located.
applications.caveats: The registered randomized trial would be the strongest dataset but was not found in PubMed on 2026-10-23.
applications.challenge: Interbody data are mixed and the RCT is unpublished; a hiring manager would ask why.

applications.evidence_summary: Ploumis 2010 (PMID 20672956): Healos graft carrier with bone marrow aspirate plus local autograft (n=12) versus cancellous allograft plus local autograft (n=16) in degenerative lumbar scoliosis PLF: similar 2-year clinical results, Healos fusion slower.
applications.caveats: Small retrospective grouping.

evidence.title: Healos and bone marrow aspirate used for lumbar spine fusion: a case controlled study comparing healos with autograft
evidence.finding: Equivalent fusion in posterolateral lumbar fusion versus matched historical autograft, but significantly lower radiographic fusion in lumbar interbody fusions.

evidence.title: Healos graft carrier with bone marrow aspirate instead of allograft as adjunct to local autograft for posterolateral fusion in degenerative lumbar scoliosis: a minimum 2-year follow-up study
evidence.finding: Equal pain, function, curve and fusion rates at 2 years, but earlier fusion with allograft than with Healos.

evidence.title: A comparative study of radiographic results using HEALOS collagen-hydroxyapatite sponge with bone marrow aspiration versus local bone graft in the same patients undergoing posterolateral lumbar fusion
evidence.finding: Radiographic fusion at 2 years was 29.6% on the Healos side versus 63.0% on the local-bone side.

evidence.title: Clinical and radiographic assessment of transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion using HEALOS collagen-hydroxyapatite sponge with autologous bone marrow aspirate
evidence.finding: Overall fusion 95% (21 of 22 levels) at an average 27 months.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: No current DePuy Synthes catalog listing was found by web search on 2026-10-23, so 'off-market' is inferred. It remains a cautionary example for bone-marrow-aspirate-dependent collagen-ceramic sponges in interbody use.

name: TRUREPAIR (PolyGraft BGS) and JAX-TCP (Smith+Nephew legacy synthetics)
ownership_history: PolyGraft came from Osteobiologics, Inc. (San Antonio, TX, per the 510(k) trademark note), later part of Smith+Nephew (acquisition year not sourced).
composition: TRUREPAIR/PolyGraft BGS: porous resorbable scaffolds of polylactide-co-glycolide copolymer and calcium sulfate with PGA fibers. JAX-TCP: beta-TCP granules used alone or with a gel in a 1:1 ratio.

regulatory.reference: K062607 (TruRepair / PolyGraft BGS, Nov 2007); K033552 (JAX-TCP, June 2004); K010557 (Jax granules, 2001)
on_label_indications: TRUREPAIR (K062607): bony voids or gaps caused by trauma or surgery not intrinsic to stability, extremities, spine and pelvis
JAX-TCP (K033552): extremities, spine and pelvis; granules used alone or 1:1 with gel

challenge: Off-market status inferred from the age of clearances.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: TruRepair OR PolyGraft BGS OR JAX-TCP).
applications.caveats: Historical products; no clinical literature located.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Smith+Nephew has no current synthetic ceramic graft in this sweep (its biologics are REGENETEN and BIO4/Osiris, both elsewhere); no current listing for these legacy lines was found.

name: RESTORE Orthobiologic Soft Tissue Implant (porcine SIS patch)
ownership_history: DePuy Orthopaedics, Inc. (later DePuy Mitek/DePuy Synthes). Product withdrawn from the rotator cuff market; exact discontinuation date not found.
composition: Layered porcine small intestinal submucosa (SIS) sheet.

regulatory.reference: K001738 (2000-12-27); K071016 (2007-09-04); product code FTM (surgical mesh)
on_label_indications: Not read (510(k) summaries unavailable on accessdata). Marketed as a soft tissue implant for tendon augmentation.

challenge: Included as the class cautionary tale: two papers advised against using it for rotator cuff augmentation after severe inflammatory reactions. Off-market status is inferred (no current product page found).

applications.evidence_summary: Iannotti 2006 (JBJS, RCT, n=30): rotator cuff healed in 4 of 15 augmented vs 9 of 15 controls (P=.11) with worse PENN scores; authors did not recommend it. Walton 2007 (JBJS, matched case-control, 10 xenograft vs 12 controls): 4 xenograft patients had severe postoperative reactions requiring surgery; retear 6/10 vs 7/12; more deficits at 2 years.
applications.caveats: Small studies; one used open repair; they led to loss of confidence in SIS patches for the cuff.

evidence.title: Porcine small intestine submucosa augmentation of surgical repair of chronic two-tendon rotator cuff tears. A randomized, controlled trial
evidence.finding: Healing 4/15 with augmentation vs 9/15 without (P=.11); no recommendation for augmentation.

evidence.title: Restore orthobiologic implant: not recommended for augmentation of rotator cuff repairs
evidence.finding: Four xenograft patients had severe inflammatory reactions requiring surgery; no benefit at 2 years.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed.
bd.notes: Historical; shows why 'patch' category skepticism persists.

name: Zimmer Collagen Repair Patch (formerly Permacol; porcine dermal collagen)
ownership_history: 510(k) holder was Tissue Science Laboratories plc (Aldershot, UK) in 2006; Zimmer marketed it as the Zimmer Collagen Repair Patch. Later ownership and whether it is still sold were not verified.
composition: Cross-linked porcine dermal collagen (Permacol).

regulatory.reference: K053562 (2006-06-23), product code FTM (surgical mesh)
on_label_indications: Not read (510(k) summary unavailable on accessdata); marketed for tendon repair reinforcement

applications.evidence_summary: Badhe 2008 (J Shoulder Elbow Surg): 10 patients, mean age 66, porcine dermal collagen augmentation of extensive cuff tears at 4.5 years: Constant 41 to 62 (P=.0003), grafts intact in 8, detached in 2, no adverse effects. Oxford biopsy series (n=3) reported one adverse immune response with Permacol.
applications.caveats: Tiny uncontrolled series; no comparator; status of marketing unverified.

evidence.title: An assessment of porcine dermal xenograft as an augmentation graft in the treatment of extensive rotator cuff tears
evidence.finding: Constant score 41 to 62 at 4.5 years; 8 of 10 grafts intact on imaging.

evidence.title: Rotator cuff repair with biological graft augmentation causes adverse tissue outcomes
evidence.finding: One of three Permacol patients had an adverse macrophage-rich immune response at 4 weeks.

bd.reimbursement: Not verified.
bd.notes: Likely a legacy product; included to document the xenograft dermal patch class.

name: Allogran-N and Allogran-R Bone Void Filler
composition: Allogran-N: hydroxyapatite bone graft substitute granules; Allogran-R: resorbable calcium salt implant in granules or preformed shapes.

regulatory.reference: K043514 (Allogran-N, Jan 2005); K061311 (Allogran-R, Sept 2006)
on_label_indications: Allogran-R (K061311): resorbable implant to fill bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (extremities, spine or pelvis), may be combined with saline or blood; Allogran-N (K043514): hydroxyapatite granules for bony voids or gaps

challenge: Current status unverified; 'off-market' inferred from absence of current listings.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: Allogran Biocomposites).
applications.caveats: Historical product; no clinical literature.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Not on any current Biocomposites page checked; included for completeness of the company's 510(k) history.

name: FormaGraft Collagen Bone Graft Matrix
ownership_history: NuVasive marketed FormaGraft (per the brief); NuVasive merged into Globus Medical in September 2023. Link between R&D Medical's 510(k) and NuVasive's sales not sourced. Company field shortened; original: NuVasive (now Globus Medical); 510(k) holder R&D Medical, LLC
composition: Collagen-ceramic sponge: bovine Type I collagen with hydroxyapatite and tricalcium phosphate (per a 2017 rabbit study describing FormaGraft as a collagen-HA/TCP void filler).

regulatory.reference: K050789 (May 2005, applicant R and D Medical, LLC)
on_label_indications: Cleared as a collagen bone graft matrix bone void filler (510(k) summary PDF not retrievable from FDA; indications text not read)

challenge: Status 'off-market' is inferred from absence on current company pages, not confirmed.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of this product in this application located (PubMed search 2026-10-23: FormaGraft posterolateral fusion).
applications.caveats: Indications text not read; the only identified study is a 2017 rabbit posterolateral fusion model (PMID 28852357) comparing FormaGraft and Bi-Ostetic against iliac crest graft.

evidence.title: Influence of 45S5 Bioactive Glass in A Standard Calcium Phosphate Collagen Bone Graft Substitute on the Posterolateral Fusion of Rabbit Spine
evidence.finding: In rabbits, both a mineralized collagen filler with 45S5 glass (Bi-Ostetic) and FormaGraft showed normal healing with fusion comparable to iliac crest graft.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG inpatient; packaged in OPPS and ASC payment; no separate HCPCS code or pass-through for bone void fillers.
bd.notes: Likely legacy; no current Globus product page found. Status and ownership are unverified.

name: PREOB (autologous osteoblastic cells) for osteonecrosis and nonunion - failed
ownership_history: Bone Therapeutics (Gosselies, Belgium) developed PREOB from Erasme University Hospital (Brussels) work; the DSMB stopped the Phase 3 for futility on 2018-11-06 and the company moved to its allogeneic ALLOB platform (existing record allob); Bone Therapeutics became BioSenic in 2022.
composition: Autologous bone-marrow-derived, culture-expanded osteoblastic cells (about 20 million in the Phase 3) implanted into the core-decompression track or nonunion site.

regulatory.reference: Never authorized; developed as an EU advanced-therapy product (Belgium). No US IND located. Phase 3 NCT01529008 terminated for futility; nonunion Phase 2/3 NCT01756326 terminated 2017 (n=5) to focus on the allogeneic platform.

applications.evidence_summary: Jayankura 2023 Phase 3 double-blind RCT (NCT01529008): composite response at 24 months 61% (14/23) with PREOB plus core decompression vs 69% (18/26) with core decompression plus placebo (p=0.54); THA 24% vs 14%. The earlier single-center RCT vs BMAC (Hauzeur 2020, n=56 hips) also found no benefit.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-run and sponsor-authored Phase 3, stopped early for futility so the final analysis is small; negative on its primary endpoint.
applications.challenge: Negative Level I evidence: cultured osteoblasts added nothing to core decompression; do not cite PREOB as support for cell augmentation of AVN.

applications.evidence_summary: Nonunion Phase 2/3 (NCT01756326) terminated after 5 patients; an academic Phase 1/2 in atrophic nonunion (NCT00916981, n=30) has no results posted. Only a 2010 review of the group's early series located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: No comparative data published.

evidence.title: Does adjunction of autologous osteoblastic cells improve the results of core decompression in early-stage femoral head osteonecrosis? A double-blind, randomized trial
evidence.finding: No difference in 24-month composite response (61% vs 69%, p=0.54) or THA rate; no treatment-related serious adverse events. n is registry enrollment.

evidence.title: Did osteoblastic cell therapy improve the prognosis of pre-fracture osteonecrosis of the femoral head? A randomized, controlled trial
evidence.finding: Osteoblastic cells vs BMAC with core decompression: progression to collapse 22% vs 46% (HR 0.47, p=0.15), THA 15% vs 35% (p=0.09); no significant differences at 36 months.

evidence.title: Autologous Osteoblastic Cells Implantation to Early Stage Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head (Phase 3)
evidence.finding: Terminated: interim analysis unlikely to meet the primary objective; results posted.

evidence.title: Autologous Osteoblastic Cells Implantation in Hypotrophic Non-Union Fractures (Phase 2/3)
evidence.finding: Terminated 2018 to focus on the allogeneic platform.

evidence.title: Phases 1-3 clinical trials using adult stem cells in osteonecrosis and nonunion fractures
evidence.finding: Review of the Erasme group's early osteonecrosis and nonunion cell studies.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Historical; the clearest negative RCT for cultured cells in AVN, useful against clinic claims.

name: PureGen Osteoprogenitor Cell Allograft
company: Alphatec Spine (private label; manufactured by Parcell Laboratories)
ownership_history: Alphatec released PureGen in October 2010 under its private label; Parcell Laboratories, LLC manufactured it. Alphatec decided in 2013 to stop marketing it, writing off $1.3M of intangibles and $3.5M of inventory (Alphatec FY2015 10-K).
composition: Concentrated adult osteoprogenitor (stem) cell allograft; Alphatec described it as 'a unique adult stem cell that supplements the body's own cells' (FY2012 10-K). Trade press said the cells came from living donors' bone marrow without culture expansion (not confirmed in filings).

regulatory.reference: Marketed as a 361 HCT/P; FDA untitled letter to Parcell Laboratories, June 2011, questioned that position (Alphatec FY2011 10-K); trade press reported FDA said a BLA or IND was required. Parcell responded July 2011; Parcell and Alphatec filed a joint appeal in January 2012. No 510(k) in openFDA for 'puregen'.
on_label_indications: None: FDA disputed 361 status; product discontinued 2013

challenge: The first public FDA challenge to a spine 'stem cell allograft' marketed as 361, a decade before the 2021 end of enforcement discretion. Outcome of the 2012 appeal not found.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of PureGen located (PubMed searches 'PureGen' and 'osteoprogenitor cell allograft lumbar fusion', 2026-10-23); company claimed >500 implants with no adverse events.
applications.caveats: Company claim only; FDA questioned regulatory status.

applications.evidence_summary: No published ACDF study located (PubMed search 2026-10-23); trials listed in a UCSF registry were not found on ClinicalTrials.gov by name.
applications.caveats: Withdrawn 2013.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable (withdrawn).
bd.notes: Illustrates the private-label risk: the distributor (Alphatec) carried the inventory write-off when the manufacturer's regulatory position failed.

name: AmnioFix Injectable / EpiFix Injectable (micronized dHACM, mdHACM)
ownership_history: Developed by MiMedx (Surgical Biologics subsidiary, Marietta GA). FDA Untitled Letter of 5 Sept 2013 to Surgical Biologics concluded micronized AmnioFix Injectable was more than minimally manipulated and needed a biologics license. MiMedx ran it as an IND/BLA program (RMAT designation for knee OA, 2018), then disbanded the Regenerative Medicine segment and suspended the knee OA program in Q2 2023, abandoning the BLA.
composition: Dehydrated human amnion/chorion membrane (PURION-processed) milled to a micronized powder and reconstituted in saline for injection (40-100 mg doses in trials).

regulatory.reference: No BLA. Studied under IND (number not public); FDA Untitled Letter 2013 (Surgical Biologics, AmnioFix Injectable); BLA effort abandoned Q2 2023 per MiMedx FY2025 10-K
on_label_indications: None. FDA treats micronized amniotic membrane injected for pain, inflammation or tendon/joint conditions as a 351 biologic requiring a BLA (2013 Untitled Letter; 2017/2020 HCT/P guidance; enforcement discretion ended 31 May 2021). MiMedx states it does not sell Section 351 products in the US.

challenge: The Level I plantar fasciitis RCT (Cazzell 2018) is still quoted in sales decks for other brands; MiMedx's own confirmatory Phase 3 in plantar fasciitis and its Phase 2b in knee OA both missed their primary endpoints, and MiMedx walked away from the BLA.

applications.evidence_summary: Cazzell 2018 single-blind RCT (n=145, 14 US sites): one mdHACM injection cut 3-month VAS pain 76% vs 45% for saline (p<0.0001). The confirmatory double-blind Phase 3 (NCT03414268) did not separate from saline on 90-day VAS (topline 13 Sept 2021) and MiMedx dropped the plantar fasciitis BLA. A 2026 meta-analysis of placental injectables in plantar fasciitis (6 studies, 324 patients) rated certainty low to very low.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; the positive trial was single-blind with a 3-month primary endpoint; the larger double-blind trial was negative and is unpublished as a paper. Achilles Phase 3 (NCT03414255, n=146) completed 2021 with no results posted. Only a 32-patient retrospective Achilles series is published.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2b RCT (NCT03485157, 446 randomized, KL 1-3) missed both primary endpoints (VAS and WOMAC at 90 days); only a pre-interim subgroup separated. A second Phase 2b (NCT05796765) was stopped by the sponsor at n=43 and the program was suspended in 2023. The only published knee data are a 100-knee retrospective series written with MiMedx employees.
applications.caveats: Negative primary endpoints; subgroup signal is post hoc; no BLA.

evidence.title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Micronized Dehydrated Human Amnion/Chorion Membrane (dHACM) Injection Compared to Placebo for the Treatment of Plantar Fasciitis
evidence.finding: Single-blind, 14 sites: 3-month VAS fell 76% with mdHACM vs 45% with saline (p<0.0001); FFI-R 60% vs 40%; no related serious adverse events.

evidence.title: Prospective, randomized, blinded, comparative study of injectable micronized dehydrated amniotic/chorionic membrane allograft for plantar fasciitis--a feasibility study
evidence.finding: Single-centre, 3 arms (saline, 0.5 cc, 1.25 cc): AOFAS hindfoot scores improved more with mdHACM at 1 and 8 weeks; 8-week follow-up only.

evidence.title: Micronized dHACM Injectable for the Treatment of Plantar Fasciitis (Phase 3)
evidence.finding: Double-blind, saline-controlled; MiMedx reported 13 Sept 2021 that it did not meet the 90-day VAS primary endpoint and that it would not file a BLA for plantar fasciitis (company release said 277 enrolled; registry lists 208).

evidence.title: Micronized dHACM Injectable for the Treatment of Achilles Tendonitis (Phase 3)
evidence.finding: Completed March 2021; no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and no publication located.

evidence.title: Micronized Dehydrated Human Amnion/Chorion Membrane Injection in the Treatment of Chronic Achilles Tendinitis
evidence.finding: Single-physician retrospective series; 66% reported symptom resolution within 45 days; no control group; MiMedx-affiliated authors.

evidence.title: Micronized dHACM vs. Saline in the Treatment of Osteoarthritis of the Knee (Phase 2b)
evidence.finding: Did not meet either primary endpoint (VAS, WOMAC at 90 days); results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; pre-interim cohort showed WOMAC separation.

evidence.title: Phase 2B Micronized DHACM vs. Saline in the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Terminated: 'Study discontinued early by Sponsor' after MiMedx suspended the program in 2023.

evidence.title: Micronized Dehydrated Human Amnion Chorion Membrane Injection in the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis-A Large Retrospective Case Series
evidence.finding: 100 knees (82 patients) given 100 mg mdHACM, KOOS followed 6 months; uncontrolled; MiMedx employees among authors.

evidence.title: Placental-derived injectable products for chronic plantar fasciitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Six studies: placebo-controlled RCTs favored placental injections (MD 3.37 points on 0-10 pain, I2=92%); GRADE certainty low to very low.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None: program disbanded Q2 2023; MiMedx FY2025 10-K records abandonment of the BLA.

bd.reimbursement: Q4145 ('Epifix, inj, 1mg') still exists in HCPCS, but the product cannot be lawfully promoted for joint or tendon injection without a BLA; any current billing of an amniotic injectable for musculoskeletal pain is a compliance red flag (see Celularity's 2022 False Claims Act civil investigative demand on injectable birth-tissue billing).
bd.notes: Useful as the cautionary tale: the best-funded amniotic injectable program in the US ended without a BLA.

name: NuCel (amniotic suspension for spinal fusion)
ownership_history: NuTech Medical product, acquired by Organogenesis 2017; commercial distribution ceased 31 May 2021; Organogenesis has discontinued clinical development.
composition: Amniotic suspension allograft (amniotic membrane and amniotic-fluid-derived cells) applied to the fusion bed.

regulatory.reference: None. Organogenesis states NuCel would need a BLA because it may be more than minimally manipulated and non-homologous; development discontinued.
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: Two Organogenesis-sponsored lumbar fusion studies (NCT02023372, n=57, completed 2019; NCT02808234, n=200, status unknown) have no posted results or publication located (2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Withdrawn; unpublished.

applications.evidence_summary: An investigator-initiated PLF study (NCT02070484, OhioHealth) terminated after 6 patients; no published PLF data located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Withdrawn product.

evidence.title: Efficacy Study of NuCel in Patients Undergoing Fusion of the Lumbar Spine
evidence.finding: Completed August 2019; no results posted.

evidence.title: Study of Nucel for One and Two Level Lumbar Interbody Fusion
evidence.finding: Status unknown; no results posted.

evidence.title: Preliminary Results of Bioactive Amniotic Suspension with Allograft for Achieving One and Two-Level Lumbar Interbody Fusion
evidence.finding: Kinematic fusion in 97.4% of one-level (n=38) and 100% of two-level (n=34) interbody fusions at 12 months or more; no comparison group.

evidence.title: Efficacy of a Human Amniotic Tissue-derived Allograft, NuCel, in Patients Undergoing Posterolateral Lumbar Fusions for Degenerative Disc Disease
evidence.finding: Randomized, participant-blinded investigator study terminated March 2017 for poor enrollment after 6 patients; no results.

bd.reimbursement: None current.
bd.notes: Example of an amniotic spine 'biologic' that left the market at the 2021 deadline.

challenge: A case of a company withdrawing its own spine biologic because it judged the product could not meet 361 criteria once enforcement discretion ended; Cigna's bone-graft policy still names NuCel under amniotic materials considered experimental.

name: NuDYN (amniotic-membrane-derived injectable)
ownership_history: US arm of Fidia Farmaceutici (Italy). HCPCS Q4233 groups NuDYN with Surgenex's SurFactor, suggesting a shared source product (not confirmed).
composition: Injectable product derived from amniotic membrane.

regulatory.reference: FDA CBER Untitled Letter, 3 April 2023: intended for injection, marketed for orthopedics, sports medicine, pain management and podiatry; non-homologous; regulated as a drug and 351 biologic needing a BLA.
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: No published study located; FDA letter cites orthopedic, sports-medicine and podiatry promotion.
applications.caveats: Status after the 2023 letter not confirmed.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study located.
applications.caveats: Unlicensed biologic per FDA.

bd.reimbursement: Q4233 listed.
bd.notes: Notable because Fidia also sells hyaluronic-acid viscosupplements (Hymovis, Triluron) to the same orthopedic offices.

name: OrthoFlo (amniotic fluid allograft)
ownership_history: Introduced by MiMedx about 2016 as an amniotic-fluid allograft for orthopedic and sports-medicine use (a lyophilized version was planned). Not in MiMedx's 2025 portfolio; MiMedx states it sells no Section 351 products in the US.
composition: Amniotic fluid from consenting full-term C-section donors (liquid; lyophilized version planned).

regulatory.reference: None. Amniotic fluid is not an HCT/P (secreted fluid excluded under 21 CFR 1271.3(d)); FDA regulates injectable amniotic fluid as a drug/biologic needing a BLA (Kimera 2023, BioLab Sciences 2022, Frontier Biologics 2024 letters).
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: MiMedx sponsored two saline-controlled amniotic-fluid knee OA trials (NCT02768155, n=60, completed 2017; NCT03074526, lyophilized, n=156, completed 2018); neither has posted results or a publication located (2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Unpublished; whether the tested product was branded OrthoFlo is not stated in the registry.

evidence.title: Clinical evaluation of an amniotic fluid product in knee osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Completed; no results posted.

evidence.title: Two doses of lyophilized amniotic fluid vs saline placebo in knee osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Completed April 2018; no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: None current.
bd.notes: Status 'withdrawn' is inferred from MiMedx's FY2025 10-K product list, which does not include OrthoFlo.

name: PalinGen Flow, PalinGen InovoFlo, PalinGen membrane and ProMatrX ACF
ownership_history: Amnio Technology, LLC (Phoenix, AZ). Warning letters August 2022 and 1 Oct 2024; private-label versions include ASGFluid, Cell-ECT, Gryphon Amnio Flow and SXFluid (per FDA footnote).
composition: PalinGen Flow: amniotic membrane plus amniotic fluid, flowable; InovoFlo and ProMatrX ACF: amniotic-fluid-derived; PalinGen/PalinGen Xplus sheets.

regulatory.reference: FDA Warning Letter CBER 24-646460 (1 Oct 2024): InovoFlo is not an HCT/P (secreted fluid); PalinGen Flow fails minimal manipulation (flowable processing destroyed membrane integrity, tensile strength, elasticity) and homologous use; unapproved new drugs; CGMP failures. Earlier warning letter August 2022.
on_label_indications: None for the flowables; sheets marketed as 361 wound covers

applications.evidence_summary: Flowables were 'intended for injection'; no published study located.
applications.caveats: Warning letters 2022 and 2024; current sale status unknown.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Amnio Technology, LLC (CBER 24-646460)
evidence.finding: Flowable amnion/amniotic-fluid injectables are unapproved drugs and unlicensed biologics; cites failed validation, stability and complaint reporting.

bd.reimbursement: Q4173 (PalinGen or PalinGen XPlus), Q4174 (PalinGen or ProMatrX), Q4354 (PalinGen DL) remain in HCPCS.

name: SurFactor, SurForce (amniotic membrane) and SurCord (umbilical cord) injectables
ownership_history: Surgenex LLC. Manufacturing stopped 16 April 2021 and distribution 28 May 2021 per the company's response to FDA. Fidia Pharma USA marketed an amniotic-membrane injectable as NuDYN (HCPCS Q4233 pairs 'SurFactor/NuDYN').
composition: Injectable processed amniotic membrane (SurFactor, SurForce) and umbilical cord (SurCord) products, purported sterile.

regulatory.reference: FDA Warning Letter OBPO 21-615254 (15 Nov 2021): drugs/biologics; fail homologous use (orthopedic conditions) and minimal manipulation; no BLA or IND; CGMP failures including 8 uninvestigated sterility failures (2017-2021).
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: Promoted 'for a variety of orthopedic diseases or conditions' by injection per FDA; no published study located.
applications.caveats: FDA warning letter; withdrawn.

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to Surgenex LLC (OBPO 21-615254)
evidence.finding: Injectable cord and amniotic products are unlicensed biologics; orthopedic use is non-homologous; processing is more than minimal manipulation.

bd.reimbursement: Q4233 ('SurFactor/NuDYN, per 0.5 cc') still listed in HCPCS; billing it for joint injection would be billing an unapproved biologic.

name: Cartilage Autograft Implantation System (CAIS)
ownership_history: DePuy Mitek program (J&J); pivotal IDE trial NCT00881023 (DePuy Mitek, n=75) was terminated; CAIS was never approved. DePuy Mitek's sports-medicine business is now within DePuy Synthes.
composition: Autologous minced cartilage from the patient loaded onto a biodegradable scaffold and fixed with absorbable staples in a single-stage procedure (general description; composition not verified in a primary source in this sweep).

regulatory.reference: US IDE pivotal study NCT00881023 (terminated); no PMA/BLA submitted that was located
on_label_indications: None (investigational; program abandoned)

applications.evidence_summary: AJSM 2011 RCT (n=29 randomized 1:2 vs microfracture, 2 years): IKDC 82.95 vs 59.5 at 24 months and KOOS subdomains better with CAIS. The 75-patient pivotal trial (NCT00881023) was terminated and not published.
applications.caveats: Tiny first trial; the pivotal trial was terminated (reason not stated in the registry data read); sponsor-funded; abandoned.

evidence.title: Outcomes after a single-stage procedure for cell-based cartilage repair: a prospective clinical safety trial with 2-year follow-up
evidence.finding: CAIS group IKDC 82.95 vs microfracture 59.5 at 24 months; adverse events similar.

evidence.title: Multicenter randomized pivotal study of CAIS for surgical treatment of articular cartilage defects of the knee
evidence.finding: Terminated December 2014; no results.

bd.reimbursement: Not marketed.
bd.notes: Historical record; particulated cartilage concept survives as DeNovo NT, BioCartilage and ProChondrix.

name: Cartiva Synthetic Cartilage Implant (SCI)
ownership_history: Cartiva, Inc. held the PMA; Wright Medical acquired Cartiva (2018, general knowledge) and Stryker acquired Wright Medical in November 2020. Class action filings name Cartiva, Stryker Canada and Wright Medical Canada.
composition: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel cylindrical plug (catalog sizes 6, 8, 10 and 12 mm per the recall record) press-fit into the first metatarsal head as a hemiarthroplasty.

regulatory.reference: P150017 (approved 2016-07-01); FDA recall Z-0598-2025 (event 95661) initiated 2024-10-31, status 'Open, Classified'
on_label_indications: Treatment of patients with painful degenerative or post-traumatic arthritis (hallux limitus or hallux rigidus) in the first metatarsophalangeal joint with or without the presence of mild hallux valgus (FDA PMA record)

challenge: Stryker recalled all Cartiva implants (distributed July 2016 to October 2024) on 2024-10-31 for a higher-than-expected rate of revision, removal, subsidence, displacement, pain, nerve damage or fragmentation; NICE and Singapore HSA followed. Despite the Level I RCT below, the product is effectively off-market.

applications.evidence_summary: MOTION RCT (Foot Ankle Int 2016; 2:1 implant vs first MTP arthrodesis, 12 sites Canada/UK; implant n=152, arthrodesis ~50): non-inferior pain and function at 24 months; 9.2% implant removals to arthrodesis at 2 years; 5.8-year follow-up (n=112 of 135 eligible): further 7.6% converted to arthrodesis in years 2-5, pain VAS improved 57.9 points. Later retrospective comparisons are mixed.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; non-inferiority design; 17% of implant patients had secondary surgeries; the 2024 recall reflects real-world failure rates higher than trial rates.

evidence.title: Prospective, Randomized, Multi-centered Clinical Trial Assessing Safety and Efficacy of a Synthetic Cartilage Implant Versus First Metatarsophalangeal Arthrodesis in Advanced Hallux Rigidus
evidence.finding: Equivalent pain relief and function to arthrodesis at 24 months; 9.2% removal rate. n is implant 152 plus arthrodesis ~50 (derived from reported percentages).

evidence.title: Midterm Outcomes of a Synthetic Cartilage Implant for the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint in Advanced Hallux Rigidus
evidence.finding: At mean 5.8 years pain VAS improved 57.9 points; 7.6% additional conversions to arthrodesis in years 2-5.

bd.reimbursement: Facility-supplied implant in outpatient foot-and-ankle surgery; Class II recall open.
bd.notes: Product liability suits followed the 2024 recall; Stryker foot-and-ankle franchise impact not quantified here.

name: ChondroCelect
ownership_history: TiGenix NV (Leuven, Belgium). EU marketing authorization 5 October 2009 (EMEA/H/C/000878) as the first ATMP; European Commission withdrew it 29 July 2016 (effective 30 November 2016) at TiGenix's request for commercial reasons (EMA EPAR). Takeda later acquired TiGenix (not verified here).
composition: Autologous chondrocytes expanded in monolayer and characterized for a marker profile predictive of cartilage-forming capacity; implanted under a periosteal flap or membrane.

regulatory.reference: EU: EMEA/H/C/000878, authorized 2009-10-05, withdrawn 2016. Never FDA-approved
on_label_indications: EU label (historic): repair of single symptomatic cartilage defects of the femoral condyle of the knee (ICRS grade III or IV) in adults (EMA EPAR)

applications.evidence_summary: Saris 2008/2009 (AJSM, n=118, 57 characterized chondrocyte implantation vs 61 microfracture): better structural repair at 1 year (histomorphometry P=.003), similar KOOS at 12-18 months; better clinical outcome at 36 months in a follow-up of the same randomized trial.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; withdrawn commercially, not for safety; included as the cautionary reference for EU cell products.

evidence.title: Characterized chondrocyte implantation results in better structural repair when treating symptomatic cartilage defects of the knee in a randomized controlled trial versus microfracture
evidence.finding: Better histologic structural repair than microfracture at 1 year; short-term KOOS comparable.

evidence.title: Treatment of symptomatic cartilage defects of the knee: characterized chondrocyte implantation results in better clinical outcome at 36 months in a randomized trial compared to microfracture
evidence.finding: Clinical outcome superior to microfracture at 36 months (abstract not read in full).

bd.reimbursement: Withdrawn.
bd.notes: Withdrawal for commercial reasons is the useful BD lesson: ATMP approval without volume/reimbursement did not sustain the product.

name: FiberCel Fiber Viable Bone Matrix
company: Berkeley Biologics (brand assets since November 2023); made by Aziyo Biologics (now Elutia), distributed exclusively in the US by Medtronic 2019-2021
ownership_history: Manufactured by Aziyo Biologics (Richmond, CA facility); exclusive multi-year US orthopedic distribution agreement with Medtronic announced June 2019 (Tissue Product Supply Agreement). Medtronic told Aziyo in October 2021 it would no longer distribute cellular bone products and the agreement was mutually terminated in December 2021. Aziyo renamed Elutia Inc. (2023). Elutia sold substantially all Orthobiologics assets, including the viable bone matrix products and the Richmond facility, to Berkeley Biologics, LLC (wholly owned subsidiary of GNI Group, Tokyo) on November 8, 2023 for about $14.6M plus up to $20M earn-out; Elutia retained all FiberCel and VBM recall liabilities.
composition: Cancellous bone particles with preserved living donor cells plus demineralized cortical bone fibers (Aziyo FY2020 10-K). Cryopreserved; single-donor lots.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER); no 510(k) in openFDA for device_name 'fibercel' (searched 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: Marketed 'for use in orthopedic or reconstructive bone grafting procedures in combination with autologous bone or other forms of allograft bone or alone as a bone graft' (Aziyo FY2020 10-K); bone void filler in orthopedic and spinal procedures (361 homologous use)

challenge: The category's defining safety event. Lot NMDS210011 came from one donor (a man aged 80 with unrecognised TB risk factors and signs); 154 units went to 37 facilities in 20 states (March 1 to April 2, 2021); 136 units were implanted in 113 patients in 18 states; 87 of 113 (77%) had microbiological or imaging evidence of TB disease; 8 recipients died (3 deaths attributed to TB); M. tuberculosis was found in all 8 sequestered unused units tested (Schwartz, Lancet Infect Dis 2022). Aziyo recalled the lot June 2, 2021. A rep should be able to explain why a living-cell graft cannot be terminally sterilized and why there was then no FDA-licensed donor TB screening test.

applications.evidence_summary: No published efficacy study of FiberCel in spinal fusion located (PubMed search 'FiberCel' 2026-10-23 returned no relevant record). The only peer-reviewed literature is the CDC outbreak investigation: 113 recipients, most during spinal fusion, 87 with TB disease.
applications.caveats: Historical tier (marketed 2019-2021). Withdrawn; any efficacy claim from Medtronic or Aziyo marketing is unsupported by published data.

applications.evidence_summary: No published study of FiberCel in posterolateral fusion located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Withdrawn 2021; listed so the outbreak history attaches to the spine applications where the product was used.

evidence.title: Nationwide tuberculosis outbreak in the USA linked to a bone graft product: an outbreak report
evidence.finding: Single-donor lot of a live-cell bone allograft implanted in 113 recipients in 18 states; 87 (77%) had TB disease, 8 died, all 105 survivors started TB treatment a median 69 days after implantation; isolates from product and patients were >99.99% genetically identical.

evidence.title: Transmission of Mycobacterium tuberculosis to Healthcare Personnel Resulting From Contaminated Bone Graft Material, United States, June 2021-August 2022
evidence.finding: CDC report documenting M. tuberculosis transmission to healthcare personnel exposed to the contaminated bone graft material or infected recipients during the 2021 outbreak.

evidence.title: Incomplete tissue product tracing during an investigation of a tissue-derived tuberculosis outbreak
evidence.finding: Colorado investigation showing the US has no system to track tissue products to individual recipients; a third patient with the outbreak strain was recorded as receiving a different donor lot.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in inpatient fusion MS-DRGs (no separate payment); product withdrawn.
bd.notes: Elutia FY2025 10-K: 110 FiberCel product-liability suits or claims since September 2021; 104 settled, 5 active at 12/31/2025; no remaining insurance for FiberCel litigation; combined FiberCel/VBM contingent liability $11.2M. In June 2024 Elutia sued Medtronic Sofamor Danek USA in Delaware Superior Court alleging Medtronic failed to defend and indemnify it under the 2019 supply agreement; Medtronic counterclaimed. Lesson for BD: the distributor's brand absorbs reputational damage, but the processor carries the liability unless the supply agreement says otherwise.

name: ViBone / ViBone Moldable Viable Bone Matrix (and OsteGro V)
company: Berkeley Biologics (brand assets since November 2023); made by Aziyo Biologics (now Elutia); ViBone distributed exclusively by RTI Surgical / Surgalign 2018-2023
ownership_history: Aziyo signed an exclusive US distribution agreement for ViBone with RTI Surgical (later Surgalign Holdings) in August 2018 ($2M upfront, minimums 2019-2021); co-marketing deal with SurGenTec (GraftGun cartridges) in 2018. Surgalign later distributed ViBone Moldable. Elutia announced a single-lot recall and the market withdrawal of all viable bone matrix products produced after a specified date in July 2023, then sold the Orthobiologics business to Berkeley Biologics (GNI Group) on November 8, 2023; Berkeley did not assume recall liabilities.
composition: ViBone: cancellous and demineralized cortical bone particles with preserved native cells; ViBone Moldable: moldable form; OsteGro V: cancellous particles plus demineralized cortical particles and fibers made with the same cell-preserving process (Aziyo FY2020 10-K). Company preclinical data (not peer reviewed) claimed less cell death than 'traditional' viable bone matrix processing.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER); no 510(k) in openFDA for 'vibone' or 'ostegro' (searched 2026-10-23)
on_label_indications: Marketed 'for use as allograft bone' (ViBone) and 'for the repair, replacement or reconstruction of bone defects' (OsteGro V) per Aziyo FY2020 10-K; 361 homologous use as bone graft

challenge: Second nationwide TB outbreak from the same manufacturer: ViBone Moldable and alloOss Plus (dental) lot TDS222820, shipped February 27 to June 20, 2023 to 13 facilities in 7 states; 36 surgical recipients, 5 laboratory-confirmed TB, 2 deaths. The lot had tested negative by nucleic acid amplification before release; culture of unused product was only done after the outbreak (MMWR 2024). Whether Berkeley Biologics has relaunched any viable bone matrix after the 2023 withdrawal could not be confirmed.

applications.evidence_summary: Kim 2023 sponsor-registered post-market single-arm study (NCT03425682, 118 enrolled): 12-month per-patient fusion 88.1% cervical by plain films read by an independent radiologist; no product-related adverse events reported.
applications.caveats: Single-arm, plain-film fusion assessment, sponsor-registered (Aziyo/Elutia); product later withdrawn after a TB outbreak.

applications.evidence_summary: Same post-market study (Kim 2023): 12-month per-patient lumbar interbody fusion 97.6% and per-level 100% on plain films.
applications.caveats: No control arm; radiographs not CT; withdrawn 2023.

applications.evidence_summary: The planned randomized ViBone vs DBM vs BMP trial in 3-level OLIF (NCT03896347) was withdrawn with zero enrollment; no lateral-fusion data located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Withdrawn product.

evidence.title: 12-Month clinical and radiographic outcomes of ViBone viable bone matrix in patients undergoing cervical and lumbar spinal fusion surgery
evidence.finding: Single-arm post-market study; per-patient fusion at 12 months 88.1% cervical and 97.6% lumbar (per-level 98.5% and 100%) on plain films; VAS, NDI and ODI improved. n is the ClinicalTrials.gov actual enrollment.

evidence.title: A Randomized Study Evaluating ViBone, Demineralized Bone Matrix, and Bone Morphogenetic Protein in 3-Level Oblique Lateral Lumbar Interbody Fusion
evidence.finding: Withdrawn before enrollment; no comparative data exist.

evidence.title: Second Nationwide Tuberculosis Outbreak Caused by Bone Allografts Containing Live Cells - United States, 2023
evidence.finding: Five of 36 surgical recipients had laboratory-confirmed TB and two died; whole-genome sequencing linked patient isolates to unused product, which had tested NAAT-negative before distribution; the response prevented up to 53 further procedures.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in inpatient fusion MS-DRGs; withdrawn.
bd.notes: Elutia FY2025 10-K: 28 VBM suits or claims since August 2023 (11 active, 16 settled at 12/31/2025) in CA, LA, TX, MI, OR and NY courts. The ViBone channel collapsed twice: Surgalign's bankruptcy (2023) and the July 2023 withdrawal. Berkeley Biologics' current viable-bone offering, if any, is unconfirmed.

name: map3 Cellular Allogeneic Bone Graft
ownership_history: Launched by RTI Surgical in 2014 using multipotent adult progenitor cell (MAPC) technology licensed from Athersys. FDA issued RTI a Warning Letter on 2017-11-08 (OBPO-1 18-01) holding that map3 could not be regulated solely as a 361 HCT/P. RTI ceased manufacturing and distributing map3 and incinerated its remaining inventory on 2018-12-19 under FDA observation; FDA's closeout letter is dated 2019-04-12 (MARCS-CMS 525318). RTI's spine business became Surgalign in 2020 (Surgalign went bankrupt in 2023; Xtant bought its assets), and RTI Surgical's OEM business was sold to Montagu Private Equity (announced 2020). Neither Xtant's FY2025 10-K nor RTI's current site lists map3: the product has been off the market since 2018.
composition: Cortical cancellous allograft chips, demineralized bone and cryopreserved multipotent adult progenitor cells (MAPC)

regulatory.reference: Section 361 HCT/P as claimed by RTI; FDA Warning Letter 2017-11-08 disputed this (map3 also subject to drug and biological product requirements); closeout letter 2019-04-12 after RTI stopped manufacture and distribution
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (361 homologous use)

applications.evidence_summary: One retrospective ALIF series (n=41) reported fusion equivalent to rhBMP-2 at 1 year (cited in the 2021 CBM systematic review); RTI's 30-patient ALIF/LLIF cohort (NCT02628210) completed 2020.
applications.caveats: Product may no longer be sold; a 2014 foot/ankle study was terminated after one patient.

evidence.title: Interbody spacers with map3 cellular allogeneic bone graft in ALIF or LLIF
evidence.finding: Completed June 2020; no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Illustrates the OEM-tissue-bank problem: when the distributor (Surgalign) failed, the brand effectively disappeared even though the processor (RTI) survived.

challenge: Discontinued 2018 (not merely absent from Xtant's list): FDA closeout letter 2019-04-12.

name: Kryptonite Bone Cement
composition: Calcified triglyceride (castor-oil-derived polyurethane with calcium carbonate) expanding adhesive cement; not a calcium phosphate

regulatory.reference: K091382 (2009-11-16, product code GXP, Methyl Methacrylate for Cranioplasty); FDA recall Z-1496-2012, event 61709
on_label_indications: Repair of cranial defects (cranioplasty)

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed 2010 to 2012 as an adhesive, expanding cranioplasty cement; a bench study found unpredictable expansion (mean 49 percent, SD 22) and a single-center cohort reported post-craniotomy infection of 17.8 percent in exposed versus 0.42 percent in unexposed patients (RR 42). The firm initiated a Class 2 recall of all lots (3,100 kits) on 2012-04-06 because strength and stiffness fell below specification at body temperature; the recall was terminated 2015-07-14 and the product has not reappeared.
applications.caveats: The FDA record is a voluntary recall, not a formal withdrawal; no relaunch, sale of the asset or new 510(k) was found.

evidence.title: The expansile properties of Kryptonite relating to cranioplasty
evidence.finding: Ten reconstituted samples expanded a mean 49 percent (SD 22) in saline, most within two hours, explaining the contour irregularities seen clinically.

evidence.title: FDA recall record Z-1496-2012, Kryptonite Bone Cement 5cc and 10cc kits
evidence.finding: Class 2 recall of 3,100 kits distributed January 2010 to April 2012 because bone cement strength and stiffness fall below specification at body temperature; terminated 2015-07-14.

evidence.title: Single-hospital retrospective cohort of post-craniotomy infection with Kryptonite exposure (Cureus, 2014)
evidence.finding: Infection 17.8 percent in Kryptonite-exposed craniotomies versus 0.42 percent unexposed, relative risk 42.1 (95 percent CI 5.1 to 348).

bd.reimbursement: n/a
bd.notes: Cautionary case for the GXP product code: cleared on bench data as substantially equivalent to PMMA, failed in the field within two years.

name: Chrysalin (TP508, rusalatide acetate) for fracture healing - failed
ownership_history: Developed by OrthoLogic Corp., which later renamed itself Capstone Therapeutics (the current ClinicalTrials.gov sponsor name). OrthoLogic obtained TP508 by acquiring Chrysalis BioTechnology (year not confirmed).
composition: TP508, a 23-amino-acid synthetic peptide from the receptor-binding region of human thrombin, injected once into the fracture site.

regulatory.reference: US IND (number not public). Distal radius Phase 2 NCT00131482 (n=274) terminated 2007: 'Treatment with Chrysalin did not demonstrate benefit compared to placebo.'

applications.evidence_summary: Placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial in unstable distal radius fractures (NCT00131482, n=274) stopped in 2007 for lack of benefit; full results were not published in a journal (PubMed search 2026-10-23), so the registry statement is the only outcome.
applications.caveats: Grade I by design only; the result exists as a one-line registry statement, and earlier positive Phase 1/2 signals were never peer-reviewed.
applications.challenge: Do not cite TP508 as a fracture-healing option; it failed its only adequately sized trial.

evidence.title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety and Effectiveness of Different Doses of Chrysalin in Adults Who Have a Broken Wrist
evidence.finding: Terminated: no benefit vs placebo.

evidence.title: Thrombin peptide TP508 stimulates cellular events leading to angiogenesis, revascularization, and repair of dermal and musculoskeletal tissues
evidence.finding: Mechanism review of animal and cell data.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Historical failure; TP508 was later studied as a radiation countermeasure, outside orthopedics.

name: KUR-111 (PTH-based fibrin bone graft substitute for tibial plateau fracture) - discontinued
ownership_history: Kuros Biosurgery (Zurich) fibrin-PTH family (KUR-111 tibial plateau, KUR-113 open tibia and TLIF). Rights to the fibrin-PTH candidates were held by Baxter for a period and returned to Kuros (per Kuros statements in trade coverage). Kuros decided in December 2023 not to take fibrin-PTH into Phase 3 and now sells MagnetOs. The sibling KUR-113 is an existing record (kur-113-fibrin-pth). A 'KUR-112' could not be found in any source.
composition: TGplPTH1-34 (PTH 1-34 engineered with a transglutaminase substrate and plasmin-cleavable link) bound in a fibrin matrix, used as a bone graft substitute in the metaphyseal void; low and high peptide doses tested.

regulatory.reference: Not authorized anywhere. The tibial plateau trial ran in Europe (Leeds, Munster and other centers); registry number not given in the abstract and no US IND located.

applications.evidence_summary: Kanakaris 2026 randomized, open-label, dose-blinded multicenter trial (n=183 closed tibial plateau fractures; iliac crest autograft vs KUR-111 low vs high dose): KUR-111 high was non-inferior to autograft for CT union at 16 weeks and better than low dose (83.6% vs 66.1%, p=0.03); loss of reduction 0.4-0.9 mm in all arms; donor-site pain 61.8% at discharge in the autograft arm.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-authored (Kuros employee co-author), open-label, surrogate CT endpoint; published years after the program was shelved, so no product will follow.

evidence.title: Novel parathyroid hormone-based bone graft substitute, KUR-111, in treatment of tibial plateau fractures: a prospective, randomised, open-label, multicenter study
evidence.finding: High-dose KUR-111 non-inferior to autograft for 16-week CT union and superior to low dose (83.6% vs 66.1%).

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: Historical; shows a local PTH approach that matched autograft in plateau voids but was dropped for commercial reasons.

name: Ampion (low molecular weight fraction of human serum albumin, LMWF-5A)
ownership_history: Ampio reportedly adopted a wind-down, delisted and was dissolved in 2024 (Fierce Biotech and secondary analysis sites; SEC filings not read).
composition: Filtered <5 kDa fraction of human serum albumin injected intra-articularly.

regulatory.reference: IND (BLA never filed)
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: The pivotal AP-013 trial (NCT03988023, n=1,043 enrolled) was terminated by the sponsor after DSMB guidance and the registry shows no significant pain difference (p=0.32); earlier phase 3 AP-003-A and phase 2 trials were mixed and the program ended.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded, company defunct; dissolution date from secondary sources.

evidence.title: AP-013: randomized, double-blind study of an intra-articular injection of Ampion in severe knee osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Terminated early by the sponsor after DSMB guidance; registry primary comparison p=0.32 (no significant difference).

evidence.title: A randomized clinical trial to evaluate two doses of an intra-articular injection of LMWF-5A in adults with pain due to osteoarthritis of the knee (Bar-Or, PLoS One)
evidence.finding: Randomized trial of two Ampion doses in knee OA pain (abstract details not extracted here).

bd.reimbursement: Never marketed.
bd.notes: Included as the cautionary tale in a crowded DMOAD field.

name: LNA043 (ANGPTL3-derived cartilage-regeneration peptide)
ownership_history: Novartis internal program.
composition: Recombinant angiopoietin-like 3-derived peptide injected intra-articularly.

regulatory.reference: phase 2b NCT04864392 terminated; phase 1 published (Gerwin 2022)
on_label_indications: None

applications.evidence_summary: The phase 2 knee OA study (NCT04864392, n=576) was terminated early 'due to lack of effect' on primary and secondary endpoints, not safety; a combination study with canakinumab (NCT04814368) also terminated.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; a randomized phase 1 was published in Nature Medicine 2022.

evidence.title: Efficacy, safety and tolerability of LNA043 in patients with knee osteoarthritis (phase 2b)
evidence.finding: Terminated early for lack of effect on primary and secondary endpoints, not linked to safety.

evidence.title: Angiopoietin-like 3-derivative LNA043 for cartilage regeneration in osteoarthritis: a randomized phase 1 trial (Gerwin, Nat Med)
evidence.finding: Randomized phase 1 trial of LNA043 in OA cartilage (abstract details not extracted here).

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable.
bd.notes: A negative data point for the structure-modification (DMOAD) approach alongside lorecivivint.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Program stopped

name: AMPLIFY rhBMP-2 Matrix (rhBMP-2 on compression-resistant matrix) - never approved
ownership_history: rhBMP-2 originated at Genetics Institute (later part of Wyeth, which Pfizer acquired in 2009). Medtronic Sofamor Danek held the spinal rights and sponsored the AMPLIFY trials; Wyeth/Pfizer kept other fields and ran the injectable rhBMP-2/CPM fracture program (record rhbmp2-cpm-wyeth-pfizer). In July 2013 Pfizer out-licensed its BMP portfolio, including rhBMP-2 fields previously reserved to Pfizer, to Bioventus (record bioventus-pfizer-bmp-portfolio). The exact field split between Medtronic and Wyeth/Pfizer is not public in the sources read.
composition: High-dose rhBMP-2 (2.0 mg/mL; 40 mg per patient in the pivotal trial, per Carragee 2013) on a compression-resistant matrix of collagen with hydroxyapatite/tricalcium phosphate granules, placed posterolaterally without autograft.

regulatory.reference: PMA P050036 (number from secondary sources; openFDA PMA database lists no AMPLIFY record because it was never approved). FDA Orthopaedic and Rehabilitation Devices Panel met 2010-07-27 (Federal Register notice 2010-15350): 9-4 safety, 10-3 effectiveness, 6-5 (3 abstaining) benefit-risk, per Medtronic. Medtronic disclosed in a March 2011 SEC filing that FDA said it could not approve AMPLIFY without additional information (reported as a non-approvable letter). No later approval.
on_label_indications: None. Proposed indication: single-level instrumented posterolateral lumbar fusion for degenerative disc disease as an autograft replacement (never approved).

challenge: AMPLIFY is the rhBMP-2 product that a panel narrowly backed and FDA still did not approve; the cancer signal (15 new cancer events in 11 patients vs 2 in 2 controls at 2 years) is why posterolateral rhBMP-2 remains off-label for Infuse today.

applications.evidence_summary: Dimar 2009 pivotal RCT (n=463, NCT00707265): 2-year fusion 96% rhBMP-2/CRM vs 89% iliac crest (p=0.014), fewer nonunion failures (6 vs 18) and second surgeries, similar ODI/SF-36 gains; Carragee 2013 reanalysis of the same trial found a higher new-cancer incidence (3.37 vs 0.50 per 100 person-years at 2 years, IRR 6.75).
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded pivotal trial; cancer events were few and FDA judged the overall risk unacceptable at this dose. Never approved: any use of this formulation is unavailable, and posterolateral use of marketed Infuse is off-label.

evidence.title: Clinical and radiographic analysis of an optimized rhBMP-2 formulation as an autograft replacement in posterolateral lumbar spine arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Fusion 96% vs 89% at 24 months (p=0.014); nonunion failures 6 vs 18; less operative time and blood loss; clinical outcomes similar.

evidence.title: Cancer risk after use of recombinant bone morphogenetic protein-2 for spinal arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Reanalysis of the AMPLIFY pivotal trial: 15 new cancer events in 11 rhBMP-2/CRM patients vs 2 in 2 controls at 2 years; IRR 6.75 (95% CI 1.57-60.83).

evidence.title: Clinical outcomes and fusion success at 2 years of single-level instrumented posterolateral fusions with rhBMP-2/compression resistant matrix versus iliac crest bone graft
evidence.finding: Fusion 88% rhBMP-2/CRM vs 73% ICBG (p=0.051); no significant differences in clinical outcomes; less operative time and blood loss.

evidence.title: Initial fusion rates with rhBMP-2/compression resistant matrix and a hydroxyapatite and tricalcium phosphate/collagen carrier in posterolateral spinal fusion
evidence.finding: Single-center subset: higher CT fusion grade with rhBMP-2/CRM at 6 and 12 months than ICBG.

evidence.title: rhBMP-2/CRM/CD HORIZON Spinal System Pivotal Study
evidence.finding: Completed 2005; registry posts no results; published as Dimar 2009.

evidence.title: rhBMP-2/CRM/CD HORIZON Spinal System Pilot Study (2-level)
evidence.finding: Completed 2009; no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable; never marketed.
bd.notes: Never sold. Matters to BD because it explains the Infuse label boundary and why Medtronic's later rhBMP-2 work moved to the interbody space.

name: OP-1 Implant / OP-1 Putty (rhBMP-7, eptotermin alfa)
company: Withdrawn from the US; last held by Olympus Biotech Corporation (rights later passed to Ember Therapeutics and reportedly Viscogliosi Brothers)
ownership_history: Creative BioMolecules developed OP-1; Stryker Biotech (Hopkinton, MA) commercialized it, receiving HDE H010002 on October 17, 2001 for long-bone nonunion and HDE H020008 (2004) for revision posterolateral lumbar fusion. An FDA advisory panel voted against a PMA for OP-1 Putty in uninstrumented posterolateral fusion in 2009. Stryker agreed on 2010-12-06 to sell the OP-1 family to Olympus Corporation for $60 million and closed the sale on 2011-02-01 (Olympus Biotech). Olympus closed Olympus Biotech's US operations and discontinued US sales in 2014. Ember Therapeutics later held the asset and announced a divestiture to Viscogliosi Brothers in 2018; the FDA HDE record still lists Olympus Biotech as applicant.
composition: Recombinant human osteogenic protein-1 (BMP-7) 3.5 mg with 1 g bovine type I collagen carrier (Implant); Putty adds carboxymethylcellulose.

regulatory.reference: H010002 (OP-1 Implant; HDE original received 2001-05-29, approved 2001-10-17; product code OKD); H020008 (OP-1 Putty; received 2002-12-23, approved 2004-04-07; product code OJZ; revision posterolateral lumbar fusion); both combination products with supplements through S033/S022
on_label_indications: Alternative to autograft in recalcitrant long bone nonunions where use of autograft is unfeasible and alternative treatments have failed (HDE; use limited to 4,000 patients per year with IRB oversight)

applications.evidence_summary: Pivotal IDE RCT in tibial nonunion (Friedlaender 2001, 122 patients/124 nonunions): OP-1 plus IM nail was statistically indistinguishable from autograft (clinical success 81% versus 85%; radiographic 75% versus 84%), with no donor-site pain. Equivalence was not demonstrated to PMA standard, hence the HDE.
applications.caveats: Tibial data; non-inferiority not formally shown; sponsor-funded; product no longer available in the US.

applications.evidence_summary: Friedlaender 2001 (n=122 patients, 124 tibial nonunions) randomized OP-1 vs autograft with IM nailing; OP-1 reached clinical and radiographic success comparable to autograft without donor-site morbidity. This remains the only RCT of a BMP against autograft in tibial nonunion.
applications.caveats: HDE, not PMA: FDA did not require demonstrated effectiveness; partially blinded; product withdrawn 2014 so the evidence has no commercial vehicle in the US.
applications.challenge: A hiring manager will ask why the best nonunion RCT in the field belongs to a dead product and whether rhBMP-2 can borrow it (it cannot, legally).

applications.evidence_summary: Diamond-concept series (Giannoudis group) used rhBMP-7 with RIA graft and BMAC in femoral and tibial nonunions (n=64; n=14 subtrochanteric) with high union rates; the 2025 network meta-analysis pools these BMP-7 era trials.
applications.caveats: Series are European and used BMP-7 that is no longer sold; cannot be reproduced in the US.

applications.evidence_summary: The HDE long-bone nonunion indication covered the humerus; comparative data (Hackl 2017, PMID:28784168) showed no benefit of adding rhBMP-7 to properly revised humeral, femoral and tibial nonunions.
applications.caveats: Product withdrawn; included for history and because surgeons still cite OP-1 data when arguing for BMP in the upper extremity.

applications.evidence_summary: Bilic 2006 RCT (n=17) is the only randomized BMP evidence in the carpus.
applications.caveats: Tiny trial; not reproducible with any marketed product.

evidence.title: Osteogenic protein-1 (bone morphogenetic protein-7) in the treatment of tibial nonunions.
evidence.finding: OP-1 with IM nailing matched fresh autograft on clinical and radiographic success at 9 months without donor-site morbidity.

evidence.title: Long bone non-unions treated with the diamond concept: a case series of 64 patients
evidence.finding: Revision fixation plus RIA graft, BMP-7 and concentrated marrow aspirate in femoral (55%) and tibial (34%) nonunions; high union with painless weight bearing as the clinical definition.

evidence.title: Osteogenic protein-1 (BMP-7) accelerates healing of scaphoid non-union with proximal pole sclerosis
evidence.finding: Faster radiographic healing with OP-1; allograft plus OP-1 equaled autograft.

evidence.title: Long-term outcome following additional rhBMP-7 application in revision surgery of aseptic humeral, femoral, and tibial shaft nonunion
evidence.finding: No difference in healing or function with rhBMP-7.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable (withdrawn).
bd.notes: The lesson for BD: an HDE caps volume at 4,000 units a year and requires IRB approval at every site, which kept OP-1 a sub-scale product; failure to convert to a PMA (2009 panel) and the Stryker Biotech off-label promotion case (Stryker Biotech pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor in 2012 over OP-1 Putty/Calstrux promotion; not re-verified here) ended the franchise.

name: rhBMP-2/CPM (injectable rhBMP-2 in calcium phosphate matrix) for closed fractures - discontinued
ownership_history: Developed by Wyeth (Genetics Institute heritage); Pfizer acquired Wyeth in 2009 and is the registry sponsor of record. Wyeth senior management terminated the tibial Phase 2/3 early (2009). Pfizer out-licensed its BMP portfolio, including rhBMP-2 fields previously reserved to Pfizer, to Bioventus in July 2013.
composition: rhBMP-2 (1.0 or 2.0 mg/mL) in an injectable calcium phosphate matrix, injected percutaneously into a closed fracture at the time of fixation.

regulatory.reference: US IND (number not public). Trials: NCT00387686 (tibia, Phase 2/3, terminated), NCT00384852 (humerus, Phase 2), NCT00161629 (distal radius, Phase 1), NCT00243295 (open-wedge osteotomy, Phase 1), NCT00752557 (low bone density, Phase 2).
on_label_indications: None; never approved anywhere.

applications.evidence_summary: Lyon 2013 double-blind RCT (n=369, NCT00387686): terminated after interim analysis; median time to radiographic union 13.1 weeks standard of care vs 13.0 (1.0 mg/mL) and 15.9 (2.0 mg/mL) weeks, no faster return to pain-free weight-bearing.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; a negative trial, consistent with the closed-tibia application note that biologics are not indicated after reamed nailing.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2 trial in closed humerus fractures (NCT00384852, n=139) completed 2010; no results posted or published (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Unpublished sponsor trial.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 1 in closed distal radius fractures (NCT00161629, n=40); no results posted or published (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: Unpublished sponsor trial.

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of rhBMP-2/calcium phosphate matrix for closed tibial diaphyseal fracture: a double-blind, randomized, controlled phase-II/III trial
evidence.finding: No shortening of time to union or to pain-free full weight-bearing vs standard of care; terminated for futility at interim.

evidence.title: A Phase 2/3 Multicenter, Controlled Trial of rhBMP-2/CPM in Tibial Fractures
evidence.finding: Terminated 2009 by Wyeth senior management after interim analysis.

evidence.title: A Study of rhBMP-2/CPM in Closed Fractures of the Humerus
evidence.finding: Completed 2010; no results posted.

evidence.title: Study Evaluating rhBMP-2/CPM in Closed Distal Radius Fractures
evidence.finding: Phase 1; completed; no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable; never marketed.
bd.notes: The best-powered test of an injectable BMP for acute closed fractures, and it was negative; useful context when anyone pitches an injectable osteoinductive for routine fractures.
